2019.notes: Joe rode his Nick Chubb and Lamar Jackson to another victory, pushing him into the 2019 Biscuit championship match. Nick Chubb scored 25 points, which was only half of what Lamar Jackson scored, which was enough to get the win, as the rest of the team barely even showed up to the game in week 15. Despite the poor performances across the board, it's tough to bet against cheat code Lamar Jackson in any game. Joe is already guaranteed to earn his best finish in the league, and will be looking to be The Biggest Biscuit with a week 16 win.

WHAT A GAME! Game Of Jones narrowly escapes the Taco Truck with 2 late Buffalo DST interceptions in a 158-156 win. This game had all the makings of a championship game in the semifinals, with the high scores and huge games from several players on both teams. Josh is clearly doing something right, as he is now playing in his 2nd consecutive championship game. Josh will be looking to come away with better results than his 2018 Finals loss to Yisha's Just The Tip.

Team Taco Truck suffers a heartbreaking loss in the semifinals to Game Of Jones 158-156, ending Gil's chance to earn his 1st Risky Biscuit championship. WR Julio Jones' 34 point game wasn't enough to overcome Game Of Jones' 2 late-game interception contributions by the Bills DST. This was an amazing game, which usually happens in the semis and overshadows the championship game, but unfortunately for Gil, he came out on the losing end. Gil will now shift his focus to tying his best league finish by winning the 3rd place game against Ryan's Wolfpack.

Ryan and The Wolfpack get Cooked by Lamar Jackson's 50 point game, and fall to Gallup On My Johnson in a close 128-114 matchup. Ryan likely was unable to stomach watching the Bucs' game, as clear superstar WR Breshad Perriman scored a whopping 33 points on his bench. Possibly even tougher to watch, was RB Mike Boone (who?) of the Minnesota Vikings come in for RB Dalvin Cook (left with an injury after scoring 7 points), and score 2 touchdowns. With Ryan's semifinal defeat, the Risky Biscuit Brigade will officially crown a brand new champion in 2019.

Yisha slapped Trevor with much more than Just The Tip in the 5th/6th place game, as he easily won 157-87. Yish coming off a tough quarterfinal loss to Ryan, showed that he may have been the most deserving team to be in the championship. Unfortunately for Yish, this game ended his season, however he at least earned himself the best pick in the 2020 draft that a playoff team can achieve (7th overall).

Trevor ends the year eating a plate full of hot garbage, as his streak 4th or better ends, and his streak of 6th place begins. Trevor got The Full Tip in week 15, and was beat so badly that not even adding benched RB Kenyan Drake's 44 point, 4 TD performance to his lineup would make up the point differential. Trevor wil close this chapter as quickly as possible and start prepping to write his 2020 chapter.

The Dingles brought all their berries to this Fight, as they wiped their butt with The Ballers in week 15. Jerry's team may not show up during the season, but boy are they interested in that 1st overall pick, as Jerry now has a chance at back to back 1st overall selections. Good or bad? Up to you.

Nick/Austin keep their 1st overall pick hopes alive, in what seemed like the perfect loser bracket game, beating Jonathan 116-99. Nothing exciting to discuss in this win, other than WR DeVante Parker keeping his hot streak going through his injury (22 points). Nick/Austin square off against Jerry's red hot Dingleberries, in arguably the most important game of both their seasons. The 2020 Risky Biscuit Brigade #1 overall selection is at stake in week 16.

The Ballers were on the wrong end of a massive Dingleberry, as they got pooped on by Jerry 167-126. In what has been a mostly disappointing season for Jim, he is now removed from the #1 pick contention, and is hoping to solidify the #3 overall pick with a win against Jonathan's Magic.

Jonathan's Magic sprinked pixie dust on Lockett and Ingram and got 49 points from them, but left the rest of the team with no Magic, recording strictly single digits. Luckily for Jonathan, he still has a shot to obtain a top 3 pick in next year's draft, and can only fall as far as the 4th overall pick. Hopefully for JAWORking My Magic, Ingram and Lockett will share their secret stuff with the rest of the team in week 16.

The Big Salami ends the 2019 season with a win, which wipes away the sting of the entire season! Just kidding, this year sucked a butt. However, it was nice to see the potential this team had if it could have been healthy at the same time. It was nice to slap the self-proclaimed Mayor in his Titties one last time this year, but Jimmie is now focused on a new formula to make the Salami bigger and better for next year.

The self-proclaimed Mayor of Titty City packed his suitcase and closed the City up a week early, as he put up a wicked 85 points in the exclusive 11th/12th place game. The high point for Jacube this week was the Indy DST putting up a -3.62 score on the week, as the rest of the team was basically business as usual. Jacube's first year as a Risky Biscuit yielded a tough 12th place/6th overall 2020 pick. The 1st year is the toughest for an expansion team, and Jacube will look to get his Titties back in line for the 2020 season.

Ryan came into the playoffs as the 5th seed and up against ,what appeared to be, a powerhouse roster in Just The Tip. The Wolfpack battled through injuries, close calls and terrible performances, and came out as the alpha Wolf in this one, winning 104-99 over Yisha. With the win, Ryan is scheduled to take on the league's top team, Gallup On My Johnson, in the semifinals. It appears as though Ryan's roster is starting to click/heal at the right time, as a chance to play for his 2nd ring is on the line.

Game of Jones gathered all the dragons in the land, and let them all loose on Trevor's Caught Daking It, as he dominated with a 184 point week. All 3 of Josh's RBs scored 20+ points, with 2 of them scoring 30+ points. Josh also played the turnover machine, QB Jameis Winston, who finished 2nd on the week with 48.89 points. Game of Jones enters the semifinals with some clout behind him, and an appetite for Tacos.

Joe Galluped his Johnson into the playoffs as the league's number 1 seed, earning himself a round 1 bye. Unfortunately for Joe, fantasy bye weeks can't prevent injuries in real life. Joe will have to sort out some major injuries/injury concerns heading into the semifinal week 15 matchup against Ryan, who has the league's only upset of the playoffs thus far.

The Taco Truck could not have had a better week to be bye than week 14, as they were dealing with the flu, injuries and terrible matchups. Despite getting his players back on the field, Gil drew a tough matchup against Game of Jones, who just put up a measly 184 points on Trevor in the quarterfinals. The Truck better be serving up their best Tacos in week 15.

A team that began as an explosive, record-setting roster, has ended with a flat and upsetting finish, as they lose their round 1 playoff matchup, and will now play for the 7th overall pick in 2020. Only scoring 99 points in the quarterfinal matchup, Yisha lost a close game (104-99) to Ryan and the Wolfpack. Injuries plagued this team at the wrong time of year, and big name trade players did not do what was needed when it mattered most. With Yisha out of the race, Ryan is the only remaining Biscuit with the opportunity to collect his 2nd championship ring.

Trevor kept his 4 year playoff streak alive, however, his 3 year "4th or better" streak came to an end in week 14. Trevor pulled the short straw and ended up on the receiving end of a 184-133 spanking. Trevor's backside is certainly red after that one, especially with the little added salt of knowing his score of 133 would have been enough to beat both of the other quarterfinal teams, but he will have to handle those wounds quickly and prepare for his matchup against Yisha to determine who will get the 7th pick in the 2020 draft.

Nick/Austin ended the regular season on a high note, and landed a round 1 bye. Hopefully mentally rested, Nick/Austin have to prepare for Jonathan's volatile lineup. Week 14 brought some injuries into this roster, but week 15 may bring back some previously injured players back into action, such as WR Juju Smith-Schuster, who missed the previous 3 games with a knee injury. A top 2 pick in the 2020 draft is at stake in this matchup.

Despite being knocked out of the playoffs in the final week of the season, Jerry could at least hang on to his round 1 consolation bracket bye, which locked him into a top 4 pick in next year's draft. Unfortunately for Jerry, his team played extremely well during that bye, and he will have to hope for back to back strong performances to win in the semis. Rolling out QB Ryan Fitzpatrick shows you what kind of Dingles Jerry has down there.

Jonathan JAWORked his Magic against Jimmie's Big Salami, as he had him tilting all Sunday morning forcing him to make bad start/sit decisions. Garbage time points from WR Amari Cooper and random greatness from WR Robert Woods propelled the Magic into the 2nd round of the consolation bracket, guaranteeing this team a top 4 pick in the 2020 Risky Biscuit draft.

Jim must have been confident that he could walk into Titty City and slap the self-proclaimed Mayor around easily, because he rested his studs (QB Drew Brees 53.31 and WR AJ Brown 34.45) and still walked away with a 26 point victory. Hopefully the easy win doesn't lull this team into complacency, as they will need to be firing on all cylinders to take down the DingleJerrys, who won't go down without a Fight.

If you've paid attention to how the 2019 season has gone for The Big Salami, then it should come as no surprise that they came up short in their round one consolation bracket matchup 111-98. This Salami was harder to swallow, as for one of the few times this year, they left enough points on the bench to win the game. A fitting finish to an extremely disappointing season.

Confidence is key when self-proclaiming your Mayoral status, however, starting a player (RB Josh Jacobs) who was ruled out, just seems insane! Luckily, even swapping in a bech player for Jacobs, would have still resulted in a loss for Jacob. All that's left for these Titties, is deciding who gets to pick 5th or 6th in the 2020 draft (exciting!).

The big Johnson won a high scoring 100-95 point thriller against Jim and The Ballers, to earn himself the top spot in the league heading into playoffs. QB Lamar Jackson and RB Devin Singletary cmobined for half the team's points in week 13, which will likely not be enough to earn wins in the weeks to come. Joe will take this round 1 bye week to prepare for his semifinal matchup against the winner of Yisha and Ryan.

Despite being the highest scoring team in the league by 100+ points, Yisha snuck into the playoffs by Just The Tip with his week 13 win over Game of Jones. Just The Tip benched a massive amount of points, but was still able to sneak out a season-saving victory. The win put Yisha at a 7-6 record on the year, which was good enough for 4th place. Yisha will be hoping for the Mahomes-hill stack of old to compliment his McCaffrey numbers against Ryan and The Wolfpack.

The Wolfpack snacked on The Big Salami in week 13, and filled up enough to stay in a playoff spot. Ryan was in a must-win position, and he handled business accordingly. Primarily on the back of QB DeShaun Watson, WR DJ Moore and RB Miles Sanders, Ryan won by nearly 25 points. The Wolfpack keep their playoff streak alive, and enter their 4th consecutive playoff appearance - this time as the 5th seed. Ryan vs. Yisha week 14.

Game of Jones drops a meaningless game, and remains in the 3rd spot in the standings. Josh had a chance to knock out his brother-in-law, Yisha, with a week 13 win, but failed to do so, and kept a powerhouse team in the playoff picture. Josh will square off against Trevor, who is coming off a red hot performance.

Team Taco Dump dropped a quadruple deuce (80 points), and dropped out of the league's top spot with a loss to Nick/Austin. While Gil dropped from the #1 spot, he didn't fall far, and landed at #2, which earns his squad the elusive week 14 bye. Injuries are hitting the squad at the wrong time of year, and Gil will hope his team can heal over the next 2 weeks to be ready for their week 15 semifinal opponent.

Caught Daking It brings the big guns into week 13 and guns down the self-procliamed Mayor, 159-148. This was a season-saving week, as a loss would have sent Trevor to the consolation bracket. Fortunately for him, every starter for this roster put together a massive game when they needed to most. Hopefully Trevor can rally the troops to put together a duplicate week, as making it to the playoffs is great, but now the hard work starts! Trevor, like Ryan, continues his streak of 4 straight playoff appearances.

BELLsnickel Left! went full DeVante Parker on the Taco Truck in week 13, and knocked Gil out of 1st place, while also earning themselves a bye in round 1 of the consolation bracket. With quality games from the entire roster, plus a booster shot of DeVante Parker, Nick/Austin put up an impressive week. They will hope to continue these big time performances in two weeks in the consolation semifinal.

Jonathan reached deep into his hat of tricks and pulled out an Aaron Rdogers, holding a Tyler Lockett, holding an Eagle, holding a W. It was quite the trick. While in his lineup, the Philly DST was playing against Jonathan in this one, scoring -1 points, which was exactly 1 point less than WR Tyler Lockett scored. Luckily for the two of them, they latched onto the 38 point cheese at QB. Even with the win, the Magic fell one win short of a week 1 bye in the consolation bracket, but still sort of win because they get to face The Big Salami round 1.

The self-proclaimed Mayor found himself in a shootout against Caught Daking It, which left Titty City destroyed in the battle, as they lost 159-148. Jacob's only mistake on the week was playing WR DJ Chark do do do do do do do do doo, over WR Alshon Jeffery, who scored 20 more points than the great white. Fortunately for Jacob, this was a meaningless game, as his week 14 consolation matchup was set against Jim regardless of the outcome of this game.

Week 13 of the 2019 season will be one Jerry will want to forget, as he saw himself go from 4th place to 7th and out of the playoffs all in one game. Jerry lost the final two weeks of the regular season, and ended with a 7-6 record and a 4-way tie for a playoff spot. 10 points was all that stood in the way of Jerry's ticket in, but came up short as bench players dominated the starters. Jerry still has a good chance at obtaining the 1st overall pick in back to back years, with his 1st round bye.

The Big Salami locked up the last place slot in week 13, but is hoping his team can rally together to put together 3 strong weeks in a row. If this team can somehow figure out how to have more than 2-3 players show up at once, they could make a run for the 1st pick.

The Ballers missed their chance at a round 1 bye in the consolation bracket by a 4 point loss to the league's number 1 team. Jim found himself on the wrong side of 100 points, and watched as multiple bench players doubled or tripled their starting counterparts' scores. Jim earned the 10th spot heading into the consolation bracket, and will face off against the self-proclaimed Mayor in week 14.

Gallup On My Johnson goes full Chubb and stands a bit taller than The Big Salami. RB Nick Chubb put up 28 points, which took a backseat to the 49 point performance from QB Lamar Jackson. The rest of Joe's team participated, but the win was obtained through Chubb and Jackson. Scary team if these guys continue to show up guns blazing.

Game of Jones goes searching for a win, and comes back with a trio of 30+ point games. QB Jameis Winston, and WRs Jarvis Landry and Chris Godwin all went for 34+ points in week 12, which would have been enough for the win on their own. Luckily the trio did score so many points, because the rest of the team weren't full participants in this one, including a 0.00 game from TE Cameron Brate. Josh's team is firmly in the playoffs, but he's looking for that elusive week 14 bye.

The Wolfpack hunted for a win, and came away with an enormous season-saving victory. Ryan defeated Yisha 133-101 in week 12, bringingboth their records to 6-6 heading into the final week of the regular season. With a loss in week 12, Ryan would have been hoping for a miracle to make the playoffs, but now has a chance to secure the spot in week 13. With RB Dalvin Cook coming off his bye week, Ryan has a good chance to continue his playoff streak.

Team Taco Truck was able to let off the gas a little in week 12, as they only needed a massive 66.05 points to win the week, which was accomplished by QB Josh Allen, TE George Kittle and RB Ronald Jones. Gil still played the rest of his roster, however, and walked away with an easy 112-66 win. This team has been dealing with injuries and bye weeks lately, and has still managed to sit at the top of the standings, but come playoff time, 112 points won't bring home the championship. Gil is looking like a lock to rest his players come week 14.

Just The Tip goes Ma-homeless in a week 12 loss to The Wolfpack 133-101. With QB Patrick Mahomes and WRs Tyreek Hill and Keenan Allen all on bye in week 12, Yisha was forced to turn to QB Jeff Driskel and WR Taylor Gabriel, who combined for 20 points on the week. RB Christian McCaffrey did all he could, again, scoring another 34.50 points, but the rest of this roster just could not put it together. The loss was a double hit, as it brings both Ryan and Yisha to 6-6 records, and fighting for the final two spots in the playoffs, heading into the final week of the regular season.

Nick/Austin attach their trailer to RB Leonard Fournette, and let him pull them to an easy 122-80 win over Jonathan's Magic. Fournette posted a 37 point score, which was the only notable performance besides the surprise 17 point showing by WR Tyler Boyd, who finally remembered how to score points. Even with the win, Nick/Austin still won't have enough to make the playoffs this year, but are in the top few teams fighting for a week 14 bye in the consolation bracket.

The Fighting DingleJerrys lean on Hopkins and Elliot, but come up short against Game of Jones in a 142-98 week 12 loss. Outside of Hopkins (25 points) and Elliot (18 points), nobody on this squad returned anything to write home about. The loss put Jerry into the danger zone for missing the playoffs. Win and he's in, in the week 13 matchup, but a loss will have him scoreboard watching.

The Big Salami becomes the most recent victim of the Lamar Jackson path of destruction, as they fall to Gallup On My Jackson 141-124. Jimmie's team is not on the same page, as some guys look like they're trying to tank, while others are trying to make a playoff push. Hopefully these guys can figure it out come the consolation playoffs.

Big Jim brings the twins to Titty City and hand delivers a can of whoopa$$ to the self-proclaimed Mayor, winning 136-86. The Ballers put together one of their better team games, as everyone was above average on the same day. With the Brees-Thomas combo going for 54 points, Jim had more than enough to dominate Jacob in week 12. This team finds itself fighting for a week 14 bye in the consolation bracket.

JAWORking to find My Magic puts up 80 points in a 122-80 loss to Nick/Austin. Jonathan saw his losing streak extend to 3 games in week 12, and his playoff hopes come to an end. In a week where RB Mark Ingram scored 27 points, and the whole team only scored 80, this team needs practice their tricks and come back more prepared in week 13.

Trevor and his team got Caught doing something this weekend, but it certainly wasn't playing fantasy football. From the high score of 23 points coming from WR Allen Robinson, to the low score of -2 points coming from the Rams DST, and all 6s and 8s in between, week 12's 66 point stinker was one to forget for this squad. Week 13 is the make or break week for Trevor, and 66 points won't cut it!

The self-proclaimed Mayor needs to do send out the fire department, because this City is burning to the ground one loss at a time. Scoring only 86 points on the week, with a 33 point game from RB Derrick Henry, this team was trash in week 12. Jacob joins the group fighting for a week 14 bye in the consolation bracket, and will need much better games from his starters if he wants a shot at the #1 overall pick.

Joe may want to change his name to Gallup On My Jackson, after QB Lamar Jackson put up his 7th, out of 10, game with 35+ points (4th over 40 points). Joe took the example of his Cleveland DST and smashed Yisha over the head with his own helmet, as he won in dominant fashion, 147-119. Beyond Jackson, Joe leaned on WR Stefon Diggs (23.60) and WR Michael Gallup (21.05) to get the win in week 11. With Jackson in the lineup, Joe has the potential to win against anyone any week.

Gil came into Titty City, parked his Taco Truck at Town Hall and fed the self-proclaimed Mayor 123-97 point loss. Both RBs Todd Gurley and Le'Veon Bell must be all about impressing for the Titties, as both RBs posted their 2nd highest scores on the season (23.05 and 19.50 respectively). Aside from the two stud RBs, Gil was lucky to have top chef, QB Josh Allen, in the kitchen this week, as he served up some mahi-mahi Tacos for about 45 points on the week. Even with poor performances throughout this roster, Gil still managed to win and score 123 points.

Yisha and Just The Tip felt what it feels like to be Lamar Jacksoned and OJ Howarded in the same week, both with very different feelings. Yisha Played against Joe and QB Jackson, who scored his usual 45.08 points, and Yisha played TE OJ Howard, who scored his usual 0.00 points. Unfortunately for The Tip, the Howard wasn't the only goose put up on the week, as WR Tyreek Hill left the game early and scored a 0.00 for himself. Outside of RB McCaffrey and WR John Brown, the team didn't do much, and they still scored 119 points. Just The Tip is still a top contender if Hill is healthy.

The Wolfpack had to decide between two leaders this week, and the Pack followed the wrong one and walked right off a cliff. Ryan benched QB Jimmy GQ, who scored a massive 41.16 points against the Cardinals, for QB DeShaun Watson, who scored a massively low 6.06 points against the Ravens. If the QB performance had been adequate at best, Ryan would have likely won this week, due to his team putting together solid enough numbers across the board. The only other player who severely hurt his team, was RB Damien Williams, who left with a rib injury. Ryan will need his team to get healthy if he wants to find a spot in the playoffs.

Game of Jones caught streaking again, with his 2nd straight loss, falling 131-102 to his siblings. Josh has now gone 0-2, 7-0 and 0-2 this season, showing that Josh clearly has no interest in wearing clothes. Outside of 19 point games from RB Joe Mixon and TE Travis Kelce, Game of Jones didn't have much to write home about. Josh has some wrinkles to iron out, as middling performances from his studs will likely cost him when it counts.

The big Dingle wins the battle of brutal QB performances, as his QB Kyle Allen edged out Ryan's QB DeShaun Watson 8.90-6.06. Jerry had the Berries rolling, with RBs Marlon Mack, Ezekiel Elliot and Carlos Hyde each scoring 15+ points, and TE Mark Andrews and the Oaklan DST each adding 16 and 13 points to the team's total. Jerry will have some roster adjusting to do with mainstay RB Marlon Mack likely out for a while with a broken hand. If Jerry can plug the holes, his DingleJerrys may be Fighting for a championship come week 16.

Nick/Austin decided to show Josh that two brothers are better than one, as they defeat Game of Jones by nearly 30 points in week 11. All but 2 players, including the kicker, scored 10+ points this week for Nick/Austin, and 5 of those 7 scored 17+ points. If this roster can continue to produce these types of games, they can compete with any team in the league.

Jonathan and The Magic pulled a rabbit out of their hat this week, except instead of a rabbit, it was Jared Goff and Amari Cooper each holding 6 points. An atrocious performance by a majority of this team, was led by QB Jared Goff, who could not figure out how to do anything against the Bears defense. Jonathan must have had "personal reasons" for playing WR Robert Woods, who was a healthy scratch in week 11, and thus scored exactly 0.00 points. However, even if Jonathan would have slotted in WR Randall Cobb (20.50 points) for Woods, he still would have come up short against the far-from-powerhouse squad in Caught Daking It.

Unfortunately for The Big Salami, this week was lost before it ever started due to just about every starter being on bye or injured. When Royce Freeman is your #1 RB heading into the week, you can plan to be in trouble. Scoring a total of just 62 points on the week, you can imagine the result. Ideally, with all(most) of their starters back, The Big Salami is hoping to serve up a tastier sandwich in week 12.

Jim had no plans to follow in the foot steps of Darth Vadar, and instead let Jimmie know he was his father in a big way in week 11, winning by more than double Jimmie's score (137-62). Despite not needing to score many points, The Ballers who balled out were QB Drew Brees (30.47), WR Michael Thomas (22.90) and WR Calvin Ridley (25.80). Jim will need to continue to have his studs go off if he wants to make a run at the playoffs or win the consolation bracket.

Not often does your bench score 60+ points in a week, and the starters still do enough to win the matchup, but that's exactly what happened for Caught Daking It in week 11 (including 1 player on bye). Trevor's bench was certainly could have matched up against any other bench in the league this week, but his starters were the ones that earned the 118-89 win over Jonathan. Clearly Trevor has some insider trading knowledge, because his aqcuisition of QB Dak Prescott (41.31) and RBs Melvin Gordon (13.40) and Austin Ekeler (18.95) has been extremely beneficial to his team's performance. If Dak comes back to earth, Caught Daking It might come back with him.

The self-proclaimed Mayor was too busy shoving his face with Tacos from Gil's Truck, that he forgot to try and win this week. Losing 97-123, Jacob only had 13 points left on his bench, so this game would not have been won regardless of start/sit decisions. With secondary injuries and bye weeks, Jacob was without a few of his top performers and left to fill the holes with WR Mo Sanu and RB Brian Hill, who combined for 9.27 points. Jacob has found a diamond in the rough in WR DJ Chark, but he will need the remaining pieces to of his puzzle to come together to put together a good picture down the stretch.

Team Taco Truck parked somewhere out in Arizona this week, as they rode QB Kyler Murray (38.26) and WR Christian Kirk (37.55) to a 157-106 victory in week 10. Gil also got a career best game out of RB Ronald Jones II, who scored 20 points for the first time. The Tacos were serving up some specials this week as well, as the replacement players for the starters on bye/injured all scored 10+ points. This roster was able to fix a 2 game losing streak, and reclaim the top spot in the league. Continuing their dominance may be what's on next week's specials menu when he parks the Truck in Titty City.

Man oh man oh Mahomes. Just The TIp couldn't be happier to have all their kneecaps back in their correct places, because QB Patrick Mahomes came back from injury to put up a modest 41.44 points this week. Coupled with Olympic sprinter Tyreek Hill, this duo scored over 71 points on the week (10 points below what was needed to beat their opponent). McCaffrey was unimpressive with only 141 total yards and just 1 touchdown (27 points) in week 10. The remainder of this team put up enough numbers to assist their superstar friends and acheive a massive win. Just The Tip is back and better than ever.

Joe enters the fahter-son battle, and comes out as the best Malak in week 10, as he takes down Jerry's DingleBerries 110-106. Joe was able to overcome a 0.00 performance from RB David Johnson, who did play, ands still earn a win to become 7-3 on the year. Joe leaned heavily on QB Lamar Jackson, who scored 44.12 points, which was just about 40% of the team's total points. This was a lucky matchup for Joe this week, and he will have to produce some better numbers if he wants to compete come playoffs.

Game of Jones sees its 7 game winning strek snapped with a 132-120 loss to Trevor and the Daks in week 10. Josh saw RB Aaron Jones do what he does best, which is score multiple touchdowns (3) in a single game. Josh also got a great game from TE Travis Kelce (18 points), but the remainder of this team didn't have what was needed to take down Caught Daking It. Game of Jones had to be frustrated as they watched RBs Devonta Freeman and Jaylen Samuels get outscored by benched RB Joe Mixon and WR Jarvis Landry 43.05 - 15.45. Josh will look to restart his next win streak in week 11.

If it was unknown before, The Wolfpack has officially found their Alpha wolf in RB Dalvin Cook, who has quickly become one of the league's elite RBs (just another 33.65 points again this week). Cook has scored no less than 15.50 points this season, and has scored 25+ points in 7 out of 10 games. Ryan is still lacking the superstar games from his other superstar players, but if they can even get slightly on track, this team could be posting 160+ weeks on a regular basis. Though The Wolfpack sits at 5-5, this squad is a dark horse for a championship run if they can make it into the playoffs.

The Fighting Dingle squared off against his only son in week 10, and was bested 110-106. Jerry got back to back 17+ point games from waiver wire WR Jamison Crowder, which always helps, but he also got most garbage from the rest of his team. The Dingles' top performer TE Mark Andrews, who scored 21.55 points, was unfortunately receiving passes from QB Lamar Jackson, who was scoring points (44.12) for Joe and the Johnsons. Jerry was facing a massive bye week (losing 4 starters), and still almost came away with a win. Jerry sits at 6-4 and will need his starters to perform like starters if he wants to secure a spot in the playoffs.

Jonathan and The Magic appear to be playing in Dallas, while the rest of their team isn't quite sure where they belong. Both Dallas WRs Amari Cooper and Randall Cobb went off for 28.45 and 21.10 points respectively, however Cobb's points only looked good on the bench. The rest of the roster played well enough to get a win on most weeks, except this week QB Aaron Rodgers let the team down by barely eclipsing 10 points. Going forward, JAWORking My Magic may be without star TE Austin Hooper and efficiency king Tyler Lockett, who both left their games with injuries. If these players miss, Jonathan will have to try and plug the holes if he wants to stay afloat down the stretch.

No kicker, no prob-... I mean, no kicker, BIG problem! For all those who believe kickers suck and have no place in fantasy football, I agree with you. However, this week, the kicker position was the demise of The Big Salami. Lack of attention to detail pushed this team to a depressing 137.19 - 137.42 loss in week 10. A 4-6 record was in sights in, what was a winnable matchup, but was turned into 3-7 very quickly. Another tough week for the already expired Salami.

Trevor Caught Josh Jones Daking It in week 10, and handed them their first loss in 8 games. Trevor got his second straight win on back to back 34 point games from QB Dak Prescott, and another 24 point game from RB Flash Gordon. The Daks also received the game winning bump from the Rams DST, who scored 23.30 points compared to Josh's Giants DST, who scored only 2.84 points. RB Kareem Hunt played his first game of the 2019 season, after serving his 8 game suspension, and contributed 12 points to this roster. If Rovert can continue getting top 5 weeks from Dak, he may be able to steal a few more wins.

The self-proclaimed Mayor of the luxurious Titty City must have called in a few favors this week to have The Big Salami distracted enough to steal a win right out from underneath their feet. Jacob snagged the final kicker to play in the week, noticing that Jimmie failed to put one in his lineup, and it paid off, as that kicker scored 7 points on Jacob's bench in a 137.42-137.19 win. The City was flashing all their Titties at their new favorite player in RB Derrick Henry, who could is apparently not fond of the Native Americans, because he ran all over them for 38 points this week. Jacob overcame a 0 point week from WR Pooper Kupp, and will need him to perform if he wants to beat teams who play full rosters in the future.

Nick/Austin went searching for a win in week 10, and came back with 82 points and their 3rd straight loss. This team had been banking on massive performanes by QB Russell WIlson, TE Darren Waller and RB Leonard Fournette, but only got a combined 27.83 points out of the trio (Fournette was on bye). This team once felt like it was built to stand up to any team in the league under any circumstances, but now, sitting at 3-7, Nick/Austin will have to win out and scoreboard watch if they want to make it into the playoffs.

The Ballers got slapped by Just The Tip duirng their byepocalypse, and were stomped 158-81. Jim basically only started WR Michael Thomas (23.45 points), because everyone else on this roster scored less than 15 points this week. Even with multiple players in plus matchups, this team could not put together a game on any level. Bye weeks destroyed the main portion of this roster, and The Ballers will look to get back on track after getting the majority of their roster back in week 11.

Joe and Gallup On My Johnson ride another lottery ticket week from WR Mike Evans to a week 9 victory over Nick/Austin 138-131. Evans caught another 12 balls (of 16 targets!) for another 180 yards and another touchdown, which puts him at 72.30 points over the last 2 weeks. QB/RB/WR/TE Lamar Jackson scored also scored in the 30s (35.17) this week, as he basically single-handedly gave the Patriots their first loss on the real NFL season. The remainder of Joe's team put in enough work to compliment these two show-offs and get the W. As per usual, this team is built to put up big boom numbers whenever it feels like it.

Game of Jones wins lucky number 7 in a row, on his way to a league leading 7-2 record. This was a workmanlike win on the backs of names such as Curtis Samuel, Jaylen Samuels and Jarvis Landry, who all scored around 15 points. Josh continues to find ways to win each week, which makes him a scary opponent to faceoff against. Will week 10 be the 8th win in a row?

Team Taco Truck has the shifter stuck in reverse, as they drop their second game in a row to become 6-3 on the year. The top 2 teams in the league faced off in a thrilling matchup that yielded a total of just over 200 combined points between the two rosters. The Tacos were on backorder this week, as Gil posted a sub 100 score for the first time this season. With injuries and byes this week, Gil had to piece together roster made up of 2nd stringers, who played like 2nd stringers. Hopefully the Truck can get its gears worked out before week 10.

Just The Tip decided that, for some reason, week 9 was the perfect week for most of their players to go ahead and post an individual top 2 score on the season. RB Christian McCaffrey may be on the wrong team, because he is much more than Just The Tip - he’s the fricken black mamba with his 25 touchdowns each week. With McCaffey paired with the other high potential players on this roster, Yisha’s roster is a high ceiling/high floor team each week.

The Wolfpack go hunting and come back with goose eggs. The goose egg from WR Adam Thielen, who decided he was only healthy enough to play 1 quarter, led to an upsetting 130-105 loss to Trevor. This week was an okay week for this roster, who saw 6/9 players post double digit scores, but unfortunately also saw the remaining 3/9 score a combined 9.96 points. Injuries may hinder the Wolves, but they should get back on track in week 10.

Tyler Lockett and JAWORking My Magic said "Give me thos titties!" as they came into the City and stole a win 131-113 over Jacob. Lockett somehow managed to be open enough times to earn 18 targets, which he turned into 13 catches, 152 yards, 2 touchdowns and 10 (TEN) first downs. Lockett's performance overshadowed the rest of the team, which aside from WR Amari Cooper (18.50) and RB Mark Ingram (16.40) didn't require a very big shadow. Either way, Jonathan put together enough to get a win and grab a 4-5 record on the season/

The Dingles outlast QB Gardner MinshEW and hang on for a 115-100 point victory over The Ballers. Jerry made the wise management decision to slot in WR Jamison Crowder over previous stud WR Terry McLaurin, which made the difference in this one, as Crowder outscored McLaurin 19.55-6.40. The rest of Jerry's roster middled their way to a win, which is all you need in fantasy football.

The only reason we know Nick/Austin haven't hacked the system and drafted a robot in QB Russell Wilson, is because they somehow still ended up with a loss this week, despite a 54.47 & 5 touchdown game from Wilson. Injuries and byes have kept some of Nick/Austin's top players on the bench, which has been costing them in close games such as this week's 138-131 loss to Joe and the Johnsons. If the rest of this roster can take a sip of "Russ' Secret Stuff", this team could go on a tear going forward.

The Big Salami is starting to get sick on this roller coaster of a season. Every time they start to look healthy, someone else goes down, or the performances just aren’t there. This week was a tough loss, after starting out on Thursday with 22 points from WR Emmanuel Sanders, and then watching McCaffrey score 12 touchdowns for the opponent on Sunday. Jimmie needs a string of wins, or The Salami will need to be put in the freezer as they start (meal) prepping for the draft.

The headlines in Titty City are reading "Self-proclaimed Mayor plays Active QB, still suffers week 9 loss. Whispers of Impeachment grow louder". Unfortunately for Jacube, big time games from WR Kenny G (24.20), RB Derrick Henry (25.95) and RB Josh Jacobs (28.55) still weren't enough to stop the Magic from coming into the City and handling all the Titties. After the byes, if Jacob could get his team to all go off on the same week, he would be looking at a 200+ point week.

Caught Daking It finally got to see their brand name player live up to the name this week, as QB Dak Prescott scored 32.23 points and helped his team achieve a week 9 win over The Wolfpack. Along with Dak, the resurgence RB Melvin Gordon (III) and the Dallas DST helped push Trevor over the top, winning 130-105. Trevor was not afraid of backup QB Brandon Allen, as he decided to play WR Cortland Sutton, and he was rewarded with a 15.65 point outing. The rest of this team is better off not spoken of, and they shall be left that way. This was an important win for this team no doubt.

The Ballers come close, but come up short on their Byepocalypse, losing to Jerry DingleBerry 115-100. Jim employs 4 Saints players, so with their week 9 bye, he had some gaps to fill. WR Calvin Ridley was also sitting out this week, which forced Jim to play old man RB Frank Gore, who scored 3 points compared to his RBBC mate, Devin Singletary, who scored 25 points this week. Jim did get the upside games of both TE Zach Ertz (22.80 points) and RB David Montgomery (23.75), but their combined efforts weren't enough to pluck the Berries this week. With the New Orleans Ballers coming off of bye in week 10, Jim looks to earn another win.

The 6 game win streak comes to an end with a week 8 loss. The Truck was serving up Tacos as fast as they could, but the chefs couldn't keep up with the appetite of Ryan and The Wolfpack, as theywere defeated 131-119. Newly acquired RB Le'Veon Bell pulled out another stinker, scoring just under 6 points on the week, and will have to produce at his potential to keep Gil atop the league standings. The Tacos continue to put their weight on the Patriots DST, which scored the 3rd highest points on Gil's roster with an even 20 points. Hopefully you play Gil in week 10 when the Patriots DST is on bye, otherwise you better hope for another down week by his studs and a big week for yours.

The Wolfpack feasts on Tacos in week 8, as they come away with a win over the Biscuit's top team 131-119. Ryan was the beneficiary of another amazing week by RB Dalvin Cook (30 points) and QB DeShaun Watson (38 points), who teamed up for just under 50% of the team's total points. Despite injuries and bye weeks, Ryan managed to end Gil's 6 game win streak and steal a much needed week 8 victory. Ryan is in a position to have a few good weeks and become one of the top teams in the league.

Game of Jones ain't playing games no more! After falling 0-2 on the season, Josh has battled to a 6-2 record and a 6 game win streak (tied for longest of the year with Gil). Josh couldn't have picked a better player to lead his name into battle than RB Aaron Jones, who now has a 40 point and 50 point performance under his belt this season. With Jones looking like the new and improved Alvin Kamara, this roster becomes much terrifying to matchup against each week. The rest of Josh's team continues to do what it needs to do in order to win games, which is exactly what you need down the stretch. Josh and the Jones' land at #3 heading into week 9.

Both Gallup and My Johnson we On the bench during this team's week 8 matchup, but they were not needed, as Joe grabbed a win in dominant fashion over Trevor, 138-80. The focal point of the week was WR Mike Evans blowing up again for another 198 yards and 2 touchdowns. WR Stefon Diggs, who posted a 143 yard game, was outshined by Evans because he lacked the touchdowns (still scored 16.80 points). Joe's roster has multiple players returning from bye this week, which will only power up his offense even more. Even though he sits at #4, Joe has the potential to take over the #1 spot.

JAWORking My Magic couldn't muster up the right spell to take down Game of Jones in their week 8 tilt, as the Magic fall by a score of 159-137. Jonathan was Working hard in this one, but just couldn't keep with the Jones's, who were out there having fun and playing Games. TE Austin Hooper did his thing again and scored another 16 points this week, while WR Tyler Lockett also kept pace and scored another 15 points. Jonathan tried to ride the Aaron Rodgers wave again this week (38 points), but even adding in the big game by RB James Conner (26 points) wasn't enough in this one, as they just unfortunately matched up agains the wrong opponent. With all the potential and solid games this team has and has been getting, they slide into the #5 spot on the week.

The Fighting DingleJerrys were much more Dingle than berry in week 8, putting up just 95 points on the week. Jerry tried to lean on WR DeAndre Hopkins and RB Marlon Mack, who each scored 18 points this week, but tipped over when they weren't enough to support the remaining players' performances, which included an 11 point showing from QB Jacoby beef brisket Brissett. Jerry was short RB Elliot and TE Andrews due to bye weeks, and will hope that the return of these two can propel him back into the world of winning. Jerry remains on the cusp of the top 5 teams, coming in at #6 after week 8.

Just The Tip was all Yisha won by in week 8, as he narrowly escapes the QB-less Titty man 113.80-113.62. Yisha is feeling the pain of injuries and bye weeks, as his once powerhouse team is now struggling to make ends meet. Streaming QB Ryan Tannehill and stud RB Christian McCaffrey carried the load in this one, combining for just over 58 points and 50% of the team's total production. Yish has the self-proclaimed Mayor to thank for this win, and will need some good bounces going forward if he wants to rejoin the top teams.

The self-proclaimed Mayor of Titty City is looking more like the self-appointed Mayor of Dufus City, with the inexplicable decision to not play an active QB in week 8. Losing by Just the Tip to Yisha (0.18 points) could have easily been reversed, if had he just chosen to play a complete lineup, but instead he now sits at 3-5 instead of 4-4. Big time games from WR Cooper Kupp, WR Kenny Golladay and WR DJ Chark were squandered by QB Matt Ryan's 0.00 point performance. The upside here, is that Jacob only lost by less than 0.20 points without a QB. If he can manage to put together a full lineup, he may earn some more wins moving forward.

RB BELL(snickel) Left! and apparently took all the fantasy points with him! He didn't bring them to the Truck, so he must have hid them, but he certainly stole them from Nick and Austin, who wound up on the losing end of a 174-108 matchup with The Ballers. Nick/Austin had 5 players score single digit points, and 6 players score less than 11 points on the week. Even QB Russell Wilson had a disappointing week, scoring 21 points compared to his multiple 30+ point games earlier in the year. Only RB Fournette and WR Juju put together solid games, which will not be enough to earn wins down the road. Nick/Austin must be hoping the return of injured RB Alvin Kamara will return their team to top-notch status.

The Ballers balled out against Nick/Austin on their way to 174.52 points on the week. Jim had 5 of 7 players go for 20+ points, which included 41 points from RB Tevin Coleman and 36 points from RB Latavius Murray. The Ballers didn't even need the 19 points from WR Tyrell Williams, 27 points from RB David Montgomery or the 34 points from QB Drew Brees, which were all on the bench, as they had an easy win over Nick/Austin. If you want to be the best in the league, get ranked 12th in the rankings, because in back to back weeks, the 12th ranked team has been the top scorer in the league.

The Big Salami can take another breath with a win in week 8, keeping them alive this year. Despite how this year has felt, The Big Salami clings to the few slices of hope they have left, as they remain competitive at 3-5 on the year. QB Matt Stafford returned from the dead and played amazing for the Salami, and he was joined by living superhero RB Saquon Barkley, who somehow has robot legs (ankles) that allow him to put up 28 points after suffering a major injury a few weeks ago. As per the weekly report, as this team gets healthier, the more competitive they become.

Caugh Daking It was too busy admiring the Johnson to score any fantasy points this week in their loss to Gallup On My Johnson 138-80. Trevor's roster made a pact that no individual player could score 15 points this week, and they stuck to it. QB Captain Kirk Cousins walked the line scoring 14.35 points, but everyone else kept their distance from the 15 point mark. When this team hits, they are tough to beat, but when the miss, they are Caught with their pants down holding 80 points. Luckily, Trevor has some players coming off byes, suspensions and injuries that may be able to balance this roster out a bit. We shall see...

Team Taco Truck went back to the well and rehired former Taco chef, RB Le'Veon Bell, to come back and whip up some more deliciousness. Bell didn't want to come back too hot, and only scored 10.35 points in a weird week 7, in which so many teams/players just did not show up. Luckily for Gil and this roster, his opponent, Joe, also refused to show up this week, gifting Gil an easy 112-75 win. With RB Kerryon Johnson headed to IR, Gil will have to find a replacement cook to hold the Truck down for the remaidner of the season. Fortunately for him, his roster is still superb everywhere else to make up for any deficits. Back to back turkeys has Gil on a 6 game win streak and a 6-1 record on the year.

Sometimes trades work, and sometimes trades punch you in the gut and then the throat on your way down. Unfortunately for Yisha, his trade with Trevor was the latter for him in week 7, with the multi-week injury to Patrick Mahomes. Losing a single player can hurt, but Mahomes injury also factors into the success of recently acquired WR Tyreek Hill's success as well. On a down week for Yish, he still managed to only lose by 17 points, and that was without league winning talent Christian McCaffrey. Yish will have to manage this group in order to remain at #2 on the list.

The Wolfpack just misses out on their prey once again, as they lose a close match against JAWOR and the Magic 130-124. Despite the Jags DST scoring 19 points and RB Dalvin Cook scoring 32 points, Ryan could not get enough elsewhere to overcome his opponent. WR Adam Thielen has come back to life these past few games, but unfortunately left early in this one after injuring his hamstring on a touchdown catch. Ryan was dealing with some big players on bye this past week, and should still have plenty of fire power for week 8, even if Thielen ends up missing time.

BELLsnickel is here decided to make a move and send its the cornerstone of their name packing. After trading away RB Lev Bell to Gil, Nick/Austin changed their name to BELLsnicke Left!. Lev Bell will not be and was not missed in week 7, as this team was too busy taking Wallerus rides this past Sunday and watching newly acquired TE Darren Waller score nearly 30 fantasy points. An already stacked team just upgraded their TE and RB position (also acquired the little-known RB Alvin Kamara), and now they look like they can be true contenders. #4 may be the lowest they land for the remainder of the season.

Gallup on my Who?? Joe better stay away from riding RB David Johnson anywhere at the moment, until his back (or ankle?) can get back to full strength. Apparently all the reports claiming Johnson was ready to go against the Giants, meant that DJ was ready to stand on the sidelines and cheer on backup RB Chase Edmunds, as Johnson only took one carry in this one. Joe had almost no help from his roster this week but welcomes the return of superback Nick Chubb and WR Mike Evans in week 8. Joe moves back to #5, while he deals with last week's loss.

The Dingles get the Win! Jerry sneaks out a victory over Just The Tip 114-97, and improves to a surprising 5-2 record. DeAndre Hopkins and Ezekiel Elliot showed out this week, and were helped out by the Gardner, Mr. Minshew II, to provide this team a victory. Upsetting games by the remainder of the team (besides K Greg Zuerlein who had 11 points), did not hinder the path to victory this week, but obviously stronger performances will be needed down the stretch to continue to compete. These Dingles fought their way back up to #6 on the board.

Game of Jones does it again and finds a way to out Game his opponent for his 5th straight win. Josh was up against injuries and bye weeks, but made quality waiver wire and start/sit decisions to earn a workman-like victory. Game of Jones does not possess the flashiness of some of the top teams, and has had to grind out his wins this year, which is why he consistently finds himself in the middle of the pack in the rankings. With 5 straight wins, it may be time for Josh to get the respect he deserves. We'll wait and see if Josh continues to battle in week 8.

JAWORking My Magic spent up and bought the "Big Book of Spells" heading into week 7, because QB Aaron Rodgers was on some wizardry level stuff this week scoring nearling 60 points on his own. Jonathan's version of "pop, drop and lock it", Hooper, Cooper and Lockett all played well enough at their positions to assist Rodgers in beating The Wolfpack, but the rest of this team was mostly upsetting. Without Rodgers balling out, or just deciding to let the RB run one in instead, this would have been a completely different game with a completely different outcome. However, this is fantasy football, and that's how it goes sometimes! Jonathan still has all the pieces necessary to be a playoff contender, and will look to build on this win in week 8.

The self-proclaimed Mayor must be on an extended vacation, because Titty City has now lost 3 straight games. What was once a powerhouse starting lineup, has proven to be more of a hit or miss squad. Jacob has plenty of talent on his roster, but can't seem to find the right mix lately to produce a win. Jacob will be patiently looking through a telescope to see his stars shine, but if they do, league-leading numbers are not out of the realm of possibilites.

Caught 156 points is what Dakin Caught in week 7! In what was a terrible week for so many fantasy players and teams, Trevor and his squad had themselves a day, scoring the highest total of the week by 25 points. Four players on this roster scored over 20 points, including the Rams DST (21.72), which would have been enought to win without playing anyone else. Trevor has shown the potential to go off if the touchdowns fall the right direction. For now, Trevor will have to prove this was more than a 1-time occurrence before moving higher than the #10 spot.

The Big Salami couldn't prove it was one of the main meats this week, as they lose a very winable matchup in week 7, dropping their record to 2-5 on the season. Too many injuries was coupled with underwhelming showings by the QB and WR positions. The upside for this team is that they may be finding a medic pack soon with enough energy to revive the health of this team. As it has been for most of the season, health = wins for this squad.

The Ballers struggle once again, and fall to Caught Dakin' It by a score 156-77. Jim's team just could not get going in any area this week, except for WR Michael Thomas, who continues to provide steady WR numbers each week. Jim has found himself handling a group of players that have not lived up to the hype, which has certainly damaged his team's chances of a playoff run. This team is seeing that "potential" does not mean anything if it can't be translated to fantasy points on the field.

Gil said #2? No thank you. I’ll take 164 points, a win and the #1 spot, thank you. These Tacos Trucked their way to a massive 164-115 win over The Ballers in week 6. Despite the absence of Gurley, Hilton and Waller, The Truck was able to post the highest score on the week and achieve the victory. Kyler Murray and the Patriots DST dominated this week, combining for over 65 points. Gil and has roster have been practicing drawing hand turkeys all week, as they have now won 5 straight games to be 5-1 on the year. Powerhouse? I think yes.

Just as quickly as Just The Tip slid into 1st place last week, they slid right back out to #2 this week - not due to individual performance. Yisha and his troops have been battling week after week, and they finally achieved a win to snap a 3 game losing streak. So far, the acquisition of Mahomes and Hill has paid off, as the two both scored 25+ points each. As always, McCaffrey was unstoppable (fantasywise) again this week, scoring 20+ points once again. The steady numbers coupled with a ceiling that’s in outer space, makes Just The Tip more than enough to handle for most teams.

Look at me, I'm #3!! Joe Gallups his way back to #3 in the charts after a down week 5. As stated before, Joe has put together a roster that has the potential to dominate week in and week out. 142.92 points on the week without the 45 point performance of WR Stefon Diggs, who was benched by Joe in week 6, was enough for 2nd highest in the league. RB David Johnson and Nick Chubb appear to be unstoppable fantasy forces, and when they are combined with whatever position Lamar Jackson is and WRs like Evans and Diggs, this team can easily score 200 points in a week. This team is one to watch out for as the weeks progress.

The Wolves are on the hunt for a stat correction this week, after suffering a heartbreaking loss to Game of Jones by a score of 127.72-127.56 (0.16 point difference). Unfortunatwly for Ryan this week, Big Montana/TE Will Dissly couldn’t manage to make 1 catch this week before departing with a torn achillies and leaving the Wolfpack with 0.00 points for the day. This roster is littered with top end talent that just refuses to bring it every week. If they can start getting on the same page on the same week, The Wolfpack will be hunting for a championship.

WIIILLLLSSSSONNNN!! Is all Nick/Austin were screaming this week, while they watched QB Russell Wilson dominate the Cleveland Browns. Unfortunately for Nick/Austin, the rest of BELLsnickel is here! was doing the same thing as they mostly laid a bunch of eggs in their week 6 games. Leading that bunch was star WR Juju Smith-Schuster who scored just 1/36 of Russell Wilson's total points on the week. This team needs to be led by its top end RBs if it wants to win. Nick/Austin land in the top 5 teams this week, but staying there is entirely dependent on whether or not their WRs decide to show up in week 7.

Josh and Game of Jones are certainly playing the game well lately, as they have taken their 0-2 start and turned it into a 4-2 record with 4 consecutive wins. If Josh would have recorded just one more reception in his week 2 matchup against Yisha, this team would be parked next to Team Taco Truck at 5-1 with 5 straight wins. However, this week came out on the good side of a marginal victory, as he narrowly escapes The Wolfpack by 0.16 points. Josh continues to find ways to win games, and is proving to be one of the best owners in the league at managing the talent and flows of the season.

JAWORking My Magic worked some tricks this week, but just couldn't find that dang rabbit, as they got out performed by the Galluping Johnsons (142-128). Unfortunately for Jonathan this week, WR Amari Cooper only contributed 0.80 points before exiting with an injury, which could have been the game changer in this matchup. Newly acquired RB James Conner was ally-ooping with TE Austin Hooper on their way to 31 and 23 points. Just about everyone performed well this week for Jonathan and the Magic, but they just couldn't overcome Nick Chubb and David Johnson. This roster will continue to battle every week and is definitely better than its 2-4 record.

The self-proclaimed Mayor must have owed someone a favor this week, because there is no other excuse to play RB Reggie Bonnawho this week. Thank goodness QB Matt Ryan was playing this week, because he scored just below half of the team's total points (42). With single digits from everyone except Golladay and the KICKER, Jacob didn't have much of a chance to win this matchup. Jacob will need his players to play in week 7 if he wishes to move back up to where the Titties are.

The Fighting Dingles ride Texas to a week 6 victory over the Titties, as Dallas RB Elliot and Houston RB Hyde scored 28.75 and 22.10 respectively. WR Scary Terry McLaurin also scored 25 points on the week, and the trio combined for the majority of the Dingles' points. Jerry has all the pieces to compete with the top teams, but it just hasn't come together to this point. For now, they remain at #9.

While week 6 was nothing special for Jim and The Ballers, it was still a week that would normally be competitive - as long as your opponent is scoring North of 160 points. Steady games by almost everyone on the roster is something positive to take away from this week. Only Ertz and the Dallas DST undeperformed for Jim. As usual, this team has the potential to boom (as seen in week 5), and it’s looking like it’s minimizing the busts. Until this team can get some Ws, #10 is home for them.

Whew! The Big Salami can breathe a little easier knowing they didn't drop to 1-5, as they find a way to take down Caught Dakin It in their week 6 matchup. This team is still plagued with injuries, but if they can get healthy, it would appear, on paper, that they could compete. We will see what happens, but in the meantime, if you have any family members in the NFL, I suggest you keep them away from this team.

Caught Daking It almost choked on something as they watched their former WR Tyreek Hill defy gravity on a 50 yard TD pass from their former QB Patrick Mahomes in their first connection since Hill’s week 1 injury. Trevor’s squad did their research before this week and figured they could score less than 80 points and still beat the Salamis, but he forgot that Salami sometimes tastes better than it looks. These Daks put up 78 points and found themselves on the wrong end of a 2-4 record. This team will have some work to do to earn a spot higher than #12.

New chefs, same delicious Tacos served from this Truck. Gambling on the hire of QB Matt Stafford and WR Corey Davis paid of big in Week 4, as Stafford scored 32 points (2nd highest score he's had this year) and Davis scored 19 (more than all 3 previous weeks combined). The rest of the Team Taco Truck did what they do and scored points, including the Patriots DST, which has now scored nearly 80 points over the last 3 weeks. Gil remains the deepest team at RB and TE, and the gamble to be light at all other positions has yet to cost him. Until that time, Gil earns himself the #1 spot in the rankings for the 3rd time this season.

LA's Finest showed everyone the less glamorous parts of the city in week 4, on their way to their 2nd consecutive loss. 3 of LA's best, Woods, McCaffrey and Ekeler, did all they could to keep the tour bus on track, but the rest of Yisha's squad wanted to visit the underpass instead. The big 3 combined for 3/4 of the team's total points for the week. Despite poor week 4 showings, Yisha still maintains a high upside with the return of superstar RB Melvin Gordon. However, another week like this, and Yisha could find himself slipping down the charts.

This was no half-Chubb performance this week by Gallup On My Johnson. No no, Joe gave The Wolfpack the enormous full-Chubb experience in week 4 with RB Nick Chubb flopping his way to 165 yards and 3 touchdowns. QB Lamar Jackson had a little Chubb in him as well apparently, because he also went off for a huge 37 points on the week. With steady showings from Evans, Diggs and David Johnson, Joe slowly Galluped off into the sunset with an easy 61 point stomping of Ryan and The Wolfpack. The ceiling that Joe's squad has shown pushes him to #3 in the rankings.

Unfortunately for Ryan, his Wolves did not run as a pack in week 4. The brightest point on his starting lineup came from an impressive 20 point night from the Steelers DST against the Bengals. Ryan did get solid games out of everyone besides Watson, Thielen and DJ Moore, which ultimately led to his week 4 thumping (163-102). This loss was not due to bad management though, as Ryan's bench posted a combined lowly score of 5.85 points. The Wolfpack drop one spot to #4 on the board, and Ryan will look to rebound in week 5 to hop back into the top 3 teams.

Another week, another Titty for this self-proclaimed Mayor, as the City celebrated its 3rd win in 4 weeks. Jacob lacks the flash and zest that Team Taco Truck's roster offers, but the self-proclaimed Mayor has built himself a solid powerhouse. If Jacob can find a way to plug some of the minor holes he has in his roster, he would be poised to make a strong push for the top spot in the league. For this week though, Jacob finds his Titties among the top 5 teams, coming in at #5.

The Fighting DIngleJerrys reached back and plucked one lucky berry this week, as they came away with a victory despite scoring the 2nd lowest score on the week (yes that means only Trevor, his opponent, scored less this week). Jerry's starting lineup is filled with star names, but they may just be celebrity look-alikes, as they scored well below superstar numbers in week 4. For some of these "stars", the season has no been kind to them yet. Unless they can turn it around soon, Jerry and the look-alikes might only be able to audition for CCTV commercials. For now, the Dingles remain in the middle of the pack, as they drop 2 spots to #6 on the week.

QB Jameis WinSOME is here to save the day for Game of Jones, as Josh walks past The Ballers to earn back to back wins and even his record at 2-2. From the depths of 0-2, Josh has managed to climb back to .500 and join the middle pack of teams. Josh's core players are appearing to come alive and be reliable players week after week, with bench players that can be easily inserted into the starting lineup with confidence (especially after 3 bench players scored 20+ points). If these players continue to perform, we may all be trying to keep up with this Jones.

It must have been charity week for JAWORking My Magic, because the better portion of this squad decided to donate their fantasy points to other players in order to help The Big (moldy) Salami get their first win of the season. Nobody likes being the team to fall to the 12th place team in the league, but Jonathan dove straight in head first, as none of his top performers scored double digits this week (excluding QB Aaron Rodgers - 34 points. TE Austin Hooper led the way in this one with 18 fantasy points, but Jonathan can't rely on the TE position to provide wins as the season progresses. For now, he'll move back one spot to #8..

Week 4 was the depressant that brought Nick/Austin down from their high of winning their week 3 matchup, as they found themselves down by 37 points at the end of the week. RB Leonard Fournette ran for 5,000 yards against the Broncos, but he left the rest of BELLsnickel back in the locker room, as the remainder of the team forgot to score points this week. What appeared to be great matchups for their starters, proved to be tougher than expected, and the output shows. Nick/Austin fall to 1-3 on the year and to #9 in the rankings until this group can prove it can play up to its potential.

For 11 Risky Biscuits, this was just Week 4, but for 1 Biscuit, this was the Super Bowl. The only winless team in the league was facing an 0-4 start, but The Big Salami showed up as the full 6-foot party sub this week, taking down JAWOR and the Magic 134-100. This was also the first time this season that Jimmie's team scraped together enough catches, yards and touchdowns to surpass the 100 point mark. Even though this team is on a poor man's cloud 9, Jimmie has plenty of work ahead if he wishes to prove Salami is better than Tacos in week 5.

Trevor and Mahomes have been walking down this Country Road for 3 straight weeks now, as this squad has dropped their last 3 games to become 1-3 on the year. Hopefully on the walk, Trevor was able to answer some questions, because his team is loaded "unknowns" and "what nexts". A mediocre showing for Mahomes (by Mahomes standards only) resulted in 68 points on the week. Right now, Trevor finds himself at a fork in this Country Road that either competes or heads toward the consolation bracket. The coming weeks are crucial for this squad, as #11 is an unpleasant place to be.

Unlike their name would suggest, The Ballers were certainly not Balling in week 4, scoring just over 89 points on the week. A team that looked like it had potential has found itself relying on RB Frank Gore to be on the highest scorers on the team each week. Jim's team has the potential to hit big on any given week, but when they don't hit, this floor is the basement. The Ballers may have to make some moves if they wish to Ball anymore. #12 is where Jim lands heading into Week 5.

New chefs, same delicious Tacos served from this Truck. Gambling on the hire of QB Matt Stafford and WR Corey Davis paid of big in Week 4, as Stafford scored 32 points (2nd highest score he's had this year) and Davis scored 19 (more than all 3 previous weeks combined). The rest of the Team Taco Truck did what they do and scored points, including the Patriots DST, which has now scored nearly 80 points over the last 3 weeks. Gil remains the deepest team at RB and TE, and the gamble to be light at all other positions has yet to cost him. Until that time, Gil earns himself the #1 spot in the rankings for the 3rd time this season.

LA's Finest showed everyone the less glamorous parts of the city in week 4, on their way to their 2nd consecutive loss. 3 of LA's best, Woods, McCaffrey and Ekeler, did all they could to keep the tour bus on track, but the rest of Yisha's squad wanted to visit the underpass instead. The big 3 combined for 3/4 of the team's total points for the week. Despite poor week 4 showings, Yisha still maintains a high upside with the return of superstar RB Melvin Gordon. However, another week like this, and Yisha could find himself slipping down the charts.

This was no half-Chubb performance this week by Gallup On My Johnson. No no, Joe gave The Wolfpack the enormous full-Chubb experience in week 4 with RB Nick Chubb flopping his way to 165 yards and 3 touchdowns. QB Lamar Jackson had a little Chubb in him as well apparently, because he also went off for a huge 37 points on the week. With steady showings from Evans, Diggs and David Johnson, Joe slowly Galluped off into the sunset with an easy 61 point stomping of Ryan and The Wolfpack. The ceiling that Joe's squad has shown pushes him to #3 in the rankings.

Unfortunately for Ryan, his Wolves did not run as a pack in week 4. The brightest point on his starting lineup came from an impressive 20 point night from the Steelers DST against the Bengals. Ryan did get solid games out of everyone besides Watson, Thielen and DJ Moore, which ultimately led to his week 4 thumping (163-102). This loss was not due to bad management though, as Ryan's bench posted a combined lowly score of 5.85 points. The Wolfpack drop one spot to #4 on the board, and Ryan will look to rebound in week 5 to hop back into the top 3 teams.

Another week, another Titty for this self-proclaimed Mayor, as the City celebrated its 3rd win in 4 weeks. Jacob lacks the flash and zest that Team Taco Truck's roster offers, but the self-proclaimed Mayor has built himself a solid powerhouse. If Jacob can find a way to plug some of the minor holes he has in his roster, he would be poised to make a strong push for the top spot in the league. For this week though, Jacob finds his Titties among the top 5 teams, coming in at #5.

The Fighting DIngleJerrys reached back and plucked one lucky berry this week, as they came away with a victory despite scoring the 2nd lowest score on the week (yes that means only Trevor, his opponent, scored less this week). Jerry's starting lineup is filled with star names, but they may just be celebrity look-alikes, as they scored well below superstar numbers in week 4. For some of these "stars", the season has no been kind to them yet. Unless they can turn it around soon, Jerry and the look-alikes might only be able to audition for CCTV commercials. For now, the Dingles remain in the middle of the pack, as they drop 2 spots to #6 on the week.

QB Jameis WinSOME is here to save the day for Game of Jones, as Josh walks past The Ballers to earn back to back wins and even his record at 2-2. From the depths of 0-2, Josh has managed to climb back to .500 and join the middle pack of teams. Josh's core players are appearing to come alive and be reliable players week after week, with bench players that can be easily inserted into the starting lineup with confidence (especially after 3 bench players scored 20+ points). If these players continue to perform, we may all be trying to keep up with this Jones.

The Ballers may have to make some moves if they wish to Ball anymore. #12 is where Jim lands heading into Week 5.

How do you take over the 1st place spot in the rankings after a loss? Just ask Yisha, because he stole away the top spot in this week's rankings after losing 171.81 to 160.37 to the Magic Man. It's looking more and more like the only way to beat LA's Finest is to have all of your players crazily over-perform, which is what we saw happen in week 3. Yisha's WR2 Robert Woods only put up 8 points, and LA's Finest still came away with the 2nd highest score on the week. It's time to stop doubting this team and get on board before you get rolled over!

Even though Team Taco Truck dropped to #2 in the power rankings this week, Gil and RB Alvin Kamara were still serving up all sorts of deliciousness on their way to a week 3 victory. Kamara was everywhere on the field and everywhere in DingleJerry's head, because he put up 161 total yards and 2 touchdowns for a total of 36.20 points on the week. Gil's questionable WR depth has been answered by Redskins' wideout Scary Terry McLaurin, who has scored a touchdown each week this year. Other than Kamara, the RBs have been stuck inside the truck and can't seem to decide how delicious they want to be. Gil will need better performances from his star RBs if he wants to regain the top spot in the league rankings.

The wolves showed up in a pack this week, as Ryan had all but one player reach double digits in week 3. Led by stellar performances from QB DeShaun Watson and RB Dalvin Cook, The Wolfpack earned its 2nd straight win to become 2-1 on the season. Losing WR Antonio Brown hasn't slowed these wolves one bit, and Ryan's team is looking as strong as ever. For this week, he remains at #3 in the rankings.

Too many Dingles, not enough Berries for Jerry this week, as he fell short of Team Taco Truck and suffered his first loss of the season. Jerry saw great games in unlikely places, such as the Chicago Bears DST scoring 22 points, and former Chicago Bear TE Greg Olsen scoring 24 points. IF only the Browns could be a little less of the Browns, Jerry may have continued his winning streak, but the Baker Mayfield/OBJ stack only connected for a score of 22.95 points. The DingleJerry's will keep on fighting with a talented squad, which keeps him among the top 5 teams again this week.

Joe told the self-proclaimed Mayor to Gallup on Mike Evans, as the wide receiver could not be stopped on his way to 190 yards and 3 touchdowns in week 3. New favorite target of Giants' QB Daniel Jones, TE Evan Engram outscored his counterpart T.J. Hockenson 23.30 to 0.60, which assisted the Johnson's to a blowout win of 151.06 to 106.86. Joe got good weeks out of both RBs again this week, and will need to continue having solid starts out of each of them to stay in the top 5 teams in the rankings.

Russell Wilson is here! That's who's here. Wilson outscored his counterpart Patrick Mahomes 50.24 to 39.21 in week 3, and led the way for an easy win for Nick/Austin. This squad puts up solid numbers week in and week out, but typically nothing through the roof. This week was no different, but the important thing to look at on this roster is the depth. Nearly every player on Nick/Austin's bench could have played in front of the starters and still achieved the same outcome. Injuries and the impending bye weeks certainly should not scare this squad, as they are built for the long haul.

Jonathan was JAWORking his magic all over the board in week 3, and got to sit back and watch his team score touchdown after touchdown. All but skill position (including TE) scored one touchdown this week, and 3 of them scored multiple touchdowns. Eventually, Jonathan had to turn off his cell phone because he had too many Yahoo touchdown notifications coming in at once (must be nice). Going forward, Jonathan will have to prove this week wasn't a fluke, if he wants to climb any higher than #7 on the big board.

The self-proclaimed Mayor was out of Titty City on holiday this week, and wasn't around to witness the 151.06 to 106.86 butt whooping his squad received in their week 3 matchup with Gallup On My Johnson. QB Matty Ice and WR Cooper Kupp were the only pieces that made this game as close as it was, and most of the remaining pieces of the puzzle were left in the box (Golladay 2.95, Jacobs 5.65 and Hockenson 0.60) for this upsetting matchup. Jacob still has plenty of fire power in his lineup and will likely bounce back in week 4 against Nick/Austin.

Everyone was tuned in to watch the battle of the titans ranked 11 and 12 in the week 3 rankings, and they were as disappointed as they should have expected to be, as they watched Game of Jones devour The Big Salami in a near 60 point differential blowout win. Game of Jones was firing on all cylinders this week, with great games by all 3 RBs and QB Jameis Winston, who threw for 380 yards and 3 touchdowns. WR Sterling Silver Shepard was looking a lot more like gold this week, scoring 24.80 points coming off an injury sustained in week 1. It appears that Josh's cannons have been lit, and will need to keep them firing at this pace to ascend even further up the charts.

This Country Road is taking Trevor Mahomes with back to back losses. If Mahomes and RB Phillip Lindsay didn't each score 30+ point this week, Trevor would have been blown out even more than he already was in this one, because all other players posted just average or below average scores. Trevor will need to make some trades, quality waiver pickups or start praying to the touchdown gods if he wants to get back on the winning track in the upcoming weeks.

The Ballers continue to find a way to put up average numbers that make them competitive, but rarely enough to win. Ageless RB Frank Gore did all that he could while trying to avoid turning to dust in this one, but his efforts still weren't enough to help The Ballers outrun The Wolfpack this time. Jim's roster has a couple of bright spots on it, but it is defintiely outweiged by question marks and poor usage (DAVID MONTGOMERY). We will have to see what Jim does this week to get out of the 11th spot in the rankings.

777 is usally a lucky number, but Jimmie was not happy to see it when his team scored 77.7 points in Week 3. Each player (minus the QB) on this squad scored fewer than 9 points this week, which led to an easy win for Game of Jones. Another week, another injury for the Big Salami, as focal point star RB Saquon Barkley went down with a high-ankle sprain and is expected to miss several weeks. This Big Salami is starting to grow mold while it waits to finally eclipse the 100 point mark this season, as this team has now had 3 straight weeks of sub 100 totals. For now, leave this salami in the basement where it belongs.

Tacos for everyone! Gil earned his 1st win of the 2019 season in week 2, as the New England Patriots DST drove the truck with WR Julio Jones riding shotgun. 37 points by the Patriots Defense was among the week's highest points across any position! No team in the history of fantasy football has ever been as strong and deep at both RB and TE as Team Taco Truck, with 4 quality RBs and 3 great TEs. While superstar RB Alvin Kamara is downgraded slightly due to the Drew Brees injury, Team Taco Truck regains the #1 spot in the rankings, as Gil's team looks to be solid up and down the lineup.

LA's Finest switched a couple of numbers around, going from 210 to 129 total points from week 1 to 2. Though he didn't score 200 points again, Yisha still managed to post the 3rd highest score of the week. Even with WR Robert Woods and RB Christian McCaffrey underperforming in week 2, LA's Finest narrowly escaped the Game of Jones by less than one reception. Winning his 2nd game in a row, Yisha looks poised to remain among the top teams in the league, and finds himself at #2 on the big board.

The Chef, Dalvin Cook himself, came through big for The Wolfpack in week 2 with 32 points, which led The 'Pack to an easy victory.
