Jim's roster is not built to destroy teams, but rather to be competitive, and will now and again destroy a team when all systems are firing at the same time.

Joe's Full Chubb got punched pretty hard and sustained a devastating injury to its namesake, but was still able to hang on for a 123-113 win over Gil's Tacos. Joe's waiver wire adds of Scotty Miller (WR for the Bucs) and RB Mike Davis came through big with a combined 40 points on the week. Joe will have to deal with his injuries by continuing to trust the nameless unsung stars as he preps for a battle with video game enthusiast, Austin and the Kamarios.

The self-proclaimed Mayor of Titty City is going to want to Mixon a water more often after that whopping 181 total yards and 3 TD masterpiece from RB Joe Mixon (44 total points). The rest of Jacob's roster was mostly average, with a little bit of boom sprinkled in. But with 44 points from one player and a weak showing from your opponent, average is good enough for a win. Jacob continues to need his stars to shine at the same time to really compete/dominate this year.

Despite 30 points from both Aaron Rodgers and Amari Cooper, Trevor and the Frogs were out-animaled by Ryan's Wolfpack 123-147. Trevor continues to get quality games from his starters, but for some reason, they just don't happen at the same time, causing him to have dropped 4 straight games. Will Trevor Bill O'Brien his team after their 0-4 start, or Adam Gase it in hopes of breaking the thick glass into the win column?

Ever wonder how to score 76 points during a fantasy football week, when you start every position and nobody gets hurt during the week? Well, one way to make it happen is to only score 1 touchdown across the entire starting lineup (QB Joe Burrow threw one, yes one, TD this week). Jimmie's DST and Kicker each put up less than 6 points, and still managed to individually outscore 4 other starting positional players on this roster. Until these guys can figure out how to be healthy at the same time (or at all) and do good things, Jimmie will be in the basement alone with the lights off.

The Touchdown Ticklers were out there Tickling all over the place this Sunday, as they dominate their way to 167-121 win over Ryan's Wolfpack. What do Josh Allen, DeAndre Hopkins, James Conner, DK Metcalf, Austin Ekeler and the Indianapolis Colts have in common, besides being starters for the Ticklers? They all scored 17+ points in week 3, with 3 of them scoring 25+, and Josh Allen scoring 38 points. With Allen setting opposing defenses on fire, Yisha's team comes into each week looking like the heavy favorite. Expect that to continue while they stay healthy, oh and when they get CMC back.

Game of Jones comes back down to earth, but still manages a win in week 3. Josh held off Jim's Twins on MNF, in what appeared to be a sure loss for this Jones (115-108). Josh received average-above average games from several positions this week, but he didn't have that soul-crushing game from anyone like he had in weeks 1 and 2. Did we see a soft spot in this team? We may have to wait until week 5 to find out, as Josh draws a weak matchup in Handoff Those Balls in week 4.

Holy Moly, Austin set his team to video game mode and let Super Kamario do the rest, as they destroy Kmet's Frogs 181-97. Austin has basically only needed 2 of his draft picks this year, as Kamara puts up his 3rd straight 2 TD week (oh, and don't forget his 200+ total yards), and Russell Wilson threw his 3rd straight 4 or more TD week (14 total TDs on the year. It's week 3). Austin also got gret games from Hill, Henderson and Singletary, which just padded the crushing victory. If Kamara and Wilson continue their outlandish performances, this team's baseline will be enough to beat anyone.

Raise your hand if your QB scored 50 points this week. Somewhere, Jerry is raising his hand with a smile on his face while people think he's nuts, but it's okay because his QB (Mr. Mahomes) put up a 50 spot in week 3. Jerry also got a combined 65 points from his 3 started RBs, which added to Mahomes' 50 points, would have been enough to win the week over Gil's Taco Truck. With the upside of Jerry's KC pieces, this team can boom and destroy anyone any week.

Gil's Taco Truck was serving up a mild version of their Tacos in week 3, as their average score was around 12 pts/player. Led by head chef, Kyler Murray's 27 points, Gil managed a total of 111 points on the week, which was destroyed by Jerry's 158 points. Gil will look to bounce back in week 4 against Joe's Full Chubb.

Jonathan brought the Magic in week 3, and handed another loss to Titty City 138-117. Some Magic dust was sprinkled on Drew Brees, who just dumped the ball off to the RB all day and sat back while his fantasy points were dragged up the hill by Alvin Kamara. Some of that dust also hit WR Tyler Lockett, who caught 3 first half TDs and ended with 36 points on the week. The remainder of this roster did enough to earn the win, but we will see if they can continue this streak in week 4, as they matchup against Big Jim and the Twins.

Joe and his Full Chubb came through once again, riding on the huge Chubb in Cleveland. RB Nick Chubb registered his 2nd straight week with 2 rushing TDs, which paved the way for 114-101 win over Jimmie's Balls. Chubb received some help from stand-in RB Mike Davis, who scored 21 points on the week, and the Ravens DST, who came through with a return TD. Joe will need the rest of his roster to contribute if he wants to beat the better teams in this league.

The Wolfpack's top 4 players (Watson, Kupp, Robinson II, Cook) all came out on the hunt, each scoring 21+ points on the week. Sounds great right? It would have been great, if the rest of Ryan's roster hadn't been held to single digit games, scoring less than 25 points combined between the remaining 5 starting positions. Ryan is hoping his week 3 trade will pay off over the next few weeks, as he cirrently sits 0-3 on the year and desparately needing a win.

Trevor's Frogs must have been allergic to triple digits this week, as they decide to score just 97 points in a disastrous 181-97 loss to Alvin Kamara and Russell Wilson. Even with the 75 points Trevor left on his bench, Kmet and the Frogs would still have lost their week 3 matchup. Trevor will need his high-end talent to show up at least once this year if he wants to get into the win column,

The sel-proclaimed Mayor commissioned a new railroad through Titty City, and Derrick Henry did his best impression as he hammered his way through the Viking defense to 2 scores and 31 points. Keenan Allen helped the construction with 25 points of his own, but after these two clocked out, construction stopped. Jacob's Mayoral speech didn't reach the players in the cheap seats, as the rest of this team was mediocre at best. Jacob will be hoping Julio can return and help this team get back to .500 in week 4.

Big Jim and the Twins get pinched in a Game of Jones and fall to 0-3 on the year. In a game that was winnable, Jim has to be regretting the start of Dion Lewis over 1st round pick Todd Gurley, who outscored Lewis 17-2. Jim's Twins are feeling the pain of being punched, as multiple players on this roster are struggling to get healthy/stay healthy. Until this team can get all of its starters back, they could see their struggles continue.

Jimmie swung for the fences by playing the Mustache Man out of Jacksonville, and struck out before a pitch was even thrown. These Balls have been kicked over and over again and appear to be a shell of their draft form. Until this roster can get out of the medical tent, it will be a Hail Mary week every week.

How does the #1 ranked team follow up his week 2 ranking of #1? They just put up a modest total of 187 points real quick. Would you believe that a team with 187 points actually had a WR only score 5 points? Well they did. Game of Jones saw 5 different player surpass 20 pts, 1 of them 37 pts and 1 with 49. This team feels like it has some divine intervention on its side, as they somehow dodged the injury demon that tormented the rest of the league in week 2. Good luck beating this team.

Yisha's high scoring losing streak comes to an end! Yish had the numbers in the right order with a 153-135 win over Jonathan's Magic. Another dominating performance by QB Josh Allen (43.5 pts) led the way, and was followed behind by 17+ point games from CMC, Ekeler, Hopkins and the Donkey. The real blow to this roster came when CMC went down with an ankle injury that is expected to keep him sidelined for 3-5 weeks. Other players on the Ticklers will have to step up in his place if they want earn another win.

Team Taco Truck cooked up another win in week 2 and served a hearty dish of loss to Kmet and the Frogs (135-109). Head chef and 2nd year stud, QB Kyler Murray, stood out once again with his 2nd straight 30+ point game. Kyler appears to be a steal in the draft thus far, as he continues to dominate. Gil let WR Mike Evans come back to work after taking a week off, and it paid off to the tune of 21 points. The Taco Truck did hit a few potholes on their journey this week, seeing a few starters go down to injury. If Gil can make sure his employees' shifts are covered, he will remain on track to earn his 3rd straigh victory.

Jerry and the Dingleberries find themselves on the wrong side of the garbage bowl matchup, losing 105-115. Patrick Mahomes did all that he could to help this team to a victory, posting 35 points, but the rest of the team could not keep up, with 4 starters being outscored by the Kicker and DST positions. Jerry sunk a pretty penny into the fountain of Hines, and pulled out a dirty penny in return. These Dingles will need their studs to remember who they are if they want to get a week 3 win over Gil's Taco Truck.

Super Kamario! was just that in week 2, recording another 2 touchdowns and 174 total yards. Kamario himself lead the way for QB Russell Wilson to score his 2nd straight week of 39+ points, and waiver wire TE Jonnu Smith to collect 23 points himself. The "one touch man", Tyreek Hill saved his day with a 50 yard TD reception, but it wasn't even needed, as this video game roster put on the star power and blasted right through the Wolpack 167-100. Austin is putting together a team to pay attention to.

Jonathan Jaworked his magic this week, getting a couple of great games from his starters. However, the combination of having two 30 point players on the bench and getting goosed by Gronk, Jona fell short to the Ticklers in week 2. The Magic still has plenty of fire power as they too dodged the injury demon, so look for them to rise in the rankings.

Big Jim N The Twins came out swinging with a 25 point night from Hunt on Thursday, and followed it up with 45 points and 23 points from Dak and Miles Sanders, respectively. The Twins outperformed projections, scoring 133 points, however the single digit games from E. Sanders, Gurley and Ertz really hurt down the stretch, as the Twins get pinched in a 145-133 loss. Jim will need some of his injuries to subside in order to propel this team to the next level.

Nick Chubb said "I AM THE FULL CHUBB!" and went wild in week 2, scoring 2 touchdowns on top of 133 total yards. Chris Carson and Tyler Higbee helped keep the Chubbs propped up with 48 points and 4 touchdowns between the two. If Joe can continue to get this production and get the rest of his stars going, he will be competing for a top spot in the rankings.

The self-proclaimed Mayor of Titty City was playing a whole different game than the one the Joneses were playing in week 2. Up against an Aaron Jones 50 point week, the Mayor had only QB Cam Newton to fight back. Unfortunately for Jacob, he received only a combined 6 points from 3 of his starters. There was nothing more this team could do against Goliath, so chalk this loss up to fate. Jacob will look to rebound with a better performance in week 3.

Kmet the Frog is feeling the strains of not having their #1 WR in Kenny G for a 2nd straight week, only receiving 20 points from both active/starting WRs. Trevor luckily dodged a neck injury to David Montgomery, his star of the week (23 points), and actually came away with all of his players intact. The Frogs will need to get hopping and score some points if they want to get into the win column in a tough week 3 matchup against Austin's Kamara-led heroes.

Jimmie prayed and prayed, and he received a Monday night miracle, as he came back from a 24 point deficit to win 115-105. These Balls have scraped by in the first 2 weeks, somehow starting the season 2-0, while only scoring 231 points total. The biggest, yet not surprising, news is that this team lost its star RB Saquon Barkley to a season ending ACL tear. Left with extreme holes in this roster, Jimmie will have to find a way to put points on the board if he wishes to stay competitive this season.

It has been a rough couple of weeks for this Wolfpack, as they go hungry once again in week 2 with a loss to the Kamarios 167-100. Ryan received good/average play from most of his roster, but was up against a power house this week. To make matters worse, Ryan left 45 points sitting on the bench. Hopefully Ryan can get this Pack back in order and earn a few wins.

Josh said 8th place ranking for the reigning champions? Prove it roster? How's 143 points in week 1 for proving it!? Oh, and I did that without a kicker! Josh was juiced up as all but 2 of his players scored 15+ points, with 3 of them scoring 29+ points. If this was not a blip on the radar, start planning ahead for your matchup against this squad.

Yisha has to be asking what year is this? 2020? Or did 2019 just continue? As he continues his unfortunate struggle of having amazing weeks against teams that also have an amazing week. Yisha Tickled the endzone numerous times this week, but came up just short to Game of Jones 143-140. This roster is still packed with studs and is going to be a force all year long.

This Taco Truck must have taken a long road trip this summer and scouted the chefs on the West coast, because the new additions to this team (Kyler, Woods, Jacobs, Mostert) cooked up something special in week 1. While the rest of Gil's team did enough to help get the week 1 dub, these 4 guys did all the heavy lifting with 3/4 of them scoring 25+ points. If this becomes the norm for these guys, it won't matter who else is in the Truck.

The Mayor is back in town and ready for business! Jacob got down and dirty in this one and grinded out a win with whatever he could. Despite only getting touchdowns from his DST and his QB, the self-proclaimed Mayor was able to pull out a win for his beloved City of Titties. This could mean he got lucky, or that his team is twice as dangerous if the touchdowns fall his way.

Look out Will Smith, there's a new Prince of Helaire, and he goes by Clyde Edwards! Jerry gambled all of his berries on the rookie RB when he took him 2nd overall, but after week 1 Jerry could be cashing in his winnings. The KC stack of Mahomes and CEH put up 49 points, and was helped along by Baltimore, who allowed TE Mark Andrews to get 21 points as well. Jerry will need nothing less from these studs as he heads into his week 2 matchup.

The Wolfpack came charging out of the woods only to trip over their own feet in week 1. Ryan's two elite WRs both won their NFL games, but somehow only combined for 10.20 fantasy points on the week. If watching these two stars struggle wasn't enough, Ryan had to watch two players rip off 25+ point games while sitting on the bench. This team has all the potential needed to be a contender, but they obviously need to perform to reach that outcome.

WILLLLSOOONNN! Is what Austin and the Kamarios were screaming all Sunday long, as Russell Wilson shelled out TD passes like Oprah giving gifts during Christmas. Unfortunately for Austin, his team was too busy watching Russ cook all day that that they forgot to score their own points. Even if Kamara's 3rd TD of the day had counted, Austin would have been rolled over by the Taco Truck. If the rest of this team can get some of Russ' Secret Stuff, look for them to soar to the top of rankings.

Jim and the Twins came out looking like Full Chubb, but ended up getting kicked where it hurts by the DingleJerries, losing 130-101. Most of the guys on this roster (almost all) underperformed from their potential, and yet Jim still hit triple digits. If this team can get as big as their name suggests, they will do some damage.

Handoff Those Balls took the handoff and narrowly escaped being tackled by Kmet and his band of Frogs. Jimmie rode the week 1 roller coaster as he watched Adams shred the Packers, followed by Lev Bell landing on the IR and Saquon rushing for 15 yards. Luckily Jimmie snuck out a win, but he will need some help if he wants to win again. Which he does.

Joe came into week 1 with a bulge that looked like a Full Chubb, but when he dropped his pants, all we saw was half Chubb. Joe looked ready to do damage, but only QB Lamar Jackson and RB Chris Carson were on board with that plan, contributing more than 50% of the team's overall point total. If Joe plans to drop his pants in public again soon, he better hope the rest of his roster is ready to help prop that thing up.

Kmet let the Frogs out in week 1, unfortunately for Trevor, they all just hopped away. Dealing with some pre-week injuries, Trevor had to scramble and throw in the Lazard King, WR Allen Lazard, who showed up big with 17 points. David Johnson and Kenyan Drake did their part to help the Frogs, but couldn't get their hands on those balls and took a week 1 L to Jimmie. Trevor will need to get some better production or find some longterm help if he wants to push for the top of the rankings.

Anyone watching the DALvsLAR game was constantly thinking "who has Zeke??", and the unfortunate answer was never "me". The pre-draft trade to acquire Elliot proved to be a great move in week 1, as he brought the Magic and carried them to a victory over Ryan's Wolfpack. Jona will need to provide Zeke some help if he wishes to continue his winning streak.

CROWN THIS TEAM THE CHAMPION AT WEEK 1! Coming in at #1 in the initial 2020 rankings is newly named Yish and the Touchdown Ticklers. After a predraft trade, and a 15th round keeper selection of RB James Conner, Yish drafted a team that is jam packed with talent. This team looks like its ready to be tickling each other in the endzone time and time again this season.

Don't call this Mayor a deuce, but he does come in at the #2 team in the week 1 rankings. Stacked with top end talent, Titty City could be partying topless all season long. Jacube has some depth pieces that could add extra power to his already jacked team.

Sliding into the #3 spot of the 2020 week 1 rankings is the one man wolfpack. Ryan doubled down on 1st round keepers by way of a trade before the draft, and gained tremendous value in a 2nd round WR Michael Thomas. Ryan's hopes of making his 5th straight playoff appearance depends on his top talent being what they were drafted to be. We shall see!
Jimmie is hoping to handoff those balls of yesteryear and start fresh with a winning squad. IF injuries dont plague this starting roster, Jimmie could be in line for some early wins.

Parking in the final spot of the top 5 teams is Gil and the Taco Truck. Littered with youth, Gil may have some questions to answer regarding the labor laws. Despite their age, these players have the ability to score points like seasoned veterans. If these players hit their potential, Gil could be be the #1 team sooner than later.

Hopping in at #6 is Trevor, Kmet and the Frogs. Entering the draft with 2 of the best keeper values in RBs Ekeler and Drake, Trevor surrounded them with great supporting pieces. If this supporting cast can help the Frogs reach their potential, Kmet and The Frogs will be a team to pay attention to.

Big Jim N The Twins are coming in hot with roster going for girth. This meaty lineup is ready to bust or boom depending on how the chips fall. If these players produce like they should on paper, then this team will make a mess of this Biscuits on their way to the top spot.

Game of Jones is riding high after their 2019 championship, but they come into the 2020 season with a "prove it" roster. With names such as Jones, Jones II, Taylor, Ridley nad Thielen, This team needs to prove they can beat out their depth charts, overcome injuries and return to glory. If the pieces align, Josh could be contending to defend his title.

Joe and his Full Chubb are strapping on their belt and getting busy as they try to avenge their championship loss in the 2019 finals. Joe kept Jackson tight to the chest during the draft, but now he's ready to let him loose on the competition. If Jackson can repeat and some of these ancillary pieces can get to the next level, this Chubb will fully be on its way to another championship matchup.

Jonathan came into his 2nd Risky Biscuit draft fully intending on drafting Choan in the first round, but when he was able to get a predraft deal done with Dingles, Jonathan had to rearrange his plans. Securing Zeke for the 2020 season was a great foundational piece, and the tools Jonathan placed around him, this Jaworker could be set for a season of Magic.

Big Dingles is fighting his way onto the Kansas City Chiefs, as he planted his flag in KC by drafting Mahomes and CEH as his 1-2 punch. He also reached into the Ravens camp and snagged their 1-2 punch in Andrews and Ingram. If this 1-2-3-4 punch does what's expected, Jerry will be fighting for the top spots in the rankings.

Entering week 1, teams ranked 2-12 could all be ranked at any position 2-12, and every team has the potential to be the top team next week. For Austin, his chances ride on super Kamario's epidural and whether or not Seattle lets Russ cook or not. This team has plenty of talent to compete with anyone in the league, and we'll see if they can deliver video game types of performances!

2021.notes: Holy Pigskin, this team wasn't Playing around with the idea of missing the championship game, as they went out and scored possibly the highest score in league history at 196.17. This high score came in a game where Saquon only scored 5 points on the week. Jimmie is now up against the storybook underdogs in his first championship game since 2016. Hopefully all the points weren't spent in week 16.

David did it! And some of us our still surprised with the outcome, even though it's a story as old as time. Ryan and the Wolves took down the leagues Goliath in the semifinals 111-98, despite being without multiple players due to injury/covid. Ryan's special talent is fantasy sports, and it has been on display in the Risky Biscuit Brigade for years, as he is now playing for back to back titles and his 3rd in the league.

The King has taken off his crown and come down from the Hill, as his run at the grand prize is officially over. Austin had a nightmare of a week in the worst possible situation, as this was his lowest score since week 2. Outside of week 2 and 3, Austin never scored less than 120+ points in a week, until week 16. Austin will have one week left to try and claim the 3rd place title (came in 4th last year), before getting back to selling propane in the offseason.

The Taco Truck served up as many dishes as they could in week 17, 131 of them to be exact, but came up 65 Tacos short of the win. While it is never easy to lose a playoff game, Gil can rest easy knowing there was nothing he could have done differently this go around. Gil will be going into the 3rd/4th place game for the 3rd time with a 2-0 record in the matchup (taking 3rd in both 2017 and 2019). However, he is unfortunately stuck up against a very hungry King of the Hill squad coming off one of their worst games of the year. Gil will have to wait until next year to try and make it into the championship game.

The budget Magician pulled out all his remaining tricks and stole Yisha's 5th place seat away from him (140-109). Jona rode the Stallion, Josh Allen and his sidekick Stefon Diggs (39 & 19) points to the 31-point margin of victory. The Bills stack finally came through big time and helped Jona to cut his best finish in half (10th to 5th). if that's the trend, is 2 1/2th on the table for Jona in 2022?

The Hiroshima Hotdog himself, Yisha, was tired of finishing 5th, so he went and took 6th instead, losing 109-140 to the Magician. The Chubbless Miles were wishing they could have been the Mileless Chubbs in week 16, as Sanders scored less than 7 points, while Chubb scored more than 30. Yisha has to be feeling a bit unhappy with his half-sell/half-buy approach at the deadline, given the 6th place result. Despite the disappointing end, Yisha can be happy that he has made the playoffs in 5 straight years, and only has one missed postseason in his RBB career.

If you had a round 1 bye (both brackets) and your name wasn't Trevor, you had a disappointing semifinal matchup. Trevor was the only team to rest in week 15 and get a week 16 win (winning 129-95 in Titty City), making you wonder if the bye is good or bad? It's good. It's always good. Trevor will be hoping to take all or most of Joe Burrow's and Damien Harris' 48 and 32 point games into the consolation finals against Big Jim. Trevor has never had higher than the 3rd overall pick, so he's already ahead of years past going in to week 17.

Big Jim dropped his drawers and showed off the Twins in week 16, taking down the once top tier Griddles, 131-117. Jim's Savvy waiver wire adds prior to week 16 helped lead him to the win and one game closer to the 1st overall pick. Waiver wonders Ronnie Jones and Justin Michael Jackson were dancing all over their opponents, giving the Twins 51 combined points on the week. Jim last picked 1st overall in 2018, which turned into a 6th place finish in 2019.

What a turn of events for Joe's Griddleiron. After making the big buy of multiple studs from Jerry, most people had Joe finding the championship game easily. A few end of season losses ended up putting Joe outside of the playoff picture and into the 1st overall pick talks. After the round 1 bye, Joe was stopped in his tracks at the sight of Jim's Big Jim and Twins flowing in the wind, losing the semifinal matchup 117-131. Joe will have to take down the self-proclaimed Mayor if he wants the 3rd overall pick in 2022.

The self-proclaimed Mayor likely won't be inviting Joe Burrow or Damien Harris back into Titty City limits anytime soon, after they dropped an 80-burger in the streets. The duo was onl 15 points short of beating the entire starting staff for the Mayor, which would have been embarrassing. The Mayor has both an 8th place and a 12 place finish in his accolades, and he will be hoping to pull out the upset over Joe to add a 9th place finish to that bunch.

The Fighting DingleJerrys remain the better of the bottom dwellers, as he claims the 11th spot over Game of Jones 103-79. Jerry and Josh had been battling it out to not be the bottom team all year it seemed, so it was only fitting that they squared off in the 11th/12th place matchup. Jerry did what he had to do to stay on top of Josh and earn himself the 5th overall pick in 2022.

If Mallory was a fan of fantasy football, and a fan of the Game of Jones squad, she may be wearing a paper bag on her head this offseason, as Josh ended 2021 with his worst finish in his RBB history. The 79-103 loss to Jerry was Josh's lowest point total on the year, so he apparently saved the worst for last. Jokes aside, this is somewhat of a riches to rags story, as Josh has only missed the playoffs once in his RBB career, and he's also coming off of a back-to-back-to-back championship appearance stretch that spans back to 2018.

The King sat up on his Hill and watched the peasants fight it out to see who would be worthy of trying to dethrone him in the semifinals. The Wolfpack cleared the path and will be taking on Austin in week 16. This team is dealing with some health issues at the wrong time of the year and will hoep to be healthy enough to get their 11th win in a row.

Jimmie was Playing with the playoff Pigskin in week 15 against Jona the Great and came away with a dominating 142-86 win. Outside of massive weeks from Mark Andrews and Cooper Kupp, who each had 136 yards and 2 TDs, this team was not overly impressive (4 starters with less than 10 points). Jimmie is taking on a rested Taco Truck thats running on full in the semifinal matchup.

Ryan, the week's high scorer with 147 points, was never really in doubt of missing the semifinals after Travis Kelce ripped the Chargers defense for 191 yards and 2 TDs and 37 fantasy points (more than his previous 4 weeks combined) on Thursday night. Ryan only needed Jalen Hurts' 32.44 points and my name is Jeff Wilson's 22.5 points to have enough to beat Yisha's 89.61 points on the week. Ryan now unfortunately has to take on the league's Goliath in the semifinals, but we all know how that story ended.

Gil spent the entire bye week off filling up the Taco Truck's tank and making sure it didn't slide a sliver passed the F line. Fortunately for Gil, he was on the bye week, as his 88 points would have made for a competitive match between a few playoff teams. Gil had the extra week to decide who to play in his semifinal showdown with the Pigskin, so who will be serving the Tacos in week 16?

A sad end to a promising season for the Chubless Miles, who wouldn't have been competitive in week 15 even with his Mile long Chubb in the starting lineup. This team was disappointing all week outside of Ekeler and Parker's 15+ point games. Yisha will now be trying to take home the 5th place crown for the 3rd straight year and 4th team in 6 seasons.

Jona's Magical playoff run came to an abrupt end, as they were defeated in round one by a score of 86-142. The Magic had all but 3 players score less 10 points, and only 2 players had above 12. The budget Magician turned this season into a better finish than his previous two years in the league (10th each year), but a sour taste in 2021 will maybe make Jona master his practice and be a full-price Magician in 2022.

Joe missed the playoffs by way of total points scored on the year, but that turned into a consolation round 1 bye, which he had thankfully, as he only managed to Grill up 99 points against nobody this past week. Even worse, 36 of those points came from Patrick Mahomes. Joe will be up against the skeleton crew propping up Big Jim and his Twins in the consolation semis, and he will be hoping for a far better week from his studly lineup.

The Mooney Toons turned off the TV and took a much needed week off to gather themselves and put a better program on in week 16. During their off-air time, Trevor rehearsed a 75 point performance for no audience. Hopefully this dry run is not a sign of things to come, as he turns the TV on in Titty City, which is coming off a 105-81 win in week 15.

The self-proclaimed Mayor kept Titty City's hopes of the 1st overall pick alive after a 105-81 win over the struggling Game of Jones. Jacube was 1 of 4 teams to score more than 100 points in week 15, and the win puts him one game close to achieving that 1st pick. Jacube had a load of 20s on his bench, so Titty City is hoping their starters play like their bench in week 16.

Big Jim and the Twins came out of a toilet bowl matchup with a win over the buttcheek-dwelling DingleJerries 83-57. This was a record low week for the league, but this was the record low game, with 2 teams that would have beaten both these teams combined. Big Jim gained some help via the waiver wire, so if he can get healthy on top of those additions, he may have a shot at the 1st overall pick.

Game of Jones has officially locked up an 11th or 12th place finish after losing the round 1 matchup in Titty City. The loss is sums up how this season has gone for Josh, only winning 3 games thus far. He has one final game against the Dingle himself, and then he can possibly live vicariously through his brother Austin, who is on the other end of the spectrum.

The Big Dingle. The Fighting Dangle. The hairy Berry named Jerry. The man who is not so merry this time of year, as he scored less than 60 points in a must win round 1 consolation battle, ending his top 4 pick hopes. Jerry will hope to bounce back in a big way to hopefully earn the 5th pick in next year's draft.

Bye, bye, bye! Austin is not the Jones brother known for reciting the dance to that famous song, but he will be dancing this week, as he ended the regular season in 1st place and earned the prized 1st round bye. The end of the season came with Austin on a 10 game win streak, which is a league record (not sure if this is factual). This team does not need the rest at all, but they will watch the rest of the league try to join him in week 16's semifinals.

The Chubbless Miles certainly have at least a little Chubb after their week 14 win knowing that they have secured a spot in the playoffs at 8-6 on the season. This was a monster 151 point week with only 2 players scoring 7 points or less, while also having 2 players score 32+ points. Yisha is matched up against Ryan in the 4th-5th seeded game.

Three little piggies have come home in a row, as they won their last three games to sneak into the playoffs, and now they just need the final 3 piggies to come home as well. Jimmie was the top scoring team in the league (only by 2 points) this week, and he's spending his winnings on a search and rescue team to find Terry McLaurin, who is on the back of a milk carton after a 0.00 point game in week 14. The Pigskin will be Playing with Magic in the quarterfinals against 6th seeded Jona the Great.

The Taco Truck had parked inside the playoff lot prior to week 14, but their 133-90 win over the Mooney Toons secured their spot as the #2 team and a bye in round 1. The extra R&R will do wonders for this team of yesteryear (Julio, AJ Green, Patterson, Cook), as age tends to slow down your game. Gil will watch closely to see which team with the lowest seed wins in the quarterfinals to meet up with him in the finals.

The Wolfpack got their wins in earlier in the season, securing their playoff spot sooner than later, which came in handy as the team is currently on a 3 game losing streak. The streak pushed the Wolves out of the bye slot and into the 4th seed, where he will try to chomp off Yisha's playoff Chubb. Ryan wil be hoping for a healthy roster who is also on their high side of their teeter totter performances.

The pressure was on in weke 14, as Jona needed to win to get in, and the Magicican came through with a Magical performance, eliminating Jacube's postseason hopes 149-110. Jona's packing some big stones inside that hat, as he picked up and played Rashaad Penny, who came through with 137 yards and 2 TDs. This is the 1st playoff appearance for Jona, after finishing the previous two seasons in 10th place. The Magic come in as the 6th seed and hope to use some of their tricks to reveal a championship.

A season that held so much promise came to an end in heart-breaking fashion, as Joe wins his week 14 matchup but still misses the playoffs at 8-6. Joe's back to back losses prior to this week pushed him outside the playoff picture and in need of some help from other teams. Unfortunately for Joe, those teams could not do what was needed to get him in, as he misses the playoffs 46 points. Joe will hope that his deadline trade will help him earn the #1 overall pick in 2022, and he gets off to a good start with a bye in round 1 of the consolation playoffs.

The Mooney Toons turned off the show for the final time this season, as their 90-133 loss to the Tacos in week 14 ended their playoff hopes and land them in the consolation playoffs for the 2nd time in 2 years. Trevor had a plethora of let down games this week, with none being worse than Lamar Jackson's 1.78 points after leaving with an ankle injury. Trevor will be unhappy with his regular season standings, but the Toon squad will happily take this bye week to heal up in preparation for their fight for the #1 overall pick.

The self-proclaimed Mayor allowed the Magic show to come to town and ended up getting duped out of a playoff position. Jacube needed to defeat Jona the Great in week 14 to have a chance to make the playoffs (which wouldn't have happened regardless), but he ended up falling 110-149. This year, Titty City went from a dominating force in this league to a broken shell of itself, losing far too many pieces to stay competitive. Jacube has yet to taste the playoffs since joining the league, but a #1 overall pick in next year's draft could change that in 2022.

Big Jim and the Twins had been waiting for this week to be over for some time now, as their postseason spot had been locked up a couple weeks back, sitting comfortably in 10th place. This outcome was truly unexpected after the amazing start to the season, but injuries can destroy any team at any time. Big Jim will try and take down his pal DingleJerry in the consolation quarterfinals to try and guarantee a top 4 pick in next year's draft.

The mighty have fallen, as Game of Jones has officially ended a 3 year streak of playing in the championship game, earning a 1st place title and two 2nd place finishes during that time. Josh will have to wade through unfamiliar territories, as he has not missed the playoffs since the leagues inaugural season back in 2016. Josh passed on some of his good fortune and gave his brother the final good luck tap heading into the playoffs, losing 139-96 and becoming the 10th straight losing opponent to Austin's Goliath of a roster. Game of Jones will head into the Battle of Titty City in week 15, as both clubs are seeking the elusive #1 overall pick.

The Fighting Dingles have been scratching and clawing for wins over the past month or so, earning them a 5-9 record in the regular season, keeping them ahead of a 12th place finish. DingleJerry is coming off of a 3rd place finish in 2020, and will have to run through some quality opponents in order to claim a top pick in 2022.

King of the Hill is one win away from 10 straight wins after starting the season 0-4. Austin has secured the #1 seed heading into the playoffs, meaning week 15 is a rest week for this squad. The starting lineup is full of players ready to boom, as seen in Taylor's 30 point week, or Kittle's 38 point night from the TE position. Austin looks like a lock for the championship week.

The Chubbless became the Milesless this week, as Sanders left in the middle of a great performance, leaving Yisha 28 points short of Gil's Taco Truck (102-130). Adam Thielen's early exit (1 catch for 0 yards) assisted in the loss, which brings Yisha on the edge of the playoff line and needing a week 14 win. Yisha could land anywhere from 3rd to 8th depending on how this week goes.

Joe takes a spanking from his father and loses a 2nd straight game (124-86). The back to back losses out the Gang dangerously close to missing the playoffs, as they are now on the outside looking in. Joe will need to win and get some help from other teams if he wants to clinch a playoff spot.

The Pigskin prayed for a miracle, and Jesus was listening on Sunday night, as Jimmie narrowly escaped getting eaten by the Wolfpack 132.99-132.06. The win puts this team's fate back in their own hands, as they now have a "win and in" situation. Jimmie's outcome ranges from a round 1 bye in the playoffs to a round 1 bye in the consolation bracket.

If one team gets a miracle, one team gets a nightmare, and unfortunately the Wolves got the latter in week 13, losing 132.06-132.99 to the Pigskin. Ryan had dominating performances from Mitchell, Gibson and Justin Jefferson, who managed to put up nearly 200 yards and a TD against the Lions. Hurtsing at the QB position, Ryan put Teddy Two INTs under center and felt the pain. This team has secured a playoff spot, but the bye week is up for grabs this week.

The Taco Truck only needed to staff 3 employees this week, as Herbert (33), Williams (32) and Michel (24) pulled the Truck to a win over the Chubless Miles (130-102) in week 13. Gil overcame garbage games from too many of his starters to put himself in contention for the 1st round bye. The Truck will be watching cartoons this week to prepare for their matchup with the Mooney Toons.

The Mooney Toons gave Mike's Secret Stuff to Johnson, Harris and Goedert, who all went Looney in week 13 (28, 20 and 26 points respectively) and helped the Toons take down Big Jim's Twins 134-103. Harris' 20 point game could have been even larger if he was hampered with a hamstring injury, which pulled him from the game early. The win ends a 4 game losing streak and puts trevor in a position to make the playoffs with a 7-7 record. Trevor will need a win and a couple teams above him to lose in orfer to make it in the 2021 postseason.

Despite losing 103-134 to the Mooney Toons in week 13, this was an impressive showing by Big Jim and the Twins. This team's starting lineup had names such as: TY Hilton, DeeJay Dallas, Jermar Jefferson and Sammy Watkins. If you don't know who some of those names are, or if you know that its not 2016 anymore, then you should be impressed that this team scored 100+ points and only lost by 31. However, even if you're impressed, week 13 was a must win game for the Twins, and the loss guarantees a consolation appearance for Jim.

Jona and the who? The Magic has faded for this show, as their 3rd straight loss has the budget Magician on verge of being cancelled. This week's loss was predictable, as he was tasked with taking the King down from the Hill in the middle of an 8 game win streak. This is a must win week for Jona, as his opponent, Titty City, would swap places with him should the Magic come away with a loss.

There are too many things to talk about in Titty City after a wild week 13 win over Game of Jones, 95-88. The self-proclaimed Mayor became the 1st manager in league history to win a game with a QB (who played a full game) to have completed only 2 passes (on 3 attempts for just 19 yards and 1.41 fantasy points). Jacube, even after having been a seller at the deadline due to multiple injuries, still has a shot at making the postseason. Jacube would need a win over Jona's Magic this week, as well as a loss from a few teams (combination of Joe, Yisha and Trevor).

Game of Jones drops a close one to the Mayor (95-88) and secures the last place title, as he is now 2 games back from the DingleJerry. Josh got half his points from Kirk Cousins and Josh Jacobs this past week, but he will need more if he wants to make it out of round 1 of the consolation playoffs. Josh is now in prep mode for his hunt for the 1st overall pick in the 2022 draft.

After getting taken down by his son in week 7 (121-86), DingleJerry returned the favor and put Joe back in his place with a 124-86 win in week 13. Jerry was led by Kyler Murray, who took the last 4 weeks off, but saved all those points for this past week (35 points on just 11 completions for 123 yards). Jerry's throwback heroes, Freeman and Gronk ech contributed 20 points to the cause, helping secure the easy win for Jerry. This team is waiting for week 15 and the start of the consolation playoffs.

How do you win a game where 5 of 9 players have less 10 points and your QB has less than 15 points? The answer is to have a team total of 146 points by way of 7 TDs from your 3 starting RBs. Leonard Forty-fournette had 4 TDs and a total of 44 points, which overshadowed Joe Mixon's 165 yards and 2 TDs (35 points), which overshadowed John Taylor's 97 yards and a TD (20 points). When you play this team, it will certainly be death by RB.

The Griddles gathered together and decided to get on the back of kicker Daniel Carlson, who scored 14 points on TNF, which was only 2nd on this team to D. Adams' 15.65 points. Not much else needs to be said about this week's loss. Joe now is in need of some wins in the next couple weeks.

The Chubbless Miles earn their 3rd straight win since trading away Nick Chubb, 114-96 over the Mooney Toons. The win streak lands Yish in 3rd place and in a great spot to make the playoffs. This team continues to ride Awesome Ekeler (21 points), who has now recorded 7 of 11 games over 20 points. If the injuries issues can go away, this team will be a strong contender in a couple weeks.

The RBB's #1 team heading into week 12 fell victim to the upset, losing to the 11th place Dingles 119-101. More than half of the team's total points came from their 2 RBs, Mitchell and Gibson, who scored 55 points together. Ryan is comfortable up in 2nd place at 8-4, but another win could earn them the round 1 bye.

The Pigskin played their best and got the week 12 win to get back to an even 6-6 on the year, but at what cost? In what was arguably the worst back-to-back play sequence in fantasy football, the Pigskin lost both Dalvin Cook and Deebo Samuel to multi-week injuries in the must-win portion of the season. This team will hopefully find a way to plug those gaping holes before the ship sinks.

The Taco Truck was full of flat tires in week 12, but they managed to survive a battle with the Big Jim and Twins to stay in the playoff picture. QB Justin Herbert and utility man Corderoy Patterson dragged this team to a 93-86 win. The Truck will be without it's best menu item in CMC for the remainder of the season, as the Panthers decided to shut him down on IR for the 2nd time this year. Gil will need to fill his empty spot if he wishes to go deep in the postseason.

The Mooney Toons don't go Looney in week 12, scoring jsut 96 points in a crushing loss to the Chubbless Miles. The loss was quite the swing for where Trevor could have been in the playoff outlook, as he now stands at 5-7 and needing plenty of help to find a way in. This team has been carried by their DST and kicker in the last two weeks, which cannot be the script going forward.

Jona and the Magic quickly went from 7-3 near the top of the league to 7-5 and on the edge of missing the playoffs with back to back losses. Jona's week 12 loss to 12th place Game of Jones was a tough one to swallow, as his stars played great (Allen with 34, Diggs with 17, Zeke with 15 and Waddle with 26), but they just could not overcome their fill-in teammates. Jona has a tough matchup this week and could be looking at 7-6 heading into week 14.

The self-proclaimed Mayor knew he was leading Titty City into a suicide battle against King of the Hill, but he sent the troops, who fought bravely. Unfortunately, Titty City was conquered by Leonard Fournette, Joe Mixon and Johnny Taylor (104-146). Even with another monster game from Aaron Rodgers (31 points), the Mayor was no match for the King. The loss puts Jacube low in the playoff polls.

Game of Jones brought his own Magic hat to matchup and stole the show from the budget Magician. Josh turned a backup RB into 22 points and a DST against the Rams into 9 points, which then turned the game into a Josh Jones win 127-117. Josh got the win, still remains in 12th place, as the 11th place team also completed the week 12 upset. Game of Jones will be looking to gain a game on the DingleJerrys before week 15.

Big Jim and the Twins were wearing a jock strap 2 sizes too small in week 12, in it showed on the field, only able to squeeze out 87 points in a loss to the Tacos 93-87. This team is hurting right now, and when you have to play the backup's backup, things are likely not going to end well. Jim's playoff chances are lacking girth.

The man, the myth, the legend, has nothing to do with the remainder of this blurb. However, an 11th over 1st upset is always something for the big screen, so this game gets its story. The Dingle himself (due to injuries, byes and possibly even insanity) played a starting lineup full of names you would have to search for on the draft board this year, but that lineup put up 119 points and took down the #1 ranked Wolfpack 119-101. This team's movie moment also kept Jerry in 11th place over the Gaming Joneses.

Another week, another win for the King, who is one win away from being King of the entire Hill. The win marks Austin's 7th of the year, now sitting at 7-4 in the standings. It's tough to lose a game when your #1 RB scores 30 points in the actual NFL, and almost 60 (58) in fantasy, which is what Johnny Football Taylor did against the Bills in week 11. Just having a player with this type of potential makes you a top team.

The Griddles get back on top, beating Game of Jones 116-91. QB Patrick Mahomes has been choosy with his fantasy points this year, scoring 44 points last week, and only 24 combined points in the weeks on each end of that 44 point game. Joe's big 3 in Adams, Harris and Evans produced what they needed to in order to get the win, and with their top end potential, Joe is a scary matchup any week.

The Chubless Miles may wish they moved on from RB Nick Chubb earlier in the year, as they have won both games since his departure. 3 players carried this team to week 11 win over the Dingles, and those 3 players were Ekeler, Conner and Thielen, who scored 41, 22 and 19 points respectively. Awesome Ekeler is one of those matchup-winning players, and he showed it with 115 yards and 4 TDs. It's crazy that a week like this was overshadowed by an even better RB performance in John Talyor.

The Wolfpack win another nail-biter, winning their 2nd straight week by a 2 point margin (146-144). The Wolves continue to prove that sometimes the Alphas can pull you to victory, as Ryan got massive games from Hurts, Jefferson, Williams and Kelce (totaling 108 of the team's 146 points). The boom potential of this steady team is what will continue to bring wins their way.
The words I have for this team this week are not suitable for most audiences.

The Taco Truck was devoured by the Wolfpack in this week's highest scoring match (144-146). Newly hired head chef, Justin Herbert (44 points) only scheduled RBs on the shift list this week, as 70 of the team's 144 points came from their 3 starting RBs. The rest of the team was outscored by the starting kicker McPherson, who had 13 points against the Raiders. The fire power is very real with this team, as seen this week.

Big Jim got his Twins back to their winning ways with a 115-105 win over the Toons. Jim's Twins are very bruised right now, forcing him to start a Houston RB in David Johnson. Jim was fortunate his main 4 starters (Brady, Moore, Lockett and Swift) came through with nice enough games to lift them to a win. The win keeps Jim in playoff contention, as he sits in 10th place at 5-6, which is only 1 game out of a playoff position.

Austin is not a fan of Magic and wouldn't the the budget Magician anywhere near his Hill, as Jona the Great got his hat stomped 105-160. Jona dug deep into his Magic hat and pulled out a name from 2017 in Duke Johnson, who plays for the Dolphins if you didn't know. The previous sentence should pretty much be enough description for how this week went for this team.

The Mooney Toons, sans Lamar Jackson, is not a cartoon you want to watch. With Jackson sitting out week 11 with an illness, Trevor slotted in rookie QB Justin Fields, who said "thanks, here's 4 points.". The Toons leaned heavily on the Pats' kicker and DST, who totaled 27 points for this team. In a battle for a playoff spot is a terrible time to be unhealthy, and this team is in the trenches of that battle while clearly ill. Trevor will need to pull out some Looney tricks to get any points/wins down the stretch.

The self-proclaimed Mayor of Titty City called in some under the table favors and got his opponent to inexplicably start Tee Higgins over Terry McLaurin, as well as convincing Dak to have his career worst fantasy game (minus injuries). Jacube gave Rodgers the key to Titty City after his 400 yards and 4 TDs (42 points) led this team to a week 11 win. Jacube remains in the playoff hunt with the victory.

Game of Jones has a streak they'd happily forget, losing their 5th straight game, 91-116 to the GriddleIron. Josh's 30 point showout from QB Kirk Cousins kept this game competitive, but most other spots in this starting lineup fell short of their needed production. Josh will be hoping to get out of this year in 11th place and with a good draft slot.

The DingleJerrys came into week 11 needing a mircale to get a win over the Chubless Yisha. With a starting 4 of Renfrow, Beasley, Darrel Williams (with CEH back) and D. Freeman, you can only home for an insane blowup from everyone to stay competitive. That did not happen, as Jerry earned his 8th loss of the season, losing 80-124. Jerry is fighting to stay out of the 12th spot and hope for a favorable consolation schedule.

The Griddles drop their 2nd straight game to put themselves back in a fight for a playoff spot. Patrick Mahomes came back to life in week 10, scoring more than his last 3 weeks combined, which happens when you throw for 400+ yards and 5 TDs. Joe's team is still beyond stacked, making him the #1 team going forward.

King of the Hill can't stop winning, as he earned his 6th straight win after starting the year 0-4. Austin beat his brother Civil War style, slaughtering Game of Jones 135-84. This team's starting four (Hill, Lamb, Taylor and Fournette) continue to dominate, as the lowest scorer had 15 points while the other 3 had 24+. The core of this team is extremely dangerous on any week, making them a lock for the postseason.

Jimmie's trades pay off quickly, as Dak and Cook each had big games in their week 10 matches. Deebo and Kupp kept carrying the Pigskin, as they total 51 points together in the win over Joe's Iron. AJ Dillon rode pine all year, but he will finally be able to Play with Pigskin in week 11, as Aaron Jones went down with a minor knee injury. These are important weeks upcoming for Jimmie, so everyone will need to be top notch to make them count.

In Yisha's 1st week without his Chubb (traded to Gil prior to week 10), he was only able to make it 79 Miles, which was 5 more than his opponent (Jim and the Twins) made it. Yisha didn't realize how much a good Chubb can boost your Sunday, but he felt it this week, as only Ekeler and Conner could manage more than 10 points. Yisha is in a fight for a playoff spot, and he will not be able to rely on winning games while scoring less than 80 points to make it in.

A nail-biter of a game between the Wolfpack and Titty City ended with Eli Mitchell running out the clock on Monday night for just enough yards to get the win for the Wolves (127-125). This was a back and forth battle, but Ryan played the perfect lineup again, leaving no points on his bench in week 10. Ryan now sits in 1st place with a 40 point lead over the 2nd place team. Ryan continues to find a way to win games, and will likely continue doing so as the season moves on. It can be annoying if you ask me. Right you are Ken, on to #6.

Gil and the Truck welcomed CMC back with open doors, as CMC delivers with a 24 point performance. Gil also rode D. Johnson's 22 points to a 107-73 win over the Toons. Outside of those two, the Truck had nothing else desirable on the menu, as J. Herbs' 15 points were the next highest by 5 points. Gil is on the inside looking out of the playoff picture, but health will need to be removed as a talking point for this team if he wants to remain inside.

Big Jim and the Twins are all about streaking, adding a 2nd loss to their losing streak (74-79 to the Chubbless Wonders). No one would have believed you if you said DJ Moore, Tyler Lockett, AJ Brown and TJ Hockenson would have all combined for 11 points in week 10, but here we are looking back at an 11 point total from those 4 players. Jim's 74 points brings his week 9 and week 10 total points to a whopping 137 points together. This team has some holes to fill and things to figure out if they want to somehow find a way to make the playoffs at this rate.

The Mooney Toons finally employ Darnell Mooney! All is right again. Well not all is right for this team, as they have lost back to back weeks and only scored 73 points in this week's loss to the Tacos. Trevor made a couple of moves prior to the trade deadline, all of which have yet to yield any positive results, but better days are ahead. The Toons are in a battle for a playoff spot, and they will be over the Moon(ey) if Darnell can come in and produce right away.

Jona the Great continues to work his Magic, pulling himself out of a hat and placing himself in 2nd place in the league standings. Despite being the 9th highest scoring team, Jona's squad is winning games, including a week 10 win over the Dingles 117-99. Jona will need to rely heavily on Zeke and the Bills' Allen/Diggs stack if he wants to hold this spot and secure his first playoff berth.

The self-proclaimed Mayor started the waiver wire Wentz over the Discount Double Check Rodgers and lost a heartbreaker to the Wolfpack 125-127. Surprise performances from Michael Carter, Rhamondre Stevenson and the Dallas DST kept Jacube alive in this matchup, but the disappointing QB performance ultimately cost this team the win. Despite being sellers at the deadline after a plague ran through town, Jacube remained in the playoff hunt at 4-5. This loss, however, puts Titty City at the bottom of a very large hill to climb they wish to make it in this year.

A rough 2021 season continued for Game of Jones, as they lost the sibling rivalry game to Austin's Hill 84-135. The Jones' have now scored in the 80s in consecutive weeks; this week largely due to TY Hilton's 1 point and TE Mike Goosicki's zero. Josh was unable to fully unload his roster before the deadline, making him a team that can still win games down the stretch, but 80 points likely won't make it easy.

The Dingles get plucked by Jona the Great (99-117) and fall to 3-7 on the year. Jerry has not scored more than 100 points since week 6, and after selling his squad garage sale style, 100+ points may be a tough accomplishment. It is wild, but the high point in this roster has been backup RB Darrell Williams, who has shown that maybe there is just a CEH issue in Kansas City. At the moment, Jerry is just crossing his fingers and hoping for a big week out of a few players to steal a win, which is never out of the question in fantasy football.

Austin's Hill was twice as large as Joe's in week 9, as he earns a 126-66 win over the Griddles. Despite the Ravens DST scoring less than 1 point, Tyreek and Lamb each scoring less than 6.5 points and Stafford having his first <20 point game of the year, Austin still managed to scofe 126 points on the week. The Hill was built on the RB foundation of Jonathan Taylor (38.4) and newly acquired Joe Mixon (28.55), which is plenty strong enough to get a win in almost any week. Austin looks like he's prepared for a deep playoff run.

In a battle of the top 2 ranked teams, with each team playing their first game after big trade acquistions, Joe bowed to the #1 team and gave Austin an easy 126-66 win. Week 9 was a nightmare week for Joe, as Patrick Mahomes' 13.64 points was the team's 2nd highest score (Najee with 18.75). Joe's trade with the Dingle's will have better days, and when they do, this team will be tough to beat.

Yisha wanted to go Burrow and hide after a p(C)ooper of a game as th e Chubb got rolled over by the Taco Truck in week 9. Joe Burrow and Amari Cooper were decided to take the week off and only contributed a combined 14 points to the cause. Without Nick Chubb's 163 yard, 2 TD performance, this team would have been really rough. However, the thing that causes the most jock itch for this squad is that James Conner's 43 points on the bench would have been enough to earn the win if he had been activated. A big week 10 is upcoming for Yisha, as it may determine the rest of his 2021 season.

Big Jim and his Twins are only in their 50s, but in week 9, they were in their 60s, as Jim lost a pooper of a game to the Magician, 96-63. Jim had 4 players score 7 points, and three more score 6 or less. The 63 points was only achieved by two garbage time drives to give Dak Prescott a usable 22 point week. Most of the Twins were taking a breather from the jock strap this week, so expect a very different outcome in week 10.

Jimmie was a buyer in week 9, acquiring Dalvin Cook from Titty City, and some of Titty City's stank came with him, as Jimmie failed to score 100 pointd in his loss to the Wolfpack (94-115). Any lineup that contains the 2021 version of Carlos Hyde should expect to struggle, and that's exactly what this lineup did. Jimmie is running out of time to be patient for his team to be healthy.

The Wolfpack eat the Pigskin in a low scoring ugly win, 115-96. You could combine 6 weeks of scores for Nyheim Hines (Ryan's week 9 RB 2) and you wouldn't be able to total his week 9 score of 21.65 points, but why wouldn't he do that this week? Ryan got just what he needed in this game from Jefferson, Hurts and Kelce, but he will have a more full roster in week 10, which should be able to keep him as one of the top 3 teams in the league.

Trevor, in his 9th week as the 'Mooney Toons' without employing Darnell Mooney, made the arguably mentally ill decision of starting a declared out WR in DeAndre Hopkins, earning exactly zero points. Trevor was within throwing distance of a win in Titty City after Lamar Jackson's 40% point share of the team's 100 point total. Trevor will certainly need to start active players going forward if he wants to win more games in the future. Right you are Kenny.

Team Taco Truck dangerously kept CMC home from work, despite being healthy, and still ended up with a 136-99 win over Yisha's Chubb. Gil's DST (Patriots) would have been the 2nd highest scoring player on Yisha's roster with 14.04 points against Carolina. Gil also went shopping at Jerry's garage sale and picked up 54 points by acquiring QB Justin Herbert and RB Myles Gaskin (38 and 16 points). This roster still feels very boom or bust heading into week 10.

How do you win a week with a starter scoring zero points and your QB puttin up less than 14 points? You make your opponent's points disappear. That's exactly what the budget Magician did, as he took beat Big Jim's week 8 score and cut it in half for week 9, beating him 96-63. What will the Magic man have in store for us in his week 10 show? Nobody knows the limits of what he can do.

The self-proclaimed Mayor had the shell of his once amazing staff in week 9, and yet he pulled out a win against Trevor's 8-man roster 109-100. Dalvin Cook's replacement, Melvin Gordon, had a great 20 point game with his new team, helping DeVonta Smith and Keenan Allen's 39 points to give the Titties the win. Jacube now sits at 4-5, 10th place, so will he continue to sell or stand pat through the trade deadline?

The basement battle was on between Game of Jones and the DingleJerries, as 11 payed 12 in an expectedly low scoring match. Josh came away as the ultimate loser on this one, getting wiped by Jerry 93-88. Not much to touch on in this game beyond Kirk Cousins' 27 points or Badgley's 8 point kicking performance. Josh will be looking to get a few wins before the season's end to avoid the 12th place finish.

Big Dingles let the Muth Luth in week 9, starting TE Pat Freiermuth, who 43 yards and 2 TDs (19 pts). The big TE game propelled Jerry passed Josh for a big basement win 93-88, earning his 3rd win of the year. Despite being a heavy salesman this year, Jerry's team still has enough power to be competitive week in and week out.

Austin starts the season 0-4, looks for draft pick trades in week 5, and is 4-4 on a 4-game win streak heading into week 9 after a 136-93 win over the DingleJerries. Austin has been relying on the Colts to keep giving the ball to Taylor and Pittman, and they have not disappointed, as the two combined for 208 yards and 3 TDs. Austin went shopping at the family shop and came away with RB Joe Mixon to add to this already stacked roster. This team will be tough to beat going forward.

Joe keeps picking up lucky pennies each week, as he once again finds a way to win a low scoring game. Joe was the 4th lowest score of the week, but was forutnately matched against the lowest score (Ryan) and win 99-69. Joe sits atop the league at 6-2, despite having the 7th highest point total through 8 weeks. Joe did open an early Christmas present from santa, which turns out to be his dad Jerry, as he obtained D. Adams and James Robinson at quite the discount. Joe's team is now an immediate championship contender if everyone can stay healthy.

Jimmie suffers a tough low scoring loss to Trevor and the Moons 115-110. Jimmie was pulled in by the Philadelphia Sirens, and played RB Kenneth Gainwell thinking he was gold, only to find out he was the rock that sunk the ship. Jimmie made a move to acquire Dalvin Cook, in a hope to stop the bleeding in this depleted RB room.

Big Jim and the Twins exploded for 152 points in their win over Game of Jones in week 8. Jim's victory snapped a 4 game losing streak, which brings him back to .500 on the year. Tommy Brady posted another 30+ point game, his 6th on the season. Jim also got big games from bounce back players like Lockett and AJ Brown (21 and 29). This starting roster is still girthy, but will we see it get any thicker come the deadline?

Yisha went into week 8 prepared to sell hos Chubb before week 9. Instead, the Mile long Chubb ran through Titty City and left its citizens with something they won't forget. The 142 points and 4 players with 20+ points week was enough to rejuvenate this program and make them go out and buy WR before the deadline. Yisha will be looking to get above .500 next week.

The Wolfpack showed that the old saying "you're only as strong as your weakest wolf", is indeed very true, as they only manage to put up 69 points on the week. Ryan's highest scorer was Eli Mitchell with 23 points, his 2nd highest had 13 points (Hurts) and he had 5 players score less than 5 points. This was absolutely a week to forget for the Wolves, and there's no doubt a better week is ahead against The Pigskin in week 9.

The Mooney Toons survive an underwhelming week 8 performance, beating the Pigs 115-110. Trevor's 20 points on MNF from Daniel Jones proved to be just enough to earn the win, making this team 5-3 on the year. The Toons head into Titty City a week after the plague hit.

Jona the great Jaworked his Magic and turned 7 players with 13 or less points into a 113-79 win against Gil's Tacos. Jona rode the stallion, Josh Allen, and his 36 points to an easy win. The Magic now sit at 5-3 and 4th place in the standings.

What a difference a week can make in fantasy football. Titty City may have been built on some ancient burial grounds or something, because a plague has been let loose in the streets. After the first domino fell, King Henry having fantasy season ending foot surgery, dominoes just kept falling. The department of player safety reached out to the self-proclaimed Mayor and asked him to save Cook and send him away. Jacube will be trying to ride out the remainder of the season without destroying any other careers.

The Taco Truck served up the kind of special that makes you sick, and that's the kind that has Robert Woods as your top scorer with 20.5 points. That special resulted in only $79 worth of sales in week 8, which turned was a discounted win for the magician (113-79 ). The Truck shipped out some staff to cover some injuries, so we will see if it pays off quickly or not.

Week 8 was a game of boom or bust for the Joneses, as his players either scored 17+ points or less than 9.5 points. This week was unfortunately more bust than boom, resulting in a 152-114 loss to Big Jim. The loss solidified Josh's 2021 direction, as seen by the shipping out of RB Joe Mixon to fellow his Jones, King of the Hill. Josh's team is still competitive and will not be a guaranteed win through the rest of the season.

A sign promoting a week 9 garage sale at the Dingle's house was hung all over the league, and three different teams showed up to the event. Jerry made big moves with 3 clubs, completely blowing up the 2021 roster for better days in 2022.

The self-proclaimed Mayor invinted the budget magicician into Titty City, let him perform and then kicked him out without payment, as Jacube and the Tittitians defeat the Magic 127-106. The Mayor wildly kept both a bye week DST and kicker on his bench, giving his bench a whopping 0.60 points on the week. But you're probably saying, "nobody cares about the bench", and I'd say, "right you are Ken", and neither did Jacube's starters. Jacube had King size games from Rodgers, Henry, Godwin and Pitts, who all 21+ points in week 7. heading into week 8, I'm not sure there's a better starting roster in the league.

Oh how far we've come. Austin is officially one slot away from being the actual King of the Hill, as he comes in at #2 in the rankings after starting the year at the league's #12 spot. Despite being without TE George Kittle and WR Ceedee Lamb, Austin had a 100% hit rate on his starters in week 7, as his lowest score came from kicker Younghoe, who ended the week with 9 points. If this team can continue to put up 80% of this week's production, they will be a tough team to beat on any given week.

With one half of the regular season in the books, big Jim and the Twins have had a tale of two season thus far. Polar opposite records to start and finish the first half, as Jim has now lost 4 straight games after starting the year 3-0. Jim's 104 points were no match for Austin's 150 spot, but the 4th straight loss has to open some concern. WR Tyler Lockett and TE TJ Hockenson have been underperforming for weeks now, as Locket hasn't scored more than than 9 points since week 2, and Hockenson now as 4 games under 10 points. This squad has tons of fire power, but they appear to be falling into the group of team's that needs all their players to hit each week if they want to win games.

The high flying high fiving five game win streak comes to a screeching halt, with a 151-82 loss to the Mooney Toons. Ryan's five game streak was long enough to keep him in first place after the loss, but this week had to scare the Wolfpack a little, as only 3 players had more than 9 points, and more than 50% of the team's production came from Jalen Hurts and Eli Mitchell (49 of 82). Ryan will have his full allotment of players in week 8, which likely means we can expect more of what we saw during the 5 game win streak than in the week 7 loss.

Joe squared off against his pops in week 7 to see who was the better Malak, and Joe came away victorious 121-86. Joe hooked his underperfoming team to the wagon carried by Mike Evans' 3 TDs, Herbert's 19 points and Ja'Marr Chase's 200 yard performance, which double what the rest of the team scored together (and that incuded Patrick Mahomes). Despite having only 3 good games, Joe came away with the win. If Ja'Marr Chase can continue to set records in his rookie season, the Gang may be in for more wins in the coming weeks.

Plays with Pigskin is the name of the newest WR only club in town, as this team continues to find production through the wideouts only. Jimmie had a combined 80 points from his three starting WRs, compared to 18 points from his two starting RBs. The 142-121 win over Yisha's Chubb puts this team above .500 on the year, but they will need some RB help if they want to make waves at the end of the year.

The Mooney Toons went off for the week's highest score, 151, and dominated the league's #1 team by nearly 70 points. Trevor's lowest skill position score was11.25 from the TE, and the highest was from RB Alvin Kamara with 32, which was his 2nd straight game with 30+ points. The Toons were playing reruns, as they started RB Devonta Freeman in the Flex spot, and got 12 sweet throwback points from him. We will see if Trev's semi-stars can continue to perform in week 8.

Yisha's Chubb has a 3 mile long losing streak, as they have now dropped 3 straight games, looking at a 3-4 record heading into week 8. Yisha was without a starting WR and two RBs in Cooper, Chubb and Ekeler, which could have been the difference in this game, as Yish only lost 142-121. The Chubb had big games from Burrow, Metcalf, Conner and Ertz (all scored between 13 and 37 points), but the big games weren't enough to make up for everyone else's stinkers. Yish has been on the bad end of a couple losses, but if his team can get healthy and play at the same time, they are as good as anyone in the league.

Game of Jones got D'Ernested on Thursday night and couldn't come back after getting slapped with that Johnson. Josh had a pretty good week from most of his starters, including another big game from TE Mike Gesicki (19). There is one less Josh on this team after Jacobs went down with a chest injury in week 7. Game of Jones has flashed their potential a few times this year, and if they can fill some holes and put a complete game together, they will win more games than they lose in the future.

$17 for a Taco!? For Gil, the price was worth it, as he paid $17 for RB D'Ernest Johnson in week 7, and came away with 28 points and a win for it. Gil's low spot was TE Tyler Higbee, who only scored 7 points. Gil's bench continues to produce almost zero points each week, so he must be careful with his starters. Gil draws a matchup with the Magic man in week 8, so any outcome is possible for this team.

Jona the Great worked his Magic once again in week 7, pulling and old rabbit ouf of his hat and getting an 18 point game from RB Brandon Bolden (who?). However, the Magic was on a budget after that, as Jona was unable to get a permanent spot in Titty City, losing 127-106. Jona was without most of his props, which were out on bye (Zeke, Diggs, Allen and Waller who had an injury), but he still managed to keep it close. Will week 8 be another Magic show, or will Jona be distracted by Gil's Taco Truck?

DingleJerry was matched up against Joe in a father vs son battle in week 7. Jerry must have felt bad for his boy, as he took it easy on him in week 7, scoring less than 90 points. QB Derek Carr's 24 points was the team's highest score, and only Davante Adams' 17 points came close, as every other player scored less than 8.5 points. This may have just been Jerry having a soft spot for his offspring, or it could be a sign of things to come, as Adams is now out with Covid for week 8. Jerry will need some help if he wants to avoid going 2-6.

Good teams find a way to win while bad teams find a way to lose, and Ryan is an example of the former, as he comes away with a 111-90 win over Yish in the lowest scoring game of the week. Ryan had nothing special from anyone, outside of WR Antonio Brown and QB Jalen Hurts, who scored 21 and 28 points each. Hurts, despite looking like garbage on the real NFL field, has never scored below 25 points this year, making him the #7 fantasy player in the league thus far. Ryan has a tough week 7 bye list, and unfortunately has to pair that with the injuries suffered by Kareem Hunt and Antonio Gibson. Ryan has overcome bigger obstacles before, so it would be no surprise to see this team leave week 7 with a 6-1 record. The only thing that may help the league gain some ground on Ryan, is that Ryan has officialy joined Club 30 and may start to fatigue a bit easier than before. Happy birthday to the Wolfpack of one!

Jimmie hired some cheap entertainment for his week 6 party and got what he paid for, as Jona the Great stole the win away from Jimmie (155-129). Jimmie couldn't have gotten much better results, as there were only 2.7 points left on his bench. Jimmie will need to get some of his injuries taken care of if he wants to get back up in the standings.

Big Jim and the Twins can't stop the bleeding and drop their 3rd loss in as many weeks and find themselves at 3-3 on the year. After starting the year needing an extra large set of pants, Jim has traded the boxers for briefs as he watched his 3-0 start turn to a 3-3 record heading into week 7. This team had a decent amount of good games, but underwhelming showings by DJ Moore and Tyler Lockett sunk this team below the mark against Jerry. It also appears that if Brady doesn't throw for 30+ points, Jim's game become much closer than what we saw early in the season. Week 7 will be another tough test for Jim, when he's matched up against the red hot King of the Hill.

The self-proclaimed Mayor of Titty City finds himself in in 10th place after back to back losses, losing to Josh Jones 152-145 in week 6. Titty City needed a miracle on Monday night to overcome the dud WR performances by his three starters (Godwin, Allen and Smith), which totaled 20 points. The Mayor almost cashed in a favor and got the miracle he needed, as King Henry scored another 3 TDs and 39 points on the week, making it his 3rd straight 30+ point game and 4th week above 30 points this year. Jacube also welcomed staff member Dalvin Cook back with open arms, adding his 26 points coming off the injury. Titty City will be operating short-staffed in week 7, as multiple starters took vacation this week.

Austin built a 167 foot Hill for Gil's Taco Truck to climb, but Gil came up 75 feet short, giving Austin the 167-95 win. Austin has now won 2 straight weeks while playing a man down, as he left his kicker spot wide open in week 6 and his TE slot open in week 5. 30s were wild in week 6, as Austin saw 4 diferent players score 31+ points, including freshly acquired CeeDee Lamb from his opponent. This team has now scored 137+ points in each of the last 3 weeks, making them a team to pay attention to going into week 7.

The Griddleiron Gang continues to be doubted, and they continue to add wins to their record, winning back to back games to improve to 4-2 on the season. Joe is only behind Ryan's Wolfpack in the standings, even though his total points for the year are in the lower half of the league. Joe continues to lean on RB Najee Harris, who stayed in the 20s again in week 6, making that 4 straight weeks with 20+ points. Joe also added fill-in points from RB Khalil Herbert, who benefited from being the only Bears RB left standing and contributed 22 points of his own. This week, Joe will have to rely on some lesser known names, such as Patrick Mahomes, Mike Evans, Ja'Marr Chase and Courtland Sutton, as Najee Harris gets a well-deserved week 7 bye.

Yisha was without his Mile long Chubb in week 6, which led to a loss to the Wolfpack in the week's lowest scoring mathcup (90-111). Yisha's starters mustered up 3 double-digit scores, with the team's highest score coming from RB Hubbard at 15.85 points. It's always tough to lose a game that could have easily been a win, especially when it comes on the back of another loss. Yisha has to overcome injuries and bye weeks in week 7, as he tries to get he Chubb back in the limelight against the Pigskin.

The Mooney Toons relocated to Buffalo in week 6, just in time for their loss to TEN on Monday night. Trevor's starting Bills (Moss, Knox and their DST) combined for a whopping 14 points on Monday night, solidifying their week 6 loss to Joe and the Gang. Trevor was also without his cornerstone RB Alvin Kamara, who was on bye, which proved to be too much to overcome. Trevor will once again be without multiple starters in week 7 due to byes and injuries, so we will see if he can get back above .500 after his match with the #1 Wolfpack.

Josh got back in the Game with his 2nd win of the year, as he was victorious in Titty City (152-145) in the week's highest scoring matchup. Josh's starting lineup dominated from top to bottom, with the exception of WR Chase Claypool, who only managed 3 points on the week.
