This team's trio of RBs (Mixon, Henderson and Jacobs) went off for 73 points, showing that they may be the strongest RB room in the league. Josh won't be hampered by byes in week 7, andhe even has multiple plus matchups, making this team a top score candidate.

DingleJerry fought his was to his 2nd straight win, despite only getting 14 points out of QB Justin Herbs. This team was stuck together through solid performances from nearly every starter, with the fewest coming from flex WR Mecole Hardman at 9.39. After an 0-4 start, Jerry has back to back wins and is pushing his way back into the competition.

Week 6 was one to forget for Gil, as his Taco Truck stalled just over halfway up the Hill, dropping a game to Austin 167-95. On Saturday, in the middle of their matchup, Gil traded away WR CeeDee Lamb to Austin for RB Javonte Williams, which turned into a 24 point negative swing for Gil (Lamb scored 33 to Williams' 9). The nightmare continued, as Gil's bench (possibly for the first time in league history) scored exactly zero points. The only bright spot this week was Kyler's 32 points, but Gil will need some sort of divine intervention if he wants his roster to get/stay healthy amd allow him to be competitive.

Jona the Great strikes again, scoring his season-high 155 points against Jimmie to earn the week 6 win. Jona now sits in 3rd place with a 4-2 record, despite being the 4th lowest scoring team in the league. The Magician clearly has something up his sleeve for each matchup to somehow get a win, so watch out when lined up across from this team, even in week 7 when half his starters are on bye.

For the 1st time this year, we have a new #1 team in the power rankings! The Wolfpack are officially the Alpha Wolf of the league coming off a 176 point, 50 point margin of victory week 5 win over Jona the Great. The only two players on this roster to score less than 15 points in week 5 were the kicker and the DST, while 4 other players scored above 20 points. This roster may have the best boom potential of any team in te league, and without facing any significant bye weeks in week 6, it is likely they continue to boom into week 7.

Big Jim and the Twins are dethroned as the league's top team after dropping their 2nd straight loss, losing 124-137 to Joe. This team was competitive this week thanks to a 5 TD, 48 point week from Tom Brady. RBs Aaron Jones and D'Andre Swift contributed 15 points and 21 points respectively, but every other starting slot score sub-nine points. The single-digit games submarined this team in week 5, but only into the #2 spot. The Twins have brighter days ahead.

Yisha's 148 Mile long Chubb was slapped again on Monday night, this time by Trevor and his 168 points. Yisha and Monday night have had a love-hate relationship for the last 3 weeks, with all three games being decided by wild fantasy performances on Monday night. In week 5, Yisha had a 34 point lead heading into MNF, but waiting for Yisha was Trevor's Lamar Jackson, who scored enough to give Trevor a 20 point win (54 points). Yisha lost his starting QB in week 5, so we will have to see how his team rebounds in week 6.

The self-proclaimed Mayor decided that youth has no place in Titty City, as he left rookie TE Kyle Pitts and rookie WR DeVonta Smith on the bench, and both outscored their veteran starters by good margins. Adding salt to the wound, Jacube got beat by a team starting a TE who was on firmly on the IR. Titty City was built on dominating RBs, so Jacube needs his stud, Dalvin Cook, back in the lineup if he wants to get back to .500.

Trevor went to bed during haltime on Monday night thinking he was heading into week 6 at 2-3. He woke up Tuesday morning to Lamar Jackson's 54 point second half miracle performance and a 3-2 record. Hopkins, Kamara and Knox all helped to set the table for a Monday night miracle, scoring 19, 30 and 22 points respectively. With bye weeks starting, we will see if Trevor can fill the holes in his roster to keep putting up 170 points each week.

Jimmie got the week 5 win, but he lost Saquon in the process. Jimmie has now lost all 3 of his first 3 picks to injuries for at least one week in this early season. After losing Saquon with only 1 point to show for week 5, Jimmie needed some help, which he got in the form of fill-in RB Mattison, who scored another 26 points while Dalvin Cook was out. The Piggies saw an explosion out of big money Mark Andrews, who scored a career high 38.2 points against the Colts. Jimmie falls int he rankings this week until we can see if he can tighten up the laces on the Pigskin that appears to be falling apart.

Team Taco Truck was without their head chef, CMC, once again this week, proving to be difficult to overcome, as they lose 124-165 to DingleJerry. Gil got off to a hot start on TNF with Robbie Woods slaying the Seahawks for 150 yards and 23 points, and Patterson scoring 18 points across the pond. However, Gil popped another tire in RB CEH, who went down with a rough knee injury on SNF after only scoring 4 points. Gil will need to bubble wrap his RBs heading into week 6, as another injury could strand this Truck in unpleasant territories.

Austin said being King of the Hill is nothing without a little adversity along the way, so he decided to put himself behind the 8 ball and start a TE who was on the IR (also, watering?), despite having a healthy TE on the bench. On top of empty TE slot, Austin was down on Monday night by 47.8 points with only Johnny Taylor and Hollywood Brown to play. Austin came back from the depths and won by 20 points over the Mayor with 32+ point games from both players. This unconventional win is the first win of the year for the Hill, bringing them to a 1-4 record through 5 weeks.

The Griddle Gang turn a less-than-average Mahomes game (26 points) into a 137-124 win over #1 ranked Big Jim. The gamble on RB Najee Harris in the 1st round of this year's draft continues to pay off big time for Joe, as Najee has scored 18+ points in 4 out of 5 weeks this year (25 in week 5). The gamble on rookie WR Ja'Marr Chase also continues to pay off, as Chase has 5 TDs through 5 games and 3 games over 21 points. The Gang also capitalized on his opponent's QB TDs by being the recipient of 2 of them late in the game (Mike Evans had 2 TD passes from Jim's Tom Brady). If these rookies continue to perform, watch out for Joe in the coming weeks.

The Dingles Fought their way onto the board for the firt time in the 2021 season, taking down Gil's Taco Truck 165-124. Jerry spent a bunch of singles early at the food Truck, with 5 of his 9 starters scoing in single digits this week, but he saved his big bills for last. Jerry had a combined 103 points from Herbert (54.57), Adams (34.35) and Robinson (24.75), with Adams having a career high 206 yards. Jerry came into some good luck going forward, rostering the handcuff to CEH, who went down with a significant knee injury on Sunday. Jerry's arrow may finally be pointing away from the Dingleberries.

The bugdet magician turned a 122 point week into a 176-122 loss to Ryan's Wolfpack. Jona continued to rely on massive games from Josh Allen, who scored 45 points for the 2nd time this year, and Zeke, who has now scored 19+ points in the last 4 games. Jona will need to Work som Magic and get some better games out of the rest of his squad if he wants to get some more wins. We wil see if the $55 spent on Giants' RB Devontae Booker will pay off in week 6.

Game of Jones drops his 2nd straight game, landing at 1-4 heading into week 6. Josh's RBs stood out in week 5, combining for 48 of the team's 92 points. Josh had to be feeling good after Henderson's massive TNF game against the Seahawks, as well as seeing Jimmie's star RB Saquon Barkley leave the game after scoring 1.1 points. Unfortunately for Josh, Giants' WR Kenny G also left the game after scoring less than Barkley (0.00), not allowing Josh to take advantage of the injury. Josh is in the tough position of having to throw darts at which players will boom each week and which players will give almost nothing.

Big Jim and te Twins are in uncharted waters here with being ranked the #1 team in the league for the 5th straight week, all while losing a game in which they scored 100 points. Jim played a DST that scored negative points, possibly the only one to do so in a starting lineup this year, and combined that with an output from Brady that was just more than 1/3 of his weekly average in the previous 3 weeks. The Big Jim got patted on the Twins in week 4, each and every time WR/RB Cordarrelle Patterson caught the ball (caught 5 passes, 3 for TDs). This roster is still filled with talent and should likely bounce back in week 5.

Titty City may be located in some sort of alternate universe. A universe where players like Keenan Allen, Chris Godwin and Dalvin Cook are all outscored by Tyler Bass, the high flying kicker from Buffalo, NY. The self-proclaimed Mayor called on the likes of Dalton Schultz and DeVonta Smith to contribute 15+ points each to try and help out Derrick Henry, Aaron Rodgers and Tyler Bass' 72 point total. Titty City is looking as strong as ever, as they try to get above .500 in week 5.

Plays with Pigskin was playing in a heavyweight matchup with King of the Hill, as both teams were throwing haymakers back and forth in week 4's highest scoring game (159-137). Jimmie felt down and out after Tyreek Hill scored his 3rd TD of the day on a 44 yard pass, giving him 186 yards and league high 46.35 points. fortunately for the Pigskin, Deebo, Saquon and Scary Terry all had late game heroics and scored multiple TDs of their own (each had 2 TDs). Will this roster be able to keep up the high scoring trend in week 5 against Josh's Game of Jones?

Yisha was down and out all week after a brutal week 3 loss that he gave away to Zeke on Monday night, but Yish gained some experience and used it in his week 5 matchup against Joe's Griddles. Yisha was down in week 5, 117.86-90.14, needing a massive 27.73 point game from Austin Ekeler to earn the victory. Ekeler got the 27 points and added 4 more for good measure, as the Chubb celebrated hard for their 121-117 win over Joe. Yisha will try to earn his 4th win of the early season against Trevor and the toons next week, and he added a little extra fire power with (John) Madden Baker making his debut this week!

The Wolfpack get out to an early season 3-1 record, after hanging on to the win against Game of Jones this week (112-107). Ryan has been on the Hunt all year, as Kareem continues to return nothing but value on his 5th round draft cost, scoring another 18 points against the Vikings. Jalen keeps hitting opponents where it Hurts, racking up 35 more points on 434 total yards and 2 TDs, showing he too was worth his 8th round draft capital. This team only got stronger this week, as Ryan gained backup RB Damien Williams to his starting roster with David Montgomery missing the next 4-5 weeks. The Wolves look poised to keep devouring their opponents.

Trevor's losing streak jumps to 2 games after losing on Monday night to Jona te Great 133-130. Trevor had to watch score just enough points on Monday night to overcome the 11 point lead Trevor had. This team was Robbed by their kicker, Robbie Gould, who left early in the game with zero points to show for his efforts. The Toon's biggest question is who will fill in for the loss of RB David Montgomery, who went down with a knee injury after scoring 2 TDs and rushing for 106 yards. Time will tell if the RB options will be able to cover the points lost by DMont.

If there was a question of who is the real King of the Hill, Tyreek made sure to answer it in week 4, shredding the Eagles DBs for 186 yards and 3 TDs (46 point week). Matt Stafford played well (25 points), while Johnny Taylor and Lenny Fournette each contributed around 20 points. The real struggle for Austin in this one was the less than 14 points totaled by OBJ, Kittle and Beasley. This type of explosion is possible any week with this roster, and if Austin's guys are starting to come into shape, this team will be one to watch out for.

The Taco Truck sent out for some fresh meat and they came back with some old, but still delicious, Patties in Cordarrelle Patterson by way of 39 savory points. CPatt's 5 catch - 3 TD performance more than made up for Aiyuk, Lamb and Higbee combining for less than 12 points. Gil will need to scrape of the burnt pieces of his roster and prepare next week's menu if he wants to get to 4-1 through 5 weeks.

If there's a team you want to be mad at in the league, it has to be Jona the Great, who consistently uses his Magic to win close or low scoring games. The Magic are 3-1 despite having the 3rd lowest total points in the league. Yet, Jona somehow gets his guys to play at the right time, including this week's 24 point game by Zeke, 22 point game by Corey Davis and even the 11 point game by kicker Matt Prater. You can't fault Jona though, as he only left 2.35 points on the bench, starting just about the perfect lineup. We will see if Jona the Great can keep this Magic show running into week 5.

Joe and the Gang have to wipe the Griddle clean and start it up fresh next week, after losing a tough one to Yish 121-117. Najee Harris has been living up to his draft hype thus far, scoring another 21 points this week, as he continues to be a focal point of this team. Mahomes scored more than 40 points for the 2nd time in 4 weeks, carrying this team to a competitive loss. Joe will need some ancillary pieces to step up and carry some of the load if Joe wants to stop this losing streak at 2.

Game of Jones battles back on MNF, but comes up just short to the Wolfpack, going down 112-107. Josh Jacobs needed to outscore Mike Williams by jsut 5 more points for Josh to be sitting at 2-2 instead of 1-3, but instead ended with a disappointing 9 point night. Kirk Cousins' 13.32 point performance is the 3rd QB outing for Josh that ended in less than 14 points (out of 4 weeks), with this week being the highest. If Josh can get over some of these injuries and find a QB to score some points, Game of Jones will likely start adding some W's to their record.

The Dingleist of Jerries ran out of Gas in Titty City and were forced to take a pitstop at the 0-4 exit. Jerry was feeling good after watching big games come from Diontae Johnson (22.7), James Robinson (23.4) and Noah Fant (14.35), but quickly became unhappy after seeing an uninjured Myles Gaskin touch the ball two times for 3 yards (0.5 points) against the Colts. If Jerry could have only stolen a few of Tyreek Hill's 5,000 yards or just one of his 15 TDs, and given it to Hardman, Jerry may have been able to pull out a win. Jerry will need to find a map if he doesn't want to have to stop at exit 0-5 next week.

Big Jim squared off against the #2 power ranked team in week 3, and held on to get the win over Jacube 112-108. Jim got pooped on by a couple of injuries to AJ Brown and Tyler Lockett, which left him with 5.75 combined points on the week. However, the Twins overcame the poop games by another huge 34 point showing from Brady (his lowest of the year), and 18+ point games from Swift, A Jones and DJ Moore. Jim will have to plug in another player to cover the temporary loss of AJ Brown, but he is still firmly the #1 ranked team in the league.

The Mooney Toons were waiting for namesake Darnell Mooney to get traded and help them secure a win in week 3, but no trade happened and the Toons secured a loss. Trevor had 6 of his 9 starting positions stay below the double-digit mark, and the highest score on the team was Alvin Kamara's 23 points. If Trevor had started the real Arizona WR1 in Christian Kirk, along with Buffalo's true RB1 in Zach Moss, Trevor would have taken this game 121-119. Regardless, this team sits at 2-1 and looks to bounce back in week 4 against the budget magician.

The Piggies are on the board with their first W of the young season, plucking those Dingles 156-125. Jimmie had 2 players get outscored by the kicker, who scored 9 points, but the rest of the team more than made up for those weak games by scoring the remaining 130 points. Copper Kupple of TDs stayed hot in week 3, scoring another 2 TDs and putting up 27 fantasy points. Rental RB Mattison looked like Dalvin Cook out there on his way to 24 points of his own. Even Saquon rejoined the fantasy world with 21 points and a TD. This team has plenty of fire power, so it will come down to execution for the Pigskin.

Yisha's Mile long Chubb got stomped on hard by Kareem Hunt and MNF in week 3. Yisha had a great head start on the week with big games from his two keepers DK Metcalf and Austin Ekeler (21 and 22 points each), however, this years 1st round selection, Nick Chubb, was dominated by his backup's monster performance (Kareem Hunt with 27 points). Even with the disappointing Chubb, Yisha went into Monday night with Amari Cooper and Miles Sanders having a 9 point lead against Zeke. Knowing the week 3 outcome, you know Zeke outscored Cooper and Sanders 28-12, personally handing Yish his first loss of the year 114-106. Yish will hope for better Mondays ahead, as he prepares for Joe in week 4.

The self-proclaimed Mayor bans MNF and any Eagles' gear from Titty City after losing a close matchup to Jim and the Twins 112-108. Jacube needed just 8 points from Eagles' rookie WR DeVonta Smith to earn the week 3 win, but instead ended up with 4.55 points and a loss on Monday night. Jacube was left without RB stud Dalvin Cook, and his replacement in Latavius Murray, was no Dalvin Cook, scoring just 4 points against the Lions. The Mayor can't have 4 of his starters get outscored by the kicker in week 4 if he wants to bring home a win to Titty City.

Ryan showed up and showed out in week 3, climbing to the top of the Hill and planting his flag as the King with a 169-101 victory over Austin. Ryan had 1 player score single digits (Allen Robinson had 3 points), and 5 with more than 20 points. The Wolfpack wasn't looking for any alpha wolf this week, and instead capitalized on the beta wolf, as Kareem Hunt and Mike Williams, both the #2 on their teams, combined for just under 60 points. This is the potential this team has, so lookout when matched up against the Wolves.

The Griddle was gifted with multiple uncommon presents in week 3, but Joe still came up a bit short of a win, losing 114-106 to the Taco Truck. Joe was gifted with a 2 quarter game from CMC, an NFL record kicking performance from Justin Tucker and 19 targets to a RB in Najee Harris all in week 3. Unfortunately for Joe, 4 of his 9 starting slots combined for 14 points. Even tougher was watching Ja'Marr Chase shred the Steelers defense for 2 TDs. This team could be sitting at 3-0 rather than 2-1, so they will remain in the middle of the pack.

The Taco Truck got back to their winning ways with the help of some unlikely cooks. Head chef Kyler Murray scored 22 points, which is half of what he had been scoring in weeks 1 and 2. Gil called on the Arizona DST, Kicker Chase McLaughlin, RB Sony Michel and TE Tyler Higbee to combine for 50 points this week and carry the team to a victory. Despite the win, the Truck blew a flat and may be stuck in one spot for a while, as CMC went down with a muli-week injury. If Gil wants to stay in the W column, he will need to fill the massive gap CMC leaves behind on any roster.

Game of Jones let Captain Kirk lead this team into battle and out with a victory, taking down the Toons 119-93. Josh had to watch Brandin Cooks score nearly 18 bench points on Thursday night, and just hope that better things were ahead. Luckily for Josh, he didn't need better things, as Trevor's 93 points did the work for him. Game of Jones will look to have more than a couple players have good games at the same time in their week 4 battle with Ryan's red hot Wolfpack.

King of the Hill looked more like King of the Bench in week 3, leaving 22 points on the bench, as the starters flooded the lineup with single digit games. At least Austin can feel a little better knowing that even with those 22 points, he still would have been stomped by Ryan 169-123. This team's bright spot remains to be QB Matthew Stafford, who scored nearly 40% of this team's total points with 38.42 out 101.61. Austin will need more boom games from his stars if he wants to get into the win column.

Jona the Great, the league's budget magician, was practicing the dark arts this week, as he pulled out an incredible Monday night victory from his hat, beating yisha 114-106. Jona used his Magic to earn a win with 7 players scoring 10 points or less, and 64% of his weekly total coming from Josh Allen (45 points) and Zeke (28 points). This was truly a reminder that fantasy football is wild and unpredictable. Unless you're Jona the Great, then you know you've got tricks up your sleeve for any situation.

Jerry finds himself and the Dingles tucked deep into the backside of the league, sitting at 0-3 to start the season. Despite the 0-3 start, this team has progressively gotten better each week, scoring 86, 101 and 125 points in weeks 1-3 respectively. As the Dingles' score has increased each week, so has DAdams', who has scored 10 points more than the previous week each time this year. Jerry finally got the 2020 version of James Robinson, who scored more than both of his week 1 and week 2 games combined (25 points). If Jerry can keep progressing and forward and maintain some of these big games, he will come up from the basement sooner than later.

Big Jim and his Big Twins have only gotten bigger through the first two weeks of the season. Jim remains the #1 ranked team in the league after dropping 177.39 points to earn the highest score of week 2. The Twins dangled three 30+ point guys and three more 11+ point guys in front of Jimmie's face this week, crushing any hopes he had of starting the year 1-1. Between Tom Brady and Aaron Jones, AKA Jim's Big Twins, this team had a 9 TD lead on the week. Jim's team is rock solid while also having the ability to bust through any ceiling out there.

The self-proclaimed Mayor welcomed Gil's Taco Truck and all its scandals into Titty City with open arms, as he knew Gil would be no match for the highest power in Titty City. We learned in week 2, that Titty City has highest rank in power is actually King of Titty City, which is held by none other than King Derrick Henry himself. Henry's royal explosion of 53.2 points (237 total yards and 3 TDS) was nearly 5 times as many points as he scored in week 1. Jacube didn't feel that Henry was enough, so he called on Aaron Rodgers to score 16x as many points as he scored in week 1, for a 33 point performance. The City is filled with superstar talent, so expect Jacob to continue dominating in the coming weeks.

The big Darnell Mooney fan moves to 2-0 on the season, after taking advantage of a rough week 2 by King of the Hill, winning 124-96. Just under 1/3 of Trevor's weekly points came from Lamar Jackson's 40 point RB performance (107 yards and 2 TDs). Trevor had good-great weeks from everyone except Kamara, who only managed 5.8 points against the Panthers. Trevor will try to stay undefeated as he matches up with Game of Jones in week 3.

The Josh V Josh matchup ended with on Chubb coming out on top, with Yisha taking it 117-101. Yisha ended the week with 4 starting skill positions getting outscored by their DST, which scored 10.56 points, but he still managed to get the week 2 victory. Russell Wilson, Nick Chubb and Austin Ekeler carried this team to the win, scoring 70 of the team's 117 points. Fortunately, The Mile long Chubb is sitting at 2-0 after this week's flop, which only makes them more dangerous with their high potential. The question in the next few weeks will be if star WR Amari Cooper's health will leave a hole in this starting lineup.

Another week, another loss for the Pigskin. Despite the 0-2 record, this roster has shown a ton of potential, as long as enough guys decide to perform well at the same time. Jimmie ended week 2 with the 4th highest score in the league, but was unfortunately matched up with the league's top scorer (Big Twins) in the highest scoring game of the week (177-138). Cooper Kupp may have been the man behind the curtain pulling the strings on the Matthew Stafford trade, because since his arrival, Kupp has 16 catches, 271 receiving yards and 3 TDs through two weeks. If Jimmie's boom potential can be helped along with some steady ancillary performances, this team can do some damage.

Ryan and his Wolfpack have a new alpha wolf, and his name is Travis Kelce, who has now scored 48 points through two weeks (24.1 & 23.9). Ryan earned a win over Jerry's Dingles in a workman-like fashion, with no super exciting blow-up games by anyone outside of Kelce's standard 20+ points. The Wolfpack had a 13 point win margin, but could have had quite the spread in this one had Rondale Moore or Mike Williams been activated. Ryan's roster can win with average performances and still has the explosiveness to be the top scoring team any week, making him a top 6 team heading into week 3.

Gil's Guatemalan Taco Truck be serving up scandal specials each week this year, get em while they hot! Despite being over the league's 53-man roster limit, this franchise was unable to capitalize on its extra bodies, falling to 1-1 on the season with a 158-128 loss in Titty City. The Taco Truck is running on front wheel drive only, as Kyler Murray and CMC are dragging this team to competitive games, combining for more than half of the team's production this week (68.85 points). Gil will look to get some bigger games from his other starters and distance himself from IR-gate in a week 3 matchup with Joe and the Gang.

Joe and the Gang saw their ranking and said, "12th? Wait and see? Watch this.", then proceeded to slap the rankings with 146 points and the 3rd highest score of the week, oh and starting the year 2-0. Joe made the great managerial decision to not buy into the Ty'son Williams week 1 hype, and bench him for WR Courtland Sutton, who went off for 159 yards and 21 points without a TD. Mahomes did Mahomes (33 points), and the Gang was filled in by great games from Evans (23), Chase (14), Najee (18) and Tonyan (13). If these players continue to hit, The Griddle is only getting warmed up.

Game of Jones joins the defeated group of losers starting the year at 0-2, after falling to Yisha 117-101. Josh was hit with the early out designation for RB Josh Jacobs, but lucky for him, he already had the backup in Kenyan Drake. Not so lucky was the fact that Kenyan Drake was barely the backup for some reason, and Josh had to watch Pine Master Tony Pollard stack up points on his bench. Josh had good weeks from Cooks, Ridley and Henderson, but it wasn't enough to overcome the $9.99 sale that Winston threw out there, completing only 13 passes for 111 yards, and two of those completions were to the Panthers. Josh will look to earn his first win of the year, when he matches up against Trevor and the Toons in week 3.

Jona the Great worked his Magic and made is undefeated season disappear, losing generously to the Girddleiron 146-99. Jona's Bills stack combined for more than 1/3 of the team's total points this week (36/99), but the duo was only slightly helped along by Zeke's 19 points and Juju's surprising 14 points. The worry for this team is that the bench, which had a high score of 9.9 points, will not be able to help out the starters when needed. The Magic needs is stars to act like stars, or another loss could be pulled out of the hat in week 3.

Austin went into week 2 looking to find who was the King of the Hill, and it appears that the Tampa DST might be the true hilltopper, scoring a DST high of 16.58 points. Stafford was serviceable and Hollywood was a surprise stud, but a bunch of poop filled in the rest of the starting lineup. Austin can have the boom games, but when the bust games come, this is what it looks like.

Big Dingles fought his way to a week 2 101-114 loss against the Wolfpack. Jerry got to enjoy watching Davante Adams shred defenses for his team for the first time this year (8 catches for 121 yards), but it unfortunately came in a week when Jerry had to watch everyone else on his team do little to nothing exciting. Jerry's RB situation is one to monitor, as Robinson and Gaskin are both struggling to get going so far in the 2021 season. If WR Diontae Johnson's final play injury lingers, along with the struggling RBs, this team could struggle in the coming weeks.

Big Jim came into week 1 as the #1 ranked team, and he showed his Twins to Ryan and the Wolfpack, winning the week's 2nd highest scoring game 156-138. Jim overcame a 3.7 point pooper from 1st round RB Aaron Jones, by huge games from Brady (36), Lockett (26), Swift (24) and Hockenson (23). The #1 overall rank is a tough place to stay, but Jim is strapped into the #1 position again going into week 2.

Yisha's Chubb went on for 165.66 Miles in week 1, as they proved that the biggest Chubb is in fact the King of the Hill. Yisha's starters did exctly what they were drafted to do, as every positional player scored no less than 11 points on the week and two players scored more than 34 points. This team is scary on paper, and will be a dominating threat all year if these stats continue.

The self-proclaimed Mayor gets Titty City off to an 0-1 start for the 2021 season, losing a MNF nail-biter of a matchup 108-105 to Joe's Gang. Despite the relatively low scoring loss, Jacube has a lot to be happy about in his team's week 1 performance. The Mayor had 5 of 7 positional starters score in the double-digits, including two 20+ games from Chris Godwin and Dalvin Cook. Had it not been for Aaron Rodgers giving the Saints a massive discount double check of 2.82 points for his week 1 stats, Titty City would be sitting at 1-0 instead of 0-1. There is too much fire power on this roster to assume week 1 was prescriptive of the rest of the season.

Trevor is apparently a big fan of Yisha's team. His team name is based on a player on Yisha's team, and he tried to copy his gameplan to score the highest points on the week, falling just less than 8 points behind Yisha for the week high. Trevor had a handful of 20s in week 1, with all 5 of his top starting skill positions scoring 20+ points. This week was a walk in the park for Trevor, as those 5 players alone would have won this matchup 104-86. This Toon squad has this type of potential each week and will be a problem for anyone matched up against it.

Team Taco Truck retained head chef QB Kyler Murray from their 2020 staff after giving him a round 3 raise, but the decision paid off big in week 1, as Murray dropped a 40 pound Taco on Jimmie's Pigskin. The truck got contributions from Lamb and CMC (21 & 27 points) to help lift the team to their first win of the season. Gil will be looking for more help from the rest of his staff heading into Titty City for their week 2 matchup with the Mayor.

New year, new team, same result. Jimmie's week 1 team did its best 2020 impression, and they were quite convincing, as all but one player significantly underperformed their expecations. However, if this were a bench points league, Jimmie would have dominated this matchup, after leaving 48 points on the bench. Plays With Pigskin's week 1 was a fart that they need to shove out a window.

Ryan came into week 1 ranked as the #10 team, but left week 1 with a top 5 score (138.77). Ryan gambled on QB Jalen Hurts in the 8th round of the 2021 draft, and that gamble paid off in week 1 to the tune of 36 points. The Wolfpack also received 24 point games from veterans Antonio Brown and Travis Kelce. This roster was solid from top to bottom (minus the DST, which scored -0.68 points), but it was matched up with a top 3 scoring team in Jim's Twins. Ryan has favorable matchups again in week 2, giving him a great opportunity to repeat this week's score.

Jona the Great used some of his Magic to pull a win out of his hat, after his RBs combined for just less than 9 points, winning 114-111 over Game of Jones. The Magic were saved by huge wees from Corey Davis and Darren Waller, who combined for 202 yards, 3 TDs and 47.70 points this week. The Allen to Diggs combo didn't hurt, but it certainly underwhelmed, going for a combined 35.50 points. Jona's team still has plenty of studs, but their biggest concern is losing starting RB Raheem MostHurt for around 8 weeks. IF Jona can use some trickery to fill this RB hole, he will reappear higher in the rankings.

Game of Jones fought hard in a week 1 battle with Jona's Magic, but sadly got Wallerussed on MNF, and fell 114-111. MNF was a back and forth battle with Josh Jacobs and Darren Waller trading TDs, and both ended up with great nights, but Jacobs came up 4 points short of Waller, which proved to be the difference in this one. However, Josh had to be happy just to be in this game on Monday night, after getting hosed by TE Mike Goosicki's 0 catch, 0 yard line in week 1. Combined with his TE's zero, Game of Jones' Matt Ryan/Calvin Ridley stack only reaching 18 points was a deadly mix. Not all bad news though for this team though, as Josh's RBs scored a whopping 64 points this week, which was the highest RB total of any team. If/when the rest of this team puts a full game together, they will be winning more than losing.

King of the Hill saw his week 1 ranking of #12 scoffed and said, "Tyreek Hill never belongs in the basement". Then he followed that up by using Hill's 197 yards and 1 TD (35) points to put up a 134 point week. Austin fell short to the highest scoring team in week 1 (165-134), but would have beaten half the league had he been macthed up with them. Austin was led by Matt Stafford's 33 points, and was helped along by Hollywood Brown's 17 and Johnny Taylor's 18 points. With Hill, and now Stafford with the Rams, This team has the potential to have 60 points in the bag to start any week, making them dangerous if the ancillary pieces pick up the pace.

Oh boy, Jerry spent week 1 trying to untangle the dingleberries from his backside instead of scoring fantasy points. Jerry's QB, Justin Herbs, was one of only three players to score double-digit points this week, and he was the highest with 18.13 points. This team's nightmare week was riddled with low-scoring games and wrong side blowouts, but it still has to be concerning to score only 86 points in the season opener. Jerry will look to bounce back against the Wolfpack in week 2, and the rankings will be waiting to see if it's possible before Jerry climbs any higher than this.

Not often do you see a team come out of a win and still drop in the rankings, but week 1 raised some questions for the ranking committee about this roster. Only 2.5 players had a notable week, which were Patrick Mahomes' 41 point thrashing of the Browns, Robby Anderson's 57 yard TD catch, and the 49ers posting the 2nd highest DST score of the week with 10.16 points. Even with Mahomes outscoring double A-ron Rodgers by 39 points, Joe's team squeeked out a win by only 3 points. Joe did have some breakout games on his bench in Ty'son Williams and Ja'Marr Chase (18.55 & 21.25) in their first NFL games, but this roster will need to be a wait and see team for now.

Week 1 rosters are in, and Big Jim placed his Twins right on everyone's heads, as he sits atop the week 1 power rankings for the first time in his career. Jim is coming off a 12th place finish, so this is truly a rags to riches story. It will be interesting to see what he does with this opportunity, but Jim's starters are some of the biggest superstars in the league. #1 comes with a lot of responsibility, so embrace the heat!

4 more years! 4 more years! The self-proclaimed Mayor has re-elected himself to another term as Mayor of Titty City, despite the 8th place finish in 2020. The Mayor must have done some under the table bribes this offseason to come away with this roster for Titty City. The combination of King Henry and Dalvin Cook at RB is almost enough to not even care that Aaron holdout Rodgers is at QB, or that Keenan Allen and Chris Godwin are the starting WRs. Jacube has all the tools to be a great team this year, but can the Mayor actually come through for his loyal Titties?

Drafted #7 now he here. And ready to climb, I might add. Yisha and his Mile-long Chubb are ready to slap teams around this year with their superstar starting lineup. QB Russell Wilson stacked with WR DK Metcalf is going to be deadly if Seattle "lets Russ cook" again, and even if they don't, Yisha still has RBs Austin Ekeler and Nick Chubb along with WR Amari Cooper to pick up the slack. If the Chubbs can stay healthy, this team will finish well above its #3 ranking.

Trevor is entering the 2021 season looking to avenge the death of 2020 season (his worst finish - 9th), which was the first time Trevor missed the playoffs in 5 seasons. Trevor didn't get his draft board wet once as he was sprinting back and forth from the pool to make his draft picks, because Trevor didn't even need to look at the rankings to know who he wanted. And with that Wild West approach, Trevor built himself a top-4 team, which is lead by QB Lamar Jackson and followed up stud WRs an RBs. Trevor looks built to find his way back into the playoffs in 2021.

With the 1st pick in the 2021 RBB Draft, Team Taco Truck selects, CMC, THE league-winning RB. You don't build a strong house with only one block, but Gil's house is looking pretty strong with CMC as the foundation. Gil has already been dealing with some injuries (CEH's ankle), and unfortunately lost a breakout RB in JK Dobbins to an ACL tear. However, Gil was fortunate to have already had RB Gus Edwards waiting for his time to shine and plenty of star pieces around his starting lineup to remain a top-5 team heading into week 1.

One hand and one finger later, here we are at #6 in the week 1 power rankings. For me, and likely for you, Jonah and the Tuna snuck into the top 6 teams under the radar. Magicians are known for their ability to be tricky, and this is no exception, as Jona is likely to be sneaky good all year after pulling off a trade that produced the scary Josh Allen/Stefon Diggs stack. Jona's bench is something that he will hopefully not have to dip into, but with a TE like Darren Waller, and RBs like Zeke and Mostert, Jona will likely be able to handle teams without glancing at his bench. The Magic is hoping to finish the season above 10th place for the first time in their short RBB career.

New year, new team, new name as Jimmie tries to shake off the stank of back-to-back 11th place finishes. When you live in the blue tent, all you know is how to draft players that live in the blue tent, which is exactly what Jimmie did when he drafted Barkley, Carson and Julio in his fors 3 picks. If this team can somehow stay healthy, which is almost impossible when you pay rent at the Blue Tent Inn, they look like they can compete as they seem good on paper. Time will tell what 2021 holds for those who Play with Pigskin.

Jerry, RBB's #3 all time ranked manager, comes in at #8 in 2021's week 1 rankings. The Dingles have the making of a top-3 team, but it feels more like a "wait and see" situation for now. Jerry will be leaning heavily on the NFL's best WR in Davante Adams, while he waits to see if RBs James Robinson and Myles Gaskin are the real deal in the NFL. If everything comes together and QB Justin Herbert continues his domination from his rookie season, the Dingles will be competing for spots well above his 8th place ranking.

Josh has always been a fan of the underdog story, so here is his chance to be the star once again, as he comes in at #9 to start the 2021 season. Josh stacked his stud WR Calvin Ridley with QB Matt Ryan, which could prove to be a lethal combo early on this year. Game of Jones wasn't playing around when he gambled on players like RBs Darrell Henderson (aka Darnell Anderson), Joe Mixon and Josh Jacobs, who are all coming off interesting years and head into the 2021 season with less-than-clear situations. Game of Jones doubled-down on that gamble with WRs Chase Claypool, Brandin Cooks, TY Hilton and Michael Thomas, who all came into the 2021 season with question marks surrounding them. Bet big to win big, and if these gambles pay off, Josh will once again be playing for an RBB title.

First to worst(ish)??? Ryan is entering the 2021 season as the reigning champion and the only 2-time champion, so he should be ranked #1 right? WRONG! Ryan is a great manager, who will likely do great things with this roster, but for now, we need to see what players like Jalen Hurts, Antonio Brown, WIll Fuller V and Kareem Hunt will be able to do in the 2021 season. Starting at 10th in the rankings leaves Ryan with some work to do to defend his title and will likely smash this 10th place ranking, as Ryan is sitting on a 100% playoff appearance rate throughout his RBB career.

Two hands and one finger later, here we are at #11 in the 2021 week 1 power rankings. Joe grabbed his Griddles and drafted RB Najee Harris with the 8th overall pick in the 2021 draft with hopes of him becoming a true league-winning RB. Joe filled in his roster with high WR talent in Mike Evans, Robby Anderson and up-and-comer Laviska Shenault, and the half-billion dollar man, QB Patrick Mahomes. The Gang has some lottery ticket players, like RB Michael Carter, WR Ja'Marr Chase, WR Courtland Sutton and QB Trevor Lawrence, and if these guys hit, Joe's roster will be looking stacked sooner than later.

During the offseason, Austin was still coming down from the high of his best finish in his RBB career (4th) and his first postseason appearance. Austin shocked the league when he traded away the value of RB Darrell Henderson to Josh, and then shocked the league again when chose to keep TE George Kittle over the #3 overall pick RB Alvin Kamara. Austin's squad has a good mix of studs, role players and lottery tickets, which could be the exact combination you need to win in this league. Austin literally has nowhere to go but up from this 12th place ranking, so I would espect to see smaller numbers next to his name in the coming weeks.

2022.notes: Look who is back at #1! The 2x RBB champion is back at the #1 spot for the first time this season, after a huge 143 - 82 win over Game of Jones. The win, and a Trevor loss, secured the round 1 bye for Ryan, making his path to a 3rd championship one game easier. The Wolves have eaten off their weaker Wolves and made the Pack as strong as it can be heading into the playoffs, with his WRs healthy and dominating. Paired with a top 3-5 QB and boom RB games, Ryan appears to be unstoppable. For reference on how good this team is and has been, Ryan has only scored less than 106 points once this season, and that was back in week 2. Ryan's 121 average score is 3rd behind Jimmie's 122 and Jacob's 129.

The self-proclaimed Mayor has Titty City bouncing after the heavyweight KO of DingleJerry 148 - 132 in week 13. Jacube was hitting on every level, playing the perfect lineup (outside of the Jets DST with 2.5 points), getting 13+ points from everyone and 22+ points from 4 starters (Mahomes, St. Brownie, Perine and Jacobs). The 148 points were enough for #2 on the week, and Titty City hasn't scored less than 122 points since week 8. JerrBerr won round 1 of this battle way back in week 2, while Jacube handled Jerry in week 13. Depending on this week's outcomes, we could see the rubber match as soon week 15, or in the finals if drama has its way.

A devastating week for the Toons, as their bye week episode was officially cancelled after the upset loss to Big Jim 101 - 109.Trevor leaned heavily on Davante Adams, who has been unstoppable lately, and week 13 was no different, scoring 37 points (177 yards and 2 TDs). The real issue for this team was not the lost bye week, as that was unlikely as is, but the tough pill to swallow was the writers potentially writing Jaylen Waddle and Kenneth Walker off the show with their injuries. Trevor still has some depth (not this week with byes), which will apparently be needed heading into the fantasy playoffs.

Bye Bye Bye! is usually the song sung/danced to by Josh Jones, but this week, Jimmie is blasting it, as he secured a round 1 bye with a win over Austin and a Trevor loss. This is the OPTH's first bye, in either playoff (main & toilet), and he will hope to save up all his points for weeks 16 and 17. This past week, the only thing getting the boxers going was Josh Allen and Stefon Diggs, who combined for 42 of the 94 points. Jimmie will need better games in the final two weeks if he wants to get that 3rd title.

The Fighting DIngles are Hurtsing bad, after a huge 132 - 148 loss to Jacube, even with a mild 43 Dingle from Jalen Hurts. Jerry's booty hairs were plucked by Kamara, ETN and Kelce this week, who all combined for just 20 points, missing their projections by 29 total points. Even more painful than a plucked Dingleberry is knowing that you could have won the week and competed for the high score had you played the bench over the big names. Jerry had plenty of points left on bench that would have resulted in a Jerry win. The first round matchup is all that is at stake for Jerry in week 14.

The league's top scoring team in week 13 can finally breathe a sigh of relief, having clinched a playoff spot following a pounding of Jona's Asser 164 - 65. This was the league's first 2.5x margin of victory, which says plenty about both teams involved in this one. Yish let AJ Brown, CMC, Saquon, G. Wilson and even the Cleveland DST loose on Jona, who would have lost to just about any combination of just 3 of Yisha's starting 8. Yish still sits in 6th place, but a win against the Dingles in week 14 could push Yish as far north as 4th place, while a loss would likely see him lineup across from some solid talent in the home of big Titties.

Gil asked for Tacos, and Scary Terry and Pachecho (pronounced Pah-chay-choh) delivered 42 of them right to Gil's plate. When Gil was done eating, he was happy to pay the bill for his 114 Taco evening, since the meal provided Gil with a win over Joe, as well as a chance to secure the round 1 toilet bye.Gil controls his own destiny now, and a win would give his guys an extra week to prep their week 16 feast.

Big Flop City is bumping again, as the Twins are bouncing all around after a huge upset win over Trevor and the Toons 109 - 101. The win was certainly unexpected, seeing as Jim hit his projections by 4 points, while Trevor missed his by a full 35 points. The flop had been building, given that Big Jim had been tucked away for the last 7 weeks prior to week 13. Despite the 4-9 record, Jim, a non-buyer, can earn a round 1 bye of the consolation playoffs with a 2nd straight win and a little help.

Joe drops another game, inceasing the losing streak to 5 in a row to force him into a week 14 win to earn a consolation bye. Joe would love for these last 5 weeks to be an Urban Myth in the history books, but unfortunately, the record will always show a rough month plus for Joe Joe. The Myth can still secure a bye week in a few different scenarios, but he will need to have a good week and get some help. Despite the 5 game losing streak, Joe is still a team with a great chance at the #1 pick in 2023.

Game of Jones falls flat again, scoring just 82 points in a blowout loss to Ryan 82 - 143. The performance was an all too familiar one for Josh, marking the 9th time this season that GoJ has failed to reach triple digits in a week. Outside of the Buc's White (15 points) and Browns' DPJ (15 points) this week was filled with mediocre and below outings. Disappointingly for Josh, the loss forces him into a must win situation if he wishes to earn the week 15 bye in the toilet bowl. A win over Gil and some help from Joe and Jim would get GoJ where he needs to be.

The Budget Magician strikes again! Back to back low scores of the week, and a 4th low score of the year has Jona struggling to book a slot in the Tuesday afternoon mall talent show. The tricks have been wild this year. Jona has been able to creat so much happiness for his fans, while almost immediately roundhousing those same fans in he face the following week. For Jona in week 13, he pulled a Swift out of his hat and received 22 applauses. Everything else was boo-ed up and down show. Jona the Great still has a chance to keep the toilet playoff round 1 bye, but he may have another unpleasant trick up his sleeve.

Austin's Automation Services (AAS) funded this week's podcast, but they did not provide the TMCs with a win, playing an OUT Michael Carter for a 94 - 65 loss to Jimmie. This was the 2nd time the AAS caused Austin a goose from an OUT player, as we saw it a few weeks back when Everett started while sitting in the stands. The week 14 loss puts Austin in last place, a complete opposite season from last year, when we all thought he was only a few weeks away from a blue shirt.

Who needs WRs to get a 4 game win streak? Not Trevor apparently, s his RBs did the heavy lifting in their week 12 win against Gil and the Tacos. The Toons, or whoever they are now that Mooney is done for the season, got neary 60 points from their 3 RBs, which, paired with J Herbs' 36 was enough to win without any other help. With such an incredible base line, Trevor can choose to Walk(er) or Waddle into the Finals this year it seems.

The Wolfpack stay hot, winning back to back games to remain tied for 1st place at 9-3 following the 122-89 win over Joe. After drafting 16 RBs, including some backup RBs, Ryan is in a position not many teams are, and that is having 3 locked and loaded wideouts (Jefferson, Chase and surprise addition Watson). With Chase rejoining the team after a 5 week absence, The Wolfpack are ready to feast on opponents. Henry can slowly accumulate yards and TDs, while the WRs boom for 100 points. Not a team I'd want to play anytime soon.

The Dingles felt the pain in week 12 and Hurts(ed) their way to a win on SNF. After losing ETN to a foot injury after just 2 rushing attempts for 3 yards, Jerry's clear path to the playoffs looked murky at best. Luckily for JerrBerr, he had the Eagle in the hole, Jalen Hurts, who destroyed the Packers for 310 combined passing and rushing yards and 37 fantasy points. Big Jim left enough points on the bench to defeat the Dingles, but instead, Jerry took the 9 point win and ran into week 13 with a 7-5 record, feeling much better about his playoff chances.

It may not be your preference, but Over the Pants Handys have been fire this season, as Jimmie claims his 3rd high score of the year in a 166-94 win over Game of Jones. The fantasy points couldn't keep their Hands off these Pants, with every positional player scoring 13.5+ points and two players going for more than 33 points. This unit has always shown it can boom, but it the two previous weeks showed that they can also bust, seeing as Jimmie's week 10 and 11 total score combined were exactly what he scored in week 12 (80 + 86, and 166). Jimmie is hoping to ride out a couple more wins to earn the important round 1 bye.

Who is the real Mayor of Titty City? I knew his name was Jacob, but is the "S" just silent? Josh Jacobs has been nothing short incredible this season, easily putting himself in the running for best draft pick of the year. Jacobs joined a group of just 9 other players to 300 scrimmage yards in a single game (229 rush yards and 74 receiving yards). This was JJ's 4th game this season over 32 points, scoring close to a season high across any position with 53 points this week. Due to Jacobs' incredible week, the self-proclaimed Mayor could have started just Josh Jacobs and Amon-Ra St. Brown and still have beaten Jona 78.85 to 78.12. With this type of boom, Jacube will be tough to beat come playoff time.

The Hiroshima Hot Dogs, better known as Roughing the Asser, got back into the win column with an easy W over Austin 116 - 87, to move inside the playoffs at 6-6. Yish was looking out for Austin's Asser because he could have Roughed it up much worse, leaving Jackson, Conner, G. Wilson and AJ Dillon on the bench, who scored 28, 23, 27 and 18 points respectively. While Yish is fighting for a playoff spot, his team is one that could easily go the distance once they make inside.

Game of Jones needed to win out and get some help if he wanted to secure a spot in the playoffs, but a week 12 loss to Jimmie's fire Pants, all but ended Josh's playoff hopes. This wasn't a terrible week for Josh, as everyone played decent, with the exception of Mr. Green Bay himself, Aaron Rodgers, who scored just 12 points (his 2nd worst of the season). Though Josh lost Najee to an abdomen injury, his team still looks like it shall do well in the consolation rounds.

Paper ain't Tacos. And Gil Needs Tacos to win. On paper, this team looks like one that could be competing for a back end playoff spot given the current landscape, however, this team in real life continues to disappoint. Week 12 was no different, as Isiah Pacheco, Aaron Jones and Tua for just under 60 of the team's 85 points in the loss to Trevor. Though they are not mathematically eliminated, Gil will be prepping for his consolation bracket buffet.

Big Jim makes losing look easy these days, with his 7th straight loss, dropping his season record to 3-9. Week 12 was no short order to get a win, as Jim was matched up against the Dingles' super team, however, Big Jim could have won this one. He left too many points on the bench, and ended with just under 94 points for the week. There is still a very real possibility for a flop to happen again this season, but the time is absolutely running out.

The Urban Myth, while not officially eliminated from the playoffs, called ahead to reserve a seat in the consolation bracket after a week 12 loss to Ryan and the Wolves 89 - 122. The lost season will be Joe's 3rd in 6 seasons, making him a 50/50 shot to make the postseason any year. For Joe, it has to be frustrating, as his team is still performing decently, with good games from Geno (25), DK (15) and Zeke (18). Joe would be my dark horse (if you'd even call him that) to take home the 1st overall pick in the 2023 draft.

The budget Magician is likely trying to figure out how to make last week disappear from his memory, losing to Jacube 78 - 152. Outside of Kyler and Pittman, every starter scored single-digits this week, which is how Jona claimed his 3rd lowest score of the week this season (73 and 59 points in weeks 9 and 4). It's an outside chance, but Jona has the best chance of making the playoffs out of any team outside the playoffs at this point in the season. If anyone can do it, it would be the team with a little Magic to Jawork.

Austin is unpacking his bags and leaving a toothbrush down here, claiming the 12th spot for the 4th week in a row, and 5 of the last 7 weeks. Austin really doesn't have too much positive to speak of, except that he is getting big games from unexpected players. This team does have players that can hit for big points, but having them all happen on the same week remains unlikely. Either way, Austin has the potential to play spoiler to someone's season in these next two weeks.

Power rank #1 VS power rank #2, and Trevor, the underdog, came through with a big 36 point win over he Dingles. Trevor's low spot this week was Darnell Mooney's 11 points, and he will effectively be benched the remainder of the year for his inadequacies. Everyone else on this team performed exactly as you'd hope after buying. This was a quick power move to show the league who is the top team without question.Oh, and the 158 points he scored were without Kenneth Walker and Waddle.

The big Dingles were big buyers, and one of those Jerry loved one of his new toys in week 11. Travis Kelce has the 50% TD rate going, scoring 3 TDs on 6 catches for 115 yards (33 total points). Despite the dominance by Kelce, and the outstanding outputs by Hurts (30) and Deebo (20), this team could not muster up much more to talk about. Yes, Jerry was without Kirk, Etienne and Hill for this matchup, but the 120 - 158 loss did show that Jerry is a beatable team on the right week. Just good luck finding that week.

The Wolfpack would be nothing without a little adversity. You have to challenge yourself to stay at your best, so Ryan chose to sit Pollard and his 39.65 point game to see if he could still get a win over Gil's couple of Tacos. Obviously, Ryan is in top shape, as he destroyed Gil 142 - 84 without Tony P.'s points. Ryan welcomed in Derrick Henry with very very wide open arms, and Henry ran right into them carrying 30 points for his first hug. The loss of Pitts may actually help Ryan, and on top of that, he is likely getting Chase back to join in the hunts. As close to a super team as you can be, Ryan will likely continue to rip through opponents.

What is happening to this team? After leading the league in points heading into week 10, this team has scored less than 87 points in back to back weeks. My 32nd year of life is starting out much worse than my 31st year, fantasy football-wise that is. Apparently some rabbits perform only for their magician, as Josh Allen scored 10 points below his worst performance of the year (15) in his 1st appearance as an OTPH. I was saved by a SNF early injury to Toney, which allowed me to win 80 - 70 over Joe. I would have only beaten 2 teams this week, and luckily I payed one of them.

The self-proclaimed Mayor had Titty City in embargo mode last week and refused to move any players in our out of its borders. Even with his decision, Jacube started off the first week after the deadline with a 125 - 62 win over the unknowns. Jacob won his matchup by more than Austin even scored (63 point margin), making this one of the most lopsided games this year. The City is potentially down one Titty, as Mixon may be stuck in the protocol through this week. Luckily for Jacube, he picked up Perine, who would likely fill in nicely in Mixon's absence. Jacube Still has work to do, but he does look poised to make his playoff debut this season.

Josh Jones hasn't Roughed many Asses this season, but he certainly had the GPS to Yisha's behind dialed in, as Yisha was torn apart by Game of Jones 140 - 87 in week 11. This week's output was mediocre at best, as Conner and CMC and Lamar led the way with 14, 16 and 19 points resepectively. Not a bad week so far, but when you add in a combined 13 points for AJ Brown and Saquon Barkley, who had one of the best matchups for RBs, the week went south quick. Yisha, like most contending playoff have these holes that can sink a week, making his playoff chances good, but not secure.

The Tacos started Daniel Jones! Need I say more? Other than saying that Jones more than doubled the next closest score on this team (Aaron Jones' 13 points) and at least tripled everyone else's points in the starting slots. Though this team looks good on paper, to me at least, they appear to be much more of a scratch off ticket than anything else. If Gil can scratch off the right Tacos, he could push for the playoffs.

Game of Jones scored 140+ points for the 2nd time this year, but only one of those games resulted in a win. This week, 140 was enough to get a win over his brother-in-law, by 53 points in fact. Josh had contributions from almost everyone, including a 14 point DST showing from the Patriots (mostly from the last second punt return). Josh's highlights were Najee (28) and Cooper (29), who each had their best game of the season in week 11. A conservative seller at the deadline, Josh can still make the playoffs after this week's win, but if he misses the postseason, he will more than likely be playing for the 1st overall pick in week 17.

Joe sold before the deadline and immediately felt the effects of not having Kelce or Henry, scoring just 70 points on the week. More than half the points were scored by Zeke and George Pickes, who appears to be the real deal (even with a rookie QB), and the rest of the roster basically took the weekend off. Except for the Ravens DST, who outscored Jared Goff in week 11. Joe will have an uphill battle on staying interested this year, but if things bounce the right way, he could actually still make the playoffs. And if not, he's ready for 2023.

Big Jim with 6 straight losses. At this point, the flop has been qeued up so long that whenever it does come, if it comes, it's likely going to hurt someone. Jim lost to Jona in this one by just 0.49 points, making this his second loss by less than 0.5 points this year (0.41 points to Ryan). Just 1 fantasy point could have Jim sitting at 5-6 this season and competing for a playoff spot. Instead, he is virtually eliminated from the postseason and will be trying for a top 2023 pick. This week was a skeleton crew, so I would not expect 87 points to be the norm for the remainder of this season for this group.

The tricks keep coming! Jona, or Joan the Great, had another trick up his sleeve after dumping Allen and Diggs to Jimmie. In week 11, Jona put Jimmy G in his hat and pulled out 31 points with him. Particularly Magic because Jimmy G hadn't surpassed 22.7 points at all this season. On his 4th TD of the game, right before being benched in a blowout win, Jimmy G secured the win for the Magic by just 0.49 points over Big Jim. The win is even more Magical though, as it puts Jona inside the playoffs at 6-5, keeping him a contender for the postseason. While his road will be tough, anything can happen in fantasy football, so we may just see the Magic show perform their best tricks yet.

Austin got double goosed in week 10, resulting in a dreadful blowout in Titty City. One of the goosings came from an OUT player, so the zero was expected. What was less expected was Cousins' 3.4 points, or that Jamaal Williams would score 27 points and the team would cap out at 62. Austin obviously went to Titty City for the sights, as he did not go there for football.

The big Dingles are all in on the 2022 season. Jerry was on the esge of the playoffs last week, so he went out and acquired CeeDee Lamb from Gil, who was on the downslope, and the trade immediately paid off with 34 points from Lamb in week 10. After the week 10 win, Jerry said, "Let's do this thing", and made two more major trades to solidify himself as a top team in the league. The additions of Hill and Kelce make the Dingles the team to beat, as they have arguably no weaknesses heading into week 11. However, Jerry better hope this year ends in a championship, otherwise 2023 will be an extra sad year for the Berries.

The Mooney Toons cashed in on Big Field Benches' promo code and left week 10 with 49 points from apparent fantasy superstar, Justin Fields, who has 5 straight games of 25+ points. Trevor made a pre-deadline move last week and acquired Waddle from Gil to shore up his WR room. After that big move, Trevor decided he also needed to shore up his RB room, so he went out and snagged Jonathan Taylor, who had been struggling up until last week. Though revorT had been trending up, his team's arrow just shot straight to the moon.

Fantasy decided that you can either have a birthday, or you can have a good fantasy day, but not both. Since time is undefeated, I got the birthday and a garbage fantasy day, 86 points of trash to be exact. Not much more needs to be said about this past week, but this team did make two moves before the deadline, shipping out Kyler and the future of Kupp for the Buffalo boys in Allen and Diggs. I will be hoping to get a few more wins and earn a bye to avoid playing some of these other powerhouse teams too early.

All is quiet in Titty City, after the celebrations went wild last week for the self-proclaimed Mayor and his marriage into this family. Whether she knows it or not, Karlie is now the first lady of the famous City, and her first order of business was to not make any changes at all after a week 10 win. Jacube's roster has been nothing short of fantastic this year, so it's not too surprising to see him lay low during the deadline. We shall see if buying is the new requirement, or can Titty City prove that winning comes from those already inside the building.

Yisha took the gamble a few weeks ago and decided to make a push for the playoffs. Two weeks and two wins later, Yish has the Assers in 6th place at 5-5. Yish was actually the one to push the first domino and trade for CMC from Austin. CMC, along with Conner and Saquon, totaled just over 70 points from the RB position in week 10. The squad is stacked, but after a few of the other moves around the league, nobody feels stacked anymore.

Ryan and the Wolfpack like to keep things interesting, so they decided to start a losing streak after their long 6 game win streak. The back to back losses has Ryan in 2nd place at 7-3, with a two game lead on 5th place. Ryan barely missed in this one, losing just 120 - 113 to Trevor, who would have been blown out of the water had the Wolfpack started their new Wolf, Christian Watson, who scored 33 points on 3 TDs. Ryan didn't need to be too active around the deadline, only making one move. That move was to turn the Yeti into a Wolf for the winter. Adding Henry to this roster means that Ryan has arguably the 3 most explosive players in fantasy in Ja'Marr Chase, Justin Jefferson and Derrick Henry. It is a wild thought to have him ranked at #6.

Gil is a big fan of the Carolina Panthers, so he took a page out of their book and traded away his big names before the trade deadline, only to have his remaining players have massive games in their absence. This was a dream week for the Tacos, who scored 136 points (the week high) with a zero from newly acquired Jerry Jeudy. Gil, who sold a week early, finds himself in a weird spot at 4-6, where he can now potentially make the playoffs or just sweep the consolation bracket after a wild deadline.

A weird year for Joe to say the least. He never broke into the top 4 ranked teams any week this year, and hovered in the bottom 5 for most of the season. A loss in week 10 dropped Joe to 5-5 on the year and into 7th place in the standings. Joe must not have felt confident in the 2022 season, as he set his sights on the 2023 championship by dumping players and gathering picks. Joe will finish out the season without the likes of Derrick Henry (Ryan) or Travis Kelce (Jerry). Joe's 2022 season followed that of his name sake, Urban Meyer and his NFL debut.

5 losses in a row. This has been a rough month plus for Big Jim. He hasn't been able to flop on anyone in quite a while, and it might be getting to him. Unfortunately for this team, most of them are taking the option on playing this week and will be watching the Twins likely get kicked around for the 6th straight week. Jim didn't make any deadline moves (yet), and will be in contention for a top 4 pick in the 2023 draft.

Game of Jone was hanging onto hope by a very small thread, but that thread snapped while he was driving home from Minnesota on Sunday, as he watched his team fall to 3-7 on the year following a 122 - 94 loss to Jacube during his special weekend. Josh didn't have the firepower to get the win this weekend, regardless of who he played, which eventually led to the departure of Tyreek Hill. Josh will happily take his new 2nd round pick into the consolation playoffs, where he may just dominate after keeping the core of his team together.

Jona the Great has slowly watched his team's value disappear, as he has lost his last 3 games, while several players' potential were never realized (notably Swift and Pittman). Despite being just on the edge of playoffs, Jona could see the writing on the wall and decided to move on from Allen and Diggs, who are heading back into the draft pool for 2023. Jona at least was able to pull a Kupp out of a hat, who will undoubtedly be a cornerstone of the 2023 Magic Show.

The who made who's? No more Johnny T or CMC, and this team is stuck at the bottom. Just like the Panthers, Austin gave away CMC and won their next game. The win puts Austin just outside the playoffs, but after dumping too many big names, it is unlikely they retain that position. Unless it's a wild end to the season, Austin is welcoming in the 2023 season in week 11.

This coming week, the self-proclaimed Mayor will likely be getting advice to mix in a water here and there, as he will officially join the family on Saturday. However, last week, Jacube was told to Mixon a TD, and he Mixon-ed in 5 TDs into the mix, as Joe Mixon rushed for 4 TDs, caught 1 TD for 211 total yards and and a small 59.05 fantasy points. Jacube also had Mahomes rolling again, who has yet to score less than 21 points on a week, as he had a 40 point game with just 2 TDs because he threw for 446 yards and ran for another 63. Those two players alone would have lost to Joe's entire team by 11 points. Titty City is riding high, being the the #1 team in the league for 4 straight weeks. even with the #1 rank and the #2 total points on the year, Jacube is currently sitting outside the playoffs!

Look who's back on top! Of the standings that is. With a week 9 win over Ryan and the Wolfpack, Jimmie re-claimed the top spot of the standings (by points) at 7-2. D'Onta Foreboy did his best to make sure Ryan extended his winning streak to 7, as the RB scored 32 points less than his week total (4). TJ Hockenson looks like he may have actually gotten an upgrade with the Vikings, catching all 9 of his targets for 70 scoreless yards with only a few days to prep. The 115 points for Jimmie was his max score for the week, as his entire team was either hurt or on bye, leaving only 3.85 usuable points on the bench. Chubb's return in week 10 will be a welcomed one.

The 6 game win streak is over! Ryan hasn't added a tally to the loss column since week 2, which is lightyears ago in a fantasy season, but the battle of #1 vs #2 ended with the Wolfpack on the losing end. The week started off blazing with Ryan scoring 4 TDs in the first 18 minutes of the early games on Sunday, but his team rested on their laurels in the 2nd half slowing coming to a stop at 111 points in a 115 - 111 loss. Ryan had most of his guys on bye or out on injury, which left him with only 3 points on his bench, meaning his 111 points was the best it was getting. Ryan's team is one that could land on either side of the fence on any given week, making him a dice roll to play against every week.

The 4 game losing streak is over! Yisha defeated Gil in a garbage fest 87 - 86 in week 9, to improve to 4-5 on the year. The win was enough to push the Assers into the playoff picture, apparently, as Yisha went out and purchased RB CMC from Austin's garage sale. Going into Monday night, Yisha needed just over 21 points from Lamar to get the win, which Lamar had done exactly 50% of the time this year. Lamar got 22 points and secured the win. So if Lamar hadn't ran that last play or two, would Gil have been buying from Yisha's garage sale??? Either way, the stack of Saquon and CMC at the RB position is not one anyone wants to face.

The Mooney Toons, to their mistake, took their up and coming star, Justin Fields, and wrote him out of the script for season 22 epsiode 9, only to watch him outscore the leading role, Justin Herbert, by 37 points as the understudy. Luckily for roverT, the other 3 leads performed excellently, as Adams, Walker and Ekeler each had 23 or more points, and combined for 87 points together. Trevor's 126 points earned him the win over Jona's Magic, making both their records 5-4 on the year. Trevor's team is too good on paper, and will definitely be one to avoid in the near future.

Big daddy Dingles rode ETN to a 111 - 90 win over Austin's Taylor-less Christians in week 9. Jerry's trip to Jacksonville paid off big, as Kirk and ETN went for just under 50 points together, making up a little less than half the team's production. The Jags' production was able to hide the lack of production elsewhere, as Duvernay, McLaurin and Kamara couldn't manage 20 points together. The Dingles are going streaking, whether you want to see it or not, with back to back wins, which has put them into 3rd place in the standings at 5-4.

Joe's chances of winning his week 10 matchup was the Urban Myth of the week, after being matched up against Mahomes and Mixon, who combined for 720 yards, 7 TDs and 100 fantasy points. Smith, Allgeier, Henry and Kelce did their best to combat the M&M combo, but fell a mere 61 points short. Joe falls to 5-4 on the year and sits inside, but on the edge of playoffs. If his guys can get healthy, I would imagine they push to remain in the playoff picture

Gil did not need more Tacos in week 9, but he did need more fantasy points because his guys only mustered up 86 of them in their battle with Yish. The 86 would normally put you in contention for biggest blowout of the week, but in this case, Gil lost by less than 2 points to fall to 3-6 on the year. The only guys slinging Tacos in week 9 were Tua, Waddle and Pierce, which is rarely enough to feed a win. Gil will need to win a game or two in the next couple weeks if he wants a chance at the postseason.

Once upon a flop, Jim was 3-2. But that was 4 weeks ago. Today, Big Jim turned his Twins into quadruplets, and they all brought losses with them, because this team has lost 4 straight to fall to 3-6 on the year. This roster is slowly losing guys to injury and/or backup roles, making it tough to trust them going forward. Without a trade or waiver move, this may be the highest this team gets ranked the rest of the year unfortunately.

He is back baby! Josh returns from a 5 week absence, not having been seen by anyone since week 3 to get his first win in over a month 117 - 83 over the Flops. Game of Jones was led by current Dolphin, Tyreek Hill, and his 25 points, as well as former Dolphin, Kenyan Drake, and his 28 points. Josh was also able to get a win, even with his QB being outscored by his defense. Which makes sense because the Patriots DST score 18 points, which has to be a season high at the position. Even with taking a month + off from winning, the win puts Josh right back into the mix for making a push.

The budget Magician has been trying out a new set of tricks lately. Primarily how to keep his fantasy score under 100 points, as he has sub-100 totals in each of the last 3 games. 42 of Jona's 73 points came from the two Bills, while the remaining 6 starters all scored between 0 and 7.4 points. Pittman and Swift are trying to follow in Jona's Magical footsteps, as they are making their fantasy value disapear with each passing week. Other than the big names, it's hard to get on board with this squad, especially with Josh Allen projected to miss this coming week and possibly beyond.

Austin was without his namesake once again in week 9, which proved to be too much of a handicap against the Dingles, as they lost 111 - 90 and are now in a four way tie for last place. With CMC on bye and JT out with his ankle injury, Austin was forced to be the Curtis Made Carters, which turned into just under 50 points from Curtis Samuel, D. Carter (LAC) and M. Carter (Jets). The loss was enough of a reason for Austin to officially open up shop, and sell to the first customer in line (Yish), who wanted half of Austin's name in CMC. Without McCaffrey, and with Thomas heading to IR, 12th is likely where this team will hover for the remainder of the year.

The self-proclaimed Mayor pulled a power move here, tempting the rankings to see if he could throw a dud week out and still remain atop the charts. Well, consider it a victory, as Titty City is still ranked as the #1 destination in the league, following the week 9 loss to Gil (95 - 137). Jacube was without his leader, Mahomes, and was forced to play Danny Dimes and Pennies, who scored just 11 points against the Seahawks. Jacube also told Josh Jacobs and Joe Mixon to cool down a bit for this one, as they only managed 18 points together. Just a quick glance at Jacube's roster should show why he's still looking down from the top spot.

Heyyo! A Big week 8 win for Jimmie and the Handies. Sometimes, when you lose someone important, the team can collapse into itself and show just how important that player was to the team. Sometimes, however, the team can come together and play their best for the player lost. Jimmie's team was the latter, as the spirit of Breece Lightning was coursing through the veins of this team, on their way to the high score of the week with 163 points one week after Breece departed. All positional players (non-defense) scored 10+ points, and 4 of those 7 scored 20+ points. Additionally, all 8 starters outscored their projections this week, and when that happens, you're usually in for a win. Jimmie will try to keep the action happening in week 9.

Does Ryan have unexplainable fantasy talent, or does he just have a horseshoe lodged somewhere we can't see? While, yes, he did lose JaMarr Chase to a hip injury, he also gained Tony Pollard by way of an Ezekiel Elliott knee injury, which turned into an a dominating 38 point Pollard performance (147 total yards and 3 TDs). Ryan needed all the Tony Pollard he could get, as he left exactly 0.23 points on his bench, and narrowly defeated Yish on a Monday night thriller. Ryan also followed Jerry's lead and turned 1 RB into 2, as Chase Edmonds was moved to Denver, leaving Mostert in Miami and Ryan in Minnesota with 2 playable RBs. This team is comfortably sitting at 7-1, and they will likely only be at full strength when it really matters, weeks 15-17.

The West Coast fans needed to watch something else for a change, and decided to turn the channel off the Toons in week 8, leaving Trevor with just 15 points from out west (0.8 from Adams and 14.25 from Walker). With Herbert and Ekeler on bye, Trevor was forced to start Justin Fields and Jerry Jeudy, who ended up being the two highest scorers for this team in week 8, with 31 and 16 points respectively. Despite the 3 game win streak coming to an end, Neilsen still has this team rated as a top 4 show.

Joe Joe the Psychic Show knew this week was his before it even started, as he had been saving his best Mythical performance to avoid being flopped on by Big Jim. Joe released the beast, King Yeti, who was the Titans offense, rushing 32 times for 219 yards and 2 TDs and 41 fantasy points (1/3 of Joe's week 8 output). Another Myth was DK Metcalf being injured for weeks, as he not only didn't miss a single game, but also had 6 receptions for 55 yards and a TD (15 points). The Myth also get a rested Travis Kelce back in the lineup, so this could have been a down week for Joe.

The mighty Dingles are back baby! Jerry wins in a 302 point shootout with a surprise week from Game of Jones (154 - 147). Jerry needed his best stuff to get back to .500 on the year, and that's what he got from the likes of Kamara, Hurts and ETN, who scored 41, 34 and 28 points respectively (totalling just over 105 points together). Jerry also could have had another 12 points on top of the 154, if he had swapped Duvernay for Kirk, showing just how good of a week this was for the Dingles. IF this is a sign of things to come for Jerry, this team will be on the move north again next week.

This is Rough. Yisha has found himself deep in some fantasy god's Asser, as his week 8 loss extends the losing streak to 4 games. Even worse, Yish had the points to win this week, but was immediately slapped in the face by Rashod Bateman, who brought Mother Goose along with him in the trade from the Mooney Toons. Batemen's minor "tweak" also turned into a multi-week injury, just extending the slap into future weeks.
