The top performer this week was easily AJ Brown, who had 6 receptions for 156 yards and 3 TDs in just 3 quarters before being benched in the 4th due to the blowout. Yish will get a couple players back from bye and injury, which may be enough to get him his first win since week 4.

Big Jim and the Twins are feeling pretty flaccid, as they drop their 3rd straight game in the loss to Urban Myth. Even with the loss, Jim had a pretty good outing, and was really only let down by an early departure from Mark Andrews (5) and a below average showing from Chris Olave (8). Had those players gotten a little closer to their projections, or averages even, Jim likely would have come away with the win. This team did move back two spots, but it is primarily due to other teams getting better, rather than his team getting worse. After 3 straight losses, Jim and the Twins are likely building up to a big flop on an unsuspecting victim.

Who Needs More Tacos? Not Jacube, that's for sure. Gil traveled to Titty City and loaded those Tatas with 137 Tacos in week 8, before leaving town with a victory. The trade for Tua immediately paid off, as the stack with Waddle blew up for 64 points in their first game together. The two in Miami were helped with big games from Aaron Jones, Lamb and Pierce, who all had 14 or more points as well. TEs though may not be big fans of Tacos, as Gil's starting TE in the last two weeks have each ended up on IR. So, if you care about any TE on a personal level, pray for whoever gets the nod for the Tacos in week 9.

The Magic show comes up one trick short, as their 3 game win streak comes to an end in week 8, losing 99 - 117 to Austin and CMC. Jona, with a healthy roster, only left about 5 points on the bench, meaning that his 99 point week wouldn't have gotten much better with the Muth in the lineup. Only 3 players outscored their projections, each by 3 points or less, while the other 5 players missed the mark by anywhere from 1 to 11 points. Jona was happy to welcome RB DeAndre Swift back into the bag of tricks, but Swift was not so happy to be back, as he only rushed for 6 yards on 5 attempts, while catching 5 passes for 27 yards and one box-score-saving TD. Jona sits at #3 in the standings, but he will need better games ahead if he wants to avoid finishing near his power rank.

Austin may be in the process of formally changing his last name to McCaffrey after CMC won the week for him against Jona's Magic. CMC became just the 11th player in NFL history, and the 1st since LT in 2005, to pass, rush and receive a TD in a single game. One of the league's true difference makers showed what he could be in the SF Kyle Shanahan led offense, which was 41 easy points. Unfortunately for Austin, the rest of his roster is lightyears away from CMC's play lately, as he and Kirk Cousins combined for 70 of the team's 117 total points this week, which means that there really is nothing else good to say about the ugly win.

Who is this guy? Scores 80 points all year, and then puts the perfect lineup together and scores almost double that (147) in week 8? Unfortunately for Josh, his 3rd highest score of the week was matched up with the 2nd highest score of the week, making his big game just another in a long string of losses (5 in a row). Game of Jones WRs (Cooper, Hill and Hopkins) all scored 20-30 points, which is usually enough to get a win in the RBB this year, but apparently not against Jerry. The loss moves Josh to the sole owner of last place with a 2-6 record, though with the way this league works, he is only down, not out.

The self-proclaimed Mayor is running from town to town showing off his RBs, who are absolutely destroying the competition right now. Stevenson just scored his 3rd straight 21+ point game, while Josh Jacobs just had his 3rd straight 32+ point game, and both RBs are overshadowing the big name of Joe Mixon, who is routinely scoring in the upper teens. Despite the massive performances by the RBs and Patty Mahomes, Jacube lost the heavyweight battle with Ryan 145-160, after losing WR Amon ra on his first catch of the day. Even with the loss, this team is the clear #1.

The Wolfpack is officially on the Chase for their 3rd RBB title, after acquiring Ja'Marr Chase in trade two weeks ago. Chase is now paired on the same roster with Joey Burrow, and the two have combined for 156.09 points over the last 2 weeks since the trade. A if that wasn't enough, the rich get richer, as Ryan now has the starting RB for the Cowboys, Tony Pollard, with Zeke going down. The Wolfpack are likely staying at the top of the standings for some weeks to come.

Jimmie and his team have their Pants down this week, as they pour one out for the rising star, Breece Lightning, who lost his spectacular rookie season to a torn ACL in week 7. This team did earn the week 7 win over Yisha's Assers, but it was done in a somber tone, as they must now try to find a half replacement for Hall's upside. Hopefully the very expensive new piece can help heal the wounds.

Trevor came into week 7 with a script based around RBs Austin Ekeler and Kenneth Walker, who delivered a masterpiece performance, totaling 295 yards, 3 TDs and 78.7 fantasy points. Te points were just over half the team's 140 points in their win over Austin, moving the Toons to 4-3 on the year and on a 3 game win streak. With the upside of big Herbs, Adams weekly 12 catches and Montgomery stealing some yards from Fields, this team should score north of 110 points a week going forward.

Yisha spent his weekend celebrating Jacube for his bachelor party, and his team apparently went with him. Just like Yish on Sunday, his team was MIA, as only two starters managed double-digit points in week 7 (Lamar's disappointing 13 points and Saquon's standard 19+). Yisha does get some players back from injury and bye weeks, and he just acquired Rashod Batman to boot, keeping this team in the top 5.

Big Jim and the Twins needed a week off from flopping, as too much flopping can damage the goods, so he decided throw a 66 out there against Gil. 43 of the 66 points came from Brady, Olave and Aiyuk, leaving the remaining 23 points to be filled by the other 5 starters, who all had forgettable outings. With Dalvin Cook back, DJ Moore possible coming back to life and Juju maybe being something, this roster still has plenty of power to flop again.

Another week, another trick by the budget Magician, as he finds a way to get a win with a backup squad. Jona was lonely out in Buffalo in week 7, so he called in his friends Tua T. and Tyler B. to join him in Josh Allen and Stefon Diggs' place. As the WR 3 for the Bengals, Boyd's 29 point game completed the show and earned Jona the Great a week 7 win over Game of Jones (91 - 84) to improve to 5-2 on the year. I stil can't trust this team on paper, but the Buffalo boys have clearly proven to be enough to win games.

This week's matchup was pulled straight from the Civil War books, as it had father vs. son in an ugly battle. Joe, formerly of Minnesota, took the win as his Northerners defeated the Dingles 94 - 82. Joe was able to withstand less than 5.5 points from his QB and #1 WR (Goff wth 3.72, DK with 1.70) by big games from his RBs Zeke and Henry, as well as rookie playmaker George Pickens. Joe did acquire a Chiefs' version of Kadarius Toney, which may end up being worth more than the New York version, but with the injuries to DK and Zeke, it's tough to push this team up the rankings.

The Tacos love the 9 spot, as they get the win with their 2nd triple-digit score of the year (104 - 66). Gil was lead by RBS Aaron Jones and Dameon Pierce, who had more than 40 points together. Gil did lose TE Njoku to a multi-week injury, and had to finally ship off Javonte Williams to acquire Njoku's replacement big Irv Smith. This feels a little like backing the Cubs before they eventually won the World Series, but I can't help but feel like this team has more wins and big scores in them this season.

The Big Dingles got 57 points from Jimmy G, Kamara and ETN, and just 25 points from the other 5 starters. Given that headline, you'd think Jerry got smashed this week, but he was actually in the game most of the weekend, and only lost by 12 points (82 - 94) to his 1st born, Joe and the Urban Myth. Even on a bad week, Jerry moves up one spot primarily because he was able to turn one RB into two, as James Robinson was traded to the Jets to fill their open role, which left ETN to take control over the JAX backfield. Time will tell if Jerry can use these new tools to turn the ship around.

The TaylorMade Christians moved their headquarters out to SF, and their first order of business was to fire Rusty Wilson for a younger, better Daniel Jones. While the move did not give an immediate win, Austin did come away with 119 points and some upside. RB Michael Carter was unhappy with Breece Hall's ascension, so he made sure Breece would start his descension in week 7, somehow assisting in Hall's torn ACL. Carter's new role has this team looking better than last week, but the upside still feels like it is entirely on the back of CMC and Taylor.

Game of Jones find themselves in the dungeon once again, after the 84 - 91 loss to Jona's Magic, who were operating as a skeleton crew. Josh is consistent, if nothing else, as he has now scored in the 80s 5 of 7 weeks, and less than 100 points in all but one week. The return of Hopkins was a wlecomed one, as he instantly put up 16 points in his first game back, but right now, this team seems to be a carousel where the good games are left on the bench and the poopers find their way into the matchup.

Here it is everyone, the moment he's been campaigning for. The self-proclaimed Mayor is not only #1 in Titty City, but he's also #1 in the power rankings for the first time in his RBB career. RhoMANdre Stevenson finally had his shot as the lone back in NE, and he ran with that opportunity to 76 yards, 2 TDs and 4 receptions for another 15 yards (25 total points). Even on a week with multiple guys OUT or on bye, Jacob managed a decent fantasy score for the dub. The squad is filled with big name known performers, as well as guys that have tons of upside and potential, making him the #1 heading into week 7.

What a rough week of fantasy. Jimmie's Pants fell down this week, but the Hands were definitely Off him, as he failed to score 100 points for the first time this year, scoring just 99.91 points (with just ONE TD from his entire team) in his 2nd straight loss. Last week, Jimmie was flopped on hard by Big Jim, and that's tough to take, but manageable. This week, Jimmie lost by less than 5 points, and left those 5 points on the bench in a winnable week. Instead, the poor decision-making leaves this team at a 4-2 record and stumbling as they try to plug the injury holes.

Here we are again, Ryan is atop the standings at 5-1. It is crazy how a single reception can change the entire season, as Ryan defeated Big Jim by 0.41 points, making him one reception less for him or more from the Twins away from being tied for 1st at 4-2. The Wolves did strengthen up this week, as they were involved in the blockbuster deal, acquiring Ja'Marr Chase from Joe, while sending D. Smith and Zeke away. Chase and Jefferson is a arguably the best WR pair in the league, which will help cover the lack of RB depth/power this team has.

Yisha had his Asser Roughed for the 2nd straight week, as he drops back to back games, scoring 90 points or less in each of the two losses. The first 3 weeks, Yisha's low score was 125 points, while averaging 132.17. In the last 3 weeks, Yisha's high score was 103 points, while averaging just 91.39 points. The difference here appears to be Lamar Jackson, who has scored 20 points or less in the last 3 weeks, while he scored no less than 28 (53 & 47 points) in the first 3 weeks. If Lamar can get going again, this roster has enough talent to jump right back to the top.

Joe and the Myth make the first, and only so far, blockbuster trade of the year, as they moved on from WR Ja'Marr Chase to bring in WR D. Smith and RB E. Elliott. This week, Elliott and Smith totaled the same score Chase put up on his own (31 points), which is never fun to see when you've just let Chase go. The 31 points from those two were not enough to overcome the budget Magician's 105 points, as Joe falls to 3-3 on the year with the loss. Even with the loss, the outlook for this team with the added quality depth from the trade, is very bright. The Myth is a team to pay attention to over the next few weeks.

Big Jim and the Twins had the pants unbuttoned and the zipper 99.59% unzipped, but just could not get it down the full 100% to complete the flop on Ryan, as he loses by just 0.41 points (114.08 - 114.49) in week 6. Jim had massive weeks from Lenny, Aiyuk and Andrews, who each had 21+ points, and would have had enough for the win had he played Juju over Tevin Coleman, as Juju outscored him 22.1 points. Jim moved back this week because of the glaring RB depth issue we can see as the bye weeks begin. With Dalvin cook being out, Fournette is basically the only RB on this roster that can play this week. Without byes, and even with them I suppose since he's here, this team looks to be locked into the top 6 spots.

The Budget Magician has been workshopping his bag of tricks, and this week, he performed another one, turning 3.3 points from all his RBs and TE into a week 6 win over an unenthused Joe (105 - 91). Jona received quite a bit of points from his receivers, who all scored more than 16 points, while Josh Allen continued to dominate with his 5th game over 34 points this year (his low is 28.77). This week though, the Magician will be lonely in Buffalo, as Allen and Diggs are taking their one week vacation. Will Jona the Great astound the league with another miraculous trick this week?

The Mooney Toons did a throwback 90s episode, as they rode their RBs to a 99 - 90 win over Yisha's Assers. The West Coast fans stayed with this team when they were losing, and they were rewarded with a brand new star of the show, Kenneth Walker, who showed out in his first episode as the lead back in SEA. The win is Trevor's 2nd in a row, bringing his record back even on the year. With the sky ceiling upside of Herbert, Ekeler, Adams and Walker, paired with steady fill in performances elsewhere, the Toons may just get back to a top rated show.

After just a few weeks of trying to control the league with his Jedi Mind Tricks, Gil has abandoned the teachings of Yoda and gone back to Needing Tacos in his life. Unfortunately for Gil, getting drunk off a barrel of Tacos won't take away the sting of a 1-5, last place, start to the season. This week was Gil's 4th straight week scoring less than 93 points. However, even with the last place title and a brutal stretch of games, this team has the talent to be able to blow up at any point and string together multiple wins in a row, which is why they sit at #9.

The annual battle of the Joneses has Josh wanting to tear some pages from the history books, as Game of Jones falls to his brother Austin 95 - 116. Josh was trying to battle on two different Hills this week, as 25 of the team's 95 points came from WR T. Hill, who appears unstoppable, no matter who is the QB, already recording 50 receptions for 701 yards. The other T. Hill Josh battled on, TE/QB Taysom Hill scored just 1/5th of his name partner's total (5.74 points). The money man in Josh has to be unhappy to know that his $42 investment in Taysom made his week 6 score cost $7.32 of FAAB for each of Hill's points this week. Despite the little bit of pooping on Josh here, he finally is rewarded with the return of DeAndre Hopkins this week, which may be enough to put an end to this 3 game losing streak.

How the mighty have fallen, or been plucked in the DingleJerries case. Once a top ranked team, Jerry finds himself near the bottom of the toilet bowl. The big names just have not produced at the level their name requires. As of right now, Hurts, and possibly Kamara, are the only names really out front pulling this team to keep them at 3-3. Jeudy, Terry, Kirk, Clyde, James Robinson and even Deebo have all been underperforming as of late, and most of them seem to be that steady path to mediocrity unforutnately. However, fantasy football is crazy, so it should not surprise anyone if Jerry turns this 3-3 record into 8-3 all of a sudden.

LEEEROY JENKINS! I mean DEEEON JACKSON! After employing and deploying all the Indianapolis' RBs, Austin got a massive game out of 3rd stringer Deon Jackson, who tore through the Jags for 22 touches, 121 total yards and TD in week 6. Austin came at his brother Josh with a roster from yesteryear, and pulled some points from the past, getting 13 from George Kittle and 21 of Chase Claypool. The JacksonMade Christians had the week's highest total with 116 points, which, being the highest score, means Austin earned a win, moving him to 2-4 on the year. Going forward, this team looks like a tough horse to back, as Johnny T and CMC will have to do almost everything they can to drag the rest of this squad up the rankings.

Moving up a spot after a loss? Well, only Big Jim would have beaten the Twins this week, so not much we can do there. The OTPs had a massive decline in production, dropping from 192 to 111. However, the 111 points came with a combined 15 points from 4 of 8 starting slots. Tee Higgins got caught by Mother Goose and contributed exactly 0 points, while TJ Hockens-one scored just 1/37th of his week 4 total. The upside is still here, which is why they have captured the #1 spot for now.

The nightmare week is over. At just under 80 points, Yisha was the Asser that got Roughed this week, losing by 60 points to the Mayor. The total was Yisha's worst of the season by 24 points, which is not surprising, as Lamar had just 20 points and 3 players were outscored by the Denver DST with 8 points. A few injuries to the starters and/or the players that directly effect their production is what moved Yish back from #1 to #2.

Another week, another win for the Wolfpack, who have now won 3 straight games. Ryan is getting the points from the guys paid to bring them, in Mike Williams (20), Justin Jefferson (26), Jeff Wilson (23) and DeVonta Smith (14 in the flex). These big names gave Ryan the cushion for poor games from Irv Smith and Devin Singletary, who each had 6 points on the week. While this team, on the surface, may not look like a championship team, they have plenty of star power and depth to go the distance.

Titty City stays hot and takes off another layer, as they win back to back games and get within one win of .500 on the year. Jacob is using his name to project his desire to win through Josh Jacobs, who now has 2 consecutive weeks of 32+ points. The self-proclaimed Mayor used City funds to acquire Patrick Mahomes, who is leading the the Titties each week with dominating QB performances. Jacube may have used some under the table methods to get rid of Damien Harris, which opened up a wonderful opportunity for one of his staff members, Rhamondre Stevenson, to have a great stretch of production coming up. Corrupt or not, the Mayor is now in the top 4 teams.

Big Jim went pantsless this week and flopped all over Jimmie and the rest of the league, taking home the high score of the week at 162 points. The Twins had 6 players in double digits, with 5 of those players going over 20 points. Jim kept himself in Tampa, rolling the dice in back to back weeks, and Tampa was thankful for his trust, contributing 62 points to the team's total. Right now, the starters on this team are all wearing XL jock straps.

The Dingles have been plucked, as they have taken their 2-0 start and turned it into a 2-3 record through 5 weeks. The 3 game losing streak continued this week with a 105 - 133 loss to the Wolfpack. 105 points seems like a decent week in the RBB this year, however, this was not a good week for JareBear. 58 of the team's 105 points came from Hurts (33) and Kamara (24), and the 3rd highest scoring slot was the 49ers DST at 11 points. While this team has shown it has major upside, it has also shown it has some major downside as well. If the upside doesn't get going, the DingleJerries may be getting pulled further down the rankings.

Joe's 0-2 start is close to being an Urban Myth, as this team's 3-game win streak has them at 3-2 and in 6th place in the overall standings. Joe strapped his team to the strongest creatures, Travis Kelce and Derrick Henry, for the last 3 weeks, which have carried him to a whopping 152 points together through that span. This week, the Myth only needed Henry, Kelce and DK Metcalf to defeat Austin's Christians, as they scored 80 points together to Austin's team total of 75 points. If Joe can get the other guys on this team to contribute even a little bit like these Mythical beasts, Joe will rocket to the top. However, they do have to figure out how to replace Rashaad Penny after his season ending injury, if they want to make that a reality.

Jona has officially moved in! He's finally done with all the stress of getting married, going on a honeymoon, packing a house and moving. He wil likely enjoy Buffalo, as he was welcomed by heart of the city, Josh Allen, who generously gifted Jona 67 points in a welcome basket from he and Stefon Diggs. Allen has scored more than 28 points in all 5 weeks, and more than 34 points in 4 of 5 weeks. A 67 point head start is typically more than enough to get a win, and this week was no different, as he smoked Gil 116 - 81. Outside of Buffalo, there isn't a whole lot of good things to talk about, but the budget Magician can keep performing the Bills-centered tricks, you won't even need to know who else is starting for the Magic.

If I told you, preseason, that a team with Russell Wilson, Michael Thomas, George Kittle, CMC and Jonathan Taylor would be 1-4, with 2 games under 80 points and a season average of just 99 points, you would think I was crazy. Well, this is crazy then, because that is the reality for Austin and his head-scratching team heading into week 6. Austin lost week 5 by 55 points, primarily because he had 7 of 8 starters score less than 12 points. All the names above make this team a threat to go off any week, but for now, even a #9 ranking feels a bit high.

Anyone seen Gil lately? Does he appear normal? Because it seems like he might be being controlled by someone else's Mind Tricks, as he has lost 3 games in a row, scoring less than 83 points in all 3 games. This team has enough good names on it for that last sentence to be surprising, but yet, here we are. Would I be surprised if this team came out next week and had 140 points? No, and that is because they have the fire power everyone is looking for. However, this team may be the definition of boom or bust, and right now we're seeing the bust. Until these Jedi's get out of their own Minds, Gil will be stuck on an asteroid filled road.

The Mooney Toons flipped the script and ended their 3 game losing streak! The West coast viewers made sure this show wasn't cancelled, as they loved their stars, Adams and Ekeler, showing off with a combined 67 points. After missing last week's episode, David Montgomery came back to his leading role and contributed 18 points of his own to the story. Due to some off-screen events, year 1 character, Kenneth Walker, is poised for a starring role going forward, with Rashaad Penny's season ending injury. Trevor could easily see his ratings rise in the coming weeks.

Game of Jones finds himself in the dungeon after 5 weeks of RBB play, as he lost to Trevor 116 - 81 to fall to 2-3 on the year. Through 5 weeks, Josh has scored 89 or more points just once, which came in week 2. Outside of week 2, Josh has averaged 85 points per game, making him a matchup you circle on the calendar. However, there are multiple boom players on this team, and fantasy football is wild, so the week you circle Josh, could be the week you find yourself in the dungeon in his place.

Yisha had his guys working as a team to Rough Big Jim's Assers, in what was a blue collar win for this squad. With Lamar scoring a fraction of his previous week's output, this team couldn't afford many disappointments, and luckily only Dionte Johnson struggled with Lamar, scoring 4 points on the day. The rest of the team scored between 11 and 22 points, which was enough for the win to move to 3-1 on the year. A week like this, plus a good Lamar, is what keeps this team at the top of the charts.

Boy oh boy, what a week! Usually Over The Pants doesn't do the trick, but this week, Over The Pants was more than enough, blasting out 192 points in a 107 point margin of victory over the Dingles. When your lowest scoring positional player has 19 points, you're likely in for a big win, and that's exactly what happened here, as all but Cooper Kupp had one or more TDs on the week. Big Jockensen led the way with a massive 8 for 179 and 2 TD performance. If this can be replicated on a smaller scale, this team gonna win some more games.

The Big Dingles never had a chance in this one. Losing by a full 107 points is something you just have to accept, throw the week away and move onto the next matchup. However, Jerry may need to take some insight away from this game, as he had 4 players score less than 8 points. Even Deebo, who is arguably the most fun to watch and manliest player in the league, couldn't carry this team to a victory like he did for his NFL team.The highs are still coming for Jerry, so he remains in the top 3.

After Justin Jefferson scored his worst fantasy score in his career in week 3, The Wolfpack was forced to search for their Alpha Wolf. Turns out, he was waiting in London for the rest of his Pack to arrive, as Jefferson showed off overseas to the tune fof 150 yards and a TD. The Pack is only as strong as their weakest Wolf, which may hold this team back a bit, as ElderWolf Cordarrelle Patterson landed on IR with a knee injury. The RB injury paired with Kyle Pitts' standard 3 point performances may make the next 4 weeks tough. For now, Ryan earns the #4 spot.

The Jedis are the good ones right? I'm not so sure after Gil used his Mind Tricks to split his week 2 score of 150 points into weeks 3 & 4, scoring 82 and 70 points respectively. This game was likely out of reach anyway, as the margin of loss was 46 points, but the biggest blows came from in-game injuries to Tua and Javonte, who totaled just 7.9 points before exiting. QBs can be replaced, but Javonte's season ending ACL injury leaves a big hole in Gil's lineup that can hopefully be filled by up and comer Dameon Pierce, who ripped off a 75 yard TD run against the Chargers. There are questions surrounding this team, so we may find next week that this #5 ranking was a bit generous.

The self-proclaimed Mayor has Titty City on the board! It took 4 weeks and the threat of bras for the Mayor to give Titty City what they wanted. Jacube was without his star WR St. Brownie, and benched Josh Jacobs' 37 points, and he still put up 139 points in his win over Trevor. Jacob is likely the dark horse near the bottom of the standings, as he has the 3rd highest points scored in the league. I would expect this team to continue to climb up the standings and the rankings.

Game of Jones was Cooking on the Hill this week, but forgot to invite most of his guys to the outing, as Tyreek Hill and Brandin Cooks were really the only bright spots on this team this week, totaling 38 of the team's 87 points. Josh has too many good names to be scoring 87 points, including Amari Cooper, Najee Harris and Darren Waller, who all together contributed just 15 points. Josh may be losing Antonio Gibson to Brian Robinson, but he at least has the return of JK Dobbins to look forward to. Maybe just a couple of name swaps is all Josh needs to get this train moving.

The Urban Myth rode the Yeti through Seattle and erased his 0-2 start just like that, as he slayed Game of Jones 129 - 87 in week 4. Joe's team jumped on the back of Derrick Yeti and his 26 points, until they jumped on the real cheap train, Rashaad Penny, who came cruising past on his way to 33 points. After the 58 spot left by those two, nobody even noticed DK Metcalf's 19 point game, or worse, the 12 points Joe brought back from LA (Stafford with 10 and Akers with 2). As always, this team has too much star power to be contained, but it will need to continue to have similar performances to keep the wins rolling in.

If this team is Taylor Made, it's no wonder they're 1-3 to start the year, as the consensus #1 RB heading into the year has just 28 points over the last 3 weeks, including his worst performance yet, being a rough 20 carries for 42 yards and a fumble (5.55 points). While this team has massive potential with CMC, Taylor, Kittle and apparently Jamaal Williams, they will need help elsewhere to get back to .500. However, this team earned its first win of the season, so they can celebrate the win while they move back from #5 to #9.

Big Jim recently relocated his Twins to Orlando, or was it Tampa Bay? Jim started not 1, not 2, not 3, but 4 Tampa Bay players this week, which ultimately capped the upside of the overal roster, notably only getting a combined 3.47 points from Julio and the DST (which had 2 of those points). The real let down was Mark Andrews, who could have won the week, had he scored even half of his last week's total. Big Jim has a good foundation, but a few layers are missing to really push this team far up the ranks.

The Budget Magician strikes again! Jona the Great successfully made his fantasy points disappear. Scoring just 59.99 points this week, the Magic's highlight, or lowlight if you will, was the 0.26 total points from the RB position (Gordon with -0.90 and Hubbard with 1.16). Without Swift and Mitchell, and with a struggling Michael Pittman, this team will have a hard time staying above .500. And staying near .500 may not even be achievable if the Bills stack can't get back to elite status. This week, Jona the Great turned a #9 ranking into a #11.

The Mooney Toons are on the verge of being cancelled after losing 3 straight weeks while averaging just 90 points over that span. The West coast viewers kept this show in business, as they loved their characters' big roles this week, as in Ekeler and Herbert combining for 60 points and Adams casually scoring 16 without a TD. Even with his West coast fandom, Trevor will have to boost the ratings everywhere else, if he wishes to stay on the air.

The Monday Night Football curse may be shifting its focus elsewhere, as Yish now has 2 MNF wins to 1 MNF loss through 3 weeks this year. While Yisha's roster is loaded top to bottom, with names Barkley, Brown, Sutton and Connor moving the team along, there is really only one name that needs to be mentioned. That name is MVP race Lamar Jackson, who has 129 points in just 3 games, including two 47+ point weeks. If Lamar can keep up this pace and consistently give a healthy cushion for the rest of the team, Yish will be Roughing everyone's Assers this year.

The ones who hate having Dingleberries are the same ones who hate this ranking of the DingleJerries. Losing to the #2 ranked team in last week's rankings have Jerry and Yish swapping spots heading into week 4. Despite the loss in week 3, Jerry remains in the top 2, after posting a 122 point week on the backs of Jalen Hurts' 33 points and Robinson's 24 points. The 122 point performance may just be Jerry's normal output, which makes him a team to stay away from.

3 weeks, 3 wins! A hot start to the 2022 season for the the reigning champion, as Jimmie slipped just Over the Pants on this one and defeated Jona 110 - 101. Hollywood was in Arizona this week, as Marquise Brown had a career high 17 targets against the Rams, turning the opportunity into 14 catches for 140 yards. The big names are doing all the work under the Pants, as Chubb and Kupp continue to smash each week, and if the rest of the squad can keep it going, this team should be competitive week in and week out.

The Jedi Mind Tricks got into their own head in week 4. After defeating Joe by more than double his score, Gil figured he could spare some points against Game of Jones, cutting nearly 70 points from his week 3 total. The over compensation led to a Game of Jones victory (88 - 82), sending the Gil into the Dark Side of 1-2. Gil's WRs still appear to be top tier, but will they all be firing at the same time and even in the starting lineup? Gil will head back Dagobah for some more training prior to his week 4 battle with Austin.

One of two teams remaining in their week 3 slot, Austin comes in at #5, even with an 0-3, 12th place position. Austin's 76 points in week 3 was 30 points below his next lowest score, which was 20 points below his highest score, so is this a trend or just a two week dip? Austin truly needs his RBs that are supposed to perform, perform better than those who are backups, such as Jamaal Williams nearly outscoring CMC and Talyor combined (27 - 29 points). If this is only to be a two week dip, Austin will need Rusty Wilson, who has back to back weeks of less than 14 points, and rest of the roster to follow in William's footsteps. If not, Austin will be looking up at the #5 spot from way down below.

The Wolfpack were on fire this week! Except the fire was almost completely on the bench, as all but one player scored more than 13 points on the sidelines this week. Fortunately for Ryan, the prey was not hard to capture, as he only had to surpass 76.34 points to get the kill on Austin. With this type of boom/bust and perceived talent, Ryan will have to tap into his unexplainably good fantasy skills to make the right start/sit decisions each week going forward.

The self-proclaimed Mayor's approval rating is close to zero right now, as Titty City can't believe they're winless heading into week 4. To make things worse, one of Jacube's top starters this week was none other than Cardinals WR, Gregory Dortch with 14 points, while his two benched RBs (Rhamondre and Herbert) rode 54.70 points worth of pine. The pieces of the puzzle are in the box, but it's up to the Mayor to put them in the right spots. The citizens of Titty City are threatening to put their tops back on if things don't turn around quickly.

Game of Jones underwhelms, but gets the win anyway over Gil and his even more underwhelming Mind Tricks (88 - 82) in week 3. Through 3 weeks, this team is one of the hardest to determine what the future looks like, as inconsistency, boom/bust, average results and big names all just cover this team in a big cloud of uncertainty. Are they Hill's 42 points or 4 point weeks? Are they a standard 20 points out of Rodgers and 14 points out of Harris? Or are they going to be led by a dominating Amari Cooper in Cleveland? If the highs for this team happen at the same time, they could be a top 3-5 team, but if the results of some of these big names are the standard this year, Josh will be playing in the unimportant Games late in the year.

The wedding is over. Jona is back from the Honeymoon, and the newlywed glow has gone away. The Magic kept their pants on, but still dropped their first game of the 2022 season to Jimmie, who does his work Over The Pants, 110 - 101. The 101 points was a full 38 points behind his next lowest score this year, showing that Josh Allen, and his 35 points, may not be able to drag this team wherever he wants after all. The biggest concern here is actually the loss of another starting RB, even if it's temporary, as Swift appears to be in line to miss a few weeks with an ankle injury. Down Mitchell and Swift, Jona will now have to lean on Melvin Gordan and....... who? Either the Buffalo duo will need to turn it up even higher, or Jona will have to pull some Magic out of his booty to fill the RB gap.

Big Jim and his Big Twins are on a two game win streak, after he entered Titty City and showed the citizens what he's working with, slapping Jacube 112 - 103. Jim, not known for making many trades, made a pre-draft trade for Mark Andrews, and that trade alone may keep Jim in playoff contention all year, as he has back to back 23+ point games from the TE position. Rookie WR Chris Olave may have had his breakout game, catching 9 of 13 targets for 147 yards. If Olave can take the leap to starter, and the rest of the Twins pick it up a bit, this team will keep swinging up the rankings.

Joe was feeling sick from his 0-2 start, so he stayed home from school, turned on the Mooney Toons and felt immediately better. If there is a recipe for curing the 0-2 blues, it's your opponent scoring less than 55 points on the week. Winter is coming, which means so is Derek Yeti, who looked like his usual self in week 3, scoring 26 points, aka just under half of Trevor's total. The big pieces of Joe's team look ready to take off, and if they do, this 0-2 start will be a thing of the past.

Oh boy. If this ranking is a shock, you clearly didn't see last week's games. Trevor's weekly show, the Mooney Toons, only had one viewer this week, and it was Joe, who absolutely loved the hilarious storyline with a surprise ending of 53 points. While this team has a couple big names, but they're hidden behind injuries and poor performances. Thus far, the boom names have been grounded, but if they do, Trevor's Toons may, may be able to climb back out of the 12th spot.

The Dingles Fought their way to the top of the rankings. After taking multiple home run swings during the draft, those picks have landed beyond the fence through 2 weeks. Hurts, Clyde, Robinson and Kirk have been dominating thus far, which has kept studs like Kamara, Etienne and McLaurin on the bench. The DingleJerries are at the top, waiting to be plucked by the rest of us.

Roughing the Asser took a sack on MNF, putting them their booty, after a combined 80.93 points (7 TDs) from Allen and Diggs ended this team's perfect season hopes. Yisha still has plenty of things to be happy about going forward though, as Lamar Jackson has 81.39 points through 2 weeks, proving that the NFL may want to consider capping contracts at 1 year deals. With a top notch starting lineup, will we get to see some of Yisha's youth find the field after rookie WRs Wilson and Dotson balled out in week 2 (27.6 and 16.9 points)?

Big man Jona, gets married, goes to Bora Bora for his honeymoon and comes back riding the high of a 2-0 top scoring team in the league start to the season. Everything is falling Jona's way lately, and if he can keep the Magic between Allen and Diggs, who have more than 147 points together through only 2 weeks, Jona may not need any other tricks up his sleeve. However, the ancillary pieces might need to show up before Jona takes the elusive #1 spot in the power rankings.

Jimmie's Over The Pants Handoff had way too big fo a Chubb in week 2, as Mr. Chubby himself scored 3 TDs on his way to 34 fantasy points). Kyler Murray and Cooper Kupp both turned things on in the 2nd half of their matchups, going off for 31 and 28 points respectively. While you may prefer under the pants, this Over The Pants Handoff may have what it takes to get you excited all year long.

Jonathan Taylor and CMC. Need I say more? This week, yes, because the top two RBs in the league only managed to come up with 26 points together in what appeared to be great matchups. Rusty Wilson is still shaking off the rust in Denver, but he will have to do it sooner than later, as the Broncos have looked horrible, which has translated to some rough fantasy outputs. Austin's investment in the second coming of Samuel appears to be paying off, as Curtis Commanded another 20.5 points in week 2. While there are many questions around this team, a couple of good bounces has them at 2-2 in a hurry.

Holy moly! The force was strong with this team in week 2, as they absolutely carved up Joe's team, winning by more than double Joe's score (150-68). When you have 3 Jedis (Wentz, Waddle and Jones), each scoring 34+ points, it is no contest against a group of regulars (or Myths for that matter). Gil appears to have plenty of WR options, and as long as he picks the right 3 every week, he should be in for a happy season.

Tough week for Ryan and the Wolfpack, being an example of how you can't base next week off the previous week, as Justin Jefferson and Cordarrelle Patterson each scored a fraction of their week 1 totals (36 down to 8 and 26 down to 6). Ryan is still embodying the Pack mentality, as he has two players from Miami, Minnesota, Dallas and Atlanta, and when you stack players, you either win as a Pack and lose as a Pack. This week was a Pack loss (120-79).

The self-proclaimed Mayor just passed a law to officially rename brownies, St. Brownies, in Titty City. Amon-Ra is REALLY good. He now has 17 catches for 180 yards and 3 TDs on 24 targets through two weeks. Jacube needs some of these other big names (Mixon, Jacobs, Evans, Thielen) to take notice and eat their St. Brownies if they want to get this team on the winning track.

The Mooney who? The only funny character on this week's episode was the leading role, Darnell Mooney, who managed to play a complete game and score 0.10 points, making his two episode total 1.40 points. Despite a Bateman bomb, Herbert's heroics and a monster effort from Montgomery, this team could not get past the Jim's Big Twins, losing a close one 105.5 - 103.96. The talent is there, but will it all hit at the same time enough times this year? We'll have to Toon in next week to see what the writers have in store.

Game of Jones came into the week 0-1 and was not playing around with the idea of going 0-2, so he just attached his entire team to the back of Tyreek Hill and prayed. Luckily for Josh, Tyreek wasn't playing Games either and went nuts with 190 yards, two 40+ TDs, leading both his NFL team and Josh's fantasy team to a week 2 victory. While Hill has this stratosphere breaking talent, Game of Jones will need some help from his other starters if he wants to win on a consistent basis.

Yikes. Less than 70 points when your original projections had you winning the game. That would be a tough pill to swallow for anyone, including the Joe, as they lose 150-68 to Gil's Mind Tricks. Mother Goose has been on the hunt, and she finally caught her first victim, as Donovan "not a man of the" Peoples-Jones had the first goose egg in a starting lineup of the 2022 season. Joe has lots of questions to ask and answer quickly, before an 0-2 start compounds to an 0-4 start.

Big Jim and his Big Twins were more of a medium this week, scoring just over 100 points, but the medium sized jock strap was enough to KO Trevor on his weekly show (winning 105 - 103). Big Jim was propped up by big games from Mark Andrews and the Tampa Bay DST, who outscored all but Andrews and Carr this week (16.52 points). This team's couple of studs will keep them in games most weeks, but they may need to make a move or two to really fill out that XL jock strap needed to win consistently in this league.

The #1 ranked team came out and Roughed the Asser big time, putting up the 2nd highest score on the week of 138.71. Yisha stole Saquon from everyone in the back end of the draft, and he looked amazing, putting up 194 total yards and a TD. And the addition of TE Everett only boosts this squad's potential. I would not like to be the next Asser in line to play this team.

The FightingDingles went with a heavy Jaguar roster this season, but decided to sit the to Jacksonville stars, Robinson and Kirk, for the dud Etienne. Despite the whiff, Jerry Hurts-ed his way to a victory over Big Jim with the help of gamble RB CEH, who dropped 22 on the doubters. If Jerry can pick the right Jaguars this week, he may be able to stay in the top 2.

The TaylorMade Christians drew the short straw, scoring the 3rd highest but playing the 2nd highest scoring team in week 1, and losing 138-125. It's no secret that this team is Made by Taylor and CMC, but the RB foundation apparenty spreads even further, including Michael Carter and Jamaal Williams (15 & 17 points). if the WRs, and the $51 man Curits Samuel himslef, can keep up, Austin will be running back to the #1 spot.

Wedding weekend luck or superstar status? Week 1 was full of crazy games, and Jona Jaworked his Magic to be a part of those games, having both Pittman and Swift explode for a combined 52 points. Jona said he was moving to Minnesota, but he meant Buffalo. His Allen/Diggs stack is arguably the most dangerous duo in fantasy, making this team a force early on. The loss of Eli Mitchell will need to be taken care of for this team to reach its full potential.

Over the Pants Handoff got a little too excited on TNF with Kupp's 26 points, and came down from the climax the rest of the weekend,as only Murray tallied more than 20 points. This team did surpass the century mark, but the win was not flattering, defeating the name brand Game of Jones 106-84. This team has the upside needed for success, but that potential means nothing if it never comes to fruition. We shall see if week 2 looks any different.

Ater 6 winless seasons, Gil sold his Taco Truck and traded it in for some Mind Tricks hoping to change the course of history forever. The Jedi Mind Tricks had their powers working early this weekend, getting the first TD of the 2022 season on a Gabe Davis reception. Gil ran into the Dark Side on SNF, however, only managing a total of 10.71 points from Dak and Lamb. With Wentz at the helm (oh boy), and the rest of the studs on this team, week 2 could be night and day.

The Mooney Toons enjoyed their new characters in week 1. Senor Adams and Big Herbs got on the big screen and took over the show, putting up 56 points together in their new roles. It may be too early to say who made who, but Adams was amazing, while Rodgers was... not. The Mooney Toons will be looking for a bounce back game from the Bears, while relying on the star power of Adams and Herbert. It seems almost impossible for this team not to be competitive all year.

The Wolfpack, for the 3rd straight year, were lead by THE alpha wolf, Justin Jefferson, who puts on the cloak of invisibility each play before catching a wide open pass for 1,000 yards and a TD. Even crazier, for the 2nd year in a row, Ryan has dropped a load of FAAB on a SF RB ($43 on my name is Jeff after dropping $80+ on Mitchell last season). This team is filled with big names, and the Wolves will eat. #8 is just a stop on the way.

The self-proclaimed Mayor has a new Chief of Staff, Patrick Mahomes, in Titty City after bringing in 43.45 points in week 1. Titty City was rented out by Jona for his wedding weekend 139 point bonanza, easily handling the Mayor by 30 points (despite being the 4th highest scoring team). Elder statesman, Keenan Allen, went down with broken hammy, making Jacube's start/sit decisions almost too easy, which means Titty City might be on the rise after week 2.

Who was the bigger Urban Myth in week 1? The Yeti, who only managed 10 points against the GIANTS, or Cam Akers, who only scored 0.3 points after being hyped up all offseason? Even though Joe has two of the most unfair human beings on his team (Henry and Metcalf), the two could only contribute 15 points in the team's week 1 111-93 loss to the Wolfpack. The 10th place ranking is a result of this league having too many good teams. This team will absolutely be a force in the future.

Not a whole lot of good things to say about Game of Jones' week 1 performance. When your squad scores 84 points, and it's the optimal lineup, you just have to shrug it off and plan for week 2. The names on this starting roster should be enough to realize the boom games waiting to happen.

Big Jim and The Twins got too excited and zipped up a bit too quicky, and ruined his 2022 season debut. Outside of the two big names, Dalvin Cook and Leonard Fournette, this team left all its potential for future weeks. There is still plenty of star talent ready to roll for the Twins, so don't be surprised if Big Jim flops himself on your team in the near future.

The 2018 CHAMP enters the 2022 season as the odds on favorite to be the 2022 champion, ranking #1 in the initial power rankings. With studs up and down the starting lineup, and a bench filled with talent, Yisha will be looking to be certified delicious for the 2nd time.

The Dingles hosted the largest yard sale event of the 2021 season, selling off as many players as possible in preparation for the 2022 season. Jerry turned all that draft capital into a starting lineup that can take down any team in the league.

This is an even-year, so Gil should expect to finish outside the playoffs for the 4th time (7th in 2016 and 2018, 8th in 2020, while finishing 3rd in 2017, 19, and 21). However, Gil's starting lineup has arguably no holes in it. This #3 ranking suggests this lineup may break the pattern for this franchise.

Trevor owned the illustrious 1st overall pick in the 2022 draft, and he capitalized on the available top-end talent (Ekeler, Adams, Monty, Herbs). Trevor also prioritized his team's name over everything, as he kept Darnell Mooney to slot in as his #2 WR. After missing the playoffs for the first time last season, Trevor has a good opportunity to jump right back into the playoffs this year.

The self-proclaimed Mayor is back for another year at the helm of Titty City. Despite the lack of quality play from this city, Jacob put together a high-end starting squad with a few bench players that can slot in at any time. If the big names produce at big levels, Titty City may finally find the postseason.

THE CHAMP IS HERE! 2x Champion, reigning trophy winner, all-time great Jimmie is ready to get the 2022 action started Over the Pants. There's no question that Jimmie's draft did not go according to plan, but he's still hopeful his top talent can carry this team to a 2nd consecutive championship.

Jona and his Magic made their first playoff appearance in 2021, and he used that same strategy for the 2022 draft by running it back and keeping Allen and Diggs at tremendous draft value. Jona added incredible upside talent in Swift, Pittman and Robinson II, and if that upside is realized, he will be in the top 6 at the end of 2022 as well.

Perennial top 3 RBB manager, Josh had the opportunity to draft in the first half of the draft for the first time in years. Josh's 6th draft slot netted him a starting lineup that includes Rodgers, Hill, Najee and Waller. Josh also jumped on Gibson's negative news dip, and may be able to ride his RB talent to a lengthy win streak. Don't be surprised if this team climbs the ranks quickly.

If there's an underrated team on this list, it's this one. While this squad can likely be carried by King Henry, Kelce and Chase, it can really take off up the charts if Penny, Metcalf and Akers all hit as well. Despite going all in on last year, Joe built a team that can do damage in 2022.

A 10 game win streak to end the regular season in 2021 had Austin ordering his championship name plate for the coveted RBB trophy, but we all know how that story ended. This year, Austin's story began with a draft day trade with Gil which secured arguably the two best RBs in fantasy football (Taylor and CMC) on Austin's roster. Giving up early picks forced Austin to be savvy with the middle rounds. If players like Wilson, Thomas and Woods splash, Austin may very well have another 10 game win streak ahead.

Even though this is fantasy football, Ryan found a way to sneak baseball into the power rankings, as Ryan missed another draft for his baseball team once again this year. Despite drafting from the dugout, Ryan managed to put together a quality starting lineup. However, his autodraft during a live draft "plan" failed to produce any real depth on this roster. If anyone can overcome a less than stellar draft, it would be Ryan and his oddly good fantasy skills.

Jim had the #2 pick this year, and drafted a very good squad. Don't let the #12 rank fool you, this team has the potential to be undefeated next month. As long as Jim doesn't have to dip into his bench too often, he will be a competitive team with everyoe and anyone in the league.

2023.notes: Despite the 14 QBs on Jacob's bench, he basically didn't start one after Purdy's 4 point horrendous outing. But as they have said multiple times in Titty City this season, "No QB, no problem", on their way to a pretty easy 27 point win. Everything is going right for the self-provlaimed Mayor right now, so all Jacube can do is hope they keep rolling, as he is matched up with a red-hot CMC group in the finals. In only his 2nd playoff appearance, Jacube has the chance at his first championship.

The division setup has certainly helped Austin walk his way into his first finals appearance. After a free round 1, Austin got matched up with arguably the best team, The Wolfpack, in what looked like it would be a shootout. Instead, Ryan put out his 3rd worse point total (88), which was also just his 4th time under 100 points this season. With Ryan's low output and Austin's explosion of points, the CMCs didn't even sweat a bit in the semis. Jacube is now the final obstacle in the way of Austin's first RBB title.

The last remaining champion falls. The depressing 88 point performance was a clear way to go down, as Ryan was defeated by nearly 60 points to Austin. Despite having a lineup with no apparent holes, the only player with a quality week 16 stat line was QB Jalen Hurts and his 27 points. Ryan will have to wait another year for a chance at his 3rd title. And if history repeats itself, Ryan will be playing in it in 2024, as he has never gone more than two years in a row without showing up in the finals (last apperance 2021).

After missing the playoffs in back to back seasons, Joe snuck into the #6 seed in 2023. Joe was able to take down fellow Burnt Biscuit, Jona, in round 1, but fell far from a victory against Jacob in the semifinals. Though anything short of a championship sucks, the 3rd or 4th place finish should feel good for Joe after a wild up and down, injury plagued season. Joe will take on Ryan for a chance at his first 3rd place finish.
Hooray, I won 5th place!! Said no one ever. A disappointing end to a promising season. 2024 here we come.
Not even a 6th place finish can bring Jona down now that Jonah Jr. is here! Congrats Jona on your 6th place medal and, so much more importantly, the new team member!

Game of Jones continued the ping-pong game going, after a 150-70-150 sandwhich. Josh may be considering a name change, after Amari Cooper just torched the league for 50 points in week 16, securing a top 2 pick in 2024. Hopefully Josh can stick to ping or pong in week 17 and keep the high scores rolling, as he has never drafted from the #1 slot. However, Josh has now become the only team to play in back to back RBB title games (2018-2020) and TB title games (2022-2023).

This year has been nothing short of amazing for Trevor. Yes, he's playing in the toilet bowl, but having won more than a game or two would have been considered a good season after the estate sale of 2022. Trevor went from bottom dwlling losers to real playoff championship contenders to sellers to almost might make playoffs to the TB final. Trev will be hoping to pick 1st for the 2nd time in his RBB career with a win over Game of Jones.

After 65 points from his WRs (Higgins, Olave & Flowers), Big Jim was feeling good about his chances to advance to th TB finals, but sometimes you get lined up against something incredible. Week 16, Big Jim went up against Amari Cooper and his 50 point, Browns' single-game receiving record performance. After Cleveland wrapped up their victory, Jim was planning for his 9th/10th place matchup. This will be his 3rd time in the 9/10 game, and the Twins are undefeated in this particular matchup.

The Big Lig had a Big whiff and watched the 1st overall pick run away with George Pickens' 38 points. Gil lost a tight one to Trev (114-104), all while Pickens' 38 points sat on his bench. Gil has 3 TB final appearances, in which he is 2-1, but he has yet to play in the 9/10 game. Maybe a new draft position will help this team in 2024!

Yish had to hold his breath for a minute, as the Dingles put up a bit of a battle. Jerry hadn't touched the 90s since week 11, when he scored 91. Luckily for Yish, he did enough to earn the 5th pick. This season is the perfect example of how a snowflake turns into a snowball, as bad things just kept compounding until the Assers went from playoff contenders to 11th placers. 2024 is a new year for all of us!

Jerry did it! I think we as a group should buy Jerry a #12 jersey as a momento to this wild season. It is over Jerbear! 2024 will undoubtedly be a much more pleasant season for the dingles. See you at the draft, this time before the 5th round!

An unimpressive week from either team in this matchup, Ryan took advantage of the Buddies' poor showing by getting the 124-101 ticket to advance. Ryan was led by an "ill" Jalen Hurts (26) and a "why not" Sam LaPorta (27), who appeared to be the 12th man on the Lions' offense all game long against Denver. Additionally, Mostert is on a record setting year, so don't be surprised if he ends up winning Ryan the championship.

Jacube was lucky to get the bye, and that's all I'll say about that. However, Jacube's bye only saved someone from getting absolutely destroyed by the storm in Titty City, as the Titters squeezed out a massive 148 points WITH Tyreek Hill in the starting lineup but on the real-life bench. It happens all too often, but hopefully Jacube did not squeeze out all of mother's milk too soon.

Austin snuck into the bye week under the division technicality, which in turn only helped Joe advance (and hurt the Tuddies), as Austin would have defeated both Jona and Joe had he been forced to play this past week. Austin gets a crack at the 2-time title winner in week 16 for a chance to play in his first ever championship showdown.

If Joe wasn't a fan of divisions before, I'd imagine he is now, as the seeding allowed for Joe to advance to the second semifinal matchup of his RBB career. With the Wolfpack and the Buddies getting moved back to seeds 4 & 5 respectively, to make room for the lesser CMCs and Baby Jaws of the world, Joe drew a matchup with division mate Jona in round 1. The two battled it out for an incredible finish, with Joe edging out Jona by just 1.11 points. Joe gets a much (much) harder test in week 16, when he faces off with the red hot Titties.
If you're on this list, I hate you: - Jared Goff - The Detroit Lions organization - Mike McDaniel - Dak Pooscott

Baby Jaws, for the 2nd time in 3 years, has made a round 1 exit from the RBB playoffs. Jona was gifted the matchup with Joe in week 15, but he could not execute, falling 1.11 points short of the Myth and a semifinal appearance. Even worse, Jona had a massive performance by Zamir White just sitting at the end of his bench, which could have turned the tables in this one. Finishing the season one week early will give Jona a little extra time to celebrate his first Burnt Biscuit division title.

You know the guy who walks into the small town bar carrying his own collapsible pool cue, ready to destroy any garbage competition in his path? That's Big Jim, and the Toilet Bowl is his bar. He knows that table like the back of his hand. Every nook and cranny, where to shoot for a favorable bounce and the way the table leans just enough to get some extra roll when you need it. He comes in to the consolation bracket with experience, expertise and a home field advantage, and Yisha felt every bit of that in week 15, losing 148-102. The Twins are on their way to a top 4 pick, and may even make it a top 2 if they can keep the bar tab open through Christmas.

The Big Lig got the 3rd bye of the toilet bowl, but faced off against Jerry for the tradition of things and walked into the TB semis on a 118-61 win. Gil's investment in Ty Chandler may finally start paying off, as the RB dominated in week 15 in a way that hasn't been seen since the young Dalvin Cook days. Gil gets to try and take down Breece Lightning, who is coming off a week of real rest.

Game of Jones rode his week 14 high score of 158 points to a week 15 bye in the toilet bowl. The big week 14 was crucial for Josh, as his only week 15 victory would have come against Jerry, scoring just 79 points on the week (exactly half of his week 14 output). Josh now faces off in a semifinal matchup with Big Jim to try and guarantee a top 2 pick in 2024.

One year removed from the semifinals, roverT is playing in a different version of the same game, as he takes on the Big Lig for a shot at the first overall pick in 2024. Trevor, after selling and almost stumbling into a playoff position, came away with the #1 toilet bye in week 15. Luckily for Trev, the Lightning was not needed, because it wasn't coming either way, as Trev's squad managed just 87 points on the week (enough to beat only Josh and Jerry). Playing against somebody vs nobody is always harder, so we'll see if Trev can take down a real human this week!

Yish is new to this territory, missing the playoffs for the first time since 2016, ending the 2nd longest active (and all time) playoff streak in league history. Yish is not new to the first round loss however, as Yish spent 3 consecutive seasons battling for the 5th place title. Yish drew the short straw in week 15 and was matched up with the high score among active teams. The Assers are now virtually guaranteed the 11th place sticker for 2023.

After 16 consecutive weeks at #12, Jerry has one last chance to move up in the rankings. I actually thought that Jerbear might have waited and saved his big win for round 1 and pull off a bug upset to finally get out of the 12 spot. But alas, here we are again at #12 after the Dawgs slapped together 61 points. The Dingles will try and snag one final win against a stumbling Asser squad. But for the good of the people, Jerry wants to lose this one to give us a record setting full season in the same #12 jersey.

The Wolfpack lose a big week 14 matchup and with it, the bye and the first Bun Spreaders title were awarded to Jacube. Week 14 was just the 3rd time this season Ryan failed to score 100+ points. Wtih Diggs, Chase and LaPorta each scoring just 4 points, Raheem Mostert scored more than double all three of them combined. Ryan's reward for a 10-4 season? A road to the championship that likely includes taking down the #3 and #1 teams in the league.

The top two teams get back to back matchups while also playing their 3rd matchup of the season! The Tuddies took down The Wolfpack in week 14, clearing the path for Jacube to take the #1 overall seed. Given the division standings, and the wild events that saw the top 3 teams in the league come from the Bun Spreaders division, The Buddies ended up with the #5 seed. The #5 lined the TBs across from Ryan for the 3rd time this season. A very unfortunate road to the championship, but if it can be done, it will be the most rewarding.

Austin lucks his way into the bye week after winning a division full of toilet bowl participants. Austin handled his business against Trevor in a week 14 matchup that ended up being much closer than most would have suspected. With the win, Austin finished the regular season at 9-5 and earned the bye as the #2 division winner. Jumping from #4 to #2 makes Austin 1 win away from his first championship appearance.

The self-proclaimed Mayor has Titty City in uncharted waters after taking home the Bun Spreaders division title and sitting atop the league as the #1 seed heading into the playoffs. Jacube had a relatively easy matchup with Big Jim in week 14, helping him fall into 1st after Ryan battled his way to a loss. Jacube will apparently be trying to gather himself and prepare for his semifinal matchup in any way possible, as he has added and dropped just about every bottom end and backup QB available. Jacube gets to enjoy the topless party in Titty City during his week 15 time off.

Joe went from seller to buyer to toilet bowl to playoffs all in the final 4 weeks of the season. Joe even came with 5 points of winning the Burnt Biscuits division title, but instead handed the title to Jona the great in a 106-101 loss. The Myth are making their first postseason appearance since 2020 when he went home with a 6th place finish. Joe's best finish came back in 2019, when he almost tasted the biggest biscuit in a championship game against Game of Jones. Joe will have to go through Jona and Jacube if he wants another shot at the title.

Baby Jaws is a champion! Jona put all the other burnt biscuits in their place and has become the first division winner of the group. The bragging rights came down to a week 14 win against Joe by just 5 points. Jona won't have to wait long to defend his title, as he gets a back to back matchup with Joe in week 15. Hopefully Jona can win the important game, as a division championship means nothing in comparison to the big one.

Game of Jones let everyone in the playoffs know how lucky they are that he will be playing in the toilet bowl this year, after a dominant league-high score performance against Yish in week 14. Everything went great for Josh, as all but two players scored 17 plus points, for a grand total of 158 big ones. The victory secured Josh a guaranteed top 4 pick in the 2024 draft, as he can sit back and relax during his round 1 bye.

The wheels have been falling off for some time now for Yish, and they may be just one game away from falling all the way off. Yish was once in a position to likely make the playoffs, but a 4 game losing streak has not only taken the playoffs away, but also removed him from a toilet bowl bye. During the last 4 weeks, Yish has only broken 90 points once (94), making his decline happen right at the wrong time. The Assers are taking a pounding right now with injuries, bad matchups and poor play, and unless week 15 is a turnaround week, Yish may find himself finishing the season a week early.

The Big Lig was one game away from the playoffs, and points away from the round 1 toilet bowl bye. Unfortunately for Gil, he had a brutal week 14 showing, while Trevor balled out and secured the bye. Luckily for Gil, he basically earned the bye by matching up with the Dingles in round 1. The matchup is a rematch of week 14, in which Gil took down Jerry 73-62. Week 15 will more than likely be a much wider margin for the Big Lig than week 14.

Breece did enough to miss the playoffs but earn the toilet bowl bye, after a few late season wins. The 6-8 regular season record was about 5 more wins than anyone expected, so this already has to feel like a win of a season for Trev. Already guaranteed a top 4 pick, Trevor can feel a bit better about missing the playoffs for just the 3rd time in his RBB career.

Big Jim was once a team to watch in 2023, but after a long 5 game losing streak, Jim finds himself just one game above the season-long #12 Jerdawgs at 3-11. The Twins are in familiar territory however, as they have now missed the playoffs in 5 consecutive years, the longest streak in league history. Jim will have to pull out something big in order to flop on down to the toilet semis.

We re here again. Jerry berry comes in at #12 after a season of disappointment. Despite being the #12 team the entire season, Jerry actually had 2-3 more wins than anyone expected, including a win over yours truly. Jerry hasn't touched triple digits since week 1 (104), which is an un-fact-checked record of most double digit scores in a single season. Jerry will be hoping he saved up just enough points all season to get anymore wins and climb up the 2024 draft board.

Ryan is the number 1 team again this week, yada yada yada, you know the drill. But seriously, week 13 was wild for the Wolfpack. Four different players had 25+ points (those players alone won the matchup), and he more than doubled Big Jim's output. We have seen Ryan's team lay an egg this season (even after the deadline), and that is likely what it will take to get a win against him.

Austin is coming into form at the right time. A few slick moves have taken his team from pretty good to really freakin good. Acquiring Lamb by way of Ekeler and Kirk may just end up being the move that we look back on as the league winning move. If Bijan turns into the real deal this season, Austin may be the only team capable of taking down Ryan. After a blowout win over Josh in week 13, Austin locked up the Gravy Goons division and secured the round 1 bye.

The Tuddy Buddies took the L that nailed the coffin shut in week 13, putting an end to their hopes of the #1 overall seed. The loss was even tougher, as they saw superstar in the making, Tank Dell, lose the remainder of the season to a broken leg on a stupid running play of all things. Though the Buddies lost 157, 124, they actually had the points at their disposal to defeat Jacube. With the amount of top end teams in this year's palyoff, it will take the Buddies to score a whole lot of Tuddies to keep up.

The self-proclaimed Mayor stays in the campaign race, adding another victory to his long list of wins this season. The win keeps his chances of the #1 overall seed alive, which is a huge deal, because it's either 1st or 4th for Jacube given how well the Bun Spreaders division has been this season. Overall for Titty City, the seeding likely will not matter because when you start the game with Tyreek already having scored two 40+ yard TDs, you become a very difficult team to beat.

The Malak battle was anything but, as Joe told Jerry "get out of the way you old bag, it's time for a new era of Malaks!", while on his way to smoking Sir Dingles, 116-58. Joe wasn't even concerned with the week at all, so he left Hubbard and Achane's pair of 26 pointers on the bench just to make sure he didn't triple Jerry's score. Things may have to go just right for Joe to make a deep run, but he certainly has the tools to make it happen.

Baby Jona do do do do do do do! Jona was not a happy shark once again this week, falling to 7-6 on the year and putting him into a winner take all game for the 1st ever Burnt Biscuits division title. Actually, if Jona lost, Trevor beat Austin, and Jona somehow was outscored by 61 points by Trevor, Jona could be the proud owner of the #1 seed in the toilet bowl. Week 13 could be a sneak peek into the next few weeks for Jona however, as it felt much more workman-like, rather than star performances, which is the opposite of what is expected out of Mahomes, Kelce, Kupp and Pollard. The Mountain is tall for this Baby, but once your on the floor, anyone can dance!

Yish may just be turning his app off until the start of the postseason, after a rough stretch of 3 weeks has not only taken him out of the playoffs, but has also placed his toilet bowl bye at major risk of being lost. The 90-79 loss to Trevor was tough to watch, outside of the breakout TE McBride looking like a combo of Mark Andrews and TJ Hockenson out there, racking up 20 points. As the regular season comes to an end, Yish has to look back on some moves that may have made or broken his season. The purchase of Walker has not panned out (injuries have been a factor). The gamble on Jefferson may pay off, just much less dividends and at a much later date than hoped. And of course, the Lamb for Ekeler and Kirk deal could be the one that fully submarined this team, as Lamb has continued his dominance, while Ekeler has been unusable and Kirk is now injured. Some years are better than others, and this year is one of the not good ones for Yish.

Game of Jones comes off back to back losses, ending his run at the postseason. It was a tough draw getting Austin in week 13, and there was no surprise when Austin ran away with this one, 142-106. There had been lots of speculation on the lack of moves made by Josh around the deadline, and one has to wonder if he saw the writing on the wall, or if this was a product of the lack of transactions. Either way, Josh is in a must win game in week 14 against Yish if he wants to guarantee himself a top 4 pick in the 2024 draft.

The Big Lig just wants to make the rankings look bad, so he performs well when ranked low, and like hot garbage when ranked high. Ranked #8 in week 13, Gil came out and had a huge win over Baby Jaws Loading 137-113, giving himself a very good chance at earning the toilet bowl round 1 bye and a guaranteed 2024 top 4 pick. Gil is currently dealing with a load of injuries to key players for this lineup, so the bye would be a welcomed week of rest for Big Lig and the gang.

Breece Lightning strikes again! Oh what could have been for this team. Consecutive pooper wins have Trev sitting at 6-7 and within reach of the playoffs (it's a long reach, but he can touch them still!) heading into the final week of the regular season. revorT's last two wins have both come while scoring less than 91 points and a two week total of 173 points. The crazy thing about this is that had Trev not sold the farm for that sweet sweet 2nd rounder, he may have had a chance in those earlier games, possibly putting him inside the playoff line and ready to do some damage. Next year may feel better, but right now it would have to sting knowing that another year slipped away when it may not have needed to.

Big Jim is almost done zipping up those Twins for the regular season, after stuffing another L into those shorts. 4 straight losses have Big Jim stuck at 4-9, which is wild, considering he was 4-5 when the streak began. This team's #2 player, by just 2.1 points behind the #1 player, was the Colts DST, which should say more than enough about the Big guy's week 13 performance. The 2023 calendar has been thrown away, and the Twins are already hanging up the 2024 edition.

Three more rankings after this one Sir Dingle. Three more and the 12 spot will hopefully belong to someone else - possibly Austin after putting his 2023 season on his 2024 credit card. Week 13 marked the 3rd time this season that Jerry took home the lowest scoring team in the league title (a record unmatched this season), while simultaneously scoring the fewest points on the entire season with 58. We said Big Jim threw away his 2023 calendar this week, well Jerry never even had a 2023 version and instead hung up two 2024s instead. Three more rankings Jarbear!

In a week where 5 teams scored more than 130 points, The Wolfpack came away as the highest scoring team by 6 points with a 159-135 win in Titty City. Ryan was out for revenge after losing the #1 spot to Jacube, and Ryan followed through, smoking the Mayor to reclaim the pole position. The Pack was led by Hurts' 38 points, Taylor and Mostert's 24s, and followed up by no less than 9.46 points from anyone in the starting lineup. Ryan does have some injuries to deal with moving forward, however, his depth is about a mile long, so the next-man-up mentality will likely work just fine.

Tittay Citay has been letting those ladies fly free for the last 8 weeks as the Self-proclaimed Mayor enjoyed the sea of areolas during his 8 game win streak. Jacube hasn't touched an L since week 3, marking one of the longest streaks in league history. Unfortunately, week 12 and Ryan reintroduced Jacube to the loss column, while also sending him back to 2nd place overall. It would currently appear that Titty City has too many good players to choose from, making Jacube a strong bet for a deep playoff run.

The CMCs went back from the 2s to the 3s after putting their feet in Yisha's booty all the way up to the knees. The big 130 did Yish dirty, giving Austin a commanding 35 point victory, but the bigger story was Bijan having his best game in his NFL history. Austin has to be riding high after virtually sewing up the Gravy Goons division. With only two weeks left, his chances at the bye appear to be in a real good position.

The rarely ever seen 4-peat!? No, it is rarely seen for a reason, as the most points in any week is difficult enough. The 143 points are good enough for 3rd on the week, which also meant a victory to send the Buddies to 8-4 on the year and into the playoffs. The only hope now is that the Tuddies keep flowing and the Buddies didn't peak too early.

Joe Joe was no hobo in week 12 tossing a definitive 66 point margin, 153-87 win over Yish. The Myth were the 2nd highest scorers in week 12, behind Ryan's 159. Allen and D. Smith went up big, scoring 45 and 21 points respectively, and the three players Joe traded for (Henry, Waddle and Stevenson) combined for 63 points together. The win puts Joe in a very competitive position to make his toilet bowl appearance a distant Myth.

Yisha's booty is not feeling all that well after a second straight loss, in blowout fashion, which has made his playoff hopes paper thin. The only consolations in week 12 for Yish were that he could not have played a winning lineup - having nowhere near the necessary points on the bench - and that some of his playoff competition had rough weeks as well. The hill continues to become a mountain for Yish, but on the upside, people do climb mountains.

Do you know the story of Jona and the Whale? Well, buckle up, because as it turns out, it has nothing to do with this at all. Well, actually, let's try anyway. Four weeks ago, Jona was eaten up by Baby Jaws, his own roster, by way of injures and just poor play in general. Jona remained in that belly for 4 weeks, making little to no changes, only to come away with 4 straight losses. But just when Jona's playoff hopes appeared to be staying in the belly of that Baby Jaws, fantasy sent Jona a Jerry. Jona grabbed onto that Jerry, escaped the poor play and was gifted a second chance at playoffs with a week 12 win. Now, Jona must make sure to not lose out while also not scoring many points, but if he does that, then Jona just may make it to the end of his journey to fulfill his destiny (whatever that is). So I guess the story actually was relevant - scratch the first sentence from your memory, as I cannot delete it once it has been printed.

The Big Lig said thank you for my 5th place ranking, here's 87 points to convince you otherwise. So, here we are at #8 instead. Howell and Pacheco combined for nearly 48 points, meaning that the remaining 6 slots of the team could barely squeeze out 40 points of their own. While this team still has plenty of players than can do it, the odds are typically in favor of it not happening.

Game of which Jones is more like it. If you're looking for a model of consistency, look elsewhere, as Josh now has 5 games of less than 100 points, as well as 5 games above 120 points. Each week seems like a toss up on who is coming to play! Week 12 was the C squad, with 5 players scoring less than 8 points for a grand total of 67 for the week. Josh is on the outside looking in on the playoffs right now, and with a hefty bye week this week and a matchup with Austin, Josh has a gauntlet to fight through to get in.

Got some talent, not sure if they can win - Breece Lightning, go Breece Lighting - don't need a lot of points when your opponent kicks his own shins - Breece Lightning, go Breece Lightning - do we like is? A huh. Does it matter? Nu uh - Breece Lightning! That was made to be sang in your head to the tune of Grease Lightning (if you somehow missed it), and I suggest an appropriate re-read if you did it wrong. Songs aside, Trev got a big win for anyone trying to get into playoffs, as it pushed Josh a little further from the playoff gates. revorT will be hoping to earn a first round pooper bye after, despite two more tough matchups.

Big Jim traded away most of what the ladies care about, forcing him to play with more undersized options.
