But, some say, it's what you do with what you have that matters most, and Big Jim did well given his predicament. 98 points from several backups and bottom options is something Jerry's been dreaming of most of the season. The Twins have a pair of brutal matchups ahead, likely capping their win total at 4 this year.

I don't even know where to go on this one. At some point, doing the predictable is just worth of a high five or finger gun, and that may even be a little over-excited. So, with Jerry landing in the 12 spot for the 13th straight week, here's a couple of double finger guns and a 13 high fives! I still <3 you Jerbear.

One of the strangest things that seems to happen year after year happened again this year. The week a team buys, they have one of their worst weeks of the season. Ryan's 87 points were his 2nd fewest of the season, landing him a loss to Austin's CMCs. If I told you that AJ Brown, Chase, Diggs and LaPorta would pool their points this week and still be outscored by Ridley by 9 points, you would think I was insane, but Ridley went wild on the bench this week. The loss moves Ryan into 2nd place in the league, but in a week where there are no byes, I would lean toward Ryan starting a new win streak in week 12.

The CMCs were matched up with the league's top team in a game with huge implacations for Austin's playoff picture, and they came up huge with a 125-87 win. J Herbs put up his 3rd 30+ point game of the season in a 20-23 loss to the Packers, suggesting that Herbert may be primed for an even bigger week if they can score more than 20 points. Senor Swift felt like a draft land mine that Austin stepped on for the rest of the league. Turns out, he is actually really freakin good and could have likely been drafted much higher than he was in the 6th round. Austin did lose A Jones, but he can just slot in Swift or Bijan in to follow behind CMC. Week 12 is a massive divisional game against Yisha that will likely determine playoffs for both teams.

The self-proclaimed Mayor navigated the deadly waters of losing a QB and TE in the first half of a game, totaling just 13 points together, and came to shore with his 8th consecutive win (110-93 over Trev). The loss of Burrow and Andrews for this season is brutal, but somehow, Jacube's roster seems perfectly fine without them. The consistent points combined with the cieling being the moon for some of these guys makes Titty City a good bet for where the RBB Bowl will be held this season. The brotherly love will be tested this week, as Jacube and Ryan faceoff in a huge divisional battle, which will leave the winner standing atop the Bun Spreaders division and the overall league standings.

The Tuddy Buddies come in at #4, but they are feeling like #1 right now after completing the three-peat with back-to-back-to-back high scores of the week. The 138 points were actually lower than what could have shown up, as DJ Moore's 20 points were benched in favor of Javonte Williams' 7. This starting group was on a tear again this week though, 5 of 7 being over 19 points and 3 being up over 21. The Tuddy Buddies would love to continue to Mixon some Dell wherever they can, as the rookie is destroying his projections for the season. Week 12 has the Buddies matched up against Big Jim, in a pivotal playoff punching type of game - a perfect family affair right in time for the holiday.

The Big Lig at #5!? Was I drunk at the time these rankings were made? I honestly don't remember, but I do know that Gil's team (at least his starters) is much better than his 4-7 record suggest. In fact, due to some injuries, GIl's team is actually getting better going forward. Kupp and Walker being sidelined has opened the door to some quality touches for both Puka and Charbonnet, locking in some guaranteed production for the Big Lig. Additionally, there may end up being some more clarity in the Minnesota backfield coming sooner than later, and since they both were "TBL" on their fantasy jerseys, Gil may end up gaining another usable RB. Week 12 will be a battle against Joe, the team who just traded next year for this year to Gil.

Things are not well at sea as of late. Either the prey has found elsewhere to live, or Baby Jaws is still learning the art of the hunt, but regardless of what is happening, Jona is staring at a hunger crisis after losing 4 straight games. The 90-138 loss to the Tuddy Buddies has Jona swimming dangerously close to toilet bowl for the 2nd straight season. To add to Jona's food shortage problem, top end WR Cooper Kupp suffered an ankle injury early in the game in week 11, likely sidelining him for a few weeks. Now, more than ever, Baby Jaws will need to find a very large pond in Kansas City and hope Mahomes and Kelce can feed him enough points to survive on until playoffs.

The Assers took a smackers in week 11, losing to the Myth 88-80 in the opposite of a shootout. So more of a pillow fight then? The hand that served up that very public bare booty slap came from none other than Zach Wilson and the Jets, who have just turned talent and fantasy points into dust. G Wilson's -0.10 points helped Yish achieve a loss that has turned his uphill playoff battle into an uphill mountain. The fantasy deciders, for some reason, felt like piling it on and pouring some extra salt in the open Ass, and took Kenneth Walker from the already struggling Yish, while also keeping Justin Jefferson on the sideline to gain exactly zero fantasy points. Yish will need to pray early and often this week, as a miracle may just be the only way to keep his playoff streak alive.

Game of Jones keeps it rolling with an easy easy wiin over the Jerpups 137-91. Josh, who somehow feels like the forgotten team as of late, has been middling for most of the season while maintaining a solid playoff hope alive. The week dominance by Saquon (30 points with Danny Devito behind center) was a great sign of life for what seemed like a doomed remaining season. The team may not be flashy, but the points can and do flow freely for Josh, making him an underdog pick to contend for the 2023 title. The upcoming games against Trevor, Austin and Yish will be the biggest of the season, with 3 of those teams still fighting for a spot.

Joe, the surprise non-selling buyer purchased himself a couple of wins and a chance at the playoffs! Kudos to the effort, as well as the trust in your team, as buying while hanging on to the cliff by a pinky is a scary proposition. The importance of the week 11, 88-80 win over Yish cannot be overstated in terms of Joe having a chance at the playoff this season. A loss would have sent him to 4-7, while also propelling Yish up to a much more comfortable 6-5 record. Despite paying up for Waddle and Henry, Joe only saw a combined 14.65 points from the new teammates. With the loss (or at least downgraded performance) of Achane after the re-injury, Joe's future will be held in the hands of those recently acquired pieces. Joe squares away with Gil before lining up against his pops and Jona in weeks 13 & 14.

Big Jim and his Twins have endured several kicks to the no no zone this year, losing Chubb in week 2, Higgins for many games and being forced to sell off his other major assets. But, even those with the strongest of underpants will eventually crumble after too many shots below the belt. And in week 11, despite a solid 102 effort, Jim just did not have enough to snag a win against the Big Lig. Anything can happen in fantasy, but with only divisional games remaining, and Jim having lent the Twins out until 2024, this team will likely just be hanging out, waiting for the consolation bracket to begin.

Trev's Breece Lighting is hemorrhaging fuel after trading away all the pieces capable of keeping this car moving. In week 11, Trev's DST, Dallas, scored a whopping 15 points! Great right? It is yes, that can be agreed upon. But what is not great is that the DST outscored everyone in this lineup except Breece Hall and Justin Fields, making for a tough 93-110 loss in Titty City. However, Trevor was likely expecting the loss, so he may have just enjoyed the trip through those curved streets of Titty City and stopping at all the big points on the map. Either way, Trev went back to Rydell High with a souvenir L cup bra to remember his trip by.

The Jerpups have made this part of the page their home this season, it will almost be wrong if they're not here to start 2024. Jerry did have one of his higher scores of the season, finally jumping back into the 90s after a few weeks stuck listening to 80s jams again. There was not much to be excited about, except for Trevor Lawrence's 35 point explosion against TEN, accounting for more than 1/3 of Jerry's points this week. While yes, the 12 spot has been a frequent spot for me to dump my jokes, Jerry does deserve some credit for his efforts and decisions. The Pups are consistently fighting through trash to find anyone who can provide fantasy value on any given week, and yet Jerry is still managing to score 80ish points each week while just slinging handfuls of darts with both hands.

The Wolfpack was without most of their pack, but they still claimed another victim, capturing their prey for the 6th straight week. With Jalen Hurts taking the week off, Ryan was forced to have a different Wolf lead the Pack, and oh boy did Joshua Dobbs lead that Pack! Chase, Taylor and Warren also helped lead this team to the 110-95 win over Josh. Ryan said 6 wins in a row and an 8-2 record weren't enough, so he went out and acquired Diggs, Kamara and LaPorta to really solidify his team as the team to beat. Ryan's only real issue now will be deciding who he wants to score 20 points for him each week.

The CMC TD streak is officially over, and so is Austin's losing streak. The CMCs rode the hot hands of CMC and Ekeler to a 118-88 win over Joe's Myth. The win brought Austin back to 0.500 on the year and in a good spot to secure a playoff position. Just being in a good spot doesn't mean anything though, so Austin went out and acquired Bijan from Gil and moved on from Ekeler and Kirk to bring in the NFL's #1 player over the last few weeks in Lamb. Austin has a tough schedule ahead, so the added help at WR might get him through this tough stretch.

Titty City comes in at #3 after the the devastation that the citizens felt on Thursday night. Though Jacube won his matchup easily, he decided to go out and spend some draft capital on Joe Burrow and Mark Andrews to lock him in as a top 2 team in the league. In arguably the wildest sequence of events, Jacube lost both Andrews and Burrow to season-ending injuries in the same half of the same game in their first Titty City apperance. The self-proclaimed Mayor is truly a threat to the health and safety of the NFL, and I can only assume the NFLPA is launching an investigation into the happenings inside Titty City. Even with the injuries, Jacube comes in as a top 3 team while quielty heading for an EIGHT game win streak playing against a sold Trevor lineup.

Holy Tuddy Buddies! 12 TDs by this group in week 10, as they just destroyed The Big Lig 183-95. The explosion of points made for back to back high scores for the Buddies, who moved to 6-4 on the year. The purchase of Dak has come through big time so far, scoring 75 points over both games since the trade. Outside of DST, every player scored over 13 points, and 5 of 7 players scored more than 20 points. This was an incredible week that you can only hope happens more than once in a season. After missing out on some big names, the Tuddy Buddies were conservative buyers this deadline, bringing in Javonte WIlliams and Deebo Samuel, while sending away Flowers and Foreman with some picks mixed in. Sadly, I must face both Ryan and Jacube again this season, making the playoff push all that much harder.

The Assers had an insane rollercoaster ride of a weekend, looking like certain death many times, only to come away with a 144.40-143.29 win over Big Jim. A crazy long TD reception by Walker and a dominant CeeDee Lamb pushed this team just over the 143.29 hill and into a 5-5 record. The win prevented the rest of the league from snagging some top end talent, as Yish decided to hang on and push for the playoffs. Yish sent away Lamb to get Ekeler in the hopes the Jefferson can come back in fill in seamlessly. This team feels loaded up and ready to make a strong run to the finish line.

Joe came into week 10 needing a win to get him back to an even record and in position to make a playoff run. Joe left week 10 with a loss and an outside chance at making the postseason. However, Joe said the idea of him selling was the big Myth of the week, because he chose to buy some talent from The Big Lig and ass Waddle and Henry to this core group. The additions really do add some muscle to this lineup and make them a difficult out on any week. With an easy end of season schedule (a game vs Jerry and Gil after having sold), Joe could defintely still sneak in if he can get, what feels like a must win, victory over Yisha in week 11.

Lots of movement in the rankings, but Jona was one of two teams staying still, coming in at #7 heading into week 11. Jona was matched up against a powerhouse performance from Jacube, without his top talent (Mahomes, Kelce, Kupp and Collins), so the loss was not much of a surprise. The bigger issue for Jona is that he has now dropped 3 games in a row, bringing his season to 6-4 and very much so into a playoff battle. Jona does return all of the names just mentioned, so the coming weeks could be a very different story. Baby Jaws did not wish to add any upgrades to his attack, so we will get to see the buy vs hold argument play out soon.

Game of Jones did start a full lineup in week 10, buuuutttt it didn't matter, as he lost by 15 to the Wolfpack (110-95). There was no calling the Kittle black this week, because R. White and G. Kittle were the only players to have decent games in week 10, each scoring 21 points in their games, while the all but Lamar of the remaining starters dropped single digits. Ryan sent Josh to 4-6 and 7th in the standings, putting Josh's playoff hopes at risk. At the deadline, Josh stood strong and kept his locker room the same. We will see how the lack of action turns out in the next few weeks.

Big Breece, once a top 3 team headed for the playoffs, is now a sold version of itself after back to back upset losses. Two weeks ago, we looked ahead and said there was no chance Trevor isn't 6-4 heading into week 11. Instead, he's 4-6 and much weaker after giving away Diggs, Kamara and LaPorta. As luck would have it, Trevor's week 11 matchup is actually within reach after a few injuries on the other side, making the fire sale seem questionable at best. Did Trev read the wrong writing on the wall? Or will 2024 draft season be worth the likely bottom 6 finish?

The Big Lig. This is a big name to stand behind. However, Gil is being anything but big right now, sitting at 3-7 on the season after an absolute blowout loss to the Tuddy Buddies. Gil actually had a pretty good week, defeating his own projections by 4 points. The problem was that he never had a chance going up against the current high score of the season at 183 points. The loss confirmed what Gil had postponed a few weeks, and the sale was on. Gil took offers left and right, dumping the likes of Bijan, Henry and Waddle for a heap of high end picks. This team can still steal a win here and there, and they will absolutely be a force to deal with during the upcoming draft season (if Gil can get out of his own way at the draft his year that is).

Big Jim is packing a forkin wizard down by those Twins it seems. After losing a shootout to Yisha on Monday night (144-143; 1.11 pt loss), Big Jim decided it was time to look to 2024. He quickly made the first big move of deadline week, agreeing to send Burrow and Andrews to Jacube for 3rd and 5th round picks. What nobody anywhere ever could have predicted was that Jim sent away two grenades in exchange for picks. Big Jim also acquired a 5th round pick for Javonte, making his 2024 total: two 3rds and three 5ths - not a bad haul for a 4-6 team with apparently expiring players.

Here we are again. Jerry. #12. The #12 has become more synonomous with Jerry than it has been with Tom Brady now that Jerry has spent 11 straight weeks looking up in the rankings. Wildly, this is being said after a massive upset win over Breece Lightning, who just had a devastating Monday night showing. The Jerdawgs made some moves to ship out any relevant name remaining on this roster, and in return, Jerry's attendance in the first half of the draft will actually be required in 2024.

The CMCs remain the #1 team in the league for the 5th time since week 6, despite being on a 3 game losing streak after the 93-104 loss to The Big Lig. With CMC, Kirk and Engram taking the week off, Austin was forced to turn to his bench for some points. The replacements played quite well, with Musgrave scoring 13 points, and Aaron Jones contributing 18 as well. The big let downs were newly acquired Adams scoring less than 6 points, and QB Justin Herbert scoring less than 10 points. 3 straight losses has turned Austin's 4-2 record into 4-5 quickly, and he gets a week 10 matchup against Joe, who is coming off his best week since week 4.

The Wolfpack are finally back at #2 for the first time since week 1, with a dominating win over Baby Jaws 108-81. As per usual, Ryan saw Hurts and AJ Brown contribute more than 40 combined points to the Wolves, as Hurts has no scored more than 24 points in 8 of 9 weeks this season, including 4 games over 30 points. Ryan also saw Mostert continue to put up high end numbers, while Jonathan Taylor finally appeared to take over, scoring 18 points in week 9. Ryan did lose a piece of the Philly offense when Goedert went down with a forearm fracture. But in typical Ryan fashion, he already has a backup in Taysom Hill, who has been killing it, to slot right in. Lots of byes in week 10, but Ryan is still locked in for the playoffs unless catastrophe hits.

Trevor followed up his best week of the season with his 2nd worst, scoring just 85 points against Joe. The loss halted the Lightning's cruise to the top of the standings, and keeps him at 4-5 and 8th overall. In week 8, Kamara and Hall each went for 22 or more points, but in week 9, the two didn't even combine for 22 points. Despite acquiring Johnson and Pittman, both players were riding the pine pony this week, but could have offered up 31 points had they been called upon. The loss will likely just be a small bump in the road though, as Trev was gifted a backup sqaud matchup with Jerry in week 10.

Titty City was without multiple big name players during their week 9 vacation, making this game much closer than it probably should have been - with the self-proclaimed Mayor getting the 93-80 win over Jerry. Jacob asked Jacob(s) to carry Jacob through this matchup, and Jacob(s) did not disappoint, scoring 25 points on 98 yards and 2 TDs. Jacube will get back some studs, but he will be without Tyreek Hill in week 10, which will limit the upside for the areolas. Luck is still on the self-proclaimed Mayor's side, as he gets matched up against Jona when Jona is without basically all of his best players.

Game of Jones has been dropping in the rankings for the last 3 weeks, moving back from 2 to 5. Going to 4-5 and 5th place instead of 5-4 and 4th place was nobody's fault but Josh's, after leaving his TE slot open until the MNF players were all that were available. Going into MNF, Josh was down just 3.07 points to Big Jim, but he had to rely on CJ Uzomah (started in less than 1% of leagues) to get those points. Uzomah actually dropped two passes, including a wide open TD pass, that would have secured the win. Instead, Uzomah came up 0.72 points shy, and Game of Jones came away with a loss. Looking forward, this team is returning ETN and Kittle from the bye, while also getting a favorable matchup against a vacationing Wolfpack.

Things are wild in the world of the Assers! After buying Walker and moving Terry and Rhamondre to acquire Jefferson, Yisha was looking to set himself up for a competitive playoff push. And in week 9, it looked like things were going according to plan, with Yisha scoring 122 points on the week. Unfortunately for the Assers, 122 was the 2nd highest score of the week, only behind the 135 points put up by Yisha's opponent during another Monday Night Miracle in reverse. Luckily for Yish, the script may not have been entirely tossed in the trash, as the entire Gravy Goons division ended up with a loss in week 9, keeping the entire division at 4-5, and the playoffs wide open. Yish will welcome back Kyler Murray and James Conner, who may make an immediate impact on this startint lineup.

The sequal to Baby Jaws' 64 point horror was only slightly better than the original, maxing out at 81 points against Ryan's Wolfpack. Headlined by Travis Kelce's 2 point performance, almost all of Jona's starting lineup underwhelmed - including a full Mother Goose appearance from Gabe Davis, who has now scored less than 2 points 3 times this season. Kelce, shockingly, has scored just over 12 points in the last two weeks combined! Usually that's his stat line after the first quarter of any game. To make things worse, back to back losses have Jona at 6-3 and only 1-2 games above the rest of the pack. Things are very up in the air at the moment, as Collins is dealing with injury issues, Kupp has a half a QB and the KC crew are on bye after two straight weeks of bad games. Things look eerily similar to the 2022 season for Jona right now.

The Tuddy Buddies came up HUGE in week 9, earning what felt like a must win game against Yisha's Assers. Needing to buy a win, The Buddies shipped out Jared Goff and 10th to acquire Dak Prescott and a 12th from Big Jim. The trade immediately paid dividends, as Dak scored 32 points, outscoring the other waiver options by 13ish points. Tank fricken Dell came through with one of the best final drive performances seen in a while, making an incredible sideline catch that set up his TD reception on the next play - earning him 30 points on the week. The win moved the Tuddy Buddies into 4th place at 5-4 with a tough stretch of games ahead. Time will tell if this team can continue to compete at a high level.

The Lig was Big in week 9, taking down #1 ranked Austin 104-93. Sure, Austin was without CMC, Engram and Kirk, but Gil still did enough to win by 11. Gil's first go wtih Henry resulted in 20 points, which was 17 more than he would have received from Kenny Walker had he not made the trade. Probably even a bigger week given the positional scarcity, Jake Fergie came through with 19 big ones for the Lig. Gil is still loaded up with big names, but we will see if he will run out of road before claiming a playoff spot.

Grande Jim and the TEs is more like it in week 9, with Big Jim scooping up a set of TEs from the wire to secure a crucial win over Game of Jones. The Twins had an great week, going for the 3rd highest score with quality performances from all but two players (J. Cook and J. Reed who each had 6.7 points). But the real talking point was this team grabbing two of the remaining 4 TEs to prevent Josh, who left his TE slot open for far too long, from scoring 3.07 points on SNF and MNF. The 118.32-117.60 win moved Big Jim tied for 5th place in record at 4-5 and kept the door open for a wild outside shot at the playoffs. Things would have to bounce super right for that to happen, but as said before, these Twins can show up to spoil your day at any time.

What was this week's Myth?? The idea that Joe was a free win! In what looked like a tough matchup with Breece Lightning, Joe made a pre-game trade with the Assers to try and buy a win by sending away superstar Justin Jefferson for Rhamondre Stevenson and Scary Terry. Though Joe had the points to win this one either way, the trade may have turned the tide for these guys, as Joe smoked Trevor 111-85 and turned his could be 3-6 record into a playoff contending 4-5 record. The win keeps things very interesting for the Myth, but the schedule didn't do them any favors, as they go into week 10 as 16 point dogs to Austin's CMCs.

Last but not least, well in our hearts anyway, is Jerry the DingleDawgBerry. Jerry has been sniffing the behind of everyone in the league this season while staring up from the bottom of the power rankings, and this week is no different. In week 9, Jerry had 4 starters be outscored by his Philly DST, who scored just 6.53 points. To put that into context, Jerry had a combined 15 points from FOUR players in the starting lineup. If not for Kmet and Gibson significantly overperforming (21 and 15 points), Jerry may have been heading for record low numbers. Though nothing has been good in the above writing about this team, Jerry has already turned a few players into 2024 draft picks, and without any chances of good coming this season, Jerry will have longer than anyone in the league to scout for his 2024 draft.

For the 4th straight week Austin comes in at #1 in the rankings, even coming off back to back losses. Austin lost in a shootout with the Mayor, missing out on mother's milk by just over 10 points (140-130). The CMCs did play their best lineup, but they just didn't have enough, with Kirk being the dead weight, scoring just 7 points - his worst week since week 1. Austin did ship out Thielen to bring out Adams, which will likely give this team an even bigger boost. However, given the bye weeks, Austin may be on his way to 3 consecutive losses in a tough matchup with The Big Lig.

Why not make week 8 your highest scoring week of the season!? Trevor's team scored more in a 10 minute span than his opponent did the entire week (don't fact check it). Breece Lightning struck way too many times in week 8, scoring TDs up and down his lineup, inclduing his bench, totaling 140 points in a blowout win. Trevor swung for the fences, and his starting lineup is full of home runs right now. A complete turnaround team from his first few weeks, Trevor has become an elite team that looks primed to be 6-4 after the next two weeks.

Game of Jones sent Jona away on vacation and paid the bar tab in KC, and he was rewarded with Jona's worst week of the season by 30 points! Josh had 16 points combined from Lamar Jackson and Adams, and yet Josh still won his game by 59 points - and that was with Hopkins' surprising 37 points on the bench. Adams' 1.85 forced Josh to trade him away to his brother in a competitive division, all so that Josh could raise the average age of his lineup by adding Adam Thielen. We will see how that trade moves these two teams in the coming weeks.

The Wolfpack are on fire! 4 straight wins, while averaging 135.31 points per game during that span. It is safe to say, Ryan's team is dominating and looking like a lock for a deep playoff run, sitting at 6-2 and #1 in the league. Yes, he is currently underrated on the power rankings. Yes, he will likely not be ranked this low again this year. The type of Brown that Hurts is normally something you want to avoid, but for Ryan, he is asking for more, as the Philly combo is destorying the NFL right now. AJ Brown set an NFL record in week 8 for most consecutive games (6) with at least 125 receiving yards and 1 TD. The 61 points between Hurts and Brown would have nearly beaten Jona (his week 9 matchup) on their own. All of these words, and not one mention of Ja'Marr Chase's 21 points shows you just how good this team can be.

The self-proclaimed Mayor is on a Mardi-Gras binge that has lasted 5 weeks now, with Jacube having them ta-tas out since week 4. The 5 game win streak has Jacube at 6-2 and #2 in the league behind only the The Wolfpack by 50 points. The week 8 win was a statement win for The City, taking down the CMCs in a blow up game, 140-130. This team team put up 140 points with TE Jonnu Smith barely even knowing where the game was in TEN, scoring just 1.8 points for Jacube. With a core of St. Brownie, Hill, Jacobs and Gibbs, Jacube has just too good of a baseline - he has yet to score below triple digits on the season. I don't see the win streak coming to an end against the Henry-less Jerdawgs this week.

The Big Lig! The name changed but the result stayed the same. A 132-102 loss to The Wolfpack has Gil sitting at 2-6 despite having a top 6 ranked team in the PR. Gil continued his puppy and grandpa rampage, reaping the rewards by swapping out Howell for Carr, and then Carr for Young, who scored significnatly less than Carr and Howell. Not many great things to discuss about week 8 for Gil, except for that the loss turned Gil to looking at 2024. Or 2023? Or what? Gil sold Walker to the Assers and simultaneously bought Henry from the Jerdawgs. So, I guess the future is murky at best for The Big Lig.

Jona took a baby moon to Cancun, and his team thought they had the week off as well, scoring just 64.85 points on the week. Mahomes and Kelce, one week after combining for 72 points, combined for 18 points against the Broncos. Had Jona not played Lockett (19.35 points), Jona would have had zero players surpass 9.99 points. This week was too trashy for this team to care much about, as it is the outlier. However, injuries and NFL team schemes are seeming to be pushing Baby Jaws further and further out to sea and away from all the easy wins around the shoreline. Week 9 doesn't get any easier, being lined up across from Ryan's Wolfpack.

Yisha was running around Dawg park Roughing as many Assers as he could get his hands on, destroying Jerry's booty 152-95. Gus Edwards (32), Lamb (37) and McBride (21) may have each had the best games of each of their careers in week 8. Rhamondre was the only starter to not outscore the DST (7.84) or hit double digits, and he could have been replaced with Moss' 15+ points to add to Yisha's dominant week. A non-trade ended up helping turn this boat's direction from potential seller into a buyer, with Yish deciding to buy Walker from the Big Lig. This team has boom ability, but hopefully they are resting up in week 9 for a week 10 blast off.

Three straight losses took this team from 4-1 and 1st in the Bun Spreaders division, to 4-4 and an outside chance at making the playoffs. An unimpressive week ended with a 140-97 loss to the red hot Breece Lightnings. Injuries have really hurt the upside of this squad, but hopefully the return of some talent and some good matchups can help this train back on track before it's too late.

Big Jim has a set of Twins after back to back wins, bringing him back into the conversation at 3-5. Jim's star WR Olave has been anything but a star this year, and was the worst starter for Big Jim once again this week. Though the Twins had a bunch of average performances, Javonte Williams and Dak Prescott had great weeks, totalling 53 points together. If some of these guys can get back to the draft form, Jim has a good chance of ruining your playoff hopes after catching you on the wrong week.

Mythical creature, Señor El, has been roaming around these parts for the last four weeks, leaving Joe with 4 losses and a 3-5 record through the first 8 weeks of the year. It has been an up and down year for Joe - never higher than when Jefferson and Achane were both in the starting lineup - but it's been more down than up lately. The 93-109 loss to Big Jim was a tough one to swallow, especially with massive games from Allen and D. Smith. This team is fully on the swing for the fences mentality, as the lows are strikeouts more often than not. Joe will hope to steal a win or two before Jefferson and Achane return, otherwise the store may be open for business again this year.

The Jerdawgs put out their 2nd best showing of the season, scoring 95 points on the back of a meat and potatoes-like week from Pittman, Bourne, Kmet, Henry and Lawrence. Unfortunately Jerry's 2nd best showing was 56 points short of the best week of Yisha's season, resulting in the 4th consecutive and 6th loss of the season. The loss confirmed it was time to make a sale, and oddly enough, the first customer was the other 2-6 team in the RBB. Jerry sent away his stability and upside in Henry, bringing back some picks and future talent. 2024 is in full swing for the Jerdawgs, and the #12 spot appears to be a comfortable home for the Dingles for the remainder of the year.

The CMCs did it again! Wait... No, they didn't. They lost 101-90 to Breece Lightning this past week. But CMC himself did it again, as he scored his 7th straight game over 14.5 points, 5th game of the year over 23.5 points and 16th straight (16!!) game with a Tuddy. He appears to be the closest thing to a cheat code in fantasy right now, regardless of how many obliques he has. Austin did not have much else to discuss in week 7, outside of Kirk being relatively awesome this year, as the rest of his team pretty much walked out of week 7 with soiled underwear. The CMCs will head into week 8 as the top team, but they have a tough test in Titty City.

Josh got the win without needing to even worry about his defense, handling the Tuddy Buddies 122-102. Lamar Jackson absolutely destroyed the Lions, scoring 3x as many points as his counterpart, Goff, helping Game of Jones feel comfortable Sunday afternoon having almost tied his week 6 score in the first couple hours of the weekend. Though Lamar was great, outside of Amari Pooper, Josh has pretty good games from every other player he started, including 59 points from his three starting RBs. This team may be old, but they have the fire power and stability to pick up win after win.

Big Breece finally made his way into the top 5, all the way into the top 3! Has Trevor's team been amazing? Not necessarily, no. However, this team's future is as bright as any team's in the RBB. Tua, Diggs, Kamara, Breece, LaPorta and Hunt possible taking over starting duties in CLE, Trevor's starters are locked and loaded to blowup always. The evidence of that being this team's 101 points in week 7, despite his QB and DST combining for 12.90 points. Though he is named after Breece, it may be Kamara who drags this team to the playoffs, as he has not scored less than 17 points in any games this year, and he has 35 receptions in his 4 games (yes 35 receptions in 4 games). Trevor used to look like a matchup to be excited about, but those days are gone now.

The Wolfpack must be eating their older, weaker wolves, because they somehow keep getting better without anything really changing on this team. Ryan is getting very comfortable in Philly, with his team's production being heavily propped up by the Eagles' Hurts, Brown and Goedert (71 points this week between those three players). The Pack is currently feeling the pain of Ridley, who is too tough to play because he probably will score 6 points or less, but also too tough to sit because he is as talented as anyone in the league and can score 30 points on your bench. If Ryan can find which peripheral players belong in his starting lineup for the rest of the season, he may not lose another game.

Jona, the league's #1 team at 6-1, fell from #2 to #5 after being the highest scoring team with 136 points? Who makes these rankings? While your closed-door life is your own business, Baby Jaws ate so many Assers in public in week 7, destroying Yish 136-80. 72 of those 136 points game from the Chiefs duo (Mahomes with 40 and Kelce with 32), which was only 8 points away from beating Yish on their own. Jona was already thin at RB, but he got even thinner with Jerome Ford going down with an anke injury after his 20 point fantasy performance. The main thing keeping Jona rolling along is that he may not need any RBs in his lineup as long as the Chiefs dominate and Cooper Kupp does what Cooper Kupp normally does. Jona gets to matchup with Josh Jones and his superstars in week 8.

After years of stale ownership, this team has rebranded TWICE this season! While "The Fantasy Disaster" was an extremely accurate team name for this group, The Big Lig was a great name to fall booty-backwards into. After making his highest points of the week call, Gil was smashed between a pair of double Ds, losing by a double dub 117-77 in Titty City. Though it had no effect on the game, The Big Lig may be on his way to slap Arthur Smith after not disclosing Bijan's illness prior to the game, managing 0.4 points in like 9 snaps against the Bucs. Outside of the name, nothing I have said to this point suggests that Gil should come in at #6, but Gil's team is absolutely one that can be the highest scoring team any week and go on a long win streak.

I think it's safe to say that Jacube is not the actual Mayor of Titty City, and that the Mayor is in fact Tyreek Hill, who makes 20 point games seem like a boring week. Hill has 5 weeks this season with 21 points and 4 of those games being over 28 points. Hill is looking like the WR version of CMC, providing too good of a baseline for Jacob to ever really get destroyed. Once you look at the lineup and get past Hill, you then realize that Jacube also has St. Brownie, Jacobs, Gibbs, Evans, Addison and Henderson (maybe something with Kyren out). #7 feels way too low for Jacube, and I woud suspect it does not last long.

The Tuddy Buddies drop back to back games and are now #3 in the Bun Spreaders division. With injuries and poorly timed bye weeks, I was forced to start Foreman and Jeff Wilson Jr. in the RB slots this week. The two combined for 36 points on the week! Buuuuttt, Jeff Wilson had less than 1 of those 36 points. This was a mostly down week for the Buddies, headlined by Goff and Keenan's combined 20 points. Hopefully the return of health and the disappearance of bye weeks will help this roster get back on track.

Yisha became the latest Baby Jaws victim after a 136-80 pounding by Jona in week 7. On what would have been a tough chance to win as is, the Assers just spent the week Roughing themselves, as they managed to have zero players break 17 points. The week looked like it might start okay after Yish was able to secure the big waiver add, Zach Evans. However as the week went on, the Rams were uninterested in Evans, leaving Yish with zero points, luckily riding the pine pony. Yisha still has plenty of good talent, like Wilson, Lamb, Godwin, and Stevenson, to add to the eventual return of Conner and Murray, so better days are ahead I would guess.

Joe's 3-1 start has quickly turned into a 3-4 record halfway through the season after dropping 3 straight games. The loss of both Jefferson and Achane has been felt throughout this lineup, since their upside seems significantly capped compared to just a few weeks ago. Joe put up the 5th highest score last week with 103 points, so it's tough to think of where they could have been with the two on IR. The lineup still looks bleak, but if Joe can sneak a win or two out in the next few games, the return of Jefferson and Achane could push him right back into the playoff mix.

Big Jim did everything he could to lose this game, after starting a QB that would have scored more points by being on the IR. Watson's -1.7 made the game closer than it should have been after James Cook and Mark Andrews both scored 21 points this week. The Twins will be happy to welcome back their Bengals stack in Burrow and Higgins, with those two combining for big time points in the past. Do I think Big Jim will be showing off his Twins often this season? No, but I do think we will see glimpses of the fellas again this year.

The Jerdawgs have little to be happy about at the moment. Losing a game to a team that had a negative scoring QB is a tough one to swallow, but Jerry did just that in week 7, putting him at 2-5 this season. While Jerry does have some valuable names on his roster, you have to really do some digging through the trash surrounding them to find them. Nevertheless, Jerry can still have a big game that may surprise you on your down week, like he did to me just a few short weeks ago. Until then, sorry Sir Dingles, the 12th spot is home.

Austin's week 6 lineup was filled with names that were forgotten, pulled through the mud or used to wipe booties during the pre-season. But now, through 6 weeks of 2023, those names are putting up unforgettable stats, including a 25 point week from Adam Thielen, his 4th game this season over 17 points. One of the hardest things to do in fantasy is to put aside the name and play the data, but Austin has been thriving in it all season. Things did look lined up for Austin to be the victim of back to back Monday night miracles, but instead got lucky that J Herbs had two left hands against Dallas. The CMCs moved to 4-2 on the year and will hope to have the week more locked up heading into week 7's MNF.

If I had placed a post-draft-pre-season bet on who would be the team to be 5-1 , I would have won it. No, just kidding, Jona's team appeared to be far from a league leader after some questionable draft selections. Here we are in week 7, and Jona is 5-1 and only getting better with some health injected back into this team. The Mahomes, Kelce, Kupp and Pollard combo is one to avoid if possible, as Jona appears set to contend in the playoffs this season.

2-4 and still the #3 team in the rankings?? Yes, it is odd to say the least, but Josh's team has clearly flashed their talents, albeit coming in pretty much every other matchup. Week 6 was the lows, scoring just 75 points after getting 46 points from to players (Lamar and ETN). But as you can see, 5 players can be almost usless, and this team can still score 75 points. If anyone chooses to play even slightly like ETN, who has scored too many TDs over the last few weeks, Josh will turn this 2-4 start into a positive differential.

Two 2-4 teams in the top 4?? Now this is getting a little crazy. But which one of them do you kick out? Gil has been a garbage person all year, and lost another close game because of it, but outside his personal life, Gil's team is stacked with quality starting options that frequently crack the starting lineup. If you were told before the draft that this would be your roster, you'd be hyped with how good you drafted. But managing a team is at least half the battle in fantasy, so the accurately named Disaster sits at 2-4 on the season. However, I would be surprised if they were not at least .500 soon.

Ryan drew the long straw in week 6, getting matched up against Jerbear, who has not been able to escape the 70s in 3 straight weeks. Ryan handled his business easily, as Mostert continued his dominance and had more than half of Jerry's weekly score on his own. Despite the Eagles only being able to manage 14 points against the Jets, Hurts, Brown and Goedert still have the Wolfpack 50 foods to eat. As of right now, the Pack's weaker Wolves are rough, but if they're not needed, the Pack won't be held back and they won't be a concern.

Titty City had their tassels on in week 6, making sure Joe couldn't get a sneak peek of the goods. Jacube breezed through the matchup winning by nearly 50 points. Jacob has been quietly dealing with injuries all season, but the loss of Kyren Williams, who wasn't even on most leagues' draft boards this year, may be very significant to this team's future success. If Gibbs can take even a small step in the direction of his pre-season hype, Jacube will likely be fine. But if it's more of the same, the Titties may struggle to find someone capable of supporting their bustiness.

The Tuddy Buddies were more like the Duddy Buddies in week 6, as 4 starters were outscored by the starting DST's 10 points. Goff and Allen did their best to make things close, combining for 46 points, while Allen had the chance for double the points had J Herbs not been throwing the ball with 2 left hands and/or an eye patch on one eye. The Monday night miracle was not complete, dropping this team to a 4-2 record before a very tough week 7 matchup with #3 ranked Game of Jones.

A 2023 Dark Horse candidate, Breece Lightning has been brewing up a storm over the past few weeks, scoring no less than triple digits in 4 consecutive weeks. While having two QBs might seem like a good idea, Trevor has incorrectly chosen which QB to start 4 of 6 weeks (yes some has been injury). Luckily this last week, he was still able to get the win over The Disaster, who is dealing their own management issues. Lightning is absolutely a surface level phenomenon, as these Breeces have no depth to discuss. Luckily for them, their stars are good enough to hide the depth. But an injury or a few tough bye weeks could really hurt Trevor's chances of making a real push.

The Assers' week 6 performance has to make you question what is considered a good week in the RBB these days. His DST scores a respectable 8 points, and all but 1 player had double digits to their name. Yet, he came away with just 97 points and a win that would have been a loss vs half the league. An odd week when those types of performances don't even get you into the 100s. Even odder for this team that once appeared pretty decent, is that they have yet to eclipse 101.1 points this season, yet Yisha is 3-3 on the year and sitting in 2nd place in the Gravy Goons division. Either this will continue to be a super weird year, or things may catch up to Yish sooner than later.

It almost feels bad writing about Joe this far down in the list after having the 1st overall pick, three 3rd round picks and three 8 rounders, but it just goes to show how devestatijg injuries and a whiffed pick here or there can be. The loss of Jefferson, Achane and Dobbins mixed with the inadequate seasons by Najee and Mattison thus far have really hurt this team's chances at success after such a promising start. Joe's week 6 loss brings him back to even on the year (3-3), which is still good enough for 2nd in the Burnt Biskies division. If the Myth can find a 4 leaf clover or reverse even a small portion of their bad luck, they may just be able to win the league with that kind of power.

Big Jim and his big Twins are at 11 solely because someone else exists to own the #12 slot. The #11 ranking is a brutal step down from where his season started, after injuries and unreached potential have taken over this team. Jim has not scored 100 points in 5 of 6 weeks, and 26% of his points on the year came from his week 2 blowout win. Unfortunately for these Twins, the dark horse is a little too far into the shadows to be found right now, BUT, if a few things click, do not be surprised if you find yourself on the wrong end of a Big Jim flop session at some point this season.

Jerbear ordered his #12 team jersey this week, after taking the last place ranking for 7 consecutive weeks (the longest anyone has been in any position in the rankings to start the season). I wish I could give some hope here, but with 1 game over 93 points this year, 3 straight games in the 70s, injuries and byes happening, there's not many places to find hope. Except this one, which is that if Jerry can get a win this week, he will be 3-4 on the season, which is 1 game off most of the middle to upper tier teams thus far. And regardless of how bad this season goes for Jerry, one of his wins this season came against the one putting him at #12, so at least there's that.

Less than 2 points away from a 4-1 start to the season. Austin appeared to have his week 5 matchup in the bag, but was left stranded on MNF by his own name brother, Aaron Jones, who was a late inactive. Austin pivoted to Renfrow, and here we are talking about his 3-2 record. While The McCaffres are 3-2, they are likely past the low point in their season, as players are getting healthy, a few bye weeks came and went and some players are finding their groove (Thielen, Kirk, Swift, London). It would be unfortunate to have to play these guys over the next stretch of games.

Back to back Joneses in the power rankings?? Seems fishy to me. Until you look at what these two have been doing and can do on any week. Week 5 was an incredible week for this Jones, with only 1 starter (Adams of all people) failing to score 12+ fantasy points, and two starters scoring a combined 66 points (Kittle & ETN). The week could have been even bigger if the Ravens didnt have 7 drops (the most by a team since 2017 or something like that), and Lamar would have scored any TDs instead of turning the ball over twice. Josh has a lineup that appears to have a pretty high floor while also a sky high ceiling, making them a tough team to square up with each week. Their 117.5 PPG average is 2nd in the league.

The self-proclaimed Mayor was out campaigning this pas week. His platform: Boobies are better than Booties! And who can really even argue that after Jacube slapped Yisha's booty in a 108-62 blowout. For the 2nd time in just 5 weeks, Jacube has had his starting QB leave the game early on (score less than 6 points) and still win the week (just a funny side note, Jacob's benched QB Love, who played the entire game, only outscored the injured A Rich. by 1.76 points). Jacube didn't need a whole lot in this one, as Yish basically beat himself, but he still got 31 points from Mr. Hill and 20 points from Mr. Jacobs. Injuries will be the question for this team, but if healthy, they are as good (or better) than any team in the RBB.

Jona had himself a Monday night miracle in week 5. Looking like the game was all but lost being up by just 3 points going into Monday night, Baby Jaws took out Austin's RB Aaron Jones right before kickoff on MNF forcing Austin to start Hunter Renfrow, who could only muster up 1.2 points. Jona cashed in his miracle for the win and improved to 4-1 on the season. Jona is dealing with injuries coming and going each week, but at least his players are returning to action rather than heading to IR. With the return of Kupp, the combo of Mahomes and Kelce (who have underperformed thus far) and Pollard leading the RB room, this little Jaws will likely claim more victims in the coming weeks.

The Disaster was no disaster this week, taking down the Ding..Jerdwags by 21 points. Gil had the donuts to start both Sam Howell and the Wshington DST against the Bears, and he was rewarded with 30 points for his dunkins. 29.5 of those came from Sam, as he battled his way to a 20-40 loss against the incredible Bears. Despite benching Puka, who has been nothing short of amazing, Gil came away with the win, bringing his record to 2-3. This team is loaded with names ready to contribute, making Gil a team that will likely do very well during bye weeks.

168 points. 168 points! What a week for the Wolfpack, who absolutely feasted on Jim's Twins, to the tune of a 105 point margin of victory. If there was any question about why Ja'Marr Chase was in the #1 overall pick conversation, his week 5 stat line should put that to rest, as he went for 15 for 192 and 3 TDs (aka 50 fantasy points). Chase is only one piece of the incredible grouping Ryan has put together. This team easily has the ability to be #1 overall, but they have also shown their ability to bust, so expectations have to be tempered until proven otherwise. However, I'd bet #6 is as low as Ryan goes moving forward.

This is the week I dreamed of when drafting this team! Especially after a week when I lost by scoring 61 freakin points. DJ give me Moore points please, as he went for a career high, 230 yards and 3 TDs on the Bears of all teams! Moore's 48 points added to the Tuddy Buddies' TNF dominance, starting the week with almost an unbeatable start. The win moved the Buddies to a hot 4-1 start, which is huge given the next few weeks against some top notch teams.

The Breece Lightning struck, but Game of Jones was ready for the storm, dropping Trevor to 1-4 on the year after the 149-136 loss. Trevor's namesake took off in week 5, dominating the Broncos with 32 fantasy points. Trevor also received massive games from Diggs, Kamara and LaPorta, who continue to be consistent performers. The Breece's would have beaten 8 other teams this week, but they came up against one of the Joneses, who would not be defeated with their 149 points. Trevor is absolutely on the rise, and I would not be surprised if he continued moving up the rankings as the year progresses.

Yisha is hoping that his Asser was Roughed so badly that he woke up in week 6 and forgot all about week 5, after having only 1 (Kirk Cousins) score more than 8.25 points this week. Yisha's 62 points were the 2nd worse on the year, and to make matters worse, Yisha lost RB James Conner to a knee injury that landed him on the IR. Thankfully Yish started with a 2-0 start, or things would look very bleak for these guys right now. While they may be in the dark right now, the sun may rise again soon for Yish.

Week 5 will be a week Joe will remember for years to come. Not only did his 3-1 record turn into a 3-2 record, but he also lost two of fantasy's top performers in Justin Jefferson and De'Von Achane to the IR. The upside these players brought to Joe's swaud cannot be overstated. Achane was the 2nd leading rusher in the NFL despite having 61 less rushing attempts (61!!!). This is where Joe will have to puke and rally to find a way and steal some wins until these studs can return to dominate once again.

Big Jim and his Twins spent the week in Mexico, probably to avoid the inevitable, as Ryan slapped those babies around 105 times on the way to Jim's 3rd straight loss. Things continue to go from bad worse, as injuries and just unrealized potential continue to pile up on this roster. Could this team turn it around and surprise many teams in the near future? Sure. But is it likely? Not so much. Jim needs to make a trade or get lucky on the waiver wire if he wants to turn things around sooner than later.

The Jerdawgs have owned the 12th spot for longer than anyone to start the season, as they come in at #12 for the 6th straight week to kickoff 2023. I wish I could say better things about this roster, but nothing is really making me happy when I look at their outputs. Jerry has surpassed 100 points only once this year (104 in week 1), and has been held to under 80 in back to back weeks. Jerry can absolutely get wins, as hes already 2-3 on the year, but they will likely come when a team has a down week, making his odds of moving up in the rankings relatively low.

Nobody knows for sure where Titty City is located, but I can tell you for sure that it's not located in Seattle, as the Seahawks DST almost stole the victory away from the self-proclaimed Mayor with a MNF monster game (23.21). The Tittitians (did we settle on anything?) held on with every areola they had to hang on to the win 125.61-125.42 over his new brother from another kiki (as they say). Jacube's RBs went absolutely ham, scoring 58 points on 266 yards and 3 TDs between the two of them (Jacobs and K. Williams). At this rate, Kyren Williams will easily be considered a top 3 waiver pickup come the end of the season. Even if Mike Evans misses time with his hamstring injury, Jacob has way too many baseline points to compete with each week.

Whoever the losers are in Game of Thrones, Josh and his roster were those guys in week 4, after losing to the winless Disaster by 35 points. Lamar Jackson attributed for more than 1/3 of the team's points, putting up 31 of the total 86, while outscoring the next closest starter by 19 points. While Game of Jones looks like they have the team to dominate, this loss drops them to 1-3 on the year and 3rd in the Gravy Goons division. Josh will have some work to do to get out of this initial hole.

Somewhere Urban Meyer is streaking across the lawns of his neighbors in honor of Urban Myth's 3 game win streak. After taking a tough loss in week 1 to his padre, Joe has gone on to win his next 3 matchups while scoring no less than 122 points during that span. The main concern for this team initially was the lack of RB production after losing JK Dobbins in week 1, but Mattison and Harris could do just enough to compliment the insane work being done by De'Von Achane right now. That kind of upside paired with Josh Allen and Justin Jefferson makes Joe's chances of continuing his streaking look promising.

The Urban Myth busted this Myth, as he was the first one to finally catch Baby Jaws this season, dropping Jona to 3-1 on the year. Nico Collins of all people on this talented roster led the team with 36 fantasy points, outscoring the next player by 20 points (which includes Kelce and Mahomes). This is the downside of a stack, the KC duo scored just 26 points on the week, barely moving the team close to Joe's 145 points. Jona still has a ton of talent, but bye weeks and injuries will make this next part of the season an interesting section for the Jaws.

CMC is not fair. He is the closest thing to a cheat code that we've seen in fantasy since starting the RBB. To think that he thre out 50.95 points and left points on the table is insane. He hasn't had less than 110 yards, 1 TD and 23.95 fantasy points in any game, giving Austin an incredible baseline. In fact, Austin only needed CMC and Justin Herbert to get the win over Yisha this week. Austin also took the gamble on Swift, which appears to be paying off, as he seems to have overtaken the starting role in Philly and is running wild with it. Austin definitely has some holes to fill for the off weeks when CMC doesn't score 50 points, but overall, this team is starting with too many points to not be competitive.

The Disaster scores a Fantasy win! In an underdog week (5 of 6 underdog teams won), Gil was on the right side of the the underdog story, taking down Game of Jones 121-86. 5 of 8 starters scored more than 16 points this week, while the other 3 spots (one being the DST) combined for just 12 of the teams 121 points. Puka continued his unprecedented dominance, recording his 39th catch, 501st receiving yard and 1st career TD in just his 4th career NFL game. Bijan was also incredible again, as he has now scored 19+ points in 3 of 4 weeks, despite not having a single rushing TD. The Disaster was anything but this week, seeing as even his bench had an incredible amount of success (Pacheco 28, Terry 19, Pierce 14 and Watson 10). The upside is real for this team people.

Holy close one! In what appeared to be a done deal, Ryan made this the closest game of the year, losing to Jacube by only 0.19 points after Seattle's DST put up 23.21 points on MNF. The Seahawks were in the top 3 in scoring for Ryan this week, trailing only the duo of Hurts and AJ Brown (68 points), who appear to be one of the most dangerous stacks in football these days. Outside of those three players, Ryan's team was an anchor holding them back. But as said weekly, when you have this type of boom potential, even a visit from Mother Goose won't ruin The Wolpack's chances of eating.

This was an annoying loss. Especially since the points were there to easily win. As a matter of fact, If I had started DJ Moore and David Montgomery only, my team would have scored more points this week. If you were wondering which players had as many or more TDs than the Tuddy Buddies in week 4, the answer is: CMC, Diggs, Kmet, Nico Collins, Andrews, AJ Brown, Justin Jefferson, Micahel Wilson, De'Von Achane, Kyren Williams, Herbert, Lamar and the Dallas DST. So, here's to week 5.

Yish had everything possible going for him this week - a new baby, a Sunday birthday - but everything wasn't enough to keep up with CMC, as the Assers got roughed up for the 2nd time this season, 130-76. In the real world, this was a week Yisha will never forget. In the fantasy world, he will try and forget as quickly as possible, with nothing really happy to note outside of Godwin's team high 16 points. This team has the appearance of a long run team that could eventually dominate, but the short term seems like it will be a hit or miss every week. With the new baby (CONGRATS YISH!), the Assers may have some future extra dad strength on their side.

Big Jim got the Twins caught in the zipper again in week 4, falling to 1-3 on the year with the loss to Breece Lightning 120-99. To make matters worse, Jim lost Javonte to a hip injury, Higgins to broken ribs and Olave to Carr's inability to throw more than 5 yards. With Injuries and bye weeks, Big Jim has some Big problems that need fixing if he's going to get through this next stretch with some wins.

The Lightning are on the board! Trevor makes his 2023 win debut after taking down Big Jim's Twins 120-99. Trevor had a very welcomed return to Alvin Kamara, who scored 17 points in his first game back. Trev also the best game of the year out of Herbert and Diggs, who combined for 244 yards and 4 TDs. If Trevor can start getting these boom games together, he will turn that losing record around quickly.

Fricken Jerry. Guy just dangles a win in your face, scoring just 79 points on the week. But somehow Jerry spells your team into quicksand, and you slowly watch your point projections dwindle until you have nothing left to steal that low hanging win. So with that, kudos to Jarebear on the win to improve to 2-2 on the year. D. Henry came through big time in a surprise smashing of the Bengals for 27 points of his own, while Doubs led the Packers WRs with 15 points in their booty slapping from the Lions. Despite paper and projections, Jerry does appear to have enough talent to sneak some wins away when you don't expect them - call them the Arizona Cardinals through 4 weeks.

Woah doggy! I haven't seen Game of Thrones, but whoever wins, Game of Jones was those guys in week 3. Josh had 5 guys score 13 or more points, with two of those guys scoring more than 33 points! Amari Cooper added 24 points to team, and actually could have had another 12-15 points had his first TD not been called back on a wild ref decision. A wild stat for QB Lamar Jackson: of his 33.78 points, only 8.28 points came from throwing the ball. The remaining 25.5 came from his rushing. But with Lamar, Adams, Cooper, ETN, Kittle, Etc, this can happen any week. Which has been the argument for this team. They have too much star power to be able to catch them all on down weeks frequently.

The self-proclaimed Mayor of Titty City may have owed some favors in week 3, as some of his start/sit decisions were suspect. However, the Mayor may be good at being sneaky, since all of those start/sit decisions did not have any affect on the outcome of the game, so Titty City is none the wiser on the Mayor's under the table dealings. Still though, the Titties. The Tittians? The Titticians? The Tater Ta-Tas? The citizens of Titty City are still looking at the big board and seeing a giant 1-2, 4th in the Bun Spreaders, 9th in the overall record through 3 weeks. Can Jacube turn it around in weeks 4 and 5?

Baby Jaws claimed another victim, all before birth, swallowing up Breece Lightning in week 3 114-104. The little ocean man was sitting in a suite with T Swift in KC, watching their men, Kelce and Mahomes play with the Bears like little baby cubbies while scoring 46 points together. Jona also suited up new starting RB Jerome Ford, who quickly made his presence known with 131 yards and a score in his first full game as the guy. On paper, Jona appears to have some holes to plug. On Sundays, Jona has no holes and is actively making holes in his opponents, so who knows how good this roster actually is right now. What we do know, though, is that Jona is 3-0 with an average score of 116.19 (2nd in the league), all with Cooper Kupp yet to touch the field.

Austin would love to order as many McCaffrés as he could with how dominant CMC has been through the first 3 weeks of the season (78.55 total points and no less than 23.95 pts on a week). Austin also gave a Swift kick to Aaron Jones and Ekeler to make room for D'Andre in his starting lineup. In his 2 games as the starting RB for the Eagles, Swift has a total of 305 yards and 48 fantasy points. Even with all this RB production, Austin will have to make the right start/sit decisions in his other starting slots to keep this strong start rolling.

The Wolfpack finally showed the reason why they were ranked so highly to start the season. Even with a combined 23 points from 4 starters, Ryan managed 133 points on the week, headlined by an insane 142 yard and FOUR TD Raheem Moster experience (not even the best performance of the week). Mostert now has 74.75 points over the last 2 weeks, making him the #1 fantasy player thus far. This team has enough players that can boom on their own and take Ryan's week from 75 points to 140 real quick.

The Tuddy Buddies caught fire in week 3, scoring the 2nd highest score of the week in a 144-76 win over Big Jim. This team saw only 2 positional players score less than 16 points, while having Keenan Allen rack up 215 receiving yards, 49 passing yards and a passing TD. While this may have been a ceiling week for the Buddies, it is now in the range of outcomes on any week.

Big Jim and his Twins came into week 3 ready to repeat last year, and flop all over the Tuddy Buddies. Instead, little Jim slapped him with his twins and zipped those big fellas right into the zipper, dominating the matchup 142-76. Despite this being a nightmare week for Big Jim, he did have some bright spots in Olave and Cook, who continue to do big things through 3 weeks. Chubb was sorely missed. But when you look at the starters (don't look at the bench please) this team has a ton of talent to repeat their week 2 performance at any point this year.

The Urban Myth headed to Buffalo to hold off The Fantasy Disaster 122-103 in week 3 to improve to 2-1 on the year. Joe asked the Bills what they could do to help this past week, and Buffalo said here's 48 points from our QB and out DST - you're welcome. Joe then went to New York and Pittsburgh, who both told him to get lost. Luckily, Joe's last stop was his former hometown, Minnesota, where the Vikings happily handed over 46 points from Jefferson and Mattison. The wild thing is that Joe could have combined starters Mattison, Waller, D. Smith, Najee, Pickens and 9 more points, and they still would not have scored as much as freakin De'Von Achane, who had the bench on actual fire! Achane's 233 yards, FOUR TDs and 55.35 points were nearly a record high, likely only short of Alvin Kamara's 60+ game on Christmas day. Joe may be ranked 6th right now, but if some of his lineup sorts itself out, he'll leave #6 in the dust real quick.

We may not see another rebrand as accurate as The Fantasy Disaster through the first few weeks of their rebrand. Gil is one of two teams sitting at 0-3 and is currently the 2nd lowest scoring team on the year. Even without Joe's bench, Gil would have fallen just short with his best lineup in. While this has all been on the negative side, Gil's team should still be on your playoff radar with all the upside and potential on the roster.

Yisha had his his Asser Roughed for the first time this season, dropping to 2-1 after the 133-100 loss to Ryan's Wolfpack. This was a tough one for Yish, as he had the points on his bench to get the win, but ended up losing by 33 points. The loss came at an even greater cost, as Yish lost WR Mike Williams to a season ending injury, Gus Edwards to a concussion, Gainwell to a Swift D'Andre and Wilson to a horrible Wilson. Yish has lots to sort out to remain above .500

The T-Birds eventually won over the Scorpions, with Danny Zuko at the healm of the the Lightning, right? Well, maybe there is still hope for this Breece Lightning to avenge their first 3 defeats to start 2023. However, I think that story took about 1 hour and 50 minutes to come full circle, so Trev might want to grab some popcorn and get comfy. The injection of Alvin Kamara into this lineup is a great way to start though, as he immediately adds a threat to the struggling RB room. Does this team have what it takes to become the protagonist of their own story? Of course, and I would not be surprised if they made some waves in the near future. Would I bet on it though? At the moment, I would prefer my money in my pocket.

The DingleDawgs put up a modest week, but ended up in the Dawghouse with the loss 115-92. Perhaps though, Jerry's WRs should be allowed out of the Dawghouse, since they have kept this team alive. The RBs have really been the chain keeping this roster stuck to the house, scoring just 10 points this week. With an injury to Deebo, Akers unlikely to start soon and Roschon being on the Bears, Jerry still needs many things to go right before getting away from #12.

Despite a week 2 loss, the self-proclaimed Mayor has Titty City sitting atop the power rankings in back to back weeks. Jacube could be sitting at 2-0 going into week 3, but some poor management has him at 1-1, as Kyren Williams and Jordan Addison racked up 46 points for Titty City's reserves. While nothing is forever in fantasy football, Jacube would love this roster to look the same come week 15, as they are lighting it up on all ends. Even on a bad day, I would bet Jacube is winning a his future matchups against most teams in the league. On a side note, suck a booty Jacube, Tuddy Buddies 4 life!

Game of Jone put forth a valiant effort, but came up just short (12 points) of a win against Joe and fell to 0-2 on the season. Josh received 27 points from Saquon before he went down with what appears to be a multi week ankle injury. The Jones luckily still have ETN and White to fill in, while now relying on some elder statesmen to supplement the loss of Barkley. This team is still very good, even without Saquon.

Baby Jaws was a fish out of water in week 2, because they were on fire, with 5 players scoring 19+ points in a 140-91 win over the Dawgs. This little Jaws was confused early on and was taking bites out of his own team (Kelce, Kupp), but it seems he's gotten on the right path and aimed for other teams now. Jona drafted Jerome Ford, and kept him, and Jaws took a bite out of Chubb's knee, making Mr. Ford an instant RB1. Jona is getting healthy and getting lucky right now. This is not a team I would wish to face in the next few weeks.

Yes, the Wolfpack are 1-1. And yes, they have been involved in the lowest scoring game in back to back weeks. And yes, they only currently have 1.25 starting RBs. But yes, the Wolfpack are still 1-1. And that is with a combined 55 points for Ridley, Brown and Chase through 2 weeks (21 of those coming from Ridley in week 1). While this roster may not seem built out with all the pieces of a full roster, they have so much upside, any week they could secure the win before halftime. Ryan won't play the lowest scoring teams each week, but if I had to put my chips somewhere, it would be where Ryan's team dominates regardless of his opponent, sooner than later.

A big win for Big Jim after being matched up with week 1's top scorer, Austin. The Twins earned their first win of the year in dominant fashion, being the week's top scorer and winning the biggest blowout (53 points). The win came at detrimental cost though, as Jim watched the gruesome injury to Nick Chubb, effectively ending his 2023 season. Chubb is unquestionably a cornerstone piece to any roster, so Big Jim will have some work to do if he wants to keep this great roster great.

The new Urban Myth is that RBs are important. Joe came back on MNF for a big time win against Josh, all with less than 11 points from his starting RBs. How? The Myth had 3 WRs who scored 21+ points, highlighted by a 70 yarder from Pickens. Joe still has a top roster, but these RBs seem to be a thorn that may need to be dealt with sooner than later if he wants to take the next step.

Yahoo said 0-14, so far it has been the opposite for the Tuddy Buddies, who are 2-0 on the year. Could Jacob have one this one? Yes, yes of course, but he didn't! I had some major production from most players in the lineup, making for a big week. I will absolutely need some of these players to pick it up, and others to not lose a step if I want to ride out the Montgomery injury.

A 2-0 start!? Who is this guy?? Yish hasn't seen a perfect start to the season in, well possibly ever, so it's good vibes all around for this team! The 11 pt win was the closest of the week, and it came down to MNF once again for Yish, after he left way too many points on the bench. The identity of this team appears to be sturdiness. They don't appear to be doing any thrashing of the Asses, but will instead slowly and steady slap your booty throughout the week.

The Fantasy Disaster is as advertised through 2 weeks, starting out 0-2 with the 2nd lowest total points thus far. It's an odd start though given Gil's roster. This team appears to have all the fire power necessary to be on the positive side of blowout wins. Week 2, Gil came up short, likely due to Puka being a pine pony, rather than running with the starters and earning 20 (TWENTY) targets and 24 fantasy points. This is still a floor ranking for the Disaster, as I see very good weeks ahead for Gil.

Austin did the rarely seen high-low combo in weeks 1-2. Austin was the high score in week 1 and in the largest win margin game. Week 2, Austin was also in the largest win margin game, except this time, he was the loser of that one, losing 142-89. Austin was hurting bad without Jones and Ekeler, who combined for 60 points in week 1. Week 3 could be the same for this team. The peripherals on this team are not where they need to be without Jones and Ekeler, so for now, Austin will need some luck over skill to get wins.

The 0-2 Breece Lightning is feeling all of 2022 in 2023. With the lowest output through 2 weeks by 14 points, Trevor is having the start of the season he expected. The Lightning were all but lightning in week 2, with all players, bench included, failing to eclipse the 17 point mark. On paper, the Breece's should compete, especially with the addition of Hunt and Kamara in the coming weeks, but we will likely have to see it before we believe it.

The Jerdawgs were riding high off their David V Goliath win over Joe in week 1, but Jerry was quickly brought back down to earth after a booty slapping by Baby Jaws 140-91 in week 2. Deebo looked like his former self with over 100 all purpose yards and a manly TD to go with it. This was a big waiver week for the Jerdawgs, and he may have fallen into some luck with Akers finding a new home so early in the season. The chips will still need to fall in the right places if Jerry wants to move up the board.

Titty City is pouring one out for their starting QB Aaron Rodgers, who tore his Achilles one drive into the season. Luckily for the self-proclaimed Mayor, he drafted 2 QBs! And he already paid up for another #2 in Jordan Love. Jacube started the year hot, scoring 100 points without any coming from the QB slot. This team is stacked without Hill, but when you add in his potential to score 40+ any week, this team will be tough to beat.

Game of Jones drew the short straw and matched up against his brother's 142 points in week 1, meaning he started the year 0-1. It's not a good day when your DST outscores your QB by 10 points, or maybe it's a really good day? This is a bad week for most teams, and I would assume the pendulum will bring Josh back toward where he belongs in week 2.

What if I told you the Dallas DST would outscore Joe Burrow and Tee Higgins by 23 points? It might make sense knowing Higgins had 0 points and Burrow only had 4. It was a disastrous week for Big Jim, including a second 0 by an OUT Mark Andrews, who Jim was surprised to find out about halfway through the early games. Even with 2 zeroes, Jim outscored half the league. I'd expect better days ahead from these starters.

Did you know that Austin only played 7 starters this week? Drake London was effectively a bench player with his zero points. Which means that Austin outscored the next closest team in the league by 38.17 points with one less player than the rest of the league. It was a picture perfect season opener for the Coffees, with all three starting RBs putting up at least 27 points. These are the types of starts that make you feel pretty good about your chances this season, but be careful not to get too excited. Just ask Jona how his week 1 blowout turned out for the rest of last season. Austin is currently stuck in the #4 spot while we wait to find out the status of Ekeler and Aaron Jones.

The worst part about being in the worst matchup of the week is that you have a chance to be the worst team in the worst matchup of the week. Which is exactly what happened to Ryan, scoring just 75 points on the week, despite having a lineup filled with Hurts, AJ Brown, Chase and Ridley. This is a very odd week in football in general, and that is likely the explanation for this team's blunder. I am quite happy to have drawn Ryan on a down week.

Week 1 was one to forget for Joe. He came in as the #1 ranked team up against the #12, and ended up losing by 15 points. On top of that, Joe lost JK Dobbins to yet another season ending injury. Joe will have to navigate his starting lineup a bit before he moves back up the chart.

Sometimes it's better to be lucky than good, and this was one of those times. In the ugliest matchup of the week, I came away with a 3 point 78-75 win over Ryan in week 1. The Tuddy Buddies were exactly that, just two Buddies with one Tuddy each, as I only got 2 TDs on the week across all positions, making it no surprise that I had only 1 player score more than 12 points (and no, it was not the QB). More Tuddys are on tap in week 2 hopefully. Until then, a middle tier ranking is it.

It's been some years, but Gil finally rebranded. And an appropriate rebrand after starting Skyy Moore over just about anyone else on his team, to earn a week 1 loss to Baby Jaws 94-87. Gil had to be excited starting his new toy Bijan, against his backup Allgeier, but was quickly stunned by the outcome. Gil also saw Waddle get outscored by his WR-mate, Hill, by 31 points and had to be wondering why Tua didn't want to spread it around more. The Disaster also lost Dionte Johnson to a hamstring injury, however he may have quickly filled his absence and then some with rookie possible sensation Puka Nacua. This team is for a sure a wait and see team at this moment.

The defending RBB Champs are on the board and looking to run it back, as they start the season with a 97-89 win over Trevor's skeleton squad. Yish got the win on the back of a surprise 23 points by Deshaun Watson. The MNF curse was in Lockport this past week, but skipped over Yisha's house, allowing the Assers to hang on by a late G. Wilson TD. The win's happiness was short-lived, with Yish now having to decide if G. Wilson is startable with Z. Wilson in the game.

Jona and the Baby Jaws suffered more post-draft-pre-sesason blows than any other team in the league, losing both Kupp and Kelce before a single snap was taken. Week 1 looked extra bleak going up against future phenom Bijan while playing his backup. But that story had very unexpected twist, when Allgeier had 75 yards and 2 TDs on 15 attempts, outscoring Bijan by 6.6 points. Jona's 11pm trade with Ryan on the drive to IL for the draft paid dividends immediately, as Tony Pollard went for 82 yards and 2 TDs in week 1, helping Jona to the win over Gil. Jona has too many questions right now to be moved higher than #10.

Another long long overdue rebrand! After not changing his name for years, despite not having Mooney on his team for years, Trevor changed his team name about 4 times in a matter of an hour until he finally landed on Breece Lightning. And for good reason, as Breece looked far better than anticpated in his 2023 debut. Trevor, out of nowhere, easily could have won this matchup had he played the right lineup, as he had 73 points on his bench.
