This team may only win whenever Lightning strikes, but when it does, you better hope it's not against you.

Do you believe in miracles!? YES! Jerry was the 1980s US hockey team VS Joe's Russians in week 1, and Jerry had his miracle completed, winning 104-89. Left for dead WR Pitty City came through big time as a top 10 WR on the week with his 20.7 points to combat Justin Jefferson's 138 yards in the 1st half against the Bucs. The US did go on to win that gold medal, so there is hope for Jerbear here, but the movie was appropriately named 'Miracle'. We will need to see a bit more before moving him out of the 12th place ranking.

Is it easy to build a powerhouse team with the #1 overall pick and two extra 3rd round picks? Ask Joe, but the answer is yes. The only real tough question Joe had all draft was whether he should take Bijan or Jefferson at the 1.01, and if history is any indication of the future, I think his choice of Jefferson will be well worth it. Joe's starters are loaded after piling up the RBs in rounds 2&3 and stealing Waller in the 4th (though it is a gamble pick). Beyond Joe's known commodities, there are multiple players who could breakout into next year's keepers. Burks, Achane, Mims and Pickens all have super boom potential if chips land in their directions.

If you were not present for Julia and Ryan's pre-wedding and wedding festivities, you may have missed that Ryan claimed his hidden talent to be "fantasy sports". Having the best overall record (34-20), tied for the most championships in the league (2) and this draft should be confirmation that Ryan was not lying about his talent. Drafting from the 9th slot, Ryan came away with Hurts, AJ Brown, Chase, Mostert, Ridley, JSN, Dillon, oh and Jonathan Taylor (should he be anything this year). This looks like a team that could win in the first 15 minutes of NFL Redzone any given sunday, so don't be surprised if Ryan is once again better than you at fantasy football this year.

What did Josh do with the 2nd overall pick and an extra 2nd round selection? He built a team that will likely dominate outside of injury. Josh took a gamble early, taking Saquon at the 1.02, but filled the rest of his lineup with moon shots like ETN, Lamar, Adams and Cooper, who could all blow up any week and should still be solid even on down weeks. The talent doesn't stop at the starters either, as Josh has plenty of WR depth on his bench. They may be the WRs of yesteryears, but the talent is still undeniable.

Big Jim and his Twins have, for the first time in the league, a full Chubb. Jim could have taken anyone (outside of Jefferson and Saquon), and he could not pass up Nick Chubb to go along with the Twins. In all seriousness though, Chubb will likely compete for fantasy MVP this season, which will just be a bonus to this roster, which is filled with the likes of Tee Higgins, James Cook, Javonte Williams, Chris Olave, Mark Andrews and Joe Burrow. Without even needing to go to the bench for flex options, Jim is likely starting with 10-15 points more than most rosters each week.

Austin may be reading these rankings as a recap and reminder as to how the draft went after an "M" was replaced with a "W" on our Mild Sunday afternoon draft. So, Austin, to recap, you're probably going to be pretty good, which should be no surprise when you start the draft with two of the top 4-5 RBs in fantasy. However, Austin will still have some work to do, as his bench feels thin on paper, making his starters have to be everything they were drafted to be and more. Either way, 2022 draft Austin is definitely invited back for the 2023 draft.

The self-proclaimed Mayor made waves when he took back to back QBs in rounds 9 and 11 without having a 10th pick. But the past is the past. There is no question about it, Titty City has to be happy with their Mayor for the talent he brought back to town. The great foundation of Jacobs and St. Brown was built on by adding Gibbs, Hill, Addison and Evans, who all should be competing for starting slots in T City. The ceiling is 1st place for this team, and it feels like this team is ranked at its floor.

This time last year, Yish was ranked the #1 team in the league with a bright future ahead. This year, Yish has dropped 6 spots to #7 after drafting 12th from his championship seat, which a host of challenges. Luckily for Yish, he entered the draft with a 9th round Garrett Wilson, who has the potential to be a top 3 WR this year and a cornerstone piece of this offense. There is plenty of upside to go along with the steadiness of this roster, and it will be interesting to see how it stacks up in the new division.

The draft did not going according to any of the mocks for me. I had no intentions of taking several players that are now a part of the Tuddy Buddies. On paper, it does not project to be a great season for the Buddies, but I am hopeful some of these darts find the bullseye!

Coming off his worst season in his RBB career (11th), Gil was gifted with arguably the most talented RB in the NFL in Bijan Robinson at the 5th overall pick. Outside of Bijan and Waddle however, this roster is a bit tough to judge with all the questionable futures. Will Aiyuk take the next step? Are Pierce and Watson legit? Is McLaurin still the #1 with Dotson? Does Charbonnet beat out Walker? Pacheco? Williams, Moore, Johnston? If even half of these answers land on the positive side, Gil will be finishing far above this initial #9 ranking.

Though Jona had two high end keepers in Cooper Kupp and Tony Pollard, Jona my be questioning his drafting abilities. He is quickly reaching into his bag of tricks to pull out some dad strength, as the JAWORking My Magic has turned into Baby Jaws Loading. From the #4 spot in the draft, Jona went with a very bold strategy and came away with an unprecedented stack of Mahomes and Kelce. Without having a 3rd, Jona turned his top two picks into onesie positions, both on the Chiefs! While yes, this is one of the most potent stacks in fantasy football, Jona will need his starters to stay healthy and produce if he wants to get ahead of this initial bottom half ranking. Oh, but that already has gone out the window, as Kupp is out for ______ weeks?? And Kelce is potentially looking at multiple missed weeks. Maybe Jona will get all the bad vibes out early on this year.

Trevor, Trevor Trevor. One of two teams who desparately sold out in 2022 had possibly a record number of draft picks between rounds 10-14, which was 8 to be exact. Despite having a skeleton of picks, Trevor actually walked away from this draft with tremendous upside. If Fields performs like the back half of 2022, Dotson takes the leap and Hall is healthy, this team will have plenty of points to compete. And that doesn't even include Diggs' natural domination, and the talent Kamara can bring after week 3. There is hope for this team, which did not exist on Saturday.

The who??? After some very suspect moves at the trade deadline in 2022, Jerry has cleaned house and re-branded as the Jerdawgs. The Dinglejerries are where they belong, in the toilet, after 7 title-less seasons. The Jerdawgs need to be patient though, similar to how patient Jerry was in rounds 2-4, as the turnound may take longer than expected after being forced to draft the replacements in rounds 16 through 25.

2024.notes: The Jerdawgs haven't been this close to a blue shirt since they blew it back in 2017. Sitting at 14-1 on the season, Big Jim is his only blemish this season. Can Jerry get revenge in the Senior Bowl?
Big Jim is shattering his personal records this year! After a stress-free semifinal, the Twins have a shot at the title in the first ever Senior Bowl!

The historic run is over. From an improbable playoff berth to taking down Austin's super team, Jacob won over the hearts of a few owners. Mistakes were made in the semis, but Titty City can still take home a 3rd place finish.

After walking through what was supposed to be the big playoff matchup with the Wolfpack, Yish found himself on the other end of an easy matchup with the Twins. With 3rd place on the line, the Bakery played all 3 playoff games vs the Bun Spreaders division this year.
Ryan secured 5th place in the most dominant fashion the RBB has ever seen (205 freakin points). The remaining playoff teams should thank Yish for removing that powerhouse from contention.
Outside of missing the playoffs, this is the worst ending to a purchased season. 2024 had an ending we did not expect, and 2025 may be just as interesting.
What I time to come alive! Saving the best of the year for the Toilet Bowl is good stuff. At least a top 2 pick is loaded up for 2025.

If Joe's team didn't wait so long to wake up, he'd likely have been playing in the semifinals last week. Instead, he's heading into the finals of the Toilet Bowl looking to earn the 1st overall pick for the 2nd time.
The Big Lig really had no chance against the red hot Buddies, but they do have a shot at 9th place against a flailing flounder.
Luckily Jona hung onto the 8th seed and guaranteed a top 4 pick, as the #4 picks seems like where he's headed. But 9th and 10th are just numbers at this time of the year.

The Mooney Toons know it's all about your last episode. Leaving everyone on a happy note and with a cliffhanger is writing 101. With an 11th place win and picks 1.06 and 1.07, Trev has the last few fans on board for next season.
After an odd stretch of greatness, Josh finished his tough season in the expected 12th spot. Game of Jones can only go up from here in 2025.

Holy bye week! If this was real life, the game tape would make the Beef Boys panic at their semifinal matchup. 124 points without Lamar's 42 in the lineup is saying something. Hopefully this isn't just another case of the bye week blow up, and Big Jim brings the big boys to play in week 16.

Yish went from feeling like a TB appearance was unavoidable to completing the upset win over the Wolf Pack in round 1. The Bakery will have to sort out their pastries, as a few top sellers were taken off the menu for week 16.

While it will never be coming to a theater near you, this story has all the makings to be the RBB version of the 1980 U.S. Olympic hockey team. Titty City already beat the Russians, but can they finish off the Miracle?

The Jerdawgs got their well-deserved week of rest and came back shocked to see their semifinal opponent. Jerry is looking to be just the 4th team in 9 years to make it to the finals as the #1 overall seed, but Jacob and his luck stand in the way.

Being 2 points away from a bye week, only to end up exiting the playoffs in round 1, the Wolf Pack has to be disappointed with the final few weeks of the season. Though divisional playoff seeding needs to change, Ryan can at least be happy that it did not change the outcome.

When the mighty fall, they fall hard. After gambling with draft picks like they were tooth picks, Austin found himself to be the 2nd team destroyed by CMC in one season. A disappointing end to a promising roster may make for a disappointing 2025 as well.

Bye weeks are fun. Especially when your roster scores 147 points without even playing a full lineup. The crash back to earth feels inevitable, as the last time the Buddies squared off with the Big Lig, Gil found himself in Atlanta with 163 points.
The fire is real. If Joe was in the playoffs right now, he'd be a scary team to play against. So everyone in the TB should be hoping Jona can squeeze out a win.

The Big Lig outlasts the Mooney Toons in a throwback battle of the 70s! While this team somehow stinks each week in real life, the paper says it should be very different. Gil only needs to get through the Tuddy Buddies to have a shot at the top pick.
Baby Jaws took the rest week seriously. Almost nobody scored points for him on the beach. He will need everyone and then some to take down Josh Allen in the TB semifinals.
Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde have found a home for the final few weeks of the season. With only one game left, Josh has likely been focused on 2025 for some time now.

Who would have thought that in week 15, for the 11th/12th place game, we would be seeing the first overall pick be matched up with the 2nd overall pick? But here we are. Trev is one game away from officially counting the days to next year's draft.

Scrooge McDuck rode those gold coins to a Gravy Goons division title and the 3rd overall seed. As a bonus, he gets to play against the trash pandas in round 1, making the odds of a semifinal appearance about -550.

From the bye week and division champs to the 4th seed, Ryan's NFL bye week destroyed his waltz into the semifinals. A big time tilt with Yish looms, as both teams can make a case to be the favorite to win their 3rd title.

A few weeks back, Yish was ready to claim his spot as the Toilet Bowl bye team. A few weeks later, after a big W over Austin and the collapse of the Tuddy Buddies, Yish easily takes the #5 seed. A matchup with the only other remaining 2x champ comes in round 1.

Jerry cushioned his newly set record, ending the regular season with 13 wins in 14 chances. Good for Jerry! He can take the week off, but hopefully the rest doesn't stop the streak, as the Dawgs are up against the numbers. No team has won the league from the #1 seed, and only 3 teams have even made it to the finals (2018, 2019, 2023).

Big Jim took advantage of a bye week nightmare for the Wolf Pack and joined Jerry at Spa15. The round 1 bye is a first for the Twins, and it guarantees them their first ever semifinal appearance in the RBB, as well as their first division title.
This trash team lucked their way into the rarely seen wildcard game bye. Either way, Titty City wanders into another postseason looking just oh so sharp.
What a joke of a week. Just moderately okay would have sufficed for the win. But Murphy's Law is a fitting end to a stupid season. Men in Black to fantasy 2024.
Though it's a little late for Gil's postseason push, his team is starting to hit its stride. One that may be able to take him to the #1 overall pick if he can get past the up and down Mooney Toons.
60 points from Allen! Who cares about the rest of your team when one guy scores more than half of most teams' totals. Joe may need those 60 points again, as he drew the straw of a red hot Josh Jones.

A surging Josh Jones has seen his backups get called into action. Apparently reserving all of his points for the final few weeks of the season, Game of Jones may very well be the Cinderella story of the Toilet Bowl this year after breaking the regular season loss record with 12 (previously 11).
Pick a name and throw it in! A carousel of starters for Trev has resulted in the #11 seed heading into the illustrious Toilet Bowl.
Despite driving himself to this destination prior to the trade deadline, Jona can't be too happy with 2024. Well Jona, join the club. At least a Toilet Bowl bye is on the docket.

Monday night came close to haunting the Bakery once again, but Yish held strong and snapped his Toilet Bowl streak at 1. Now all that is left is to see which seed the Boys will be sitting in next week.

CMC could not keep up with the Joneses, as their sights were set on a 2nd straight championship, and CMC needed to take the remainder of the year off. The reigning MVP is a huge loss, but the rest of this lineup is still filled with talent, so don't be too worried about Austin's chances at a repeat.

The Wolf Pack showed some mercy and kept the Tuddy Buddies alive with a huge win over Titty City. The win also gives Ryan the control over his own destiny, as a win in week 14 would give him the #2 seed and a week off.

Say hello to the new regular season win total record holder, as Jerry becomes the first team to ever win 12 games in one regular season. Regular season titles mean nothing without the blue shirt though, so the Dawgs have their sights set on something a little higher.

Big Jim needed everything he had to come away with the season sweep over the Tuddy Buddies. The Twins are now just one win away from guaranteeing their best finish in their RBB career, as the winner of Twins V Wolves earns the 2nd round 1 bye.

Another week, another example of why fantasy football sucks. The Buddies did get some help and now find themselves in an early wildcard matchup with Titty City to see who will be the 3rd Bun Spreader to make the playoffs this year (shout out to that division for having 3 playoff teams in back to back years).

The Big Lig has been in bathroom mode for weeks now, but this week will have round 1 implications. There is still a chance, slightly outside though, that Gil will steal away the TB bye from Baby Jaws.

Titty City has come so close to punching the postseason ticket multiple times this season, but jsut keeps coming up short. The self-proclaimed Mayor may just be a fan of the dramatics, and if so, he found it. Titty City has all the ta-tas on deck for a win and in game vs the Buddies in week 14.

In a previous power ranking, Joe was coined the "all upside team", and the name is finally coming to fruition. If these guys can continue to hit, Joe has a better than most chance at the #1 overall pick.

The week 14 loss felt a little better than most, seeing as his loss came to the team that essentially traded a 1st round pick for Adams and Kelce. Trev is solidified in the bottom 4 teams, meaning week 14 is strictly for seeding.

Baby Jaws has been hunted for weeks now, and he has taken blow after blow. Another roster spot dedicated to the IR is becoming a weekly thing for Jona. If Gil loses, or the Shark can win, or even just outscore The Big Lig by 12 points, he will hang on to the #2 bye in the TB next week.

Whoa baby did Josh get close to throwing some chaos into the playoff mix, as he channelled some frustration through Jerry Jeudy to make his game vs Yish quite interesting. With only one game remaining, Josh will try and split the 2024 series with his brother.
Yes, half of the first round was on bye for Austin, but the output still has to raise some questions about this team. Are they still the odds on favorites? Sure. But teams are creeping up closer.

Hopefully the David V Goliath game didn't happen too early in the season. Needing every win and some help, Yish took down Austin and received the help he was looking for in losses to the Buddies and Sharks. The postseason door is opening for the Beefers.

Does one player make your team? In real life, no. But this is fantasy, and it's about time Saquon gets the respect he deserves, as he drags Jerry up the rankings. Also, Jerry became the 4th team to ever reach 11 wins in one season with his week 12 win, and he now has 2 games left to break the all-time regular season win total.
Ryan must have gone digging up Austin's booty hole, as 1 singular play (potentially the highest scoring play in RBB history) won him the week. The Pack is now firmly in the round 1 bye conversation.

Big Jim loves chaos. Why get into playoffs easily, when you can make it interesting while also inflating the bubble for more teams to fit on. The loss in Titty City could have major playoff ramifications that we will see play out soon.

Fantasy football sucks. The only thing that sucks worse is every player on the Dallas Cowboys defense, who should be required to spend every practice rep this week attempting to lick their own buttholes, as that is what they apparently do during games.
The Big Lig can't stop winning! With 3 straight wins following the sale of some talent, Gil may want to consider selling around week 2 or 3 next season to kickstart his streak.

Garbage is literally piling up in Titty City, yet this team continues to win games. A team that should have been grabbing a newspaper and warming up the seat, is now very close to making their 3rd straight playoff appearance.

One more win would have put Joe at least in the question of a round 1 TB bye, but then Saquon ran away with those chances, leaving Joe at 3-9. He will happily welcome back Chase Brown and Allen off their bye, as he pushes for a solid week 1 matchup.

The Booby Toons decided RBs aren't really worth casting, so he used just 0.9 of one and still beat Game of Jones by nearly 40 points. Trevor is unlikely to get a TB bye, so he will be hanging around to surprise someone into a loss.

A slop fest of a matchup ended with Baby Jaws pushing his playoff chances virtually out of reach. Which, at this point, is likely the goal, as top 4 pick in next year's draft is close to guaranteed for Jona.
Injuries, byes and backups oh my! Josh is as close to waving the white flag on this season as possible, as the talent is just not there to compete against just about any team right now.
If you're looking for your lost horseshoe, there's a good chance you can find it somewhere around Austin's as. The team is stacked, but anything can happen any week.

If you're looking for luck, you won't find it anywhere near the Bakery. The Beef Boys have been getting beefed for weeks now, with top 5 weekly scores hitting on the reg, leaving Yish needing a few wins and some help to find the playoffs.

The Wolf Pack took the week off in order to inject some chaos into the playoff race. While this team is ready to dominate, they also have shown the propensity to disappear. The playoffs should be exciting times!
Another week, another win. This is becoming routine now. Except this time, Jerry needed everyone to hold off Titty City's final dance.

Big Jim falling victim by just under 3 points to an insane 40 point game from Mixon on MNF should not make you forget how good this team has been. A couple wins in the divisional games will have him looking at a round 1 bye.

The Tuddy Buddies took a step in the right direction with a win in week 11. But averaging around. 100 points per game over the last 3 weeks will almost certainly result in an 0-3 record over the next 3 divisional games.
Gil's back to back wins have him a little closer to the round 1 TB bye, but he'll likely still need a little help and a few more wins to make that happen. The Big Lig is rising though.

Titty City was all tatas on deck in week 11, offering the handsiest of dances to anyone with a point to give. Just 5 points shy of virtually locking in a playoff spot, the self-proclaimed Mayor now has to fight his way into the room where it happens.

Joe decided not to ship anyone out during the early Black Friday sales, and he was rewarded with a razor thin 0.44 point crushing blow to the Bakery's chances at the postseason. Joe still has an outside chance at the week 1 bye.
Holy moly, Breece coming to life for 1/3 of the team's week 11 total, which was just short of what was needed for a win. At 3-8, Trev is just hoping for an easy toilet bowl schedule.
Well here we are. A couple players lighter, and Jona is in a decent position to play in the 2024 playoffs. Stuck somewhere in the middle, Baby Jaws can't decide which water he'd prefer to roam in.

Seemingly the only thing left in these final 3 games is to play spoiler to someone else. Jerry Jeudy's 93 yard TD 10 seconds into Sunday made it seem like Josh was going to do just that. It will have to be a divisional upset if one happens.
Eek. A first rounder turns into 107 points the very next week? Knowing that this is a possibility leaves some vulnerability to what appears to be a US olympic basketball roster.
The Bakery was closed before Friday of week 10. They spent the weekend changing their menu for the upcoming holiday season and have solidified themselves as one of the best teams on paper.
Ja'Marr Chase's 56 points overshadows how Ryan's QB (10.58 points) was his lowest scoring starting position by at least 4 points.
If week 9 can lick a booty hole, week 10 needs to go to thunder from down under and get to work.
Feeling like the most fraudulent 9-1 team to ever exist, Jerry will probably enter the semifinals 13-1 and win out and finally grab the elusive blue shirt.
Big Jim survived the background actors of the Mooney Toons to keep his shot at a round 1 bye alive. 3 weeks of divisional matchups are still ahead.
In an annual occurrence for the Big Lig, a sale sparks big performances. Will his streamlined team continue to rack up wins heading into the toilet bowl??

After trading for two instant injuries last season, Jacob turned off his phone during trade season. His goon squad enters the final weeks of the regular season with the 4th lowest amount of points scored, and still somehow 6 wins.
Don't let Joe Burrow's 41 points fool you, the Mooney Toons are still using scab actors in their episodes. But, Burrow can clearly keep this team relevant on any given week.
Staying quiet during the RBB stock exchange, Joe's team remains in contention for the first overall pick in 2025.
A surprise seller, Jona unloaded some top notch talent into the playoff pool. His departure from the playoff race drops the bubble teams to 3.
With 3 players combining for 3.65 points, 92 points on the week should feel like an accomplishment. Josh is just counting the days until Labor Day 2025.

Nobody faults the Yankees or Dodgers when they win a World Series after spending $300 million on their roster, but the people certainly cheer harder for the Marlins when they take down Goliath on 1/3rd the budget. Bonus: A favorite quote from That 70s Show - "there's nothing wrong with you that changing yourself completely couldn't fix".

Unless you were OUT or on BYE, you pretty much had a TD by the end of the first quarter on Sunday just by being a member of the Wolf Pack. An already dangerous team added two more players to give Ryan a real shot at his 3rd RBB title.

5 weeks ago, an undefeated season was not out of the question for the Bakery. Heading into week 10, the Beef Boys are in danger of a .500 record going into the final stretch of regular season matchups.
Week 9 can lick a booty hole. The Buddies will be working on the "Tuddy" part in week 10 against the 8-1 Humpers.
Two weeks early, Jerry positioned his team for a deep playoff run. At 8-1 he can already start planning his start/sit decisions for weeks 14-17.

Baby Jaws is skinny dipping into week 10, as he is streaking in the win column with 3 Ws in a row. The arrow is up, and there is a real chance the little shark does not go hungry another week this season.
The Twins are getting kicked at the wrong time of the season. If Lamar and the RBs can keep the banana boat afloat, Big Jim will have a good shot at the postseason.

The Big Lig had several picks before round 5 in the 2024 draft, and things will be no different in the 2025 draft. Gil will have to manage the names leaving while still trying to have a shot at the #1 pick.

A heartbreak loss to the Big Malak in week 9 confirmed Joe's 2025 playoff appearance was only a myth. He will have to officially turn his sights to try and win the #1 overall pick and a fresh start in 2025.
Despite having a recovering team on the rise, Trevor opened up a Dollar Tree in place of the network studios.

The self-proclaimed Mayor is 1-1 when starting a 0 in his lineup over the last two weeks. This boat was full of holes prior to week 10, and after some flea market type deals occurred elsewhere, those holes only got bigger.
If Trevor is Dollar Tree, Josh is Five Below. Either way, Austin brought his money and rented out both stores for his 1%ers party.
Two tough losses brings them back to #1. If you thought Mason is what made this team good, check again.
With almost 300 points scored over the last two weeks, the Buddies are being gifted too many startable options. They'll need every point in their divisional matchup with the Wolf Pack.
Flop city pulls the zipper on the last remaining shot at a perfect season. The league's highest scoring team is a dynamite ready to blow any Sunday.
Jerry could never play for Coach Carter, as he is not perfect anymore. Will being the lowest scored points against team start to catch up to the Dawgs down the stretch?
Narrowly missing out on winning back to back weeks without a full QB start, Ryan falls to 5-3. Somehow, even with injuries, the Wolf Pack appears as strong as ever.
No Puka no problem? We'll see how the team fares with one less dominator. At 2-6, this team is a prime example that "on paper" does not mean wins.
It has been an up and down go for Jona so far, but the stars just might be aligning. If they do, Jona could easily be a team that runs the table on the regular season.
Almost nobody was keeping up with the Joneses in week 8, with Austin ripping out a quick 152 while leaving points on the bench. This is easily one of the oddest teams to try and get a read on.

Where there is life, there is death. Game of Jones exploded for their highest point total of the season, while simultaneously losing a key contributor in Diggs. At 2-6, grasping at straws is all one can do.
I mean what can you say really? This is the most expensive cast to be aired on daytime television.
Unexpectedly, this team showed out to get to 2-6 on the year. It would take literally everything right to happen, but the pieces may be in place for Joe to make things interesting.
Jacobs and Gibbs is the name of the new law firm in Titty City. Any other business taking place there appears to be some sort of a scam.
Wild week. Malik Nabers was the only Buddy without a Tuddy. If this is the new direction and even a portion of week 7 can remain, the end zone might become their new backyard.
The Bakery was short on dough this week, producing its lowest output of the season. I'd assume the Beef Boys will have their business back in shape by week 8.
Lamar was the Big Jim this week, launching this team to a victory. The Twins have been kicked, and now we get to see how they manage the injuries.
Fantasy football can be ruthless. Starving for a win, The Big Lig felt the flop of the Twins hit and heavy on Monday night. A quick recovery is vital to Gil's season.
It's possible Jerry humped a golden egg this offseason. His opponent has scored more than 99 points only TWICE this season. A fancy new WR purchase is likely on the horizon.
This has not been Josh's year. 1-6 should have told you that before I did. But don't be shocked if this team goes on a run over the next month or so.
King Henry is truly the alpha wolf. In fantasy and real life. Ryan has to feel blessed to be 5-2 after the way he won this week. However, injuries and QB changes have week 8 looking quite different.
Jonah narrowly avoided being beached, and the tides have pushed back to sea. Is Cooper Kupp the heartbeat of this baby beast??
There must be a writers strike taking place, as these scabs have now penned 5 weeks of less 85 points in 7 chances. This show is ripe for antenna tv only.
A crushing defeat on both the scoreboard and in the lineup. A 2nd season-ending injury has some very unsexy names going to bat for the Joneses in week 8.

Only needing 75 points for the win, Jacob broke the 119 ceiling of last week with 128. Despite back to back good weeks, the self-proclaimed mayor has to have almost no confidence going into each Sunday.

Even with the handicap of Jayden Daniels barely playing week 7, Joe could not come within 15 points of the Wolf Pack. There was potential for this team, but almost none of it came to fruition this season.
Beef Boys be back to Beefin' after a week of vacation. Easily one of the safest floor teams, with a ceiling as high as anyone.
Self-inflicted wounds are the hardest to heal. This 3rd cut stings the worst of them all this season.
The Twins took a couple of hard kicks this weekend and still managed a W. With games against Gil and Jerry coming up, Jim is just as likely to be 6-2 and he is 4-4.
Derrick Henry is the alpha wolf. In 6 games he has 750+ total yards and 9 TDs. As long as Henry is in and the starters stay healthy, Ryan likely doesn't lose many more games this year.
Jerry is the only team to score above 110 points in every game this season. Knowing that's the bar, bring your best against the Dawgs.
The Big Lig never had the points to hand Jerry his first L of the season. A 32 point swing for Chase will do that to you.
Disappointing to have your best week of the year thus far on a week when you didn't even need your worst (89). The depth was a concern, and it may begin to show with a top performing WR going down.
Who would have expected the Davis' to drop 40 points? Leaving 43 points on the bench across 3 positions in a loss is never an easy one to swallow, even if they weren't autostart points.
It's either a great episode, or a racist joke has viewers tuning out immediately. In 6 games, Trev has either scored 110+ (twice), or less than 85 (2 of those were less than 70).
Baby Jaws is lost in the ocean somewhere, looking for any familiar water. 4 straight losses, but the prodigal son, Kupp, may be enough to bring this baby home.
Titty City was at its best in week 6, but still couldn't best their division rival. 4 TDs from 2 Bears in one game is unlikely to occur again. 119 may be Jacube's ceiling.

An 87-85 win is exactly how the models would have projected Joe to get his first W of the season. Regardless, a win is a win, and you can't have an incredible underdog story without first being an incredible underdog.
The Beef Boys finally got beefed by the only other undefeated team in the RBB. The loss will not stop the Bakery for its 4th straight week as the #1 place to eat.

The Twins are trying to make their first RBB baby and drape it in that baby blue sweetness that just feels like home. This may be their best chance yet, as they have only scored less than 114 points once this season.

Winning wasn't in the cards for the Buddies this week, but Deebo and Wicks did their best to make sure of that by removing all the wildcards from the deck. Both of the TBs losses have come against a top 2 scoring teams.
The jam-packed Bun Spreaders (all at 3-2) division is lead by the Alpha Wolf, who still leads the league in points scored. #4 is less about Ryan and more about the other teams.
When I said 170 points, I didn't mean to be so specific. Gil must have been watching old reruns of the Oprah Show all week, as his generosity in handing out touchdowns was unmatched.
Preseason polls would have had the O/U of wins through 5 weeks at 0.5. Just one game shy of 0.500, the reigning champion has a starting roster that can explode at any moment.

5-0 and ready to go! Jerry is spending this season doing the humping rather than the receiving he did in 2023. Injuries are a real concern, but an undefeated mark in the middle of October allows for some injury management.

The writing staff does just enough to keep the network execs interested. Adding some extra lines to ancillary characters and giving new scenery to the leads just may be enough to keep the show alive long enough to climb the charts.
Josh is on the board! His first game over 100 points since week 1's 113, and it resulted in a win. The hole is deep, but now there's a little less dirt.
Baby Jaws is so hungry after 3 straight missed kills that he started eating his own players. If he can survive without a few fins, he might be able to kill again.

Titty City is a weird place to be right now. A's are D's, pepperoni is in, people are even giving beads away to the men. This team is the opposite of exciting, yet they're 3-2. Stranger Things season Jacob episode 6.
The Malaks are on exact opposite trajectories. Joe's loss to the other 0-4 left him alone at 0-5 and potentially already looking ahead to Labor Day weekend 2025.
Beef Boys be Beefin. And when they beefin, you probably gettin beefed. Zero of four opponents have scored within 22 points of the Bakery, which is averaging 126 baked goods per week.

Big Jim is the only team with a win to not have spent a dollar on the waiver wire. If he can stay healthy, navigating bye weeks may be the easiest it has been for the Twins in their RBB career. 2-2 should not make you think you have an easy win coming up against this lineup.
Okay so more pixie dust was leftover than I thought. Only about 5 times in the last 5 years has a team scored 150+ in back to back weeks. The Pack is hunting right now.
The WR injuries are never-ending, but the star power is burning bright right now. If it continues and health returns, the Buddies will be bringing the Tuddies.

Trending upward, but still losing. This roster should be better, but 4th lowest PF in the league is not getting it done. However, of all the teams, this one is top 3 that would not shock me to drop 170 any given week.

Meeting the other undefeated team when you're not at your best is a recipe for not being undefeated anymore. Jerry will have hurdles to jump in the coming weeks to fill the gap of a top 5 WR through 4 weeks.

Consistency can be key, if it's working. Austin has swapped in 1 different flex player and 1 different QB through 4 weeks (that includes DST). The locked in positions have scored no less than 98 points, but the upside may not be much higher than the 127 we've already seen.

The fantasy gods have kept their focus on the Burnt Biscuit Division, ravaging Jona's team with injuries, ineptitude, and byes. Luckily it may only be one bad week, as 14 of Jona's players are taking the week off.

Titty City might be finding its groove… just in time for bye weeks to come in. A thin starting lineup makes for a thin bench. The self-proclaimed Mayor is willing to show the goods for beads and wins.

The writers of The Mooney Toons are clearly trying to prove a point to the networks execs. Following up an 84 point week with their 2nd week in the 60s is a strong way to say "we'll stink as long as we want".
On Labor Day, 0-4 for this lineup would have been +100000. Now that 0-4 is real, the model gives Josh just a 0.6% chance of making the playoffs.
Already struggling, Joe can't catch a break. He's the only <2 win team to have 400+ points scored, and he's currently #3 in points against. It's a big hole, but crazier things have happened.
The Beef Boys are Baking only wins right now, and seemingly getting better each week. However the Big Lig may be in good graces with the gods again, making week 4 tough.
Nothing Big Jim could have done in this one against Ryan. The Twins have had nearly 100 more points scored against them than the next closest team.
Jerry hasn't had a team score within 12 points of him this season, with 2 of 3 weeks being blowouts. Does the hotness continue?
The fantasy gods turned their attention away from the Big Lig for one week, and he turned it into a win. Does he have their attention again this week?
The Wolf Pack had a magic lineup last week, devouring Jim's Twins. It's not likely to continue as magically, but I bet some of the pixie dust remains.
Austin was on the positive side of the 0.05 point margin and is on the cusp of having everyone try to keep up with the Jones again.
Jona got humped by the Bark(ley)ing Jerdawgs in week 3. Dealing with injuries now, Jona may have to hope his rations are enough to survive the next few weeks.

Even with Mark Andrews playing left tackle instead of TE, the Tuddy Buddies put up the 2nd highest score of the week at 124 points. 60 came from two players. Points need to be spread around, or 2-2 is likely.
Game of Jones was 0.05 points away from 1-2. Now at 0-3, every week seems like a must win situation.
The ratings have been dropping for weeks. A few more bad episodes and the show may be on the verge of being cancelled.

Titty City put their tassels back on after the self-proclaimed Mayor scratched 98 points from their lineup on purpose. If Jacube wants some milk, it's probably coming from the grocery store this week.
0-3 is a tough spot to be. According to Yahoo, only 12% of 0-3 teams make the playoffs. Joe has an uphill battle to say the least.

The Beef Boys, or should I say Beef Boy, was on FIRE this week. Alvin Kamara was looking like the limited edition collectible Christmas Kamara this past week, as he racked up 180 total yards and 4 freakin TDs against the freakin Cowboys! Alvin's 49 points were awesome, but Jordan Mason reach 20+ points in both of his starts is what may propel Yish into a lengthy win streak to start the season. There are currently no holes in this team's starting lineup, making them the likely favorite each week.

Baby Jaws is 2 for 2 on hunts in 2024, as he easily tracked down and destroyed Game of Jones 126-74 in week 2. The big sharks were out, as Jona has 5 players score more than 17 points, 3 of which were all the way up over 25 points. Arguably a top two pick in the draft, take your pick between Mason and this guy, JK Dobbins is torching the NFL right now with one great leg and one okay leg - rushing for over 130 yards in back to back games. Nico Collins, the nobody of a 2 years ago, is potentially on the same career arc as Davante Adams, which means Jona has birthed a star into the league. The injury bug is not shy thus far in 2024, and overcoming some big names going down will be Jona's biggest hurdle early on this season.

Big Jim, involved in another high-scoring battle for the 2nd week in a row, except week 2 brought his record to 1-1 rather than 2-0. TNF had Jim feeling like Sunday and Monday weren't even necessary after James Cook dropped 32 points on 3 tuddies vs the Dolphins. Even after deciding to play Sunday and Monday, the Twins put together a solid outing, scoring 114.75 points, good enough for 4th best on the week. Pops has some fire power in those shorts this year, making you wonder if flop season is upon us.

One week after FlopFest 2024, the Mooney Toons released an episode that cheered up the loyal fan base, earning a W in the ratings. Trevor was feeling the sweat of another bad episode slipping down his back and into his butt cheeks, as Achane was destroying the Bills and Marv had about 130 yards and 2 TDs in the first quarter. But, Trev called upon his best characters to deliver believable performances, and they did not disappoint. The shows ratings have come back in, and the viewers are currently hating this rendition of Travis Kelce, who has managed just 4 catches for 6.6 fantasy points through two weeks and two KC wins.

The diggity doggs be humping their way to a 2-0 start with a win over Ryan's Wolves in week 2. Jerry didn't even need KW3, and subbed in Christian Kirk to prove a point, getting just 0.4 points more than he would have gotten by starting the inactive Kenneth Walker. Luckily for Jerry, his other RBs were once again great, totaling 42+ points. The real story so far is the emergence of rookie TE Brock Bowers, who looks like he's still playing against college students through two weeks of NFL action. As long as Jerry can keep his group mostly healthy, he should have no problem making a run in the playoffs.

Game of Jones drops a dub in week 2. No, not a dub, a dud in week 2. Autocorrect doesn't have access to yahoo. Josh really never had a chance in this one after Jona had a 3 players score 25 or more points (more than Josh's entire team combined). After blow up games and shattered ceilings in week 1, the up came down in week 2, with 3 players (Hill/Diggs/Mixon) scoring a combined 57 less points than they did in week 1. Josh has way too many big names to be ignored, so I would assume that this is more of a blip on the radar than a reading of the tarot cards.

Austin had the rest of the league trying to keep up with the Joneses early on Sunday, after Shaheed, Lamb and Godwin each had a 40+ yard touchdown within moments of each other, setting the table for an easy win over the Tuddy Buddies 127-91. Austin overcame just 17 points from Herbert and Pitts combined, primarily thanks to some massive scoring plays and quality RB efforts. The mid round was good to this team during the draft, and the rewards are coming in hot right now with Pollard and Godwin looking better than ever. The big plays will continue to come for Austin, and when it's paired with the safe production of his stars, Austin may be a tougher win than initially expected.

When I said the fantasy gods were unhappy with Gil, I was apparently severely understating their distaste for the Big Lig. Week 2 saw Gil lose another 2-4 players to injury, putting this season in contention for worst injury seasons in RBB history. Despite the hurdles, Gil nearly managed a win in Titty City, narrowly losing 102-97 after London came up just short on MNF. Luckily for Gil, he had 10 picks in the 9 o'clock hour on draft day, so his team is still competitive. However, at this rate, Gil may be starting practice squad guys by week 5.

A disastrous week for the Buddies began on Thursday night, when Tua managed to slip 3 interceptions in before leaving the game, and possibly the season, with another head injury. Tua set the benchmark at 8 points, and 4 other players scored within a point of the mark or significantly less. The lone bright spot this week was Malik Nabers showing off his skill set, as after the week was over, Deebo and AJ Brown decided they would be taking the options on at least weeks 3 and 4.

For having 3 guys score 11.25 points total, this was a solid week for Ryan and some of his studs, who put together 98 points in the week 2 loss. Derrick Henry, Johnny Taylor and DK all had high end performances, but could not overcome the stink of McLaurin, LaPorta and Dionte Johnson's aforementioned 11.25 points. QB Jayden Daniels also cut his week 1 stats in half, managing just 17 points of his own. The bench is thin for Ryan, though less thin now after waivers have added Chubba and the hopes of Carson City Steele into the mix. But overall, this team will have to rely on their studs to get wins, which can lead to a boom/bust type of season. Just hope you're up against the Pack on a bust week.

Campaigning ain't cheap. And politicians can choose to spend their funds however they see fit to get the W. The self-proclaimed Mayor is seeking another term in Titty City, and with his freshly infused bank account, Jacube turned $100 in FAAB into two players. Two players and 6.45 points in week 2 to be exact. However mismanaged the funds may seem, the results are what they are, and Jacube has Titty City sitting at 1-1 after a close win over the depleted Ligs. Jacob might be in line for another easy win over the Tuddy Buddies in week 3, but it would be a bit surprising to see them keep the streak going much longer than that.

Joe hopped on the week 2 rollercoaster ready for a thrilling ride of performances. Unfortunately for Joe, this roller coaster only had 2 hills; the rest of the ride was filled with slow moving turns and periodic brakes. Of Joe's 105.05 week 2 points, a whopping 60.45 came from 2 of the league's most exciting players (Achane and Harrison). Meaning the rest of the 6 roster spots accounted for less than 45 points. This type of production from stars is awesome, but the reliance on it is unsustainable. If Joe can nudge Allen and Kincaid along, he could very easily be one of the best teams in the league.

Big Jim was in the running for the #1 team in week 1. Dodging injuries and some actual gameplay showed that this team will be one to pay attention to all year. The rushing QB combo having a baseline of 32 points, Dallas DST being the 3rd highest scoring slot on the team and having only 1 player under 10 points on the bench is a solid start to the season. Justin Jefferson outscored only one RB and the TE, and the team still scored 133 points. That alone should be enough to show you how goo this team can be.

Gil might want to burn some sage around his computer or something, as the fantasy gods appear to be unhappy with the Big Lig. 3 injuries in week 1, one of which landed Puka on IR, has Gil's roster looking a bit different just one week into the season. Outside of Pacheco and Aaron Jones, who was on the bench, nobody else was worthy of the "Big" title, managing to produce just 64 points after coming into the season ranked #1. Despite the injuries, Gil's starters can keep him in the top 4 teams.

Game of Jones drew the short straw in week 1 and hit matched up against the league's 2nd highest scoring team on the week. Josh had some sore spots - a combined 16.69 points from his QB, WR2 and TE - but he also has plenty more bright spots - Mixon, Diggs, Hill, Stevenson, etc.. - to be happy about. Josh already appears to have multiple picks that could be in the running for biggest steal in the draft, and they are likely only getting started.

The Bakery was loaded up on WR bread going into week 1, but it was the RB dough that paid for the win over the Mayor. The 41.25 points from the 2 RB slots outscored the 3 WRs by a full 14 points. Yish didn't need much for the W, since Jacube only managed 81 points against him, which was good, as Yish's 103 points were good enough for 8th best on the week. The RBs may continue to beat out the WRs, after the Bakery cooked up something special, turning their 13th round pick into the starting RB for the 49ers before a game was even played.

El Niño de Jaws took some grief on draft day about a few of his selections, but the confidence to like who you like has already started to payoff. Cooper Kupp may be in line for another triple crown season after Pacua landed on IR basically 1 quarter into action. JK one leg Dobbins only needs one leg apparently, and may be the biggest beneficiary of the new scheme in LA, dumping 23 unexpected points out in his first contest. Jaws never settled for one kill, and I'd expect junior is planning for his 2nd meal to arrive this Sunday.

The Jerdawgs were easily one of the biggest surprises in week 1. We knew his RB room could rival anyone in the league, but they were phenomenal out of the gates. I watched 5 picks go off the board without calling Saquon's name, and I started to think I might poop myself. Jerry was in the lucky #6 spot and snagged him right before me, and was immediate rewarded with 36 points. If Mahomes and Rice continue to click and the the RBs stay healthy (KW3 already in doubt), this team has a shot to go on a long winning streak.

A sigh of relief came on Monday night, after Kyren Williams surpassed the 10 point mark and secured the win for the Tuddy Buddies, who had watched the Bears DST and Josh Allen go off for 57 combined points for Joe. Start/sit decisions were not a strength for the Buddies in week 1, but the bench looked great and appears to have a lot of upside. The WRs may be able to carry this team, but the RB position may drag the team back just as hard. The loss of Tua will certainly hurt this team's upside as well.

The Mooney Toons spent weeks, nay, months hyping up season 9 of their longstanding show. They added new characters, had a beautiful script to keep fans engaged all season, and even brought in TVs most famous star, Christian McCaffrey. Well right before episode 1 was set to film, the highest paid star, CMC, refused to show up to the set. In a gesture of solidarity, the rest of the crew of Mooney Toons turned in one if the shows worst episodes. 63 points later and an IR stint from the superstar the ratings have dipped this show into the bottom half of the league. Hopefully Trevor brought in some new writers for episode 2.

The Wolf Pack go 1-0 and move back 2 slots. What is that about?? Well, in their 84-64 win over the Lig, 33 of those 84 points came from QB Daniels while the Bucs were going to town on Washington. On paper this team should be great. But the reality needs to match up, and that has yet to be seen. Two weeks from now, though, they could be the #1 team after Henry scores 40+ twice and Ryan has 300 more points than he does right now.

Good drafting? Good keepers? Bad drafting by the league? Good luck? I don’t know what it is yet, but I don't hate this team. Given his circumstances, Austin put together a team that will likely be competing for a playoff spot if things continue to follow the week 1 pattern. This roster has a good baseline of points, and has a ton of boom potential. Will there be weeks of sub 80-90? Probably. But could they drop 150 on you just as easily? Definitely.

So much of this team's success sits on the shoulders of Allen, Achane, Marv and Kincaid (kinda). To this point, Achane appears ready to handle that burden and be the #1 RB this season, but the other 3 need to be the other 3 cornerstones of this roster. If Harrison is not what he was drafted to be, Joe will have a difficult time getting the rest of the gang to spit out wins.

As of this writing, what's the O/U on things to like about this roster? 3.5? The 3 RBs are in and maybe Stroud. But these 3 locked in RBs all showed cracks in week 1, forcing the public to question their confidence in their recently reelected self-proclaimed Mayor to manage a winning city. Week 2 might have those same 3 RBs scoring 90 points. But if they don't, wins will be tough to come by

The Big Lig's theme song has been sung by Lit for the past 8 seasons, but Gil may not actually be his own worst enemy this year, after putting together the league's top team int he 2024 draft. With the first 2 picks being locks, Gil had all offseason to decide who would be #3. After splitting hairs for months, Gil gambled on Ja'Marr Chase to lead is WRs into battle. IF Chase chooses to fight, Gil will have him leading the likes of London, Pacua and Pickens, who all have extremely high upside potential. 2023's #2 RB, Mostert, will start the year on the bench, showing you just how much talent is at The Big Lig's disposal. If Gil can silence his theme song long enough to make some good start/sit decisions, he should only be competing for the round 1 bye.

Coming in at #2 in the first rankings of 2024 is Mr. CMC himself, revorT. Trev tried to throw some curveballs out there and get the group thinking CMC was available, but there was no chance McCaffrey was wearing anything but a Mooney Toons jersey this season. The Toons went back to some older episodes and pulled some classic characters in Davante Adams and Travis Kelce, while also introducing some newer characters like Breece Hall, Zay Flowers, Rome Odunze and Jonathon Brooks to the audience. A few of these starters have single-handedly carried teams to championships, so putting them all on one team seems a bit unfair.

Big Jim, not normally known for his draft prowess, came out of the 2024 draft with arguably his best team to date. Jim said "ADP? What the heck is an ADP?", and drafted from the heart, stealing names off the board whenever they felt fit. The Twins this season will be Jim's QB persona, Lamar Richardson, this season, as they have a real chance at rushing for more yards than some teams' RB rooms. This team is built with stars, such as Jefferson, Evans, Cook and Kittle up front, with plenty of depth, such as Swift, Ford, Najee, Olave and Worthy in the back. There should be a real fear of the Big Jim spreading the buns this season.

Game of Jones entered the 2024 draft with the 2nd overall pick for the 2nd time in two years. Josh took about two seconds with his 1st round pick, as Tyreek Hill joined the former champion as his star wideout for the upcoming season. Josh, being an older brother, knows that wisdom comes with age. So nataurally, he went heavy on wisdom this year and drafted the all-wisdom team in Amari Cooper, Joe Mixon, Stefon Diggs, Evan Engram and Austin Ekeler to be key pieces of this offense. Game of Jones did not ignore youth, however, and injected some freshness through Purdy, R. White, Aiyuk, Stevenson and Coleman to contribute as well. Experience aside, this team is well-rounded and may give Josh a chance at returning to the playoffs for the first time since 2020, when he finished 2nd.

The Tuddy Buddies spent the offseason making moves, including the largest trade in RBB history, to acquire picks and RB Kyren Williams. Their faith in Kyren must be grand, as they waited until the 6th round to add their 2nd RB, taking players such as Mark Andrews and Malik Nabers over improving the backfield. The Tuddy Buddies went swinging for the fences with their WR room, and if a few of the receivers become home runs, the Buddies will have plenty of Tuddies to go around.

The Beef Boys Bakery closed its doors on the 2023 season, and opened up shop in Detroit for the 2024 kickoff, hoping to serve up some gravy to the goons in the Midwest. Yish went into the draft not wanting to double up on the Cardinals, after having kept McBride, so instead, he tripled up on the Lions in Amon Ra, Monty and Goffers. If the Lions follow the NFL expert predictions, Yish will be quite happy he relocated this offseason. The WR talent on this team is enough to make it a playoff contender as is, but if any of the depth RBs pan out, Yish will be a shoo-in for another trip to the postseason.

The Wolf Pack, who love throwing draft capital to the wind, entered the 2024 draft without a 2nd round pick once again. And once again, it did not seem to matter, as Ryan put together a team capable of dominating until he trades for another stud or two in November. A 5th and 10th round keeper value in Taylor and LaPorta, my high school pal, Ryan was dealt a winnable hand. With the cornerstones in place, the Pack took swings at upside in the Daniels/McLaurin stack, DKalf and Derrick Henry, who may have 25 TDs of his own this season. Yish boldy predicted that this is Ryan's first postseason in the Toilet Bowl, but this roster certainly seems like one that can compete.

Jerbear was trying to increase his record of 17 straight weeks ranked at #12, but instead, he drafted a team with a chance to win now. With two RB keepers (Walker and Edwards), Jerry spent his first two 2024 picks on RBs Saquon Barkley and James Conner. Jerry's RB group is now in the top 4 in the league, giving him the potential to just ride them to a winning season without much help from elsewhere. Despite not needing the help, the Dawgs will have Patrick Mahomes leading the way, while Rashee Rice and Jayden Reed headline the receiving corps. If thos two WRs hit, and if any of Kirk/Sutton/Hopkins/Bowers pop, Jerry could easily become a top 4 team.

Baby Jaws, comes into the 2024 season ranked #9 and is easily the team most likely to jump up the board over the coming weeks. The #9 ranking is highly predicated on the unknowns of the core of this team. Is Kupp back? Will Smith be as good with Saquon in town? Who does Stroud love? Are Zamir and Brian Robinson true #1s? And that's just the starters. The bench is filled with ready blow potential in C. Watson, Ridley, Dobbins, Corum, Wicks and even Taysom Hill. This team is ambiguous to say the least, but often times, ambiguity results in high end results. This may very well be the last time Jona is near the #9 ranking.

Yahoo gave Joe a draft grade of D, after failing to secure safe points out of the gate. However, Joe put together the unquestionable all-upside team from this year's draft, with spike weeks and future stars coming from Marv Jr., Chase Brown, Achane, Big Ladd, Jameson Williams, Jaleel McLeel, Jaylen Wright and Dalton Kincaid. All of those names have ceiling-breaking potential and are all paired with a steal of a QB in Josh Allen in the 4th round. This team will go as Allen does, but if he is successful post-WRs, and any of the upside options come through, Joe will be just a boom week away from destroying your Sunday.

Titty City went from 2nd best to 2nd worst over the offseason, after losing the title to Austin and canceling the parade, forcing those tassels to stay on for at least another year. The self-proclaimed Mayor wanted to distract from his roster by upgrading the town's aesthetics with a new, breathtaking logo, but the RBB would not be fooled. Spending the offseason overserved is understanable after being so close to a championship, and the trades that went along with it appear to be a product of the devil's juice as well. Jacob elected to keep Gibbs and Jacobs, while also taking ETN with the #11 pick this year, giving him a top 3 RB room. Jacob will absolutely need to be carried by the RBs, which is not out of the question with those 3, or hope that Keenan, Higgins or JSN can blow up to produce some competitive numbers. Either way, Jacob may be asking Chris Hansen to revive an episode of "To Catch a Predator", as Austin ALREADY stole his 2025 3rd round pick for a QUARTERBACK.

The 2023 CHAMP is here! "Here" as in in the league, because "here" in the rankings is not somewhere to yell about.. Austin stole the title away from jacob's dominant team last season, and quickly rebranded as "Keeping Upwith the Joneses", as more than half the league is still chasing a title. Drafting from #12 is not easy, but it gets eeven harder when you keep players in the 1st and 2nd rounds, and you traded away your 3rd round pick the prior season. Luckily for Austin, the rest of the RBB was making it easy on him this draft, allowing him to pull in some quality talent to pair with his elite keepers. If Pollard and Pitts can add the points needed, Lamb and Bijan should do more than enough to keep Austin in games each week.

2025.notes: Yish narrowly survived a major upset by the Cindererlla-ing Mooney Toons in a low scoring battle. The Bakery has the opportunity to become the first franchise in RBB history with 3 league titles.

Joe has had an up and down career in the RBB, but he is back in the title game for the first time in 6 years. This team has needed everything it has given through the playoffs up to this point, but he may have needed to save his best for last. urban Myth will be going up against a Bakery team that looked vulnerable last week and may be ready to recitfy its poor outing.

For the 3rd straight season, the self-proclaimed Mayor will have Titty City coming home without the coveted RBB Biscuit. Instead, the once dream team will try and take home 3rd place in consecutive seasons.

The insane streak is finally over, along with Trevor's hopes of a blue shirt this season. It came down to the Monday night of the semis to end it, but Trev now will play for 3rd place, which he won back in 2022.

The dinglest Jerry missed it by one week. Coming up just 4.15 points short in the quarterfinals, only to outscore the rest of the league by 10 in what would have been the semis is a tough pill to swallow. The 5th place finish will distract from Jerry having made the playoffs in 3 of the lat 4 seasons.

Game of Jones' return to the postseason ends about as poorly as it can, losing both games to end up in 6th place with the 8th pick. Josh will have a plethora of talent to choose from for keepers to build on in 2026.
Most of the team could have sat this one out with Ryan barely showing up in the match. It will be a father-son battle for the oh so cool 1st overall pick.
Big Jim was pushed to the edge Gil, but luckily he saved his best week of the season for this battle. The win makes it a father-son match to see if he can go from 1st overall to 1st pick overall.

The Big Lig held onto his best week of the year for the consolation semifinals. Unfortunately, the best week of the year (by 6 points) did not even amount to a win. Gil will hope to not be upset by Ryan's up and down roster to take home the 3rd pick in 2026.

The rest of the league should give thanks to El Tuddy Buddy for making sure The Wolfpack did not have a chance at the 1st overall pick. Given his extra 1st and track record of winning without extra picks, we do not need to be doing this team any favors.
Austin has not scored 100 points since week 7, but he pulled out a quick 105 to edge out Jonathan for 11th place and that sweet sweet 5th overall pick.

It's hard not to look at Trevor and Jona's seasons and see how they could have easily been inverted based on a few minor changes. A team that may have threatened for the playoffs finds themselves on the wrong end of two upsets, landing Baby Jaws in the overall #12 position for 2025.
The Bakery was closed last week, but it is open for business in week 16. Squared up with the Toons in the semis, Yish is looking to build upon his dominance over Trevor.

After a week with the lights off, Titty City is back in full swing, with tops nowhere to be found. Playing in his 3rd consecutive semifinals, Jacob is looking to repeat his 2023 week 16 performance, where he took down Joe 130-103 to make his first finals appearance.

Back in 2019, Joe played Josh in the championship game and lost 144-125, giving Josh his 1st title. 6 years later, Joe was back for revenge, taking Josh down early in the playoffs by a score of 143-125. Will this year end with reverse finish from 6 years ago?

The Toons are back in the semifinals for the first time since 2022, when they went on to finish 3rd. Ironically, back in 2022, Trevor also defeated Jerry in the quarterfinals by just 2.02 points, bringing his combined margin of victory vs playoff Jerry to just 6.17 points.

The Jerdawgs lose a heartbreaker to the Mooney Toons, leaving too many points on the bench in this one. After making it through the most difficult end of season schedule for any bubble team, Jerry became just another part of Trevor's playoff story.

Game of Jones' first playoff appearance since their 2nd place finish in 2020, ended as quickly as it came. With a score of 125, Josh would have not moved on vs any playoff team this round, proving this may be one of the best playoffs in RBB history.
After the crushing week 14, ETB is back for the 2nd consecutive year in the 7th seed, seeking the 1st overall pick to re-start the cycle. Hooray.

After claiming the league championship last year, Big Jim is chasing a different title this season. The Twins join Jimmie (2016 - 2017) and Yish (2022 - 2023) as the only teams to win the championship and miss the playoffs the following season.
An upset one week late huh? Couldn't have done this in week 14 huh? Even with a negative score from Bam Knight, Ryan won by 20+ points on the back of Kyle Pitts career outing.

The Big Lig did advance to the consolation semis, and they did it with just 64 points. Gil is one game closer to the top pick, and gets a week 11 rematch with Big Jim, where he lost with just 55 points scored.

Jonathan has found himself finishing in 5th, 6th, 9th or 10th in every year of his RBB career, so being upset at the hands of Kyle Pitts' monster game puts Jona in new waters playing for the 11th/12th place honor.

Outside of his miraculous week 14 win, Austin has not won or surpassed 93 points since week 7. That trend continued in a booty battle with Gil, which ended with Austin securing, at best, a 5th or 6th overall pick in 2026.
