Not the cleanest of wins, but it did the trick. The Bakery will be closed in week 15, as they have secured a round 1 bye. A win in week 14 would secure the #1 overall seed as well.

Jacube apparently likes the drama, going 2-3 since week 9, which puts his #1 overall seed and even the bye week in jeopardy. Yes, we fully expect Jacob to beat Jona and take the #2 seed, but there's a chance the Titties are on duty in week 15.
In case my tone before came across as sarcastic, I want to make it clear: FANTASY FOOTBALL IS DUMB.

Game of Jones was giving away TDs like turkeys this holiday weekend, as all but 1 (and the DST) player scored at least one TD this week. The 154 points helped Josh to a more secure playoff spot, but there is still an outside chance he finds himself in the consolation bracket.

The upset of the week came at the hands of Amon-Ra St. Brown, who provided 0 points before going out injured and opened the door for the Toons to take over Titty City. The W puts Trevor in a very comfortable spot going into a softer matchup with Ryan,.

Jerry took his 63+ points acquired during the Chargers game and the MNF football game and turned it into a 25 point win. Back-to-back wins have Jerry in a win-and-in situation in the final week of the season.

The week 13 win was never really in question for Joe, but the surprise loss of Titty City to the Toons gave Joe a chance to steal the bye. He would need another win and another loss by Jacob (VS the 69ers) for that to happen. However, a loss in week 14 could send Joe all the way back to 5th place.
Big Jim survived the onslaught by Jonathan and the 10 combined points by Lamar and Justin Jefferson to secure himself as the #8 team heading into the consolation bracket.

Austin had the points on the bench to make this one a bit more interesting, but chose to let Joe get to 9 wins comfortably. Austin needs to win or have Ryan lose in order to stay out of the last place watering.
Jona said 69 points did the trick for a 17 point win in week 12, so let's try that position again in week 13. This time, he was surprised by a pair of Twins in his face and a 17 point loss instead.
The Big Lig getting 4.12 points from his QB and WR1 slot still didn't stop him from blowing out his week 12 total output (77 to 52). One week closer to the 2026 draft.
Ryan has been up and down the last few weeks, hitting 130+ and also hitting less than 61. With 1 week left, Ryan needs to win AND have Austin lose in order to get out of the basement.

When I said Titty City likely had another 170+ point week in stock, I did not mean they had to show it so quickly. 177 points in a game where Taylor had less than 10, the TE had less than 2, and the QB had less than 20. There is no team in the league that has this many ready to pop players in the starting lineup.

The game of the week did not disappoint, as the Beef Boys outlasted Game of Jones by just 3.68 points. The win secures Yish a spot in the playoffs and nearly guarantees a top 3 seed. One more win (or a Joe loss) will secure the bye week as well.
This was a must win game for El Tuddy Buddy to have a shot. Two more crucial matchups ahead, with week 13 basically being a playoff game.

A tough loss to swallow, especially knowing the points were there to do it, as the win would have given Josh the inside lane to a playoff spot. He still has an inner lane, but now it's just one or two further away.

The Toons had the understudy Josh Allen, who is clearly not the real Josh Allen, for their week 12 episode, which featured just 11 points compared to the 50 from week 11. Trev won a low-scoring battle, which keeps his playoff hopes alive and well.

The Malak fellas were both undermanned this week between injuries and byes. Jerry rode the Stafford brand Dike to a huge win to keep his season alive. The Dawgs are squarely on the bubble going into week 13.

Joe's bench put up as many points as my fantasy soccer team did this week. With not a single alternate option, Joe threw out a lineup that came close to a playoff-clinching win, but fell just (19 points) short. Though it would take a huge collapse and the perfect storm of events, Joe is technically not locked into the postseason yet.

Dads never like losing to their children in anything - even Candyland - so you can imagine Big Jim's frustration in being outscored 290 - 207 in their two matchups. The Twins have two more games to solidify their consolation bye week.

Baby Jaws is the new recordholder of lowest points in a win in RBB history at 69.74. The Previous owner of the record? The guy he just beat, Gil, at 73.63. Jona could sneak away with one more win this regular season, but it still will not be enough to move into a bye week.

After Josh Allen's dud on Thursday night, Austin looked poised for an upset win over the Mooney Toons. He followed it up with 4 duds of his own and just 72 total points. Austin is well outside the consolation bye week, regardless of these next couple weeks.

The Atlanta Falcons DST was the top scoring player on this team this week. The Atlanta Falcons DST scored 13.53 points this week. Ryan did not have a good week. He has two chances to get out of the 2026 draft watering.
Losing to an opponent who scores in the 60s is bad. Adding in that the margin of victory was 17.32 points is really bad. 2026 can't come soon enough for the Big Lig.

The 200 point man himself might be Jonathan Taylor, as without him in the lineup, TItty City was fully clothed. Don't worry though, I would bet the Maye-r has another 170+ point week in stocke over the next 4-5 weeks.

This was a pretty good week financially, as only the DST scored less than 12.85 points. Not just consistent but also super high ceiling, the Bakery looks good. The injury concerns will probably go away before it matters.

With a score of 120+ and beating another good team by nearly 50 points would make you think this was a great week, yeah? What if I said only 2 players scored more than 9.7 points? Between Allen and Bijan, they had 73 points. This type of win is likely not sustainable during the playoffs.
GoJ continues to get mid-level games from many different players, which produce quality end results. It feels like a lineup that will be a difficult out come playoff time.
I've said it before, and I'll say it again. Fantasy football is DUMB. Beyond just injuries, spitting on people has El Tuddy Buddy as about as questionable as it gets to make the playoffs.

Death by RB is the new Myth that can't be busted, as Joe cruised to a 121-85 win on the back of 75.8 points from the RB position. If these guys continue to perform AND the WRs get back on track, Joe will cruise to the semifinals.
Dinglejerry is trying to find the right combination of players to make a run down the stretch. The loss of Josh Jacobs, for however long, could be a massive blow to this team.
When your top socring player doesn't reach 11.5 points, you end up with a score less than 56. Gil has been more interested in 2026 for a while now, so this is no surprise.
Needing only 56 points to win, Big Jim let the Twins float to an easy 91 points. The roster is not scary, but they are very much so in a position to make the playoffs.
The small shark is dealing with what teeth he has left after injuries and garage sales removed the big biters. I think scores between 75-95 are probably where Jona lives the rest of the season.

The 1-9 team drops 135 to be the 2nd highest scorer on the week. Do you expect this to happen again? Probably not, but the potential is obviously there for Ryan to push for a top 2026 pick and/or steal a win from a bubble team.

Between selling, injuries, and byes, Austin was backed into the lineup that managed just 56 points in week 11. I would not expect a whole lot better down the stretch unless Joe Burrow can contribute 25+ PPG.
Jacob is the only player to ever score 190+ points more than once in the same season. With Taylor and Gibbs, anything is possible for Jacube.
The Bakery keeps cooking, winning back-to-back in the most important part of the season. With this roster and the remaining schedule, the Boys are a lock for the playoffs.

The Mooney Toons took advantage of an easy episode, getting the 113-99 win over Big Jim. The writers likely saved the best episodes for the end of the season, so it should not surprise anyone to see them with 8 or 9 wins come playoffs.
Achane. Only name you need to know from week 10. The win propelled Joe into making a big move to acquire Henderson during his breakout and Ladd for a stretch run.

Such an odd roster. They look like they could kill you with 170 points every week, yet every week they do just enough to win/keep games interesting. On an of week, you likely have no chance beating GOJ, but on an week, he still may boat race you to the finish line.
Who doesn't love losing to one player? This was a collective effort by El Tuddy Buddy to be just bad enough to lose to one RB. Well done team, well done.

Staying alive with a big win in a game that cannot be given away against Austin, Jerry moves to 6-4. His ROS schedule is not an easy one, so he made the move for some big help in Breece and Waddle. This will be an interesting race down the stretch,
The Twins suffered a near death nail with a loss to another bubble team in week 10. With a medium ROS schedule, Big Jim is still not out of the race.
The Big Lig bought a few weeks and began the selling last week. After the re-sale of Breece and Waddle, the Lig is 100% focused on 2026.

Jona continued his quality transaction trend by flipping two players for two other players that would outscore (by a lot) who he just gave away. Jona is making the best of 2025 while looking ahead to 2026.
Austin tried to keep up with Jerry and almost did until Jacobs ran away with things. Austin has been playing for a higher draft pick in 2026 and will keep that rolling the rest of the way.

Ryan is throwing a handful of darts (not literally anymore with the injury) at the wall to see if anything sticks for 2026. Luckily for him, he has extra picks that will make up for any darts that land on the ground.

This was quite the dropoff for a team that has 328 points over the last two weeks and was only missing one player. At least there is hope for other teams that this may happen again during weeks 15-17.

The Beef Boys were extra motivated after suffering the brutal loss in week 8, and they came out with a week best 158 points (nearly doubling Austin). The Bakery keeps buying that tainted fish, however, so health will continue to be a concern going forward.

Swept by the Toons in the 2025 regular season (279-239 total points), Josh will have to get those games back elsewhere. Luckily, he will probably be sitting at 7-4 after week 11 (week 10 v Ryan, week 11 v Jona).

El Tuddy Buddy went out and acquired some reinforcements specifacally for this matchup in hopes to stay close. Turns out waiver additions of Flacoc and Loveland would have sufficed. Arrows pointing up for ETB.

In typical TV fashion, the Toons built up the dramatics heading into week 9 - not having scored more than 107 points since week 4. They showed out when they needed to and kept their playoff hopes alive. With 3 very winnable games of the 5 remaining, Trev still has some work to do at 4-5.

A wild week in the RBB was capped off by The Big Lig being the CHOPs most recent victim on a week of just 72 points. Things have not come together for the Log this season, and it would be a shock if they finally came together now.

Dealing with injury upon injury, Joe has managed to not only stay afloat, but also almost be leading the way at 6-3. Given his upcoming schedule, Joe like has another 2 wins locked in, making him a nearly sure bet to reach the postseason.
Brock Bowers saved up all his points missed during his 3 week absence and let them loose on Jona. This week was nearly as good as the Dawgs week 7 and 8 output combined (150 to 154).
Winners of 3 straight, Big Jim & The Twins have unzipped and are ready to sit at the table. Only one win outside of playoffs, you never know what can happen.

After selling away all his teeth for sand dollars, the vicious shark attack has certainly lost its bite. Though he may not be able to rip into you like before, Baby Jaws is still capable of an attack on a weaker prey.

In a wild sequence of events, Austin went to the players tab on Yahoo, only to find that every NFL player was already rostered, forcing him to start an OUT Pacheco and BYE week Eagles DST. At least those two positions would not have made up the 78 point hole KUwtJ were in, but still.

Ryan is all about pushing himself. Usually it's for wins, but when that can't happen, go the other way with it. One thing is for sure, Ryan will have an easy path to dominate next year having extra picks for the first time in his RBB career.
3 of the 4 best players went on vacation in week 8, and Titty City didn't even notice. There is a very real chance that Jacob doesn't lose another game this season without some help from above.

The Bakery continues to order goods from the ocean, primarily receiving halibut sold as mahi mahi. A surprise out from London and a called back TD from Slayton turned Yish's 6-2 record to 5-3 real quick. Don't worry though, this is just a small hiccup.

Game of Jones, or more appropriately named Game of Touchdowns, had a whopping 10 TDs in their week 8 win. Josh is cruising right now, with back-to-back weeks as a tope 2 scoring team with at least 130 points.

Easily one of the oddest shows in the league, the Mooney Toons can't seem to decide what they want to be. All the talent is there (Allen, Rome, Rice, Marv, Bijan, Jeanty, Flowers, Kincaid, Tracy now even), yet they've been featured as the near chop team in consecutive weeks. Your guess is as good as mine as to which version shows up this week.

Hope is a powerful thing. It's what keeps most things alive with a will to go on. Prior to the week, there was no hope in a week 8 win, but by halftime on MNF, that once lost hope returned with a vengance. That same hope was crushed moments later. Fantasy football. The end.

Joe narrowly outran the Wolfpack in a high-scoring mtchup. Losing another major roster spot to season-ending injury will be difficult to overcome. At some point these injuries have to derail a season, don't they?

After looking to make a change in the locker room, The Big Lig stood still and Halled his way to a week 8 win over the Toons. The all-upside team is still here waiting to be fully realized in their potential.

In what was the best chance for anyone to beat Titty City for the remainder of the season, Jerry set his aims on a double chop performance instead. Vibes are weird in Dinglesville, but with some healing, things could get better and look much different in a hurry,

After shipping out all the big names, the single (digit) fellas were all that remained. Outside of Jordan Love, who had 244 of his 360 passing yards come from yards after the catch, and Michael Pittman, this week was setup for a loss. We would all take a sub100 win though.

Big Jimbo & The Twinbos pulled off the upset even with a late out from Lamar, a goose by Fergs, and 18 points from Hunt on the bench. A quick 40 burger from the Cook will do that for you. The Twins are quietly in the mix with some winnable games ahead.

Ryan may just be bored of RBB and need a challenge, as he removed Nabers and JT from his roster, only to still be putting up competitive numbers. With that said, the Pack is still not favorited to win any game left this season.

After the shocking win over the Big Lig in week 7, Austin had his hopes high in catching a shark. Instead, he found a shark tooth along the shoreline. Austin is the current manager of more players rumored to be on the move before the NFL deadline than anyone in RBB history (look it up). This team could look quite different in 1 week.

Welcome to the 200 Club Titty City! An incredible feat given our current scoring settings, so congrats to you sir. This is easily one of the highest baselines and ceiling teams we've seen in a long time.
New faces in the Bakery after another big trade goes through. Yish went back to the well after Jona dumped an expiring bag of Mike Evans at the Beef Boys' door.
Most of the writers went on vacation with Trev last week, leaving only Rice and Bijan to carry the show. Inconsistency is the dark cloud in Mooney Town.
Trying to survive the bye week blues in week 8. Check back in week 9.
These are the games that make you hate fantasy football. How do you score 150 points and still be the biggest blowout of the week. Bad luck, suck butt is the RBB motto.
Buying from the team you play against, only to lose to that same team, is for sure not the plan when buying. Plenty of depth, but let's see what next week looks like.

Joe appears to be destined for the 50% line this season, as his team continues to be indecisive on how good they want to be. They will likely never go away, but they don't seem like they want to take the next step either.
Yikes. This was a bad one all around, lending to the idea that a few players have been carrying this team through their best and worst days.
The waters are open for business, as Jona makes another big time trade. The season was already heading the wrong direction, but now it's officially needing a new GPS.
The magic is still lingering around Ryan, as many players you barely know are contributing big pints after the sale of JT. I'm guessing there's another couple wins coming this season.
Injuries are still killing this team, as Lamar was a cornerstone piece. However, the league should say thank you for stealing a win away from Jerry in week 7.
The coaching change bump was in full effect for Austin, who dominated his buyer by nearly 30 points in the same sales week. The booms can come and kill any team - except probably Jacob right now.

Titty City has been in party mode for weeks now, and it doesn't look like tops are going back on any time soon. JSN, JT and Maye can't be stopped right now, making the rest of the studs not even necessary for the Mayor to get wins.

The Toons are an odd team. Probably not sure of their identity because they're named after a player who hasn't been on their roster in years. Either way, this team can't decide if they want to battle Titty City for best team in the league or make a push for the #1 overall pick in 2026. The return of Rashee Rice will likely tilt the writers to the former.

The top half of the team came to play in week 6, while the bottom half took the option. Luckily it didn't matter against an ill pack of Wolves. El Tuddy Buddy needs to find a way to steal a few wins during injuries and byes.

Not sure how far apart they are separated in years, but the battle of brothers came down to 8.26 points after Mahomes continued his resurgence. When your DST's 9.98 is one of your best starters and you won, you take it and run as quickly as you can to the next week. Despite the loaded roster, Game of Jones only has 1 game over 115 points this season.

From waiver wire to league winner, did Dowdle save the Bakery from going out of business?? Down to almost no RBs, Yish found Rico, who has been unbelievably good as the starter. If he stays the starter, the rest of this unit is good enough to put up 120+ on the reg.

Achane and Skattebo for the win! 68.75 points between two RBs should just about lock up a win for anyone, and it did for Joe this week. IF Chase Brown figures it out and Lamb comes back healthy, Joe will be a playoff lock after surviving (and thriving) these last few weeks.

It's not good when your RBs are outscored almost 4x by your opponent, yet Jona almost had a chance with the efforts of London and Daniels. With 3 winnable matchups coming up, Jona could be a middle of the pack team come the deadline.

If you didn't listen to the podcast the last few weeks, Gil created a hitlist and is actively crossing off names. Most recent victims: Garrett Wilson and Emeka Egbekboo. These injuries may be devastating, but the Big Lig has plenty of depth. It's now or never for his upside plays to payoff.

The DingleJacobs came away happy with a huge win to stay tied with 5 other teams for 2nd place, but also extremly sad that Puka may be watching their next few games from the sideline. Jerry is not built for injuries, so if QJ, Puka, Bower, Etc.. remain off the field, the Dawgs may be looking up at the league standings sooner than later.

Nobody wants to lose, but definitely not to their brother. 10 of the 16 starters in this matchup scored single digits, and only 3 players scored more than 14 points. There are enough points to go around on this roster any week, but odds are that we've seen best days already.
Yahoo had this one pegged, missing Big Jims projections by 0.12 points in a massive blowout. With no Jefferson, Kittle, Lamar and a less-than-stellar James Cook, these are the expected results.

Dumpster diving for replacements after injuries and trades, Ryan actually may have found some non-trash in Bam and Vidal. This team is not good, no, but it certainly still has enough talent to score 100+ and beat you on a down week.
Being the booty side of the upset of the week was quickly replaced by acquiring the top RB in the league to date. Titty City is looking like a pretty nice place to be right now.

The heart and soul of this cast is Bijan Robinson, who could not will the episode to a winning rating while sitting in the audience. Trev is a locked and loaded team that is only getting better, who could also be 4-1 if not for one play.

Despite the loss of Hill, Game of Jones is easily the deepest team in the league with startable talent. They are not scoring huge numbers, but each week someone else picks up the slack of another starter, giving GOJ a baseline that is tough to beat.
Another great week extends the win streak to 3, but another RB goes down, ending the week on a sour note. Omarion Hampton heading to the IR will be a tough hurdle for ETB.

Who is the Big Lig? The answer may just be Emeka Egbuka, who is dominating the NFL through 5 weeks of action. More contributors would be nice, but Gil can probably compete most weeks with what he's already got.

Waiver wire additions made the week 5 win come to fruition, as Darnold and Dowdle combined for 65.64 of the Bakery's 145 points. I would expect this output every week, but some underperforming guys could start performing and take Yish to the next level.

The no quit team of the league this year came back for a last minute win on MNF, bringing Joe to 3-2. Battling direct and indirect injuries, this team has managed to stay above 500 and in a good spot to make a run.
A couple of key players out on bye and injury, and the Dawgs struggle to produce. Jacobs and Bowers may be the core of this team.

The points were not there for the win, but if they had been, what would today look like for the Wolfpack? After an 18 point loss to the Lig, Ryan made history and sold for the first time in his RBB career, sending Johnny Taylor to Titty City with three 32+ point games to his name this season.
Decimated by injuries coupled with bye weeks, and Jona should be happy with 97 points on the week. The injuries will have to disappear, quickly, if Jona wants a shot at the postseason.

Not only covering the spread but destroying it along with the Moneyline. Austin has back to back upset wins that move him into 9th place. With Dak slinging it the way he is, anything is possible right now.
Without Lamar, this team cannot survive. Add in a mixture of other injuries and bye weeks, and the Twins are wearing a cup 2 sizes too small.

The big boy game did not fail to deliver, as a high-scoring matchup ended with another topless party in the streets of Titty City. The self-proclaimed Mayor is out to his best start in office and doesn't appear to be slowing down any time soon. The Ta-Tas are just too perfect right now. They are filled out with arguably the safest starters, while also being pumped up by some of the highest potential out there. Jacob is showing them off, and he don't care who sees.
A massive week from half the lineup allowed for the other half to hit snooze. If a couple more pieces can contribute, El Tuddy Buddy will be feared as much as El Chupacabra.

This one was close and definitely within reach if not for injury or missed start decisions. Game of Jones sits atop his castle with too many good players to start, which creates a problem in itself. A 1 percenter problem yes, but a problem nonetheless.

The cast of superstars is getting longer and longer for the Mooney Toons, as the boom potential for this team is through the roof. Jeanty had 8+ points more than his entire career combined this week. We may not be able to turn this show off this season.

Meat & Potatoes my butt! The Jerdawgs were all dessert this week, cruising to a 144 point top score of the week. Puka and Jacobs are awesome. QJ is apparently a real thing, and Baker may be one of the best players to watch play football. Oh, and his 144 points came while benching 3 guys that scored no less than 28 points.
A lot of promise this week, and probably a lot better weeks ahead. The trouble will be trusting the right players to do it on the right weeks. A final drive TD saved Gil from the first chop.

The Bakery is happy that business was booming out of the gates, as it allows the business to make it through slow periods like their current 2-game losing streak. CMC is awesome, but Yish is still waiting for some other products to start contributing to the overall bottom line.

Never have I seen a team waiting on results from 5 players on a Monday night, but it certainly made for an interesting evening. Joe needed just about everything he got from his squad this week, and the win is a testament to the depth he drafted.

The Wolf Pack mourns the loss of the #7 overall pick, Malik Nabers, whose membership came to an end after an ACL tear. The Pack is already out to their worst start since 2020, and losing a top end WR won't help. But, if you remember 2020, Ryan went on 6-game win streak to end the regular season at 8-5 and win the championship 3 weeks later.

While the surprise inactive of Warren did not change the outcome in this matchup, it did deliver Jona the first ever RBB chop. With a devastating amount of injuries and bye weeks arriving, Baby Jaws' back is against the nets.

Big Jim started his optimal Twins and even got Justin Jefferson's best week of the young season, but it still wasn't enough to hold off the upset from Austin. With another injury (Lamar) to this roster, the number of playmakers is razor thin.

Covering the spread in back-to-back weeks, Austin rode Dak and Philly to an upset win over Big Jim. This was about as good as a week as Austin could get (only leaving 2.75 points on the bench), so the upside is still not there. However, on a down/bye week, the Joneses have proven they are able to Keep Up and win.
Week 3 was much closer than it needed to be thanks King Henry, but what's a show without some drama, right? The 0.38 point win was a major swing to push Josh to 2-1 instead of 1-2 and Yish to 3-0.
Things began coming together in Titty City sooner than expected. Back-to-back top 2 scores on the week is hard to ignore, and the ceiling of this team may not have even been seen yet.

By all acounts, this was a magical week for El Tuddy Buddy, who saw Ja'Marr Chase be one of 2 starting spots to score less than 10 points. There are certainly questions here, but the potential is undeniable.

Sometimes shows pay the wrong stars the big money, only to have the camera love a complimentary role more. David Montgomery has nearly double the points (on the year) than rookie sensation-to-be Ashton Jeanty. All the right pieces are in this box, but Trev still has to find which are which each week.
Still an all-potential team makeup, but the potential is starting to be realized. I would not be surprised if the Big Lig started dropping Big numbers weekly - if we picks the right starters.
If not for Johnny Taylor, this would have been a disasterous week (69 points in 2 weeks!). Eiher way, I'd bet on the talent within this starting lineup to come through with a much better week 4.

Though it was unexpected going into MNF, a 0.38 point loss is heartbreaking, especially when 3-0 is a huge step toward the postseason. Not the way Yish hoped for it to happen, but his RB issues have worked themselves out a bit with Trey Benson slated to take over after the devastating injury to James Conner (pour one out).

Jerry took on his youth in week 3 and proved it is age before beauty, as he cruised to his 2nd win in a row. This team may not look like a winning team on paper, but they may be the A's of Billy Beane.

Destruction rolled through Joe's neighborhood in week 3, claiming the 2025 James Conner and the next-few-weeks CeeDee Lamb (round 1 & 3 picks) to injury. The upside is that Joe does have the depth to plug and play next week and have a good chance at a win.
Baby Jaws is taking a bite out of his own tail. More injured/IR players than weeks played this year. Acquiring points while waiting for health will be crucial for Jona.

Big Jim had a near blemish-free 2024 in terms of injury, but 2025 is a different foe, claiming Kittle, Najee, Shipley & J.J. McCarthy aleady. The Twins will have to see players step up, as Lamar and Cook cannot do it alone.

Mark Andrews is not a fan of being a 31 point underdog, so he 23 points to his combined week 1 & 2 totals to keep this one closer than expected. The Joneses are struggling to keep up with anything right now, but the Andrews game is a reminder that anyone could pop on any week.

The writers poured their hearts into week 1's script, which left them with little to offer in their follow up episode. The cast (outside of the lead, Bijan), came crashing back to earth. Possibly more of a boom/bust roster than we thought, which means weeks like this happen, and then you get torched by the Toons to the tune of 160 PA.

Was this a great showing by Game of Jones? No. Did he nearly double his opponent's score? Yes. The matchup was over almost before it started, which may keep what Josh's roster did under the radar. The start/sit problem is a good one to have, and Josh has it right now. If he gets it right, he could be dropping 130 regularly. If he gets it wrong, he's probably still hitting 100-105 easily.

If you were a member of The Wolf Pack, you had yourself a day, And why not have it this week? Makes sense. Nabers and Taylor combined for nearly 70 points, which would have been enough for a comfortable win over Austin this week.

The #3 team has met the #1 team in consecutive weeks, and this week this team drew the short straw. Never a fun way to go down. El Tuddy Buddy is 0-2 for the first time since 2021 (the last year they won the championship).

A big win for Joe to avoid going 0-2 to start the season in consecutive years. Ugly wins are wins, and when you can get them with a roster built like this, it rockets you up further, as the big games are still coming. Are there some questions after week 2? Sure, but this team is going to have a decent floor going forward.

Surprise! The Mayor came to the party fully stocked in week 2 and made it rain TDs in the Titty City. I do not forsee the Lions embarassing Ben Johnson every week this year, so the 57 points between ASB and Gibbs may be a bit of an outlier. However, this is a weekl of celebration for Titty City. We will see what next week holds has Jacob tries to break his week 3 winless streak (0-6) in a matchup with the surging Wolf Pack.

The Big Lig's big names did not deliver in week 2, and probably only raise questions going into week 3, such as why the heck is Henderson behind Gibson? Too much talent on this team, so I would presume this is the lowest week of the year for Gil.

Baby Jaws has an odd roster, with underperforming big names and overperforming small names even if they're long names. Lots of talent in the ocean, but the big questions center around direct (Daniels, Jones, Worthy) and indirect (Fields) injuries. Week 3 doesn't get any easier against The Big Lig.

Leading the league in overall record through 2 weeks (12-2 since 2019), the Bakery is off to another great start in 2025. The RB room is a problem, but other talent may make the RB2 unneccessary. Week 3 is a big test in the battle of the Joshes.

If you were a Bun Spreader, you had a good week (the top 4 teams all came from there), but that means 2 teams still had a bad week. Even with 120 points, Big Jim got his Twins smashed by the Mayor's 138.

The Jerdawgs hopped on the back of Puka and rode that 45 yard rush TD to a win over The Big Lig, in what was an uninspiring matchup. Meat and potato wins may be the recipe for these pups the rest of the year.

Do not try and Keep Up with the Joneses. Austin set 2 more records in week 2, becoming the first team to start the season with back-to-back scores in the 60s, and while also having the lowest score through two weeks by nearly 40 points (123.66 compared to Gil's 161.73 in 2024). Sounds rough? What if I told you Austin also just lost Joe Burrow for at least the next 3 months?
Overall, this was not a bad week for Joe. Outside of Nix and Engram, everyone did mostly what they were supposed to. An encouraging start despite the discouraging result.
Fitting week 1 result for the #1 overall picking team. Trust the process. But you still suck Jacob.

The writers started off the new season with a hit, dropping the #1 QB, #1 WR, and #2 RB on the week. With just those 3 players, Trevor would have beaten at least 4 teams this week. If the stars are stars, who cares who else you have.

What appeared to be an easy matchup on paper, ended up being a nail-biting, 1.89 point loss to Big Jim to start the season 0-1. The bench is still uninspiring, but the starters could drop big numbers any week.

The 3rd highest score met the 1st highest score, and Josh was still 25 points away from a win (all while possibly becoming the 1st team ever to hit their projections exactly). The WRs definitely took the option this week, while the RBs (including the benched ones) dominated (Henry looks like he's back in HS again). I would expect things to get better for Game of Jones with the talent level on board.

The Big Lig handled business with a near 30-point cushion to be wrong in his start/sit choices. These may have been peak performances for some, but otherwise appear to just be warming up. I'd expect Gil to be a team you don't want to face most the season.
Baby Jaws with the baby point margin win (1.59) over the Jerdawgs. With some mixed performances, week 1 may have created more start/sit questions than answers for Jona.

The Bakery was gifted an easy order to fill week 1, just 62.57 foods would do the trick. Despite the injury concerns, CMC rewarded Yish with 23 non-TD related points, showing he is still so very good. The swing for the fences approach taken by B3 only produced 87 total points, but 1 win. We will see what week 2 has in store.

Jacob drew the long stick and only needed 88.01 points for the W, which he accomplished. The hope is there forTitty City, especially after a promising week 1 for some players, as well as the impending return of Judkins.
Jerry drove his Ford until it died 1.60 feet short of a victory. While this team will likely stick with this general point total, the Bowers injury is a concern for that stability.
Big Jim picks up where he left off, earning win #1 of the season in a barn burner VS The Wolf Pack. Stars played well, but the loss of Kittle hurts the odds the next few weeks.

Was this a preseason matchup? The only two players seeking a job performed well (Breece & Meyers, 19 & 15), while everyone else appeared to have been pulled after a couple drives. It can only go up from here, but how high is the more relevant question.

Joe took what fell to him each round and made the best of the 2nd overall pick, securing a locked in roster that will be tough to beat any week. Beyond the loaded starting roster, Joe has 2-3 guys that could slot in during week 2 as starters for most teams.

Having the 1st overall pick feesl like only you can get in your own way. At the moment, El Tuddy Buddy looks like they should be just fine and not have squandered a great opportunity. The starters are loaded, but the bench has too many guys you might be seeing on the waiver wire at some point this year.

Ryan may have done it again somehow. Not having a 2nd round pick is usually a death token, but the Wolf Pack may have one of the best starting lineups in the league if 1-2 players perform as hyped. The bench is not stacked with players you want to start this week, but almost everyone has a path to success at some point this season.
Balanced as they come, Jona has major upside with strong starters in every position. Outside of injury, Baby Jaws should expect to see the postseason.
There was clearly an age requirement to join Game of Jones, as Brock Purdy is the least experienced player on this roster. Older and wiser may be the outcome, but older and dustier is just as likely.

In an effort to not step on his own toes, Trevor sought out the entire Bears organization and acquired most of them. Lukcily for the Toons, those will likely be background actors, as Bijan, Jeanty, Josh Allen and Marv will carry this show every week as the stars.
With 4 picks prior to the 3rd round, Gil rode the hype train to a far more boom or bust roster than one would expect. However, the boom potential is absolutely there.
The Boys Beefed up talent on the front end with Nico, TMcB and CMC, and the bench has plenty of upside. If even just 1-2 of the upside plays hit, this team will be stacked.

Drafting from the 11 spot without a 3rd or 5th round pick is challenging, but the Jerdawgs did well all things considered. The team appears to be built for early success that may taper off, but a hot start can't be overvalued.

Austin went into the 2025 draft with the least enviable setup, yet he beat expectations on his final roster. The core of the team certainly can be competitive and even steal an unexpected win here or there, but any postseason hopes will require some luck, waiver talent and/or trade activity.

In a non-dynasty league, this may be as close to a run-it-back type of roster as I've ever seen. The bench went full handcuff mode, but Lamar, Jefferson, Cook and Kittle may be plenty to keep this team in the fight on most weeks.

Keeping a 2nd round player without a 3rd round pick meant Jacob had to swing for the fences, and time will tell if he hit a home run or not by drafting unsigned/likely to be suspended Quinshon Judkins to a starting position. The BAC was way down from last year in Titty City, but the results may be the same.
